title: Medicine
description: Internal Medicine — Cardiology, Pulmonology, Nephrology, Gastroenterology, Rheumatology, Endocrinology.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man with diabetes and hypertension is admitted with extensive anterior ST elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). had successful angioplasty and stenting to left anterior descending artery. Aspirin, clopidogrel, bisoprolol and enalapril were started (see lab results). Cholesterol (HDL) 1.0 > 1.03 mmol/L Cholesterol (LDL) 3.36 <3.36 mmol/L Total Cholesterol 5.0 <5.1 mmol/L Triglycendes 2.2 <2.16 mmol/L Which of the following is recommended?

A 55-year-old man with diabetes presented to the Cardiology Clinic with vague chest pain with exertion for 2 months (see report). Electrocardiogram: Normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
A 5-day-old cyanotic infant with a diagnosis of Tricuspid Atresia. Which of the following is the most important issue to consider during the discussion with parents?

options.text: Make sure that you have left no question unanswered
Make sure the parents understand the dismal prognosis
Make sure the parents understand that you are doing everything you can
Make sure you leave the parents with a follow-up plan and provide them cardiac consultation

questions.stem: A 3-month-old infant diagnosed with congestive heart failure with follow-up by cardiology. Mother asks regarding the nutritional needs for her infant. What is the most appropriate counseling should be given?

options.text: The same as a healthy infants

questions.stem: A 7-year-old boy case of congestive heart failure on digoxin. Which of the following is the most important step to improve his compliance?

options.text: Send a nurse to his home to check on compliance
Having the child participate in devising the plan
Inform the family about side effects of medication

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best advice to decrease anxiety of a child's parents who is scheduled for cardiac surgery?

options.text: Obtain an order for anti-anxiety medication for the parents
Explain the steps that will occur before and after surgery
Send education material to parents and the child about the surgery
Tell the parents not to worry, because the surgeon performs this procedure daily

questions.stem: A child with tetralogy of fallot present for regular check-up. Mother asks why her child squats after exertion. Which of the following is the best explanation?

options.text: Decreases blood volume in the extremities

questions.stem: A 7-year-old girl presents to the clinic with fever and skin rash for 1 day. She also has pain and swelling in her both knees and wrists. The family gave a history of fever and sore throat two weeks ago which has been recovered completely. On examination, she has pain, swelling and limited movement in both knees and wrists. She has erythema marginatum rash. The remaining exam is unremarkable. She is started on antibiotic and anti-inflammatory medications. Which of the following is the best next step in management?

A 2-year-old boy brought to the Emergency Room for the second time with non-resolving high-grade fever 39.5 °C. Fever started 6 days ago and was prescribed antipyretic when he was evaluated initially 3 days ago. However, antipyretic did not help much in relieving the fever. Kawasaki disease suspected. Which of the following is one of the five principal clinical features of Kawasaki disease?

options.text: Anterior uveitis by slit lamp examination
Bilateral bulbar conjunctival injection without exudate

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most common congenital heart defect in Down syndrome?
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old woman with history of rheumatic heart disease since childhood presented with exertional dyspnea and occasional paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Physical examination showed JVP of 5 cm above sternal angle, loud S1, loud P2 and mid diastolic rumbling murmur in the apex. Fine basal crackles are present on lung auscultation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-old man presents with abdominal distension dyspnea and orthopnea. The JVP is markedly elevated and fails to descend during inspiration. Lower limbs showed massive pitting edema up to the thighs. Heart sounds are normal. There are bibasilar crackles on lung auscultation. Abdominal examination showed hepatomegaly and positive shifting dullness (see report). Echocardiogram: Both atria are dilated. Left and right ventricles are normal in size and LVEF is 60%. No valve lesions. Which of the following has the highest diagnostic value?

An 18-year-old boy presents with recurrent syncope with exercise. Physical examination showed normal JVP, jerky carotid pulsations and thrusting apex. There is an ejection systolic murmur, which is best heard in the left parasternal area that increases in intensity with standing and reduced during handgrip (see report). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 76 /min Electrocardiogram: Shows left ventricular hypertrophy. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A young man with diagnosis of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy presented with recurrent exertional chest pain and syncope. Which of the following is the best management?

A 65-year-old woman with diabetes and hypertension, presented with retrosternal chest pain at rest for 3 hours. Physical examination is normal except for $4 gallop (see lab result and report). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg, Heart rate 76 /min, Oxygen saturation 95 % Troponin 10 < 0.2 pg/L Electrocardiogram: T-wave inversion in leads V2-V5. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-old patient with a previous ischaemic stroke presents with a regular narrow complex tachycardia. The patient is hemodynamically stable. The decision is made to administer IV adenosine. In the presence of which of the following should the dose of adenosine be reduced?
Which of the following drugs used in the treatment of chronic heart failure has been shown to increase survival?

A 30-year-old man presents with burning retrosternal chest pain associated with dyspnea. His history is significant only for common cold 2 weeks ago (see image). Which of the following clinical signs is likely to be present?

A 70-year-old man presents with dyspnea, fatigue and presyncope. On examination, the JVP showed Cannon a-wave and variations in the intensity of the first heart sound (see image). Which of the following is the definitive treatment?

A 39-year-old man presents to the clinic with unexplained fever 19 days after an attack of acute rheumatic fever. Several of his teeth have been extracted prior to the hospital admission. Clinical examination confirms a systolic murmur and splenomegaly (see lab results). Test Result Normal Values WBC 14.0 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Neutrophils 72 40-60% Urinalysis: Erythrocytes 25 0-2 per HPF Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 64-year-old woman with advanced breast cancer complains of dyspnea on exertion. On examination, her systolic blood pressure is noted to markedly decrease during inspiration. Heart sounds are distant to auscultation. Chest is clear (see report). Blood pressure 95/65 mmH, Heart rate 100 /min, Respiratory rate 24 /min, Temperature 36.6 °C, Oxygen saturation 95 % Chest x-ray: Marked cardiomegaly with clear lung fields. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following immediate action should be taken?
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 70-year-old man with hypertension, diabetes and aortic sclerosis discovered to have atrial fibrillation on routine health check-up. He denies dyspnea, chest pain or palpitations. Which of the following drugs is recommended to prevent systemic embolization?

A 22-year-old woman presents with retrosternal burning chest pain, which is worse during breathing and coughing. Precordial auscultation showed an added sound of 3 components; systolic, diastolic and presystolic (see image). Which of the following is the best initial treatment?
In a patient with heart failure due to dilated cardiomyopathy presenting with fast atrial fibrillation, which of the following drugs is the most appropriate to control the heart rate?

A 40-year-old man is admitted with palpitations of 4-hour duration. He had similar attack a month ago but did not seek medical advice. His initial electrocardiogram showed atrial fibrillation with controlled ventricular rate. He subsequently converted to sinus rhythm. Which of the following drugs is the most appropriate to maintain sinus rhythm?

A 62-year-old man presents with recurrent retrosternal chest pain, which he said has become much worse over the last 3 weeks. He describes the pain as lasting much longer than before and that it occurs even while he is setting in a chair or in bed at night reading. Which of the following is the most likely type of angina?

An 18-year-old girl is recently diagnosed to have rheumatic fever with carditis. Echocardiogram showed mild mitral stenosis with mild regurgitation. To what age the rheumatic fever prophylaxis is recommended?

A 28-year-old woman presents to the Cardiology Outpatient Department with recurrent palpitations for the last 6 months. She describes the palpitations as fast heartbeat, which starts and ends suddenly. Each attack lasts 5-10 min. No associated chest pain, dyspnea, syncope or presyncope (see lab result and report). Hb 132 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone 3.8 0.4 - 5.0 jU/mL. Electrocardiogram: Normal sinus rhythm with rate of 70/min. Which of the following is the best next investigation?

A 52-year-old man comes to the clinic for a checkup. He has hypertension for 5 years is currently being treated with hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg/day (see lab results). Blood pressure 155/101 mmHg Heart rate 84 /min Test Result Normal Values Sodium 141 134-146 mmol/L Potassium 4.1 3.5-5.1 mmol/L Creatinine 105 44-115 umol/L Glucose, fasting 7.3 3.5-6.5 mmol/L Which of the following is the most appropriate management modification?

options.text: Add an angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitor

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man with paraplegia following road traffic accident one year ago is brought to the Emergency Department because of sudden onset dyspnea and chest pain. On examination, he is in severe distress and cyanosed. He has left parasternal heave and loud P2. Chest is clear to auscultation (see lab results and reports). Blood pressure 80/55 mmHg Heart rate 110 /min Respiratory rate 30 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Oxygen saturation 86 % ABG HCO3- 22 22-28 mmol/L ABG PCO2 4.2 4.7-6.0 kPa pH 7.4 7.36-7.45 ABG PO2 8.6 10.6-14.2 kPa Echocardiogram: Dilated right ventricle with pulmonary artery pressure of 55 mmHg. Venous Doppler: Confirmed DVT in the left leg extending to the thigh. Which of the following is the best line of management?

A 55-year-old man with COPD, presented with increasing dyspnea, cough and bilateral lower limb swelling. Physical examination showed elevated JVP, hepatomegaly and pitting edema in both lower limbs. Chest auscultation revealed scattered rhonchi in both sides. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.text: High resolution CT scan of chest

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man with diabetes mellitus and ischemic heart disease is admitted to the Critical Care Unit in shock. The following parameters are obtained from pulmonary artery catheterization (see table). Pulmonary Artery Catheter Test Result Normal Values Right atrial pressure 2 2-8 mmHg Pulmonary artery pressure 15/3 16-24/5-12 mmHg Wedge pressure 4 5-12 mmHg Cardiac output 2.5 4-6 L/min Systemic vascular resistance 1800 800-1200 dyne/s/cm5 Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
Which of the following is the most appropriate test to confirm the diagnosis?

A 52-year-old man was diagnosed in the Emergency Department with an acute inferior wall myocardial infarction. An intravenous morphine bolus and IV nitroglycerine infusion were administered for severe on-going chest discomfort. 20 minutes later, and while preparing the patient for a primary percutaneous coronary intervention, his condition became worse. His JVP at this time was elevated and his lungs were clear. Initial Emergency Department Record: Blood pressure 120/70 mmH Heart rate 90 /min (regular) Respiratory rate 22 /min Oxygen saturation 96% (room air) 30 Minutes Later: Blood pressure 75/40 mmHg Heart rate 105 /min (regular) Which of the following is the most likely cause of the hypotension?

A 55-year-old man who is a heavy smoker is being evaluated for increasing bilateral lower limb swellings. Chest examination confirms resonant lungs with reduced breath sounds and occasional rhonchi. The apex beat could not be easily located. No cardiac murmur is heard, but P2 is markedly loud. The JVP is elevated and bilateral pitting edema was confirmed. Which of the following is the most likely cause of the lower limb swelling?

A 15-year-old boy presents to the clinic for an annual physical assessment. The patient has normal growth and development and is able to do usual activities. His elder brother died due to a sudden cardiac death while walking to work. On physical examination, there is no cardiac murmur. Pulses are equal in all extremities. Which condition must be excluded before any sport is allowed?

A 55-year-old man presents with a 3-month history of exertional chest pain. He has a previous history of myocardial infarction. Which of the following is modifiable risk factor in the treatment of ischemic heart disease?
A 43-year-old healthy man concerned about heart disease. Which of the following is the most important risk factor of ischemic heart disease?

options.text: 2 separate fasting plasma glucose of 8.2 and 8.3 mmol/L.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old that underwent a cardiac bypass, presented with central abdominal pain. Examination confirmed high cardiac output and cardiac index with low peripheral vascular resistance. Blood pressure 90/60 mmHg Heart rate 120 /min Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old man presented with fever, rigors and weight loss for 10 days. He underwent Mitral valve replacement by prosthetic valve a month ago. Echo showed small vegetation. Blood pressure 90/70 mmHg, Heart rate 100 /min, Temperature 38.7 °C Which of the following organisms is the most likely to be responsible for his presentation?
Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
Which of the following is the best management option for endocarditis prophylaxis?

A 64-year-old man presented to Emergency Room with symptoms of dyspnoea, SOB, and palpitation. He is a known case of diabetic mellitus, hypertension and hyperlipidaemia. He is smoker with history of stroke. On examination, found to have irregular pulse. Cardiac and chest examination showed high JVP, S3 and bi-basal crackles. Atrial fibrillation on ECG. Blood pressure 150/90 mmH Heart rate 144 /min Oxygen saturation 89 % What is the CHADS2 score of this patient?
Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.text: Repeat blood pressure determination in 4 months

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man is evaluated during a follow-up visit for management of newly diagnosed hypertension and diabetes mellitus started on metformin and gliclazide but not started on antihypertensive therapy. Physical examination is unremarkable (see lab results). Blood pressure 155/95 mmH Heart rate 80 /min BMI 32.5 kg/m2 Blood urea nitrogen 5 (2.8 to 8.9 mmol/L) Creatinine 100 (44-115 mol/L) Random Glucose 6 (3.9-5.5 mmol/L) HbA1C 6.9 (4.7-5.6 %) Protein Present: absent Glucose Absent: absent Which of the following is the most appropriate antihypertensive treatment for this patient?

A 70-year-old patient has a sudden onset of pain in the left lower limb. The pain is severe and associated with numbness. The patient had an acute myocardial infarction 2 weeks before and was discharged 24 hours before this presentation. The left leg is cold and pale, the right leg is normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A patient with atrial fibrillation is on warfarin 5 mg daily, the latest INR is 7.0 on routine evaluation. There is no evidence of abnormal bleeding. Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Continue with same dose of warfarin
Hold warfarin and repeat INR next day

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate to be included in immediate management?

A 70-year-old man, with no past medical history, presents to the Emergency Department 4 hours after the onset of a severe crushing substernal chest pain radiating to the neck and left arm (see report). Electrocardiography: Significant ST-segment elevation in leads I, AVL, V5, and V6. Where is the most likely site of cardiac infarction?

A 60-year-old patient presents to the hospital, complaining of a sudden onset of chest pain radiating to the back. The blood pressure is low in the left arm and the left femoral pulse is not palpable (see reports). Chest X-ray: A left pleural effusion. ECG: Left ventricular hypertrophy. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

A 46-year-old man recovering from an acute myocardial infarction 10 days ago. He develops a sharp pain behind the sternum which is made worse by coughing. The patient gets relief when sitting forward. On examination, a scratchy superficial sound is heard at the left sternal edge, and heart sounds are muffled. There is ascites and a 2 cm raised JVP is confirmed. Which of the following ECG changes would most likely be found?

A 60-year-old man is admitted to the Coronary Care Unit with an acute myocardial infarction. His hemodynamic parameters 2 hours later are: Blood pressure 80/50 mmHg Heart rate 40 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 36.6° C Oxygen saturation 95% on room air Which of the following would be the appropriate management?
Which of the following is the most appropriate initial intervention?

A 60-year-old man presents to the Emergency Department with heavy retrosternal chest discomfort. The discomfort started 3 days earlier as intermittent brief episodes which became more frequent and prolonged over the last 24 hours. In the Emergency Department he experienced a similar type of discomfort (5/10 on the pain scale of 1-10) which responded well to sublingual nitroglycerin. Serial cardiac enzymes are normal (see report). ECG: An initial ECG showed ST segment depression of 0.2 mV in the antero-lateral chest leads, which later normalized completely. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment after the initial Emergency Department management?

A 75-year-old man who has been followed up routinely for hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus was found to have an irregular pulse which was not found 6 months earlier. In addition to hypertension and diabetes, his past history confirms a previous transient ischemic attack. He is currently asymptomatic and is compliant with his medications (see report). ECG: Atrial fibrillation at a rate of 70 beats per minute. Which of the following is the most appropriate management plan?

options.text: Add digoxin to his current treatment regimen
Start anticoagulation therapy to prevent stroke
No further step is needed as he is asymptomatic

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman presents to the Emergency Department complaining of being unable to sleep flat for the last 2 nights due to difficulty in breathing. She has just delivered 1 week earlier. Physical examination confirms a laterally displaced apex beat and the presence of a third heart sound. The jugular veins were distended and bilateral lung crackles could be easily heard. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old man had a myocardial infarction 6 days before. He suddenly develops dyspnoea, cough and frothy sputum. For the first time a harsh systolic murmur is heard over the precordium. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this development?
A 55-year-old man presents to the Emergency Department with continuous retrosternal chest pain. An ECG was obtained (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

options.text: Acute coronary syndrome with unstable angina

questions.stem: Which of the following drugs is indicated?

A 23-year-old woman evaluated for dyspnoea and recurrent palpitation. She has a history of Fallot tetralogy repair at the age of 3. On cardiac examination, apex was normal with left parasternal impulse. S1 is single with grade 2/4 decrescendo diastolic murmur that increases with inspiration noted at left sternal border. Blood pressure 110/70 mmg Heart rate 94 /min Oxygen saturation 92 % Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old woman presents with fatigue, SOB, arthralgia and fever for 2 weeks. It is worsened with time specially the fever. She has no significant medical history apart from sore throat 3 weeks ago and dental extraction 2 months ago. Skin examination revealed petechia over lower limb. Cardiac examination demonstrated 3/6 holosystolic murmur that radiates to axilla and mild splenomegaly (see report). Blood pressure 100/60 mmH Heart rate 88 /min Temperature 38.5 °C Urine dipstick: Showed mild proteinuna and microscopic hematuria Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old woman is admitted with dyspnea, SOB, PND and orthopnea 3 days post vaginal delivery. She gave a history of lower limb edema. She has no significant medical history. On examination, she looks in distress with bilateral LL pitting edema, bilateral basal crackles on lung examination. On cardiac examination, apex was displaced down with pan-systolic murmur at the apex radiating to axilla and S3 gallop. Blood pressure 90/60 mmH Heart rate 110 /min Temperature 37.6 °C Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old woman is admitted with cough, dyspnea, chest pain, SOB, PND and orthopnea 3 days post vaginal delivery. She gave a history of lower limb edema. She has no significant medical history. On examination, she looks in distress with bilateral LL pitting oedema, bilateral basal crackles on lung examination. On cardiac examination, apex was displaced down with pan-systolic murmur at the apex radiating to axilla and S3 gallop Blood pressure 90/70 mmHg Heart rate 120 /min Temperature 37.6 °C Oxygen saturation 90 % Which of the following is the most appropriate step in this patient management?

A 70-year-old man was hospitalized 6 days ago for a 4-day history of acute leg ischemia treated with angioplasty and stenting. He is now asymptomatic. He has a history of stage 3 chronic kidney disease and hypertension that is well-controlled with diltiazem and captopril. Other medications are aspirin and clopidogrel. On physical examination, the patient is febrile and normal blood pressure. The remainder of the examination is unremarkable (see lab results). Creatinine 140 44-115 mol/L Total Cholesterol 5.9 <5.1 mmol/L LDL (cholesterol) 4.9 <4.0 mmol/L Which of the following is the most appropriate therapy for secondary prevention of cardiovascular disease in this patient?

A 61-year-old man with suspected left ventricular heart failure. He had B-type natriuretic peptide (BNPy test, which came back as being slightly elevated. Which of the following factors cause a falsely elevated NP?

A 60-year-old man with diabetes, hypertension and intermittent claudication due is diagnosed to have stable angina. Decision is made to manage him with intensive medical therapy. He is started on aspirin, rosuvastatin and nitroglycerine but still gets angina with moderate exercise. Blood pressure 130/85 mmHg Heart rate 86 /min Which of the following is the most appropriate additional drug?

A 20-year-old woman presents to the Emergency Department with palpitations for 2-hours (see image and lab results). Blood pressure 135/80 mmHg Heart rate 150 /min Hb 138 (130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female)) Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone 3.2 (0.4 - 5.0 U/mL) Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?

A 65-year-old man with diabetes is admitted to the Coronary Care Unit with diagnosis of acute ST elevation anterior myocardial infarction. He developed massive hematemesis following streptokinase infusion. Which of the following drugs would reverse the action of streptokinase?

A 69-year-old man is admitted with acute chest pain and shortness of breath. Workup confirmed acute myocardial infarction. Upon discharge, he is advised to quit smoking. but he is unwilling to do so. What should be said to the patient during the counselling session?

options.text: "We will involve the family in this issue"
"If you do not stop smoking you will die"

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man with congestive heart failure on multiple treatments came to the clinic for follow up. The physician discussed with him the importance of compliance and the effect of the treatments on his life. Which of the following medications is associated with reduced mortality rate in congestive heart failure?

A 65-year-old man presents to the Emergency Department with exertional syncope and progressive shortness of breath. Clinical examination reveals fine crackles at both lung bases and mid-systolic murmur at the right upper sternal border that radiates to carotids. Chest radiography demonstrated clear evidence of pulmonary edema. Which of the following statements about the assessment and diagnosis is the most accurate?

options.text: The murmur will be augmented by standing position
The main treatment for symptomatic patient is diuretics
Electrocardiogram (ECG) will show right bundle branch block (RBBB)
Presence of symptoms of congestive heart failure are poor prognosis

questions.stem: A 48-year-old woman is seen in the clinic because of recurrent severe nocturnal chest pain for several months that rapidly resolved with sublingual nitrate. She had a normal cardiac catheterization and positive ergonovine echocardiography testing. She does not want to use multiple medications and she accept to use only one drug as a long-term maintenance therapy. Which of the following drugs is the best strategy for long-term management of this patient?

A 60-year-old man is evaluated in the clinic for cardiac risk assessment. He is asymptomatic and physically active. He has never smoked. He has no chronic health issues and takes no medications. His physical examinations are normal. Cardiovascular risk calculation using the Pooled Cohort Equations predicts a 6.5% risk of a myocardial infarction in the next 10 years that indicate an intermediate risk of myocardial infarction. Which of the following investigations should be done next?
Which of the following is the most appropriate test to perform next?

A 55-year-old woman presents to the clinic for her regular follow-up. 6 months ago, she presented to Emergency Department with palpitations and dyspnea and diagnosed to have atrial fibrillation. She is currently asymptomatic with no palpitations. Her medical history is also significant for a transient ischemic attack and hypertension. Her medications are warfarin, metoprolol and candesartan, Her physical examination is unremarkable. Her most recent electrocardiogram shows normal sinus rhythm. which of the following is the most appropriate management?
Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in the management?

A 26-year-old pregnant woman visits the clinic for regular follow-up. She is asymptomatic. She is in her 30th week of pregnancy. Her physical examination reveals a mid-systolic ejection murmur at the right upper sternal border. The murmur radiates to carotids. No diastolic murmur is heard. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old man is evaluated in the Emergency Department for severe persistent chest pain for 1-day. The pain is constant but exacerbated when leaning forward and not associated with other symptoms. Physical examination is unremarkable apart of a friction rub at the left lower sternal border. Electrocardiogram shows diffuse, concave upward ST-segment elevations and PR-segment depression most prominent in leads V1 through V6. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 58-year-old woman was admitted with a diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction received appropriate treatments and now she is ready for discharge. She is so concern about the secondary prevention of infarction. Which of the following statements is the most appropriate?

options.text: Anti-platelet agents should be used for short period to reduce the risk of recurrent infarction
Calcium channel blockers should be used indefinitely to reduce the risk of recurrent infarction
Hormonal replacement therapy should be given to postmenopausal women to prevent coronary events
Angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) Inhibitors should be used indefinitely by patient with clinically evident heart failure

questions.stem: A 55-year-old woman with non-decompensated systolic heart failure and ejection fraction of 25% presents to the clinic for routine follow-up. Which of the following medications is the most appropriate management?

A 45-year-old woman is evaluated for a 3-week history of progressive shortness of breath that limit her activities. Medical history is significant for asthma and moderate mitral regurgitation. Her only medication is an albuterol inhaler as needed. On physical examination, her vital signs are normal. Cardiac examination reveals a grade 3/6 holosystolic murmur radiating to the axilla Lungs are clear to auscultation. Which of the following is the most appropriate diagnostic test?

options.text: Helical (or spiral) computed tomography (CT) of the chest

questions.stem: A 67-year-old man presents with insomnia, irritability and palpitation for 3 months. He is known to have hypertension, depression and atrial fibrillation. He is on amiodarone, fluoxetine and enalopril. Clinically, he is unremarkable. Blood pressure 130/70 mmHg, Heart rate 76 /min, Oxygen saturation 95 % Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 62-year-old man presents to Outpatient Clinic with recurrent episodes of steal chest tightness, which occurs mainly after heavy physical exertion. He has no chronic medical problems. Clinical examination and baseline ECG were normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

A 28-year-old man presents with recent onset of chest pain. The pain is retrosternal, localized, sharp and constant in intensity. He noticed increase in seventy with movement. He started active exercise program a week prior to the onset of the symptom. Blood pressure 110/70 mmH Heart rate 76 /min Oxygen saturation 95 % Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 65-year-old woman came for routine annual check-up found to have with harsh ejection systolic murmur, which propagated to the neck. Which of the following factors is the most important in deciding the time of the surgery?

A 65-year-old man found to have an ejection systolic murmur on clinical examination. There is no history of chest pain, shortness of breath nor syncope. ECHO confirmed aortic stenosis with good left ventricular systolic function. Aortic valve gradient of 40 mmH. Blood pressure 100/65 mmHg Heart rate 67 /min Which of the following is the most appropriate management option?
Which of the following is the best treatment option?

A 38-year-old Indian man presents with progressive dyspnea for 3 months. He has past history of old tuberculosis. He has no other medical problems and not on any medications. His JVP was elevated and rises further on inspiration. Cardiac examination was normal with no murmurs. Blood pressure 105/60 mmH Heart rate 120 /min Oxygen saturation 93 % Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old woman who is a known case of mitral stenosis came to the clinic asking about how critical is her condition. Echo was done and mitral valve orifice was recorded. Which of the following mitral valve orifice measurement is consider critical?
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 65-year-old man with heart failure requires rate control to treat coexisting atrial fibrillation. Which of the following is the best treatment option?
Asymptomatic healthy 24-year-old woman came for a check-up visit and found to have grade II mid-diastolic murmur over the apex. Which of the following is the best next step in diagnosis?
Which of the following medication should be added at this stage?

A 70-year-old man admitted with left lower limb swelling and pain diagnosed as DVT where heparin was started. He has a history of diabetes mellitus, hypertension and chronic heart failure. He is on insulin; furosemide and enalapril (see lab results). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg, Heart rate 76 /min, Oxygen saturation 94 % Sodium 135 134-146 mmol/L Potassium 6,0 3.5-5.1 mmol/L Chloride 107 97-108 mmol/L Urea 7.9 2.75-7.4 mmol/L Creatinine 120 44-115 mol/L APTT 50 30-40 sec Prothrombin time 14 10-13 sec Which of the following medications should be discontinued at this stage?

A 50-year-old man who works as a bank employee is discharged following a 7-day admission for acute myocardial infarction. He was given 5 different drugs. What further information regarding lifestyle and daily activities should be given to him?

options.text: Advise him to change his job
Refrain from sexual activities for 3 months
Perform mild aerobic exercise from next week

questions.stem: A 23-year-old man is brought to the hospital after an episode of collapse. He states that on a few occasions while playing football he has had some chest pain, breathlessness and felt as he was going to faint. Last night during training, he collapsed and blacked out for a few seconds. Clinical examination revealed a harsh ejection systolic murmur with a palpable systolic thrill at the left sternal edge; and a prominent jerky carotid pulse. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 68-year-old man is seen for a follow-up. He has long standing breathlessness and symptoms of cardiac failure. The ECG confirmed a diagnosis of heart failure due to left ventricular dysfunction. His currently on enalopril 10 mg OD, simvastatin 40 mg OD, furosemide 40 mg OD and omeprazole 20 mg OD. Examination revealed that the chest is clear and heart sounds are normal. There is no peripheral edema. Blood pressure 125/83 mmHg, Heart rate 76 /min. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in the management at this stage?

A 78-year-old man diagnosed with heart failure due to left ventricular dysfunction. His currently on aspirin 75 mg OD, simvastatin 40 mg OD and furosemide 40 mg OD. On examination, heart sounds are normal, his chest is clear and there is no peripheral edema. Which of the following is the most appropriate drug therapy to initiate at this stage?

A 78-year-old woman presents with exertional syncope. On clinical examination, she has a slow rising carotid pulse and a loud ejection systolic murmur at the upper right sternal edge, radiating to the carotids. Which of the following is the most likely cause of these findings?

A 58-year-old man comes to the clinic for a follow-up. He has been discharged after an acute inferior myocardial infarction. He is diabetic type 2, on metformin 1g BD, aspirin 75 mg. atorvastatin 10 mg OD and lisinopril 10 mg OD. Examination revealed bilateral basal crackles on auscultation of the chest. Blood pressure 148/88 mmH, Heart rate 76 /min, BMI 24 kg/m2 Which of the following is the most appropriate medication to add to his regime?

A 61-year-old woman comes to the clinic complaining of palpitations. She has also noticed some weight loss over the last 2 months. On clinical examination, she has an irregularly irregular pulse and a fine tremor. Her ECG shows atrial fibrillation. Which of the following is the next most appropriate investigation to do?

A 66-year-old man comes for follow-up. He has shortness of breath on exercise, which have increased over the past few months. He became unable to walk more than 200-300 meters on the corridor and cannot climb the stairs easily. He has history of hypertension and currently on amlodipine 5 mg OD and indapamide 2.5 mg OD. On examination, he has bilateral basal crackles and mild pitting ankle edema (see lab results). Blood pressure 188/96 mmH, Heart rate 79 /min. Hb 133 {130-170 g/L (Male) | 120-160 g/L (Female)} Sodium 138 {134-146 mmol/L} Potassium 4.2 {3.5-5.1 mmol/L} Creatinine 133 {44-115 mol/L} Which of the following is the most appropriate next therapy?
A 66-year-old man presents with a diastolic murmur best heard at the left sternal edge. On examination, the apex beat is displaced outwards. Which condition typically presents with these findings?

A 64-year-old man is diagnosed with persistent atrial fibrillation. His past medical history includes hypertension and type 2 diabetes. He has no contraindications to any antithrombotic treatments. What antithrombotic treatment should be considered first line for this patient?

A 77-year-old woman comes to the clinic for a check-up. She has an irregular pulse when the nurse checked her vitals. An ECG has confirmed persistent atrial fibrillation. She is completely asymptomatic. She has a past medical history of migraine and asthma and on salbutamol PRN for asthma and PRN ibuprofen for her migraines. Other clinical examinations are normal. Blood pressure 138/85 mmHg, Heart rate 88 /min. What antithrombotic treatment should be considered first line in this patient?

A 29-year-old man is seen in the pre-employment clinic for routine exam, He is asymptomatic. Physical examination revealed a systolic murmur that heard at the apex. The murmur is augmented with sustained handgrip and reduced with Valsalva manoeuvre. Which of the following is the most likely cause for this murmur?
A 57-year-old man who is intolerant of aspirin is started on clopidogrel for the secondary prevention of ischemic heart disease. Which of the following drugs can make clopidogrel less effective?

A 77-year-old man with a history of atrial fibrillation is admitted to the hospital following an acute coronary intervention and treated with a percutaneous coronary intervention. His medication on admission were warfarin, paracetamol and allopurinol. Antithrombotic therapy immediately given after his event. Which of the following regimen should he be prescribed?

options.text: Continue warfarin with the addition of 2 antiplatelets

questions.stem: A 59-year-old man presents 4 weeks after being discharged from hospital. He had been admitted with chest pain and thrombolysed for a myocardial infarction. 2 days later, he developed marked tongue and facial swelling. His vital signs are within the normal limits. Which of the following drugs is most likely to be responsible?
A 47-year-old man presents with intermittent chest pains for the past 2 days. On examination, he tachycardic and sweaty. ECG is done (see image). Blood pressure 133 /81 mmHg. What does the ECG show?

A 61-year-old man comes to the clinic with a 2-day history of dyspnoea on exertion. He has a long standing hypertension and a 30-pack-year smoking history. Physical examination is unremarkable except for rare crackles at the bases of the lungs. Which of the following tests would be most helpful for detecting left ventricular dysfunction?

A 65-year-old man presents with severe chest pain to Emergency Room. ECG showed st segment elevation of inferior leads. He received thrombolytic therapy (PA). 3 hours later, started to feel dizzy. ECG showed 2:1 AV block. IV atropine given with no effect. Vital signs 3 hours later: Blood pressure 80/45 mmH, Heart rate 39 /min, Respiratory rate 18 /min, Oxygen saturation 90 % Which of the following is the best management option?

A 65-year-old man presented to Emergency Room with severe chest pain. He was diagnosed as inferior MI and received thromolytic therapy (PA). Few hours later, he developed dizziness. ECG is done (see image). Blood pressure 80/50 mmg, Heart rate 41 /min Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old woman presented to the clinic with new onset SOB and fatigue. She is diagnosed as a case of mitral stenosis with pulmonary hypertension. She is planning to get pregnant and she is hiding the diagnosis from her husband. Which of the following is the most appropriate advice?

options.text: She can go ahead with her plan
Call her husband and tell him the diagnosis
Counseling her about the risk and squally of the pregnancy

questions.stem: A 33-year-old man presented with shortness of breath, orthopnea and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Exanimation revealed collapsing pulse and wide pulse pressure. Early diastolic murmur over left sternal border and pistol-shot sound heard over femoral arteries. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 55-year-old patient comes to the clinic. He is hypertensive and on captopril. ECG showed tall, tented T waves. Which of the following is the best next step in management?

A 70-year-old woman known to have chronic heart failure presented with severe shortness of breath, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea and orthopnea. On examination, she looks unwell, high JVP with bilateral basal crackles at both lungs. S3 was heard at the apex. Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 100 /min Oxygen saturation 88 % Which of the following is the best next step in management?

A 65-year-old woman known to have heart failure presented with severe shortness of breath, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea and orthopnea. On examination, she looks unwell, high JVP with bilateral basal crackles at both lungs. S3 was heard at the apex. Blood pressure 100/70 mmHg Heart rate 93 /min Oxygen saturation 88 % Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old athlete man attended routine clinic visit. He is asymptomatic and has no significant past medical history but found to have a resting pulse of 47 beat/min, normal blood pressure and cardiac examination. Normal CBC, renal function, LFT, and TSH. ECG normal only sinus bradycardia. Which of the following is the best advice?

A 67-year-old woman diagnosed with heart failure being treated with loop diuretic and ACE inhibitor with good control of her symptoms. Which of the following medications helps in reducing her long-term mortality?

A 67-year-old diabetic patient with atrial fibrillation is hesitant to start anti-coagulant due to its risk of inducing bleeding. which of the following factors is the most important in making the decision?

options.text: The patient has no risk for bleeding
The patient has mild risk of thrombosis
The bleeding risk is higher than thrombosis risk
His risk of thromboembolic events is higher than bleeding

questions.stem: A 60-year-old woman admitted to the hospital for cardiac catheterization but she is concerned about its complications. Which of the following is the best way to address her concerns?

options.text: Tell her it is very rare and no need to worry
Inform her that her husband will sign the consent
Listen to her concern and explain what are the expected complications
Listen to her concern and explain what are the expected complications and give alternative

questions.stem: A 21-year-old woman with history of recurrent palpitations, light-headedness and 2 attacks of fainting. ECG showed short PR interval and Inferior leads Q waves. She was diagnosed as Wolf-Parkinson-White (WPW) syndrome. She was given atenolol with no response. Which of the following is the best management option?
A patient with infective endocarditis started on antibiotics. What is the simplest way in monitoring antibiotics response?

A 21-year-old primigravida is currently at 20 weeks gestation. Her past medical history is significant for mitral stenosis secondary to rheumatic heart disease as a child. What physiologic change places her at risk for the development of heart failure during pregnancy?

A 72-year-old man presented with an episode of right-sided weakness that lasted 10 minutes and fully resolved and he is clinically stable. He has no other medical illness. On clinical examination, he is in atrial fibrillation. Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg, Heart rate 95 /min, Temperature 36.6 °C. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in the management?

A 65-year-old man presents to the clinic with progressive exertional shortness of breath that is associated with syncope. His examinations show a mid-systolic murmur at right upper sternal border that radiates to carotids. Chest x-ray shows cardiomegaly. ECG reveals left ventricular hypertrophy. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Start antihypertensive with tight control of his blood pressure

questions.stem: A 28-year-old man presents to the Emergency Department with sudden onset of chest pain that reduced with sitting forward associated with shortness of breath class II. No history of fever. Examinations reveal a normal heart sound with friction rub. His cardiac enzymes are within normal range. ECG shows diffuse ST segment elevation. Blood pressure 130/70 mmHg, Heart rate 90 /min, Respiratory rate 24 /min, Temperature 37.9 °C, Oxygen saturation 95 %. What is the most appropriate treatment for this patient?

A 62-year-old man presented with 2-weeks history of tiredness, dyspnea and 5-days history of fever. No previous surgical history. Cardiac exam shows pan-systolic murmur at the apex. Hands exam shows splinter hemorrhage on nails. Temperature 38.8 °C Which of the following is the most likely causative organism?

A 58-year-old man presented with 2-weeks history of tiredness, dyspnea and 5-days history of fever. No previous surgical history. Cardiac exam shows pan systolic murmur at the apex. Hands exam shows splinter hemorrhage on nails Temperature 38.5 °C Which of the following is the most appropriate empirical therapy?
Which of the following is the most effective preventive measure to improve post-myocardial infarction prognosis?
Which of the following is the recommended age in years to start screening for dyslipidemia in a low-risk man?
What is the recommended age in years to start screening for high blood pressure in adults with no risk factors?
In cardiovascular disease prevention, which of the following is considered primordial prevention?

options.text: Prevention of coronary heart disease risk factors
Initiation of therapy to reduce recurrent coronary heart disease events
Decrease cardiac mortality in patients with established coronary heart disease
Modification of risk factors in order to prevent or delay the onset of coronary heart disease

questions.stem: Which of the following is the treatment goal for diabetic patients with coronary artery disease?
Which of the following is the major preventable cause for dyslipidemia and coronary heart disease in women?

A 65-year-old man with a history of myocardial infarction (see lab results). Blood pressure 140/90 mmHg BMI 25 kq/m2 Cholesterol (LDL) 3.7 <3.36 mmol/L Cholesterol (HDL) 1.1 > 1.03 mmol/L Apo A-1 1.37 0.88-1.8 g/L (Male) 0.98-2.1 g/L (Female) Apo B-100 1.16 0.55-1.51 g/L (Male) 0.44-1.48 g/L (Female) Which of the following is the most powerful risk prediction value for cardiovascular disease?
which of the following is most likely to increase the risk of cardiovascular disease?
After how many years the excess risk of myocardial infarction will decline significantly for individual who stop smoking?
How many times the risk of myocardial infarction is increased in smokers compared to nonsmokers?
Which of the following agents has been shown to reduce mortality in patients with congestive heart failure?
Which of the following is a recognized side effect of furosemide in congestive heart failure?

A 71-year-old man is referred to the Outpatient Clinic for advice on his antihypertensive treatment. He has a history of stroke and longstanding uncontrolled hypertension. 6 blood pressure recordings at home and at his surgery within the past 2 weeks were 188-216/03-112 mmg. His therapy comprised ramipril, atenolol, and amlodipine (see lab results). Sodium 138 134-146 mmol/L Potassium 2.9 3.5-5.1 mmol/L Urea 8 2.75-7.4 mmol/L Creatinine 88 44-115 mol/L Which of the following is most likely contributing to the treatment failure?

A 48-year-old man presents with central and severe chest pain, which started around 1 hour ago. There is no radiation of the pain or associated shortness-of-breath. He has had some similar fleeting pains over the past 2 weeks but these settled spontaneously after a few seconds. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 64-year-old man, who has hypertension, presents with increasing shortness of breath. His symptoms are worse at night. On examination, there is bilateral basal crackles and a third heart sound (S3). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 39-year-old man presents with shortness of breath for 2 weeks. The symptoms associated with activity and relieved by rest. He is otherwise healthy, takes no medications and denies chest pain or pressure. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 77-year-old man with poorly controlled hypertension presents with a 6-months history of fatigue and dyspnea on exertion. He denies edema, orthopnea, chest pain and palpitations. His only medication is hydrochlorothiazide (25 mg) once daily. On examination, he has a grade 2/6 midsystolic ejection murmur, which is loudest at the right upper steal border. An S4 is heard at the apex, there is no S3. His lungs are clear and there is no peripheral edema. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 49-year-old smoker man has type 2 diabetes mellitus, morbid obesity and a recent diagnosis of symptomatic peripheral arterial disease. He is started on atorvastatin (Lipitor), offered a supervised exercise program and discussed smoking cessation and interventions. Which of the following should be recommended to prevent cardiovascular events?
A 34-year-old woman with a history of prolonged QT syndrome presents with severe acute bacterial sinusitis. Which of the following antibiotics should be avoided?

A 75-year-old man has lung cancer comes to the clinic to manage his back pain. A month ago, his oncologist told him that the prognosis was poor and that he is unlikely to survive for more than a year (see lab result). Calcium ionised 3.2 1.1-1.3 mol/L Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 68-year-old woman is admitted to the hospital with first episode of acute heart failure. She has a history of hypertension treated with a thiazide diuretic. An echocardiogram reveals no evidence of valvular disease and no segmental wall motion abnormalities. Left ventricular hypertrophy is noted, and her ejection fraction is 55%. Which of the following is the most likely cause of her heart failure?

A 76-year-old woman with a history of hypertension and osteoporosis presents to the clinic for preoperative clearance for an upcoming eye surgery. She complains of progressively worsening fatigue over the past 8 to 10 months. She states she often feels dizzy but denies syncope. Her current medications include alendronate and hydrochlorothiazide. Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Referral to a cardiologist for evaluation
Clearance for eye surgery with no further evaluation

questions.stem: A 61-year-old man complains of shortness of breath. He has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes and hyperlipidemia. He was a smoker for more than 30 years but he quit 4 years ago. On physical examination, he is not in respiratory distress, but he has diffuse wheezing bilaterally over lower lobes of his lungs. His cardiac examination demonstrates an S4 and distended jugular veins. Which of the following is the best treatment to relieve his symptoms?

A 38-year-old man has episodic chest pain. He states that the pain feels like tightness, located right behind his sternum, lasts less than 3 minutes and is relieved with rest. He takes no medications. He has no family history of coronary disease and has never smoked. His ECG in the office is normal. What is the most appropriate test to exclude cardiac ischemia?

A 55-year-old man has congestive heart failure due to left ventricular systolic dysfunction. He has no history of medications allergy or interaction, Which of the following is the best first-line treatment option?
A 58-year-old man has chronic atrial fibrillation. Which of the following is this patient at increased risk for?
A 55-year-old man presents to the clinic with history of atrial fibrillation. What is the drug of choice to prevent complications of his condition?
A 59-year-old man is admitted to the hospital with infero-lateral myocardial infarction. Which of the following medications would improve his survival?

A 56-year-old man has a low-pitched diastolic rumble heard at the apex, a widened pulse pressure and a grade 3/6 diastolic decrescendo murmur at the left steal border. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-old man, with type 2 diabetes, presents with persistent diffuse neck pain for the past hour, diaphoresis, shortness of breath, a normal troponin I level, and an electrocardiogram that reveals only nonspecific ST-segment and T-wave changes. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.text: Recheck the troponin I level in 6 hours

questions.stem: A 42-year-old man presented with worsening pleuritic, positional chest pain. Examination revealed pericardial rub, a clear lung examination, and no evidence of lower-extremity edema. ECG shows non-diagnostic findings. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step for diagnosis?

options.text: Reassure the patient about insignificant symptoms

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman had 2 episodes of syncope in the past 2 months during micturition and coughing. Physical examination and electrocardiogram are unremarkable. Which of the following is the most appropriate management options?
A 22-year-old woman with vasovagal syncope comes to the clinic. She has a normal physical examination and a normal electrocardiogram. Which of the following management approaches is most appropriate?

A 45-year-old man with previous history of rheumatic heart disease presents with worsening dyspnea, orthopnea and PND. Physical examination shows holosystolic murmur in the apex and bibasilar crackles on lung auscultation. His symptoms improved with furosemide, spironolactone, enalapril and carvedilol (see report). Echocardiogram: Showed mildly dilated left ventricle, LVEF 45% and severe rheumatic mitral regurgitation. Which of the following is the best next step in management?

A 45-year-old man was being investigated for hypertension. He was prescribed a drug for his lipid disorder but returned 1 week later with intense face flushing after taking the tablet prescribed. He was then advised to take a full dose of aspirin 3 times daily instead of a low dose once daily. This gave complete relief (see lab results). Tests at first visit: ● Cholesterol (HDL): 0.72 <1.03 mmol/L ● Cholesterol (LDL): 5.30 <3.36 mmol/L ● Total Cholesterol: 6.12 <5.1 mmol/L ● Triglycerides: 2.20 <2.16 mmol/L ● Alanine aminotransferase: 35 5-40 IU/L ● Creatinine kinase: 205 24-195 IU/L Which of the following drugs was he prescribed?

An 8-year-old child is brought to the clinic for a routine physical examination. During the exam, the physician notes a cardiovascular murmur that is high pitched and heard best at the midsternal border and late systolic in timing. The pattern is crescendo-decrescendo in nature. Which of the following is the most likely type of murmur? #Anki
Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 20-year-old woman presents to the Out-Patient Department with mild dyspnea, malaise, low-grade fever and arthralgia. Physical examination showed tender erythematous nodules measuring 2-3 cm in both shins. Chest auscultation revealed fine basal crackles. Which of the following is the next best action in management?
Which of the following is the best oxygen delivery system in a patient with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease?

A 65-year-old man known to have COPD presented to the Emergency Department with increasing dyspnea, cough, expectoration and fever. Initial assessment revealed fully conscious patient with mild distress, central cyanosis and bilateral wheezing on chest auscultation. The patient was started on high flow oxygen and salbutamol nebulizer but 1 hour later, his level of consciousness is reduced (see lab result) ABG HCO3. 36 22-28 mmol/L ABG PCO2 9 4.7-6.0 kPa pH 7.18 7.36-7.45 ABG PO2 15 10.6-14.2 kPa Which of the following is the best initial step in management?

A 50-year-old woman presented with fever, dyspnea and weight loss. Physical examination showed evidence of pleural effusion in the left hemithorax (see report). Pleural fluid analysis: Shows exudative fluid with high gamma interferon level. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
In a patient with COPD and cor pulmonale, which of the following improves survival?

A 30-year-old woman is evaluated for a 6-month history of recurrent dyspnea, cough, and wheezing. She is awakened with asthma symptoms 6-8 nights a month. Her current medication is salbutamol inhaler. On examination, there are wheezes in both lung fields. Which of the following is the most appropriate next best step in management?

options.text: Inhaled budesonide and inhaled albuterol as needed

questions.stem: A 55-year-old obese non-smoker man with hypertension presents with exertional dyspnea for 2 years. His wife stated that he is uncomfortable while sleeping at night and produces loud snores. Examination revealed central cyanosis, suffused conjunctivae and clear chest. BMI 40 kg/m2 Which of the following has the highest diagnostic value?

A 55-year-old obese non-smoker man presents with loud snoring, daytime somnolence and exertional dyspnea for 4 years. Examination revealed central cyanosis: suffused conjunctivae and clear chest (see lab results). BMI 40 kg/m2 ABG HCO3- 38 22-28 mmol/L ABG PCO2 6.9 4.7-6.0 kPa pH 7.38 7.36-7.45 ABG PO2 9 10.6-14.2 ka Which of the following is the best treatment after polysomnography?

A 65-year-old man with idiopathic bronchiectasis presents with persistent cough of large amount of mucoid sputum and dyspnea on exertion. He is compliant with his medications, which include azithromycin. Physical examination showed finger clubbing and mild bilateral coarse crackles. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment option?

A 56-year-old man who has chronic productive cough underwent a CT chest, which was consistent with bronchiectasis. He came today to discuss his disease. Which of the following would convey the diagnostic information to him?

options.text: Read to him the CT report
Show him the chest X-ray film
Inform him that he has bronchiectasis
Tell him that his air tubules are inflamed and damaged

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best option in management?

A 65-year-old woman with diabetes mellitus and old myocardial infarction is admitted to the Intensive Care Unit with urosepsis and septic shock. Her blood pressure did not respond to fluid challenge for which she is started on norepinephrine infusion. She has hypoxia despite optimizing the ventilator parameters and Fi02 of 100% (see table and report). Pulmonary Artery Catheter Test Result Normal Values Right atrial pressure 3 2-8 mm Hg Pulmonary artery pressure 13/3 16-24/5-12 mm Hg Wedge pressure 5 5-12 mm Hg Cardiac output 4 4-6 L/min Chest X-ray: Bilateral lung infiltrate. Which of the following is the most likely cause of the lung infiltrate?

A 39-year-old man came to the clinic for follow-up. He is recently diagnosed as pulmonary tuberculosis and was started on rifampicin, Isoniazid, pyrazinamide and ethambutol for 4 weeks. Basic lab workup were normal. LFT test was repeated (see lab results). Direct bilirubin 56 1.5-6.5 mol/L Total bilirubin 76 3.5-16.5 mol/L Aspartate aminotransferase 465 12-40 IU/L Alanine aminotransferase 620 5-40 IU/L Alkaline phosphatase 720 39-117 IU/L Gamma glutamyltransferase 387 6 to 37 1U/L Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
Which of the following drugs should be given?

A 59-year-old man comes to the clinic, with a 45 cigarette pack-year history, complaining of breathlessness on exertion and a productive cough of white sputum over the last 6 months. Cardiological investigations are normal (see report). Spirometry: Shows an FEV1/FVC of 60% with minimal reversibility after a 2-week trial of oral steroids Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old man known to have asthma. He has never been admitted to hospital with an asthma exacerbation and experiences symptoms once or twice a week but he is not on any medication. Today he come to discuss the treatment options and he prefer to start medications only if needed during the attacks. His peak expiratory flow reading is currently 85% of the normal predicted value expected for his age and height. Which of the following is the most appropriate first step in treatment?

A 40-year-old man diagnosed with pulmonary TB who started treatment 3 months ago, presents to the clinic with a week's history of pins and needles in his hands and feet with associated numbness. He tells that his symptoms started since he stopped taking the vitamins given to him at the start of his TB treatment. Which of the following drugs is responsible for the symptoms described by the patient?

A 58-year-old man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is ready to be discharged home after acute exacerbation of the disease. Which of the following parameters indicate offering long-term oxygen therapy?

options.text: 1 arterial blood gas measurement with p02 < 7,7 kPa
2 arterial blood gases measurements with p02 < 7.3 kPa
1 arterial blood gas measurement with p02 < 8.0 kPa
2 arterial blood gases measurements with p02 < 6.3 kPa

questions.stem: A 50-year-old man presents to the clinic with chronic history of productive cough and shortness of breath. A diagnosis of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is suspected. Pulmonary function test is ordered. Which of the following pulmonary function tests is most likely to represent COPD?

options.text: Increased total lung capacity (TLC), decreased vital capacity (VC), decreased FEV1/FVC ratio
Increased total lung capacity (TLC), decreased vital capacity (VC), increased FEV1/FVC ratio
Decreased total lung capacity (TLC), increased vital capacity (VC), decreased FEV1/FVC ratio
Increased total lung capacity (TLC), normal vital capacity (VC), decreased FEV1/FVC ratio.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old-man presented to the Emergency Department with 5-day history of fever, shortness of breath and productive cough. Lung examination reveals dullness to percussion to approximately half of the lung field on the right and his breath sounds are markedly diminished. Chest radiography, shows right lower and middle lobes consolidation with moderate pleural effusion. Which of the following would indicate the need for tube thoracostomy?

options.text: Pleural fluid with more than 90% polymorphonucleocytes (PMNs)
Pleural fluid/ serum protein less than 0.4

questions.stem: A 36-year-old man presents to Emergency Department with 5-day history of fever, productive cough and shortness of breath. On examination, he is febrile with temperature 38.5 C and his lung examination reveals dullness to percussion with markedly diminished breath sound over half of the lung field on the right side. Chest radiography shows right lower and middle lobes consolidation and moderate pleural effusion. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Start azithromycin, ceftriaxone and do thoracocentesis
Start azithromycin, ceftriaxone and do CT scan of the chest

questions.stem: A 36-year-old man presents to Emergency Department with 4-week history of low-grade fever, non- productive cough and shortness of breath. On examination, he is febrile with temperature 37.9 °C and his lung examination reveals dullness to percussion with markedly diminished breath sound over half of the lung field on the right side. A diagnosis of tuberculous pleural effusion is suspected. Chest radiography shows moderate pleural effusion (see lab results). Leukocytes 4500 <1000/pL Total Protein 6 10-20 g/L Glucose 1.6 >2.2 mmol/L LDH 650 <200/UL Which of the following tests is the most sensitive to establish the diagnosis?

options.text: Pleural fluid with very low glucose concentration
Pleural fluid adenosine deaminase more than 45 IU/L

questions.stem: A patient with a diagnosis of advanced chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) who is discussing with his doctor the therapeutic benefits of different therapies on his survival rate Which of the following therapies is most likely to improve his survival?

A 25-year-old man presents to the Emergency Department with progressive shortness of breath, non- productive cough and wheezes for 1 day. On examinations, he has obvious difficulty in breathing and his lungs show with diffuse wheezes but no crackles. Blood pressure 120/70 mmHg, Heart rate 100 /min, Respiratory rate 28 /min, Temperature 36.6 °C, Oxygen saturation 93 % Which of the following is the most effective initial treatment at this time?

A 25-year-old woman non-smoker presents to the Emergency Department with sudden onset of severe chest pain and shortness of breath. Her past medical history is significant for caesarean section 4 days ago. Her examinations show a distressed woman with oxygen saturation 92% but otherwise unremarkable. Chest radiography is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 38-year-old man who is smoker for several years presents to the clinic with progressive shortness of breath. Pulmonary function test (PFT) done which results in the following parameters: forced expiratoy volume (FEV1/forced vital capacity (FVC) ratio < 0.7 with minimal improvement after bronchodilators low diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old woman with a chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) on combination of long- acting B2-agonist and inhaled glucocorticoid and albuterol as needed presents to the clinic with worsening of her symptoms. On physical examination, there is no jugular venous distention. Pulmonary examination reveals decreased breath sounds. Bilateral lower extremity edema is noted to a level above the ankles. Echocardiogram is normal apart of high mean pulmonary artery pressure, 52 mmH (see lab results). Blood pressure 125/75 mmH Heart rate 84 /min Respiratory rate 20 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Oxygen saturation 86 % BMI 30 kg/m2 Test Result Normal Values ABG PCO2 7.5 4.7-6.0 kPa pH 7.6 7.36-7.45 ABG PO2 8.6 10.6-14.2 kPa Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment at this time?

A 66-year-old woman is evaluated for a 6-week history of increasing dyspnea and right-sided pleuritic chest pain with occasional cough. She has lost significant body weight in the last 3 months. She has no other medical problems and takes no medications. Her physical examination reveals dullness to percussion and decreased breath sounds over both lower lung zones. A 4-cm right breast mass is palpated. Chest radiograph demonstrates bilateral pleural effusions but no evidence of infiltrate or pulmonary vascular congestion. Thoracentesis is performed. Pleural fluid Gram stain is negative (see lab results). Total Protein 40 10-20 g/L Fluid Protein/Serum Protein 0.67 <0.5 Glucose 3.5 >2.2 mmol/L LDH 350 <200/UL Total Proteins 60 60-84 g/L Lactate dehydrogenase 125 60-160 IU/L Leukocytes 3600 <1000/pL Which of the following is the most appropriate statement about the diagnosis?

options.text: Exudative pleural effusion due to malignancy
Transudative pleural effusion due to malignancy
Exudative pleural effusion due to heart failure
Transudative pleural effusion due to empyema

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman with bronchial asthma that controlled on budesonide and albuterol inhalers is evaluated in the clinic as she is 6 weeks pregnant. Her symptoms are well controlled on the treatment. However, symptoms usually flare in fall and she treats these symptoms with an add-on oral leukotriene inhibitor. She currently has no asthma symptoms. On examination, vital signs are normal. The lungs show good air entry and no wheezes. She is so concern about the safety of medications during pregnancy. What is the best information to be delivered to her with regard to medication safety?

options.text: Continue the current treatments as they are safe during pregnancy
Stop budesonide and continue albuterol inhaler
Stop albuterol and continue budesonide inhaler

questions.stem: A 26-year-old man presents to the clinic with shortness of breath and occasional wheeze that occurs several times per week. He develops significant shortness of breath when playing football. He notes that it takes several minutes to recover his breath when this occurs. He also notes coughing during exercise as well. He takes no medications. On physical examination, vital signs are normal. Mild nasal congestion is noted. His systemic examinations are unremarkable. A chest radiograph is normal. Spirometry findings are within normal parameters. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in assessment?

options.text: Helical (spiral) computed tomography (CT) for the chest

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman is evaluated because of daily wheezing and breathlessness that limit her activities several times a week. Medical history is otherwise unremarkable. She has never smoked. She is diagnosed with moderate persistent asthma. In addition to a short-acting 32-agonist, which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

options.text: Add a low-dose inhaled corticosteroid and long-acting B2-agonist

questions.stem: A 66-year-old woman with severe COPD is admitted with 4 days of dyspnoea and cough. She is alert, in moderate respiratory distress, and has an oxygen saturation of 93% on 3 L/min supplemental oxygen. A chest radiography demonstrates no consolidation. She receives intensive bronchodilator therapy and systemic steroids (see lab results). ABG PCO2 8.8 4.7-6.0 kPa pH 7.28 7.36-7.45 ABG PO2 9.9 10.6-14.2 kPa Which of the following is the best next step in the management?
A 58-year-old woman with acute onset shortness of breath and pleuritic chest pain. She is diagnosed with pulmonary embolism. Which of the following is an indication to do thrombophilia workup?

options.text: Has a history of connective tissue disease
Has negative family history of thrombosis

questions.stem: A 32-year-old man is evaluated in the clinic because of an abnormal chest computerised tomography (CT) scan that revealed a small lung lesion (7 mm) without any other abnormalities. He is non-smoker and he is asymptomatic. Physical examination shows no lymphadenopathy and normal lung examinations (see lab results). Hb 140 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Platelets count 300 150-400 x 109/L WBC 8 4.5-10.5 x 109/L ESR 11 2-10 mm/h (Male) 3-15 mm/h (Female) Calcium 2.25 2.15-2.62 mol/L Which of the following is the most appropriate procedure to do next?

A 54-year-old man presents with shortness of breath and fever for 1 week. On physical examination, the patient is febrile and dyspneic. His oxygen's saturation is 89% on room air. Chest examination shows absent breath sounds and dullness to percussion over right lung field. Chest radiography confirms a large right-sided pleural effusion. Which of the following is the most useful to establish a diagnosis of exudative pleural effusion?

options.text: Pleural fluid LDH >1/3 normal upper limit for serum

questions.stem: A 54-year-old man presents with shortness of breath and fever for 1 week. On physical examination, the patient is febrile and dyspneic. His oxygen's saturation is 89% on room air Chest examination shows absent breath sounds and dullness to percussion over right lung field. Chest radiography confirms a large right-sided pleural effusion. Which of the following factors indicating the need for therapeutic thoracentesis?

options.text: Pleural fluid glucose more than 80 mg/di
Negative gram stain of the pleural fluid

questions.stem: A 5-year-old child with bronchial asthma seen in the clinic because of uncontrolled course of disease despite using Ventolin regularly. Mother has asthma and using similar inhaler but she expresses poor technique of Ventolin delivery to her child. Which of the following is the most likely reason for her child's problem?
A 5-year-old child with bronchial asthma under control with inhalers. Mother concerned about the future of her child's asthma during adulthood. Which of the following is the most likely prognosis?

options.text: Most of the children grow out of it
No correlation between childhood and adulthood asthma

questions.stem: A 3-year-old child with bronchial asthma on ventolin nebulizer at home as per needs. The mother expresses concern that the family cannot go out of the home most of the time because the nebulizer machine need electricity power source. Which of the following is the most appropriate counselling should be given?

options.text: Agree and support their decision as the priority is asthma control
Find someone to take care of asthmatic child if family goes out of the home
Educate with clear instructions inhaler usage and advice to stop nebulizer
Find out nebulizer machine with portability feature

questions.stem: What is the most effective treatment for moderate bronchial asthma severity?

options.text: Long acting beta agonist agents with steroids
Long acting beta agonist agents with anticholenergics

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most likely reason for admission? А. Нурохіа
Which of the following reasons justifies the child hospitalization?

A 3-year-old child seen in the clinic with fever and cough for 5 days following flu-like prodrome. On examination, he had decrease air entry and crackles over right lung middle zone. Chest X- ray is done (see image and lab results). Blood pressure 90/64 mmH Heart rate 110 /min Respiratory rate 20 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Oxygen saturation 97 % Hb 12 165-195 q/L (Newborn) 112-165 g/L (Child) Platelets count 328 150-400 x 109/L Neutrophils 80 40-60% WBC 22 4.5-13.5 x 109/L (2-10 years) 4.5-11.1 x 109/L (11 years-older adult) Neutrophils 84% (2.4-7.3 × 109/L) 30%-77% (2-10 years) (2.7-6.5 x 109/L) 40%-75% (11 years-older adult) Lymphocytes 15% (2.8-9.3 x 109/L) 26%-56% (Birth) (3.7-10.7 × 109/L) 20%-64% (1-23 months) Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
Which of the following sites is the best to aspirate a sample of right pleural effusion with a syringe and needle?

A 45-year-old man presents with difficulty in breathing and a nocturnal cough for the last 3 weeks. Spirometry results show a forced vital capacity and the FEV/FVC ratio lower than normal. Which of the following is consistent with these findings?
What is the optimal treatment for community-acquired pneumonia in an otherwise healthy patient?
What is the optimal duration of anticoagulation following an initial episode of pulmonary embolism?
In which of the following conditions is interstitial pneumonitis a characteristic histopathologic finding?
Which of the following pneumoconiosis will commonly predispose to the development of pulmonary tuberculosis?
A 38-year-old woman with pleurisy requires a thoracentesis. The needle should be placed on the midaxillary line of the affected side. Which rib level should the needle penetrate through?

A 72-year-old man presents to the Emergency Department with fever, night sweats and cough for 2 weeks (see report). Chest X-ray: Right upper lobe consolidation. Which of the following is the best next step in management?

options.text: Admit the patient to the Intensive Unit
Isolate the patient in a single, negative pressure room

questions.stem: Which of the following can improve survival in patients with severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease?

A 25-year-old patient with moderate persistent asthma is currently on a low-dose, inhaled corticosteroid but needs to use a beta-2 agonist rescue inhaler at least once a day. Which of the following should be added to the current treatment?

options.text: Leukotriene inhibitor to the steroid regimen
Long-acting beta-2 agonist to steroid regimen

questions.stem: A 55-year-old patient with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease presents with shortness of breath. The patient is in severe respiratory distress and hypoxemic with decreased breath sounds and a prolonged expiration phase. There is no improvement with bronchodilators. The patient is conscious with a pH of 7.3. Which of the following is the best next step in management?
Which of the following is the most effective treatment for adults with obstructive sleep apnea?

options.text: Maintain a BMI less than 30 kg/m2

questions.stem: A 28-year-old patient with mild intermittent asthma, has daytime symptoms about once to twice a week, and none at night. Which of the following initial treatment should be given when necessary?

A 28-year-old woman has had mild intermittent asthma for years. She uses a short-acting bronchodilator, as needed. Over the past 2 months, she has noticed that she is using her inhaler at least 3 times a week, and on occasions has had to wake up in the middle of the night to use her inhaler. Which of the following treatments should be added?

A 55-year-old man presents with shortness of breath and a productive cough. The patient has a history of smoking. On auscultation, there is wheezing throughout the chest (see reports). Chest X-ray: Normal. Arterial Blood Gases: Normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old patient suddenly develops chest pain and dyspnoea. Vocal and tactile fremitus are reduced, and breath sounds are diminished (see report). Chest X-ray: It shows absent lung markings on the left side. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is the most likely cause of lobar pneumonia in adults?

A 45-year-old man is admitted with general tiredness and fever. There is a past history of a chest infection of 4-week duration, for which he was given oral antibiotics. He felt better initially. but never fully recovered and is now becoming worse (see report). Chest X-ray: It shows a right-sided pleural effusion. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old nurse working in the pulmonary clinic, complains of fever and a productive cough for the last 3 months. She has received 2 courses of oral antibiotics, but showed no improvement (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient presents to the clinic with shortness of breath and a cough productive of yellow sputum for the past 2 days. There has also been blood-stained sputum for the last 3 hours. The patient has smoked 2 packs of cigarettes a day for the past 35 years. On examination, there are rhonchi, wheezing, and crepitations heard over the right hemithorax (see report).
