Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 84 /min Respiratory rate 22 /min Temperature 38.8° C Oxygen saturation 95% on room air Chest X-ray: It shows a dense infiltrate in the right lower lobe. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old woman with asthma has not had a severe attack for the last 3 months. However, she has a history of cough and wheezing 2-3 times each week. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 21-year-old woman comes to the clinic with episodes of shortness of breath on exertion for one year. She has to stop after 15-20 minutes of exercise, because of dyspnoea and coughing, which get better after about one hour of rest. There are no symptoms at rest. Physical examination and spirometry are normal. Blood pressure 125/75 mmHg Heart rate 80 /min Respiratory rate 12 /min Temperature 37.0° C Which of the following is the most appropriate inhaled treatment before exercise?
Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.text: Observe the patient using his inhaler

questions.stem: A 67-year-old patient presents to the Emergency Department with chest pain, shortness of breath, and haemoptysis following a car trip for more than 5 hours (see report). ECG: Right axis deviation, an S1-Q3-T3 pattern, and a right bundle branch block. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old smoker presents to a clinic with progressive shortness of breath (see report). Chest X-ray: It reveals a massive right pleural effusion. Which of the following is the best next step in management?
A 28-year-old patient develops the sudden onset of dyspnoea and tachycardia 5 days post a knee surgery. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A patient with stage IIIB small cell lung cancer complains of new onset of back pain for the past 12 hours. Initial neurological examination is normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate action to take?

options.text: High dose IV corticosteroids and MRI

questions.stem: A 78-year-old man and current smoker, with 50 pack-year smoking history, complains of shortness of breath, dry cough and fatigue progressing over the past 8 weeks. The patient also reports a significant weight loss, corresponding to approximately 15% of body weight over the last 12 weeks. Physical examination is normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A patient with active rheumatoid arthritis presents with pleural effusion. Which of the following is typical finding in the pleural fluid analysis?

A 40-year-old woman presents with recurrent attacks of dyspnea and cough when exposed to dust and perfumes. Physical examination is normal except for mild expiratory wheeze on lung auscultation. Which of the following tests has the highest diagnostic value?

A 44-year-old obese woman presents with sudden onset dyspnea. No cough, chest pain orthopnea or PND. History is significant for hemorrhoidectomy 2 weeks ago (see image, lab results and report). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 105 /min ABG HCO3- 20 22-28 mmol/L ABG PCO2 4.5 4.7-6.0 kPa pH 7.5 7.36-7.45 ABG PO2 10 10.6-14.2 ka Chest x-ray: Normal except for the obliterated left costophrenic angle. Which of the following has the highest diagnostic value?

A 30-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis presents with progressive dyspnea and dry cough for 3 months. No fever or weight loss. Physical examination revealed cyanosis, digital clubbing and bibasilar end-inspiratory crackles (velcro type) on lung auscultation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 44-year-old man with poorly controlled epilepsy presented with fever, cough and left side chest pain for 6 weeks. The cough is productive of copious foul-smelling sputum. Physical examination revealed digital clubbing and course crepitations in the right infra-clavicular area. Heart examination is normal (see image and report). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 100 /min Respiratory rate 25 /min Temperature 39 °C Sputum culture: Mixture of aerobic and anaerobic organisms. What is the most likely mechanism for the underlying condition?

options.text: Direct extension from infected chest wall

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman with bronchial asthma developed worsening dyspnea and cough following paint inhalation from neighborhood apartment. On examination, she is in respiratory distress, cannot complete a sentence and cyanosed. Chest auscultation revealed reduced breath sounds in both sides with short inspiratory and exploratory rhonchi (see lab results). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 130 /min Respiratory rate 20 /min Oxygen saturation 85 % ABG HCO3- 24 22-28 mmol/L ABG PCO2 7.8 4.7-6.0 kPa pH 7.3 7.36-7.45 ABG P02 7.5 10.6-14.2 kPa Which of the following is the best immediate action in management? A. Intravenous magnesium infusion

options.text: Nasal continuous positive airway pressure ventilation

questions.stem: A patient with poorly controlled bronchial asthma developed hypertension, which of the following antihypertensive medications is contraindicated?

A 60-year-old man with advanced squamous cell bronchogenic carcinoma presents with massive malignant right pleural effusion. He has been admitted several times with similar findings for which he undergoes several therapeutic pleural taps. Which of the following is the next best option in management?

A 40-year-old woman presents with progressive dyspnea, dry cough and reddish nodular skin lesion over both shins. On examination, she has palpable cervical lymph nodes and bilateral diffuse fine crepitations in both lungs (see reports). Chest radiograph: Diffuse bilateral interstitial infiltrates with bilateral hilar lymph nodes enlargement. Purified protein derivative (PPD): Negative. Cervical lymph node biopsy: Non-caseating granuloma. Which of the following is the next best option in management?

A 60-year-old man with post pulmonary tuberculosis bronchiectasis presents with massive hemoptysis. Physical examination shows coarse crepitations in the right scapular area (see image). Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?
A 69-year-old man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease on oxygen therapy for the last 5 years. Which of the following markers is most useful for monitoring the progression of this patient?

A 51-year-old woman with asthma complaining of increasing shortness of breath and wheeze in the past few hours. She has a long-standing diagnosis of asthma but her medication history suggests a lack of compliance. Her best peak flow measurements in previous consultations have been 300 L/min. Which of the following features suggests acute severe asthma in this patient?

options.text: Inability to complete sentences in one breath

questions.stem: A 31-year-old man with asthma complaining of increasing wheeze in the past few hours. His medication history suggests a lack of compliance. His best peak flow measurements in previous consultations have been 600 L/min. Which of the following features suggests acute severe asthma in this patient?

options.text: A peak flow rate of 250 L/min

questions.stem: A 22-year-old man, whose asthma is uncontrolled on beta agonist therapy, is commenced on a steroid inhaler. Which of the following is the most likely adverse effect?

A 58-year-old man presents with a 6-month history of breathlessness. He has been smoking all his adult life, he smokes 10-15 cigarettes per day. On examination, he has lost the nail fold angle of his fingers. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 36-year-old man with multiple health problems presents to the Emergency Department with an episode of bronchospasm. He has a history of asthma and hypertension. He is undergoing a medication review. Which of the following medications is most likely to be responsible?

A 21-year-old man presents with paroxysms of coughing for the past week, following a mild flue illness. The paroxysms have been so severe that they have resulted vomiting and chest pain. He had been immunised for pertussis as a child. What is the best advice about the protection following immunisation?

options.text: Immunization offers lifelong immunity against pertussis
Immunity following immunization wanes within 3 years
Immunity following immunization wanes within 10 years
Immunity following immunization wanes after 25 years

questions.stem: A 31-year-old man with asthma complaining of increasing wheeze in the past few hours. He rarely attends asthma clinic and his previous best peak flow readings has been 400 L/min. Which of the following would suggest acute severe asthma?

A 38-year-old woman presents for annual asthma review. Her symptoms are very well controlled and she has not had any attacks since her last review a year ago and has not used her salbutamol inhaler once in that year. She is prescribed an inhaled beclomethasone steroid twice daily in addition to her salbutamol inhaler. What is the most appropriate next step in modifying her medication?

options.text: Double the dose of the inhaled corticosteroid
Stop both the salbutamol and beclomethasone inhalers
Half the beclomethasone dose and review in 6 months

questions.stem: A 38-year-old man is admitted with a sudden onset dyspnoea and pleuritic chest pain. He is a smoker but has no history of respiratory disease. He considers himself healthy and regularly plays football. On admission, he has a chest x-ray that shows a pneumothorax with a 3cm rim of air. Aspiration is successful and he is discharged. A follow-up chest x-ray 2 weeks later shows a complete resolution. What is the single most important piece of advice to reduce his risk of further pneumothoraces?

options.text: Arrange a course of respiratory physiotherapy pnemothorax

questions.stem: A 28-year-old wood worker presents to the clinic complaining of episodic shortness of breath. He describes feeling wheezy and having a tendency to cough. A diagnosis of occupation asthma is suspected. Which of the following is the most appropriate diagnostic investigation?

options.text: Serial peak flow measurements at work and at home

questions.stem: A 66-year-old man presents with shortness of breath. He smokes 20 cigarettes/day but is otherwise well. Spirometry shows a restrictive picture. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 31-year-old man came for smoking cessation support as his father has recently been diagnosed with lung cancer. He has a past medical history of epilepsy, which is well-controlled on carbamazepine. Which smoking cessation medication would be contraindicated for this patient?

A 57-year-old man with known history of asthma, congestive heart failure and peptic ulcer disease was admitted with asthma exacerbation and rapid atrial fibrillation. He was managed with nebulized salbutamol, IV digoxin, and his home medications was continued (ACE inhibitor, Ranitidine, Spironolactone). 24 hours later, his serum potassium is noted to be 2.8 mEq/L. Which of the following medications is the most likely to cause this abnormality?

A 32-year-old man presents to the Emergency Department with 3-days history of generalized body aches, sore throat, runny nose, productive cough and shortness of breath. Chest exam shows right lung crepitations. The patient was admitted and according to the results of throat swab was started on oseltamivir (see report). Temperature 39 °C. Chest X-Ray: Right middle lobe infiltrate. Which of the following isolation precautions should be considered?
Which of the following is the next best step in obtaining a definitive diagnosis?

A 28-year-old woman with mild intermittent asthma presents to the Health Clinic at 24 weeks' gestation and says that her symptoms have worsened as the pregnancy progresses. Prior to the pregnancy, she had an occasional exacerbation of asthma and used only an albuterol inhaler for treatment as needed. However, she now complains of daily symptoms and once per week symptoms at night time. A forced expiratory volume in 1 second test shows 70% of normal. Which of the following medication regimen is now most appropriate?

options.text: Long acting beta 2 agonist and inhaled glucocorticoids

questions.stem: Which of the following tests is initially most appropriate?
Which of the following is the most important question to ask next in history? A. History of fatigue
Which of the following is the main method for prevention of tuberculosis?

options.text: Treatment of the patients with tuberculosis

questions.stem: A 76-year-old man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) comes to the clinic for a follow-up. He is currently taking salmeterol, using albuterol rescue inhaler 2 to 3 times per day for the past 3 months. He has been hospitalized for COPD exacerbations twice in the past 6 months. Which of the following medications should be added to the maintenance regimen?
Which of the following is the most likely acid-base abnormality?
A 61-year-old man with stable chronic kidney disease stage 3. Which of the following drugs is it safe to prescribe for this patient?

A 62-year-old man presents with progressive lower limbs edema for the last 4 months otherwise he is asymptomatic. He is known to have diabetes complicated with diabetic nephropathy and hypertension. His current medications are insulin, thiazide, ramipril and amlodipine. On examination blood pressure is 144/78 mmg, JVP not raised, +3 lower limbs edema with normal cardiac and respiratory examination. Renal function was similar to 3 months ago (see lab results). Sodium 138 (134-146 mol/L) Potassium 4.8 (3.5-5.1 mmol/L) Urea 12.9 (2.75-7.4 mmol/L) Creatinine 230 (44-115 mol/L) Creatinine clearance 22 (70-103 mol/L) Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

A 55-year-old man who has developed chronic kidney disease secondary to focal segmental glomerulosclerosis is reviewed in the clinic. His renal function is deteriorating. Haemodialysis is planned to start soon (see lab result). Creatinine clearance 10 (70-103 mol/L) What is the preferred method of access to start Haemodialysis?
Which of the following scenario with acute kidney injury should be referred for urgent Haemodialysis?

options.text: Potassium of 7.5 after 3 courses of medical management
Patient who has had 10ml of urine output over the last 24 hours
Patient who has previously had acute kidney injury three times

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man has been admitted with abdominal pain and he need urgent contrast- enhanced CT but there is a concern regarding his kidney status as he has chronic kidney disease stage 3 (see lab results). Sodium 143 (134-146 mmol/L) Potassium 4.5 (3.5-5.1 mmol/L) Blood urea nitrogen 9 (2.8 to 8.9 mmol/L) Creatinine 160 (44-115 mol/L) Which of the following is the most important step in reducing the risk of contrast-induced nephropathy?

options.text: Intravenous 0.9% sodium chloride pre- and post-procedure

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man comes to the Outpatient Clinic because of the recent development of marked peripheral edema. He has no significant past medical history. On examination, he has 4+ edema of the lower extremities (see lab results and reports). Blood pressure 105/80 mmHg Test Result Normal Values Albumin 18 34-56 g/L Urea 5 2.8-8.9 mmol/L Creatinine 85 44-115 mol/L Dipstick analysis: 4+ proteins. Urinalysis: Oval fat bodies, and some hyaline casts and occasional RBCs. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old woman is recently diagnosed as nephrotic syndrome secondary to minimal change glomerulonephritis after being presented with proteinuria. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment to reduce proteinuria?
A 30-year-old woman with Crohn's disease presents with hypokalemia refractory to aggressive parenteral and oral KCI supplementation. Which of the following is the next step in management?

options.text: Assess her serum plasma aldosterone to plasma renin ratio

questions.stem: A 60-year-old woman presents to the clinic with a 10-year history of type 2 diabetes treated with insulin. Recently diagnosed to have hypertension and proteinuria (see lab results). Blood pressure 150/90 mmHg Heart rate 87 /min BMI 29 kg/m2 Blood urea nitrogen 4 (2.8 to 8.9 mmol/L) Creatinine 80 (44-115 mol/L) Glucose fasting 6.4 (3.5-6.5 mmol/L) HbA1C 7 (4.7-5.6 %) Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 30-year-old patient presents with recurrent urinary tract infections, polyuria, and electrolyte imbalance (see report). Ultrasound: Bilaterally enlarged kidneys with multiple, variably-sized and thin-walled cysts distributed throughout the renal parenchyma. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 27-year-old man who has a sister with adult polycystic kidney disease came to screen for the disease. Which of the following is the most appropriate screening test?

A 70-year-old man presented to Emergency Department with generalized fatigability. 2 days ago, he had CT brain with contrast for possible transient ischemic attack. Physical examination is unremarkable (see lab results). Blood pressure 130/70 mmHg Heart rate 76 /min Hb 170 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 q/L (Female) Urea 30.4 2.75-7.4 mmol/L Creatinine 378 44-115 mol/L Which of the following is the most likely mechanism for the renal impairment?

A 30-year-old man is found to have a repeated BP of 170/110 mmg. He is not on any medications. Physical examination is unremarkable (see lab results). Sodium 138 134-146 mmol/L Potassium 2.1 3.5-5.1 mmol/L Urea 3.67 2.75-7.4 mmol/L Creatinine 66 44-115 mol/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 20-year-old man presents with hematuria, 1-day following a throat infection. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old woman is admitted with pulmonary hemorrhage and rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis. She has history of recurrent sinusitis and numbness in her right upper limb and left lower limb. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 50-year-old man with diabetes, hypertension and chronic kidney disease. presents to the Nephrology Clinic for follow-up (see image and lab results). Blood pressure 160/98 mmHg, Heart rate 80 /min Potassium 6.5 3.5-5.1 mmol/L Creatinine 440 44-115 mol/L Which of the following is the best immediate step in management?

An 18-year-old man is complaining of red urine for 5 days. He has no abdominal pain and no dysuria, urgency or frequency. His history is significant for tonsillitis 3 weeks ago. Physical examination is normal except for elevated blood pressure. Blood pressure 160/100 mmH, Heart rate 76 /min Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 68-year-old woman known to have dilated cardiomyopathy with an ejection fraction of 30% one month ago is admitted with a diagnosis of acute gastroenteritis. She had repeated vomiting and watery diarrhea for 3 days. Her urine output is reduced in volume. She is on furosemide, lisinopril, spironolactone, and carvedilol. On examination, she is dehydrated, confused, has cold clammy skin and the JVP is 1 cm above the sternal angle (see lab results and reports). Blood pressure 88/55 mmH Heart rate 70 /min Sodium 142 134-146 mmol/L Potassium 5.5 3.5-5.1 mmol/L Urea 230 2.75-7.4 mmol/L Creatinine 220 44-115 mol/L Sodium 15 40-230 mmal/day Osmolality 1300 280-910 mOsm/Kg H20 Central venous line: inserted and is 3 cm of H20. Fractional excretion of sodium: 0.6%. What is the best option in management?

A 65-year-old man diagnosed with obstructing lower esophageal cancer and planed for surgery, patient is cachectic with more than 20% weight loss over 3 months. The treating team decided to start on preoperative TPN. Which of the following is the most expected electrolyte abnormality?

A 44-year-old man who was recently diagnosed as chronic kidney disease stage 4, presented to the clinic to discuss the diet in regard to his condition. He has read that potassium rich food should be consumed in moderate amount. Which of the following foods should he eat in moderation?

A 66-year-old man with hypertension comes to the clinic for a follow-up. He is currently taking a combination of losartan and amlodipine, which is failing to keep his blood pressure within target. Examination is unremarkable. His blood test and renal function profile were within the normal limits. What is the most appropriate next step assuming he has no relevant contraindications?

A 58-year-old man with diabetes mellitus came for follow-up. He is on metformin (Glucophage), 1000 mg/day, as well as atorvastatin (Lipitor), 40 mg daily for hypertipidaemia. There is no diagnosis of hypertension. His urine albumin/creatinine ratio is in the microalbuminuria range for the first time (see lab results). Blood pressure 128/77 mmH НА1C 6.3 4.7-5.6 % LDL (cholesterol) 2.1 <4.0 mol/L Which of the following would be most appropriate next step?

A 25-year-old woman presents with symptoms of extreme fatigue, no appetite, and bloody urine She developed a very sore throat 3 weeks ago but did not have it examined or treated. 3 days ago, she began to have bloody urine and swelling of her hands and feet. A 51-year-old man with chronic and progressing renal disease. His GF is decreasing and most likely he will need dialysis sometime within the next year. Which of the following will be the most likely cause of death in his case?

A 77-year-old man with a history of ischemic heart disease is seen in the Hypertension Clinic. He is taking 4 anti-hypertensives drugs. Physical examination is unremarkable. RBC 4 4.7-6.1 x 1012/L (Male) 4.2-5.4 x 1012/L (Female) Hb 13 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 q/L (Female) Platelets count 145 150-400 x 109/L WBC 11 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Neutrophils 22 40-60% Lymphocytes 69 20-40 % Monocytes 9 2-8 % Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 56-year-old diabetic man presented with cough and fever. Chest-XR showed cavity at upper lobe of the left lung. What is the type of precaution required when dealing with this patient?

A 25-year-old patient came to the clinic concerned about her sexual relationship after discovering that her husband was diagnosed with hepatitis B and was just started treatment. She was tested and all her serology came negative. What would be the best advice for her sexual relationship with her husband?

options.text: Advice to resume normal sexual activity
Advice to use of condoms during intercourse

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man with chronic hepatitis C present to the clinic for regular follow-up. His examination reveals a palpable right upper quadrant mass. CT scan of his abdomen shows a large 6*6 cm mass in the right lobe of the liver. A mass biopsy confirms the diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma. What is the most appropriate management steps at this stage?

A 30-year-old asymptomatic woman presents to the clinic as pre-employment screening. Her examinations are unremarkable. Her laboratory tests revealed, positive HbsAg, anti-HBc (IgG) and anti- HBe, but negative anti-HBs and HBeAg. Which of the following statements is the most accurate?

options.text: She has received hepatitis B vaccine
She has been exposed to hepatitis B but now in recovery period

questions.stem: A 53-year-old woman recently returned from Egypt, known diabetic, presented to the Emergency Department with 3-days history of progressive redness and pain on her right shin. Positive history of allergy to penicillin. On examination, right leg has red lesion, which was tender with no ulcer. She was started on oral antibiotics. Next day she complained of abdominal pain, watery diarrhoea and fever. Temperature 37.8 °C. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old woman presents with headache and myalgia for 5 days. 2 days ago, she started to have fever and noticed a skin rash on her face. She returned from Jeddah 10-days ago (see lab results). Hb8 130-170 g/L (Male)120-160 g/L (Female) Platelets count 80 150-400 x 109/L Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 27-year-old soldier going to a military mission at the Southern border of Saudi Arabia. His medical history is insignificant apart from a positive history of depression, which is controlled by medication. He came for counselling regarding malaria prevention. Which of the following is the best malaria chemoprophylaxis regimen?

A 30-year-old man presents to the Emergency Department with history of fever and headache. He recently came from a trip to Sudan, where he stayed there for 10-days. Abdominal examination, palpable spleen 3 cm below costal margin (see lab results). Temperature 40 °C Hb 9 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Platelets count 90 150-400 x 109/L Aspartate aminotransferase 88 12-40 IU/L Alanine aminotransferase 94 5-40 IU/L Which of the following is the first line treatment option?
Which of the following is the most appropriate intravenous treatment option?

A 34-year-old man patient a known case of ulcerative colitis on azathioprine 100 mg/day and tapering dose of steroid presented to the clinic with 6-7 bloody bowel motions, lower abdomen pain and low grade fever. On abdominal examination, there is mild tenderness at left lower abdomen. Stool culture was negative. Stool for colostrum difficile toxins was positive (see lab results). Blood pressure 110/70 mmgh Heart rate 100 /min Temperature 38.4 °C Oxygen saturation 95 % Test Result / Normal Values: RBC 5 / 4.7-6.1 x 1012/L (Male) 4.2-5.4 x 1012/L (Female) Hb 11 / 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Platelets count 456 / 150-400 x 109/L WBC 16 / 4.5-10.5 x 109/L ESR 67 / 2-10 mm/h (Male) 3-15 mm/h (Female) Albumin 29 /34-56 g/L Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
Which level of prevention we apply when detecting a pregnant woman infected with hepatitis B?

A 35-year-old Indian man came to Saudi Arabia for Hajj. He presented with a 4-day history of intermittent fever, shortness of breath, drowsiness, convulsion and confusion. Which of the following is the most probable diagnosis?
A 34-year-old male presents with chills, fever to 39 °C, retro-orbital pain, and severe muscle and joint pains. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following measures is recommended to avoid malaria infection in people traveling to an endemic country?
Which of the following medications is the most likely that malaria parasites develop resistance to? A. Malarone
What is the most common diagnosis for travelers returning with fever from sub-Saharan Africa?
What is the most common disease diagnosed among travelers returning with fever from Southeast Asia?
Which of the following is the peak biting period for Aedes aegypti mosquito (the primary vector of dengue fever)?
A 17-year-old man with history of intravenous drug abuse presents to the clinic for clinical evaluation. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in investigation?
Which of the following is the most likely clinical condition?

A 20-year-old woman is diagnosed of type 1 diabetes mellitus after presenting with diabetic ketoacidosis. Her blood sugars are now stable and she is ready for discharge. Which of the following is the best insulin regimen she should be offered as outpatient?

options.text: Basal-bolus insulin regimen with once-daily insulin glargine
Rapid-acting insulin analogue before each meal with no longer acting insulin

questions.stem: A 70-year-old woman known to have type 2 diabetes mellitus. She is currently taking metformin 1g bid physical examination is unremarkable (see lab results). Creatinine 80 (44-115 mol/L) Glucose fasting 6 (3.5-6.5 mmol/L) Random Glucose 7.5 (3.9-5.5 mmol/L) HbA1C 6.9 (4.7-5.6 %) Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management plan?

A 32-year-old woman was admitted 2 days ago complaining of feeling unwell with vomiting, postural dizziness and weight loss. Synacthen test confirmed the diagnosis with Addison's disease. She was started on treatment with hydrocortisone 3 times a day, as well as fludrocortisone on a daily basis. She has been taking hydrocortisone 10mg at 9:00 and then 5mg at 12:00 and 15:00. On discharge, she informs the medical team that she sometimes does shift-work. What is the most appropriate advice to give regarding steroid dosing for night shifts?

options.text: On shift days omit taking steroids
Take doses at 09:00, 12:00 and 15:00 regardless of shift patterns
On shift days take doses at 09:00, but then take other doses at night
Adjust to take first dose at waking, then doses at 3 and 6 hours from starting

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman is referred to the Endocrinology Clinic due to abnormal thyroid function tests. Otherwise, she is asymptomatic. On examination, there is no evidence of goiter (see lab results). Blood pressure 139/85 mmHg Heart rate 66 /min Temperature 36.6 °C BMI 29 kg/m2 Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone 15 (0.4 - 5.0 pU/mL.) Thyroxine (T4 free serum) 6.5 (8.5 - 15.2 pmol/L) Which of the following is the most appropriate management plan?

options.text: Arrange for US of the neck

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman presents with 2-day history of generally unwell, nausea, vomiting and lethargy. She is a known type 1 diabetic using a long-standing subcutaneous insulin regimen. She was started on treatment for diabetic ketoacidosis with intravenous fluids and fixed rate insulin. Her blood sugar is reviewed 3 hours after treatment was initiated. On admission, blood tests are done (see lab results). ABG HCO3- 8 (22-28 mmol/L) pH 7.2 (7.36-7.45) Random Glucose 32 (3.9-5.5 mmol/L) What should be the aim in managing hyperglycemia in a diabetic ketoacidosis patient?

options.text: Reduce blood glucose to under 14 mol/I as quickly as possible
Reduce blood glucose by 3 mmol/I per hour
Reduce blood glucose by 6 mmol/ per hour

questions.stem: A 20-year-old man with type 1 diabetes presents to the Emergency Department with vomiting and abdominal pain. He has been suffering from diarrhea for 2 days and then became severely dehydrated and started to vomit. He has not had his insulin for the last 24 hours. Normally, he has a basal bolus regimen with Glargine as a long-acting insulin, and Humalog as short-acting. On admission, he is found to have acidosis, elevated serum ketones and elevated blood glucose, and was diagnosed with diabetic ketoacidosis. He is started on IV fluid What insulin should he be prescribed now?

options.text: Fixed rate IV insulin as well as long-acting insulin

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
What is the most likely explanation for these lab findings?

A 42-year-old woman gives a history of recurrent fractures and the passage of stones in the urine preceded by renal colic. Family history and a clinical examination were normal (see lab results and report). Test Result Calcium 2.60 (Normal Values 2.15-2.62 mol/L) Albumin 41 (Normal Values 34-56 g/L) Phosphate 1.1 (Normal Values 0.82-1.51 mmol/L) Parathyroid hormone 402 (Normal Values 1.1-5.3 pmol/L) Plain X-ray abdomen: Multiple radio-opaque shadows in the renal area. Which of the following is the most appropriate investigation?

A 60-year-old man came for follow-up evaluation of Cushing syndrome. He presented with new. onset diabetes mellitus and a 15.1-kg weight gain over the last 6 months. Medical history is otherwise unremarkable. He is currently taking no medications and has had no exposure to exogenous glucocorticoids in the past year. On physical examination, he has facial plethora, central obesity, and bilateral supraclavicular fat pads. There are purple abdominal striae measuring 1 cm wide and multiple ecchymoses on the extremities. Initial laboratory studies as following and a 24-hour urine free cortisol level was greater than 3 times the upper limit of normal (see lab results). Blood pressure 165/92 mmHg Heart rate 88 /min Respiratory rate 15 /min Temperature 36.9 °C BMI 29 kg/m2 ACTH < 1 2-11 pmol/L Cortisol 8 a.m. 248 mol/I post 138-635 mol/L 1 mg overnight dexamethasone test Which of the following is the most appropriate next diagnostic test?

options.text: CT scan of the adrenal glands

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman is evaluated for a 10-day history of severe neck pain with heat intolerance, palpitations, and insomnia. Medical history is significant only for a viral upper respiratory tract infection 4 weeks ago. She takes no medications. On physical examination, she appears anxious and she has sinus tachycardia. There is no proposis or lid lag. Examination of the thyroid show a normal-sized tender gland. 24-Hour radioactive iodine 5% (low) uptake (see lab results). Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone < 0.01 0.4 - 5.0 wU/mL Triiodothyronine Reverse (RT3) 4.8 0.9 - 2.8 mol/L Thyroxine (T4 free serum) 34 8.5 - 15.2 pmol/L Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 70-year-old woman was admitted 1 week ago to the Intensive Care Unite with pneumonia requiring intubation, intravenous fluids, and dopamine support for her blood pressure. On physical examination, her skin is warm and dry, no proposis, examination or the neck shows a normal-sized thyroid without nodules. Cardiovascular examination reveals regular tachycardia otherwise unremarkable systemic examination (see lab results). Blood pressure 90/57 mmH Heart rate 120 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 39 °C Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone 0.1 0.4 - 5.0 U/mL Triiodothyronine (T3 free serum) 2 3.5 - 6.5 pmol/L Thyroxine (T4 free serum) 11 8.5 - 15.2 pmol/L Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patients abnormal thyroid function?

A 49-year-old woman is evaluated because of fatigue and weight gain although she follows a daily diet control and exercises 3 times per week for 45 minutes. She has hypercholesterolemia requiring statin therapy. Her mother had hypothyroidism. On physical examination, she has dry skin, thyroid gland mildly enlarged with a diffusely nodular texture. Laboratory studies are with similar results for TSH and T4 were obtained 4 months ago (see lab results). Blood pressure 143/93 mmHg Heart rate 66 /min BMI 29 kg/m2 Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone 7.0 0.4 - 5.0 pU/mL. Thyroxine (T4 free serum) 9.5 8.5 - 15.2 pmol/L Thyroid peroxidase antibody (TPOAb) 150 <35 lU/mL Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.text: Repeat serum TSH measurement in 12 months
Schedule thyroid radioactive iodine uptake and scan

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man presents with excessive sweating and headache. An oral glucose tolerance test and MRI brain were ordered to confirm the diagnosis of acromegaly. What other investigation will be required in the future?

A 55-year-old man is referred to the Diabetes Clinic after presenting with polyuria and polydipsia with strong family history of type 2 diabetes mellitus. Physical examination is unremarkable (see lab results). Blood pressure 136/85 mmHg Heart rate 76 /min Temperature 36.6 °C BMI 34 kg/m2 Glucose fasting 9 (3.5-6.5 mmol/L) HbA1c 7.8 (4.7-5.6 %) Which of the following is the most appropriate first-line treatment?

A 43-year-old man comes to the clinic for a follow-up. He has been recently diagnosed with type 2 diabetes and has been following a plan of lifestyle measures to improve his diet and increase his level of exercise (see lab result). Blood pressure 129/80 mmHg BMI 32 kg/m2 HbA1c 6.9 (4.7-5.6 %) Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment option now?
Hydroxy Vitamin D3 (Women) 10 (25-90 mol/L) Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment approach?

An 18-year-old woman complains of dizziness feeling light-headed frequently with standing up and weight loss around 5 kg over the last 5 months. She has noticed a recent scar on the back of her hand, which has started to turn very dark. Blood pressure 90/60 mmHg, Heart rate 99 /min What is the most appropriate investigation to confirm the diagnosis?

A 29-year-old man is evaluated for a diagnosis of hypercalcemia. 5 days ago, he was treated of a kidney stone in the Emergency Department. Physical examination is unremarkable (see lab results), Blood pressure 140/79 mmHg, Heart rate 85 /min, Respiratory rate 13 /min, BMI 30 kq/m2 Test Result Normal Values Sodium 139 134-146 mmol/L Potassium 4.0 3.5-5.1 mmol/L Chloride 99 97-108 mmol/L Bicarbonate 23 21-28 mmol/L Calcium 2.95 2.15-2.62 mol/L Phosphate, inorganic 0.76 0.82-1.51 mmol/L Parathyroid hormone (intact PTH levels) 200 1.1-5.3 pmol/L Blood urea nitrogen 9.5 2.8 to 8.9 mmol/L Creatinine 125 44-115 mol/L Which of the following is most likely cause for his hypercalcemia?

A 35-year-old woman is evaluated for amenorrhea, weight gain, facial hair, alopecia, difficulty walking and easily bruising for the last 6 months. Her medical history is significant for psoriasis for which she is using clobetasol cream (topical steroid). On physical examination, vital signs all normal, she has round face, hirsutism, mild facial acne, central obesity, and a few wide purple striae on the back of her arms as well as her psoriatic skin lesions (see lab results). Sodium 139 134-146 mmol/L Potassium 3.5 3.5-5.1 mmol/L Blood urea nitrogen 6.7 2.8 to 8.9 mmol/L Creatinine 96 44-115 mol/L ACTH 1.4 2-11 pmol/ Cortisol 8 a.m. 55 138-635 mol/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

Stress leads to an increase in cortisol and catecholamine secretion that can alter the levels of lymphocyte production that fights disease. Which of the following is the most likely explanation for these effects?

A 28-year-old woman developed gestaonal diabetes during her second pregnancy. She gave birth to a healthy baby 6 months ago. There is a strong family history of type 2 diabetes and now wants to be evaluated for diabetes (see lab resuits). Height 166 cm Weight 91 kg Glucose, fasting 6.5 3.5-6.5 mmol/L bA1C 5.5 4.7-5.6 % Which of the following is the most appropriate therapy?

A 38-year-old man is unable to lose weight despite being on an intensive lifestyle management plan of a low calorie diet and exercise (see lab results). Blood pressure 145/95 mmH Heart rate 80 /min Height 173 cm Weight 125 kg Glucose, fasting 7.1 3.5-6.5 mol/L HbA1C 8.1 4.7-5.6 % Which of the following is the most appropriate advice to reduce weight?

A 66-year-old woman has recently been found to have high blood pressure. She had a cholecystectomy 15 years ago and has osteoarthritis in the knees for which she uses ibuprofen (see lab results). Blood pressure 160/95 mmH Heart rate 84 /min Creatinine 138 44-115 mol/L Sodium 142 134-146 mmol/L Potassium 2.9 3.5-5.1 mmol/L Chloride 100 97-108 mmol/L Bicarbonate 31 21-28 mmol/L Which of the following is the most likely Diagnosis?
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 72-year-old patent is evaluated for mid-thoracic back pain. The patient does not smoke cigarettes and rarely drinks alcohol. The only medications taken are aspirin, calcium supplements, and a multivitamin. Very few dairy products are consumed. On physical examination, the patient has a mild dorsal kyphosis with mild tenderness over the mid and lower thoracic regions (see lab results and report). Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone 8.2 0.4 - 5.0 U/L Calcium 2.45 2.15-2.62 mmol/L Phosphate 1.26 0.82-1.51 mmol/L Albumin 35 34-56 g/L Alkaline phosphatase 290 39-117 U/L T-Score (Bone mineral Spine L1-4) -1.9 > -1 T-Score (Bone mineral Total hip) -2.1 > -1 24 Urine Analysis Urinary calcium 5.1 < 7.5 mmols /day X-ray Spine: Compression fractures at T8, L2 and L3. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old patient presents with a 3-day history of seizures (see lab results). Test Result Normal Values Sodium 112 134-146 mmol/L Potassium 3.9 3.5-5.1 mmol/L Urea 3.4 2.75-7.4 mmol/L Serum osmolality 240 280-300 mmol/kg 24 Urine Analysis Osmolality 860 280-910 mOsm/Kg H20 Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 36-year-old patient presents with a 6-month history of decreased libido and weak erections (see lab results). Prolactin 2100 < 870 pmol/L Follicle-stimulating hormone 12 5-20 IU/L Luteinizing hormone 18 5-22 U/L Which of the following is the next most useful investigation?

A 55-year-old woman has had type 2 diabetes for the past 20 years. She is on an 1800 kcal/day diet and takes metformin 850 mg 3 times a day (see lab results). Blood pressure 130/85 mmHg Heart rate 80 /min Glucose, fastng 7.1 3.5-6.5 mmol/L НА1C 7.8 4.7-5.6 % What should be the target Haemoglobin A1C percentage?
Which of the following findings in the urine would indicate diabetic nephropathy in type 2 diabetes?

A 40-year-old man presents to the doctor with a history of central weight gain, change in facial appearance, poor libido, easy bruising, and back pain. Examination reveals pigmentation of the skin, a buffalo hump, edema, proximal muscle wasting, and an elevated blood pressure. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old man presents with a history of increased urine output, especially during the night and increased thirst for the past 2 months (see report). Water deprivation test: Serum osmolality above normal without adequate concentration of urine osmolality; no response to desmopressin administration. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-old patient complains of irritability, heat intolerance and recent onset of heart palpitations. The neck examination is normal. (see lab results). Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone 0.1 0.4 - 5.0 U/L Thyroxine (T4 free) 30.4 8.5 - 15.2 pmol/L Triiodothyronine (T3 free) 9.5.3.5 - 6.5 pmol/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A patient with hypothyroidism, on 0.025 mg of L-thyroxin, complains of fatigue, cold intolerance, and weight gain (see lab result). Blood Pressure 120/60 mmH Heart Rate 57 /min Respiratory Rate 16 /min Temperature 36.6° C Test Result Normal Value TSH 19.9 mU/L 0.4-6.5 mU/L Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

options.text: Increase L-thyroxin and check TSH in 6 weeks
Increase L-thyroxin and check TSH in 3 weeks
Decrease L-thyroxin and check TSH in 6 weeks
Decrease L-thyroxin and check TSH in 3 weeks

questions.stem: A 35-year-old man complains of discomfort in both breasts with milk production when expressed manually for a month. It has been associated with headache and low sexual interest. He has been married for 3 years and his wife has not been able to become pregnant. On examination, he has mild acne on his face (see lab results). Weight 97 kg Height 173 cm Thyroxine (T4 free) 8.4 8.5 - 15.2 pmol/L Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone 6.8 0.4 - 5.0 U/L Follicle-stimulating hormone 5.8 5-20 IU/L Luteinizing hormone 7.1 5-22 U/L Prolactin 2350 < 870 pmol/L Which of the following is the most likely visual field defect?

A 32-year-old woman complains that her menstrual cycle has stopped for the last 9 months. She also has discomfort in both breasts with milk production when expressed manually. Her sexual drive has been decreased for the last year. She has been married for 3 years and failed to become pregnant. The physical examination is normal and pregnancy test is negative (see lab results). Weight 81 kg Height 165 cm Thyroxine (T4 free) 9.1 8.5 - 15.2 pmol/L Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone 5.2 0.4 - 5.0 yU/L Follicle-stimulating hormone 5 5-20 IU/L Luteinizing hormone 10 5-22 U/L Prolactin 2450 < 870 pmol/L Which of the following is the most appropriate investigation?
Which of the following is the most appropriate radiological imaging?

A 28-year-old woman presents with a painful neck swelling for the last week. The swelling has been increasing over time. She has a sore throat and difficulty in swallowing. She has frequent bowel motions. On a physical examination, there is a diffuse tender anterior neck swelling and both hands show a fine tremor (see lab results). Blood pressure 140/90 mmHg Heart rate 105 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 38.1° C Thyroxine (T4 free) 26.4 8.5 - 15.2 pmol/L Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone 0.03 0.4 - 5.0 mU/L ESR 58 3-15 mm/h Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 45-year-old woman comes to the clinic for a follow-up. She was started on levothyroxine for treatment of hypothyroidism 2 weeks before (see lab result). TSH 7.5 0.4-6.5 mU/L Which of the following would be the best treatment plan?

options.text: Same dose, check TSH level in 1 to 2 months
Reduce dose, check TSH level in 1 to 2 months
Reduce dose, check TSH level in 48 to 72 hours
Stop treatment until TSH normal, and then restart

questions.stem: A 23-year-old pregnant patient complains of irritability and sweating. On examination, she is thin and appears anxious. Her thyroid gland is nodular, diffusely enlarged, but not tender. She has brisk deep tendon reflexes. Her uterus is appropriate for gestational age (see lab results and report). Blood pressure 115/70 mmH Heart rate 110 /min Respiratory rate 12 /min - Temperature 37.1 °C Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone 0.1 0.4 - 5.0 mU/L Antithyroid Antibody negative Thyroid ultrasound: Diffuse nodular enlargement. No cyst identified. Which of the following is the best next step in management?
A patient has presented with a 2 cm solid thyroid nodule on the Ultrasound. Which of the following is the best next step in the management?

A 17-year-old woman presents with her mother to the clinic complaining of never having had menstruation. On examination, she is webbing of her neck and cubitus valgus. Lacks pubic hairs and no breast development noted. The mother is worried about the daughter and would inquire about the simplest test to start with. Height 135 cm Weight 46 kg Which of the following is the simplest and most useful test?
A 51-year-old woman presents to her appointment complaining of hot flushes. She would like to get an explanation of her symptom. Which of the following involves hot flushes?

options.text: Peripheral vasodilatation reflecting an elevation of core body temperature
Peripheral vasodilatation resulting from direct effect of elevated FSH and LH
Peripheral redistribution of blood flow leading to sweating and increased heart rate

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman presents to the clinic with a history of irregular menstrual cycles for the last 2 years. Her last delivery 5 years ago. Currently, she is not on any contraception. Examination shows all within normal limits except breast examination revealed frank galactorrhea. Which of the following is most helpful investigation?
Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in the management?

A 45-year-old man is evaluated for recent onset type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension for the last 1 year. On physical examination, he has moon like face, dorsocervical fat pad and striae measuring 8 to 12 mm wide are noted on his upper arms and abdomen. Laboratory studies reveals the following as well as 24-Hour urine cortisol excretion which was 5 times upper the normal cut value and CT scan of the abdomen with and without contrast reveals a 5-cm right adrenal mass with contrast washout at 10 minutes is 60% (see lab results). hour postprandial blood glucose 190 to 200 mg/dL. (10.5-11.1 mmol/L.) In addition to lifestyle modifications, which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?

A 37-year-old man with type 1 diabetes mellitus presents to the office with history of prolonged hypoglycemia during intense exercise, despite eating a meal prior to the activity. He is using insulin glargine and insulin aspart with meals (see lab result). Test Result Normal Value Н6А1C 7.0 4.7-5.6 % Which of the following is the most appropriate management of this patient's hypoglycemia on the days that he exercises?

options.text: Decrease meal-time insulin aspart dose prior to exercise, continue insulin glargine dose
Increase meal-time protein prior to exercise, continue current insulin doses
Switch insulin aspart to a sliding-scale regimen, continue insulin glargine dose

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man is evaluated because of fatigue, constipation and cold intolerance for the last 8 months. Medical history is significant for Hodgkin lymphoma treated with radiation therapy 3 years ago and there is no family history of thyroid disorders. On physical examination, he has dry skin with mild periorbital edema and normal thyroid exam (see lab results). Test Result Normal Values Hb 120 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Sodium 129 134-146 mmol/L Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone 5.0 0.4 - 5.0 U/mL. Which of the following will establish diagnosis of hypothyroidism?

A 30-year-old woman is admitted to the hospital for an elective adrenalectomy for non-ACTH dependent Cushing syndrome confirmed by a contrast-enhanced adrenal CT scan finding of benign right adrenal adenoma. Which of the following is the most appropriate perioperative management?
Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment of this patient's hypothyroidism now?

A 59-year-old man is admitted to the hospital for evaluation of chest pain. His medical history is significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus, coronary artery disease, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia. He manages his diabetes as an outpatient with diet, exercise, and metformin. His other medications are aspirin, metoprolol, atorvastatin, and sublingual nitroglycerin as needed (see lab results). HbA1C 8.5 4.7-5.6 % Plasma Glucose 9.4-14.9 mmol/L Which of the following is the most appropriate diabetes treatment for this patient while hospitalized?

A 23-year-old woman is evaluated after a recent diagnosis of polycystic ovary syndrome. She is concerned about hirsutism and irregular menses. She is not planning for pregnancy at this time and takes no medications. On physical examination, she has mild hirsutism and the remaining of her physical examination, including pelvic examination, are normal. Blood pressure 120/70 mmH Heart rate 76 /min Respiratory rate 15 /min Temperature 36.7 °C BMI 36 kg/m2 Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 61-year-old man with a 20-year history of type 2 diabetes mellitus is evaluated for bilateral burning sensation in his feet for the last 8 months, which worsens at night. His haemoglobin Ac levels have remained less than 7.0% for the last 1 years but were between 9.0% and 10.0% before adding insulin therapy to metformin 1 years ago. His medical history includes coronary artery disease, non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia. Medications are aspart insulin, glargine, aspirin, metoprolol, atorvastatin, and lisinopril. On physical examination, findings are compatible with distal symmetrical polyneuropathy. Which of the following is the most appropriate management of this patient's neuropathy?
Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Observation and retest thyroid function test in 6 months

questions.stem: A 19-year-old woman is evaluated for management of type 1 diabetes. She was diagnosed 4 months ago after presenting to the Emergency Department with diabetic ketoacidosis. Her hemoglobin A1c level at the time of diagnosis was 14.5%. She was discharged from the hospital on a basal and prandial insulin regimen with minor adjustments required as an outpatient. Recently she started to have episodes of both fasting and postprandial hypoglycemia. Medications are insulin glargine and insulin apart. Her systemic examinations are unremarkable (see lab results). Blood pressure 115/77 mmH Heart rate 80 /min BMI 22 kg/m2 Test Result Normal Values НА1С 6.0 4.7-5.6 % Random Glucose 4.5 3.9-5.5 mmol/L Which of the following is the most appropriate management for her hypoglycemia?

options.text: Decrease insulin glargine, decrease insulin aspart
Continue same doses of insulin glargine and aspart
Discontinue insulin glargine, discontinue insulin aspart
Discontinue insulin glargine, change insulin aspart to a sliding-scale regimen

questions.stem: A 44-year-old man is evaluated for an 8-month history of decreased libido and severe erectile dysfunction, including absence of morning erections. He and his wife would like to conceive. His medical history is otherwise unremarkable, and he takes no medications. On physical examination, vital signs are normal with unremarkable clinical examination (see lab results and report). Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone 2.5 0.4 - 5.0 wU/mL Follicle-stimulating hormone 1.2 5-20 IU/L (Follicular phase) 15-35 IU/L (Mid cycle peak) 5-15 IU/L (Luteal phase) 50-100 IU/L (Postmenopausal women) 5-20 IU/L (men) Testosterone 4.2 10.4-41.6 mol/L (Male) 0.7-2.8 mol/L (Female) Luteinizing hormone 1.0 3-15 U/L (Male) 5-22 U/L (Follicular phase) 5-22 U/L. (Luteal phase) 30-250 U/L (ovulatory phase) > 30 U/L (Postmenopausal) Prolactin 1500 < 652 pmol/L (Male) < 870 pmol/L (Female) MRI of the pituitary: Reveals a 0.8-cm anterior pituitary mass consistent with an adenoma. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 79-year-old man was admitted to the Intensive Care Unit with features of septicaemia due to severe urinary tract infection. His blood tests showed thyroid dysfunction that was attributed to a non-thyroidal iliness or sick euthyroid state. Which one of the following is the common typical pattern of thyroid dysfunction seen in a sick euthyroid illness?

options.text: Elevated levels of T3 and T4; low levels of reverse T3
Elevated levels of T3, T4, and reverse T3
Low levels of T3 and T4; elevated levels of reverse T3
Low levels of T3 and T4; normal level of reverse T3

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man presented to thyroid clinic with a 5-month history of feeling unwell, weight loss, anxiety, and panic attacks. He also complained of redness and grittiness of eyes, with painful eye movements. On examination, he had bilateral tremors, proposis, and lid retraction, Which one of the following factors is associated with increased risk for the development of severe Grave's orbitopathy?

A 39-year-old man incidentally found to have a 2-cm left adrenal gland mass while she underwent CT of the abdomen to investigate the cause of her pelvic pain. Which one of the following is the most common cause of an incidentally detected adrenal mass?

A 40-year-old woman was incidentally detected to have a 13-mm pituitary macro-adenoma on a CT of the head arranged to evaluate cause for her recurrent headaches. Apart from the headaches that she had suffered for the last 8 months, she had no history of any significant medical illness and was not on any regular medications. Her general physical and systemic examination was unremarkable. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in her management?

A 25-year-old woman complains of dizziness and feeling light-headed. She is a teacher and most frequently experiences this when she stand up in the class. She has never fainted. She lost 5 kg, but attributes this to eating healthy food. She has noticed a recent scar on the back of her hand, which has started to turn very dark as well as generalized skin hyperpigmentation. What is the most appropriate investigation to confirm the diagnosis?

Dipeptidyl peptidase inhibitors 4 (DPP4) are novel oral hypoglycaemic agents that inhibit the enzyme DPP4 and prevent breakdown of endogenous incretins, which will improve blood sugar control in patients with diabetes mellitus type 2. Which of the following DPP4 inhibitor does not require any dose modification in renal disease?
At which estimated GFR level, metformin should be stopped in diabetic patients?
Which of the following osteoporosis treatment has FDA approval to treat malignancy induced hypercalcemia?

A 35-year-old pregnant woman with gestational age of 30-weeks comes for a follow-up. She was diagnosed to have gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) at week 24, she was maintained on diet control but unfortunately her blood sugar reading between (150-200 mg/di). The physician decided to start insulin but she is totally refusing injections and she asks about any safe oral medication to be used in pregnancy. Which of the following oral hypoglycemic agents has safety data and recommended to be used in pregnancy?

A 44-year-old man with a strong family history of type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease was recently diagnosed with pre-diabetes. He came for advice regarding healthy eating patterns and physical activity that will help him to prevent type 2 diabetes (see lab result). BMI 31 kg/m2 HbA1C 6.1 4.7-5.6 % In helping this individual to achieve and maintain his target weight loss, which of the following is the best advice?

options.text: Exercising 30 minutes per day on 5 days per week
Diet low in protein and relatively higher in carbohydrates
Exercise for at least 30 minutes most days of the week and low carbohydrate diet

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman comes to the clinic for a follow-up. She is diagnosed with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) at week 24. She is asking for an advice regarding the best dietary habits she can follow to control her blood sugar and avoid insulin injection. Which of the following is the best diet option?

options.text: Energy restriction is not recommended during pregnancy

questions.stem: A 62-year-old woman receives a diagnosis of prediabetes based on routine lab work showing mildly elevated glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c. She has had obesity for many years. She eats a diet rich in processed foods. She rarely exercises. Physical exam reveals mildly elevated blood pressure along with trace acanthosis nigricans at the nape of the neck. Blood Pressure 145/87 mmH BMI 30 kg/m2 What advice should be given to reduce her risk of developing diabetes, in addition to increasing her physical activity to >150 minutes per week?

options.text: Low glycemic index diet to produce 5-10 % weight loss
Low fat diet to produce 5-10 % weight loss
Diet is less effective than metformin to reduce the risk of diabetes
Low carbohydrate diets are more likely than low fat diets to prevent diabetes in the long-term

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man comes to the clinic for evaluation and management of obesity. His obesity is complicated by type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), hypertension, sleep apnea, dyslipidemia, chronic low back pain, osteoarthritis of the knees, and depression. He was prescribed medications for these problems but that he is not compliant to treatments. His wife accompanied him to the visit was anxious about his health and she want the doctor to council him for the best solutions he can do. BMI 55 kg/m2 Which of the following is the most appropriate advice will help in treating this patient?

options.text: Emphasizing the importance of adherence to his medications
Referral to an orthopedic surgeon for knee arthroplasties

questions.stem: A 39-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes for 20 years was married recently; she and her husband want to get pregnant. The woman has hypertension treated with an angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor and a diuretic with maintenance of blood pressure at 118/80 mmHg. Her insulin doses are all administered through a continuous insulin infusion pump using insulin aspart. She reported that she would try to become pregnant next month (see lab results). Test Result Normal Values 24 hr urine protein 2000 0.8-14 mg/di (Male) 2.5-11 mg/dI (Female) Creatinine 88 44-115 mol/L HbA1C 8.0 4.7-5.6 % What is the best advice at this moment to control her blood sugar and prevent congenital malformation?

options.text: Eliminate snacks and begin to take 3 heavy meals daily
Substitute an angiotensin receptor blocker for her ACE inhibitor
Her age and risk factors indicate the need to begin taking a statin at this time
Delay conception until her HbA1c is as close to normal as possible, if this can be safely achieved

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman pregnant at 15 weeks presents to the clinic complaining of palpitation, tremor and diarrhea for the last 3 weeks. On examination, she looks anxious, she has graves ophthalmopathy and goiter. Other systemic examination are unremarkable. Diagnosis of grave's disease was confirmed but she is refusing to start any treatment while she is pregnant (see lab results). Blood pressure 110/65 mmHg Heart rate 125 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 37.6 °C BMI 20 kg/m2 Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone < 0.01 0.4 - 5.0 U/mL Triiodothyronine (T3 free serum) 10.0 3.5 - 6.5 pmol/L Thyroxine (T4 free serum) 35.0 8.5 - 15.2 pmol/L Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Agree with her opinion and discharge her from the clinic
Call her husband and force her to start the treatment
Give her follow up after 2 months and repeat her thyroid function test
Explain clearly the risk for her and the fetus and try to convince her to start the treatment Immediately

questions.stem: A 22-year-old man developed traumatic paraplegia secondary to a road traffic accident about 8 months ago, requiring prolonged immobilization. His general physical and systemic examination were unremarkable and intact PTH levels (see lab results). Calcium 2.75 2.15-2.62 mmol/L Phosphate, inorganic 0.9 0.82-1.51 mmol/L Parathyroid hormone 1.0 1.1-5.3 pmol/L Which of the following is the most probable underlying aetiology for his hypercalcaemia?

A 40-year-old man was referred to the endocrine clinic with symptoms of reduced libido and lack of energy for the last 10 months. On examination, he had normal general physical and systemic examination (see lab results and report). BMI 40 kg/m2 Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone 0.3 0.4 - 5.0 wU/mL. Thyroxine (T4 free serum) 7.5 8.5 - 15.2 pmol/L Follicle-stimulating hormone 2.5 5-20 IU/L (Follicular phase) 15-35 IU/L (Mid cycle peak) 5-15 IU/L (Luteal phase) 50-100 IU/L (Postmenopausal women) 5-20 IU/L (men) Testosterone 8.0 10.4-41.6 mol/L (Male) 0.7-2.8 nmol/L (Female) Luteinizing hormone 1.3 3-15 U/L (Male) 5-22 U/L (Follicular phase) 5-22 U/L (Luteal phase) 30-250 U/L (ovulatory phase) > 30 U/L (Postmenopausal) Prolactin 450 < 652 pmol/L (Male) < 870 pmol/L (Female) MRI brain: Showed 2.5 cm pituitary adenoma. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 20-year-old woman presented to the Maternal Health Clinic with severe facial acne and irregular menstrual bleeding. Examination shows fine hair growth on the chin, upper back, breasts and lower abdomen. A pregnancy test is returned negative. She returns to the clinic on the 5th day of her menstrual cycle and has a serum sample drawn for analysis (see lab results). Follicle-stimulating hormone 10 (5-20 IU/L) Luteinizing hormone 28 (5-22 U/L) Prolactin 890 ( < 870 pmol/L) Testosterone 3.2 (0.7-2.8 mol/L) Which additional laboratory values should be obtained?

options.text: Thyroid stimulating hormone and free T3 and T4

questions.stem: A 50-year-old woman presented with a few months history of feeling dizziness when getting out of bed she also feels very warm and flushed. She visited the Emergency Room several times with frequent episodes of abdominal cramps and watery diarrhea over the past year. She gave a history of itchy skin. On examination, she has a 2/6 systolic murmur at left lower sternal border, chest examination reveals wheezing, abdomen was unremarkable. Laboratory results and stool cultures were normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?
Which of the following is the most appropriate intervention for primary prevention of type 2 diabetes?
Which of the following is the strongest risk factor for diabetes in adults?
A 75-year-old woman presented with significant height loss. Which of the following is the most appropriate investigation?

options.text: lateral thoracic and lumbar spine X-ray

questions.stem: Which of the following number of sleep hours is associated with more weight gain?

A 78-year-old man was admitted to hospital with lethargy and back pain. He had a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and rheumatoid arthritis (see lab results). Calcium 2.72 2.15-2.62 mol/L Creatinine 196 44-115 mol/L Urinary protein: creatinine ratio 154 mg/mmol (<30) Which of the following is most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following the patient should be screened for?
Which of the following is the most appropriate management for palpitations?
Hour Urine Analysis: - Osmolality: 310 mOsm/kg H2O (Normal: 280-910 mOsm/kg H2O) Which of the following is the most likely cause?

#Anki 121- A 60-year-old diabetic patient presents for follow-up. Currently, the patient takes metformin that maintains fasting blood glucose levels lower than 5.5 mmol/L with HbA1c level of 5.8%. Physical examination is normal, including a lower extremity neurological examination. The patient has regular eye exams that show no signs of retinopathy. Blood pressure: 149/90 mmHg (three readings)Heart rate: 76 /minRespiratory rate: 18 /minTemperature: 36.6°C Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

#Anki 122 - A 25-year-old patient is diagnosed with diabetic ketoacidosis (see lab results). Vital Signs: - Blood pressure: 80/50 mmHg - Heart rate: 140 /min - Respiratory rate: 26 /min - Temperature: 36.6°C Lab Results: - Random Glucose: 52.7 mmol/L (Normal: 3.9 - 5.5 mmol/L) - Potassium: 6 mmol/L (Normal: 3.5-5.1 mmol/L) - Bicarbonate: 5 mmol/L (Normal: 21-28 mmol/L) Which of the following is the best initial management?

options.text: Dopamine drip to raise blood pressure above 90 mmHg
2L of normal saline with KCl 20 mEq/L intravenously
20-unit regular insulin intravenously, followed by 5% dextrose in water at 200 mL/h
Normal saline 2 L as an intravenous bolus and insulin intravenous infusion at 0.1 U/kg/hr

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best management?

A 67-year-old man comes to the clinic complaining that he has a tremor in the right hand. It is best displayed when he reaches for a pen and is manifested easily in the finger-to-nose test. In which of the following locations is the lesion?

A 72-year-old woman with Parkinson's disease, complaining of a very annoying tremor of the dominant right hand. She is not on any medication. She states that her tremor is the only feature that disturbs her functioning. Which of the medications would be most likely to improve her tremor?

A 69-year-old man comes to the clinic complaining of increasing fatigue and drowsiness and difficulty to arouse. History reveals he was on a vacation 2 weeks ago. Although he admits to taking several falls, he is unaware of any head injury. Neurological examination showed no lateralizing or focal findings. Head and scalp examinations are negative for focal tenderness and deformity. Plain X-ray of the skull is negative (see lab results). RBC 5.1 {4.7-6.1 x 1012/L (Male) | 4.2-5.4 x 1012/L (Female)} Hb 132 {130-170 g/L (Male) | 120-160 g/L (Female)} HCT 0.40 {0.42-0.52 (Male) | 0.37-0.48 (Female)} MCH 30 {28-33 pg/cell} MCHC 322 {320-360 g/L} MCV 88 {80-95 fl} Reticulocyte 0.9 {0.2-1.2 %} Platelets count 200 {150-400 x 109/L} WBC 5.5 {4.5-10.5 x 109/L} Neutrophils 50 {40-60%} Eosinophils 2 {1-4 %} Basophils 0.8 {0.5-1 %} Lymphocytes 32 {20-40 %} Monocytes 4.1 {2-8 %} Calcium 2.3 {2.15-2.62 mmol/L} Calcium ionized 1.2 {1.1-1.3 mmol/L} Magnesium 0.8 {0.7-1.2 mol/L} Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone 4.4 {0.4 - 5.0 p/mL} Thyroxine (T4 free serum) 12 {8.5 - 15.2 pmol/L} Sodium 136 {134-146 mmol/L} Potassium 4.2 {3.5-5.1 mmol/L} Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 73-year-old diabetic man presents with right-sided weakness. The weakness is equal in the right face, arm and leg. Sensation, speech and comprehension are intact. Which of the following arteries is affected?

A 70-year-old man complains of a sudden severe headache while bending down to pick up his keys this morning. He describes it as the worst headache he has ever had; he says it was like being hit on the back of the neck. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 48-year-old woman has a 2-year history of a slowly progressive bilateral tremor. The tremor interferes with her writing and eating. She has recently noted head bobbing and a change in her voice. Which of the following would be an appropriate first-line medication for her problem?

A 50-year-old woman comes to the clinic with numbness in the lower part of the ear, lower face, and upper neck. History reveals, she underwent a lateral neck dissection. Examination shows loss of sensation over both surfaces of the lower part of the pinna and skin overlying the angle of the mandible on the same side of the operation. Which of the following nerves is most likely injured?

A 25-year-old man is brought to the Emergency Room after a motor vehicle accident. Examination shows he has a severed nerve in the right upper limb, resulting in a loss of adduction of all the digits of the right hand.Which of the following is the most likely affected nerve?

A 19-year-old patient comes to the clinic because he is unable to bring the fork to his mouth to feed himself. History reveals the patient had a closed head injury in a motor vehicle accident 10 days ago.Which of the following is the most likely involved area?
A 41-year-old woman developed atrophy of the thenar eminence, but the sensation over it is intact. Which of the following nerves is the most likely damaged?
A 27-year-old patient with a known carpal tunnel syndrome, experiences difficulty in finger movements. Which of the following muscles is most likely paralyzed?

A 36-year-old man has unilateral mild pain in the neck which radiates to the right interscapular and shoulder regions. The pain is followed by sharp, electric shock-like pain, which goes down the arm with numbness, weakness and loss of tendon reflexes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old obese patient complained of numbness and tingling of the little and ring fingers on the left hand. The patient said that the symptoms are worse when the hands are raised. The elevated arm stress test is positive on the left Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old woman presented with few months history of increase forgetfulness, fatigue and numbness of lower limbs. She is a known case of crohn's disease, post terminal ilium resection 2 years ago. She is on azathioprine. She denies abdominal pain or diarrhoea (see lab results). Test Result Normal Values RBC 4.5 4.7-6.1 x 1012/L. (Male) 4.2-5.4 x 1012/L (Female) Hb 90 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) MCH 38 28-33 pg/cell MCV 99 80-951 Platelets count 199 150-400 x 109/L A deficiency of which of the following nutrients would be responsible for her current clinical presentation?

A 48-year-old woman had terminal ileum resection due to Crohn's disease. She presents this time with difficulty in walking. She is anemic and has lost position sense bilaterally. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 58-year-old man presents to the clinic with a history of a disturbed recent memory as a cardinal feature of his disturbed state of mind along with behavioural changes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is the main difference between delirium and dementia?

A 72 -year-old man experiences an inability to sustain attention, disorganised thinking, hallucinations, and disorientation commencing 12 hours after an aortic femoral, popliteal bypass. The symptoms fluctuated during the next 2 days. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 70-year-old man with Alzheimer's dementia becomes agitated and aggressive after Developing hallucinations and delusions. A complete evaluation does not reveal any environmental, medical, or psychiatric cause, and behavioural interventions failed to improve the agitation. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 78-year-old man is brought to the Outpatient Clinic with a 2-year history of slow and progressive deterioration in his memory. He is able to perform some activities in daily life. Including dressing, bathing, and cooking. He has personality changes; once a kind and caring parent, he now displays periods of both agitation and aggression. Neurologic and musculoskeletal examinations cannot be carried out. Which of the following is the best management?

options.text: Admission to a chronic care facility

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man presents to the Psychiatry Clinic for follow-up accompanied by his son. He has had progressive memory loss, difficulty in finding words, wandering, and agitation, as well as urinary and fecal incontinence for the last 3 years. On examination, he was conscious but not oriented in time and place; his short memory was severely impaired, with an intact long memory (see report). Brain CT scan: Atrophied hippocampal and temporal lobes. Which of the following chromosomes harbors the mutated gene is responsible for this presentation?
Which of the following clinical signs is caused by a lesion in Wernicke's area?

options.text: Can understand but unable to say words easily
Cannot understand spoken or written words
Loss of ability to recognise faces

questions.stem: Which of the following drugs used in Alzheimer's disease is most likely to cause hepatotoxicity?
Which of the following conditions is the most likely cause of dementia?

A 51-year-old woman presented to the hospital with 2-days history of malaise and headache. The headache became more intense and was associated with pain in her neck. Her husband reported that she had also fever. She was previously well with no significant medical history. On examination, she looked unwell confused, febrile and with positive Kemig's sign. CT scan brain was normal. Lumbar puncture done (see lab results). Colour Turbid colourless Cells 200 0-3 /pL Total protein (Women) 0.9 0.15-0.45 g/L Glucose 1.6 2.50-3.89 mmol/L Which of the following is the most likely causative organism?

A 78-year-old man presents with 2-year history of slow and progressive deterioration in his memory. The patient is able to perform some activities of daily living, including dressing and bathing. His personality has changed from that of a kind and caring person into someone who has periods of agitation and aggression. Neurologic and musculoskeletal examination cannot be carried out. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 46-year-old women with schizophrinea presents to the clinic with 1-month history of abnormal orofacial movements. She has been prescribed amisulpride 600mg for many years and procyclidine 5 mg daily. Which of the following is the most likely cause?

A 36-year-old woman presented with 2-year history of recurrent headaches. These headaches occur 3 to 4 times per month and last 12 to 24 hours. The headaches are usually located over the right or left frontal sinuses. This particular headache has lasted 2 days now, and she has some nausea associated with it. The patient has been using an over-the counter analgesic-decongestant combination without significant relief. Neurological examination is within normal limits. The optic fundi are normal, Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 76 /min Temperature 36.6 °C What is the appropriate next step to determine the etiology of this headache?

options.text: CT scan of the paranasal sinuses

questions.stem: A 41-year-old man complains of double vision. Whilst looking forward the patients left eye turns towards the nose. On looking to the patient's right there is no obvious squint. However, on looking to the left, the patient is unable to abduct the left eye and double vision worsens. Which of the following is the most likely cranial nerve palsy?

A 42-year-old man comes to the clinic with his brother. The brother is concerned that he has been acting strangely over the past 4 months. In particular, he has been irritable and criticizes everyone at home. The changes were subtle at first but now arguments arise every other day. He has difficulty initiating conversation and even pauses halfway through sentences. There is no family history of note and he is not taking any medications. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old man recently returned from Umrah, presents to Emergency Department with 1-day history of fever and headache. Upon arrival to the Emergency Department, he started to have seizures on the right extremities. On examination, positive Kering 's sign (see lab results and report). Temperature 39 °C Cells 380 0-3 /pL Total protein (Men) 1.2 0.22-0.33 g/L CSF analysis: WBC differential count: 87% neutrophils and 5% lymphocytes. Which of the following is the most appropriate intravenous treatment option?

A 22-year-old man presents to Emergency Department with 4-days history of fever, headache and confusion. On examination, Kering 's sign is present (see lab results and reports). Temperature 39 °C Cells 380 0-3 /pL Total protein (Men) 0.8 0.22-0.33 g/L Glucose 3.7 2.50-3.89 mmol/L CSF analysis: WBC differential count: 5% neutrophil and 90% lymphocytes. CSF Culture: Pending. Which of the following is the most appropriate intravenous treatment option?

A 22-year-old man recently returned from Hal, presents to Emergency Department with 1-day history of fever and headache. On examination, Kering 's sign is present. Skin examination showed petechial rash on extremities and trunk (see lab results and report). Temperature 39 °C Cells 380 0-3 /pL Total protein (Men) 0.9 0.22-0.33 g/L Glucose 1.2 2.50-3.89 mmol/L CSF analysis: WBC differential: 87% neutrophils and 5% lymphocytes. Which of the following isolation precautions should be considered?

A 27-year-old man recently returned from Umrah. Presents to Emergency Department with 1- day history of fever and headache. On examination, positive Kernig's sign and petechial rash on extremities and trunk. He was isolated and started on antibiotics (see lab results and report). Temperature 39 °C Cells 380 0-3 /pL Total protein (Men) 0.9 0.22-0.33 g/L Glucose 1.2 2.50-3.89 mmol/L CSF analysis: WBC differential 87 % neutrophil and 5 % lymphocytes. How many hours after starting antibiotics should isolation be discontinued?

A 59-year-old man has unsteady gait. On examination, he has decreased proprioception in the lower limbs with positive planter reflexes (positive Babinski) and absent ankle and knee's reflexes. He has anemia. Peripheral smear done (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following factors is directly related to increased risk of stroke?

A 46-year-old man has dyspnea on exertion and palpitations. On examination, he has patches of vitiligo and has absent reflexes with positive Babinski in the lower limbs (see lab results). Test Result Normal Values Hb 91 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) MCV 103 80-95 f1 Platelets count 129 150-400 × 109/L Ferritin 120 20-300 g/.
