An 81-year-old man with memory loss and difficulty recognizing his grandsons. He has no cardiovascular risk factors. Which of the following is the most common cause of his cognitive impairment?

A 79-year-old man comes to the clinic for a follow-up. He has a 1-year history of progressive memory impairment and clinical evidence of early Alzheimer dementia. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial diagnostic tests?

#Anki 53- A 45-year-old patient presents to the clinic with a 3-month history of stumbling, weak grip, dysphagia, and generalized weakness, and also had 2 episodes of aspiration pneumonia in the last 2 months. Examination confirms brisk reflexes, spastic muscles, and fasciculation of tongue and thigh. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

#Anki 54- A man on treatment for multiple sclerosis, presents with acute onset diplopia, ataxia, and weakness of the right hand(see report). MRI brain scan: New active lesions compared to previous scans. Which of the following is the best treatment for this development?

#Anki 55- A 71-year-old man comes to the Outpatient Clinic with difficulty walking and a hand tremor at rest for the last 3 months. There is no history of trauma or past illness. General examination reveals an expressionless face, slow and slurred speech, and a hand tremor at rest. There is no sensory abnormality but the motor system showed brisk reflexes and hypertonia. The gait is quick, with short steps and diminished associated movements, such as no arm swinging. Which of the following is the most probable location of the defect?

#Anki 56- A 70-year-old patient presents with a 6-month history of decline in cognitive capacity and conscious level. On examination, the patient has bradykinesia, resting tremors, a mask-like face, and a shuffling gait. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

#Anki 57- A 32-year-old patient is having repetitive generalized seizures that continue for 35 minutes. The patient received 20 mg of diazepam intravenously, but there has been no response. Which of the following is the best next step in management?

#Anki 58- A 44-year-old woman comes to her physician as she is unable to close her left eye. There is a facial asymmetry when she smiles and inability to wrinkle the left side of her left forehead. Which of the following nerves is mostly affected?

#Anki 59- A 35-year-woman comes to the clinic complaining of severe "pins and needles" sensations on the dorsum of her left hand over parts of the thumb, index, and middle fingers. Edrophonium test is performed that shows transient improvement in the ptosis (see report). Chest X-ray is normal. Which of the following would be the most suitable treatment?
Which of the following imaging is the most diagnostic?

On a follow-up consultation of a patient with a squamous cell carcinoma, some abnormalities are noted in blood analysis (see lab results). Parathyroid hormone 1.0 (1.1-5.3 )pmol/L Calcium 3.30 (2.15-2.62 )mmol/L Calcium ionised 1.6 (1.1-1.3)mmol/L Sodium 140 (134-146) mmol/L Potassium 4.3 (3.5-5.1) mmol/L Which of the following is the most likely cause of the metabolic abnormality?

options.text: Secretion of PTH-related peptide by the tumour

questions.stem: What is the most effective drug to reduce this incidence?

A 26-year-old woman has become increasingly tired for the past 2 months. During the past week she has noted purple blotches on her skin. A 39-year-old man with asymptomatic hereditary hemochromatosis presented to the clinic for a check-up (see lab results). options.text: Repeat the serum ferritin after 6 month

questions.stem: Which of the following anemias is most likely associated with SLE at this stage?

A 48-year-old man who is a smoker for the last 20 years, had a routine exam (see lab result and report). Test Result Calcium 3.1 (Normal Value 2.15-2.62 mmol/L) Chest X-ray: 4 cm diameter left hilar mass. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

options.text: High methyl malonic acid and normal homocysteine
High methyl malonic acid and high homocysteine
Normal methyl malonic acid and high homocysteine
Low methyl malonic acid and low homocysteine

A 48-year-old man develops right popliteal vein thrombosis post-sleeve surgery. He is started on enoxaparin and warfarin. What is the target therapeutic international normalization ratio range for this patient?

A 53-year-old woman admitted to the hospital with pneumonia. She has diabetes, hypertension and is on hemodialysis for end-stage renal disease (see lab results). Hb 98 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Platelets count 151 150-400 x 109/L APTT 33 30-40 sec INR 0.9 0.8-1.2 Prothrombin time 9.8 10-13 sec Creatinine 460 44-115 mol/L Which of the following is the most appropriate venous thromboembolism prophylaxis for this patient?

A 38-year-old woman admitted with pyelonephritis. 2 days after admission, she develops sudden severe shortness of breath (see report). Blood pressure 84/50 mmHg Heart rate 124 /min Oxygen saturation 84 % CT-pulmonary angiogram: A saddle embolus at the bifurcation of the pulmonary artery and multiple segmental pulmonary emboli bilaterally. which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 59-year-old man has diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia and chronic renal impairment. He was admitted 5 days ago to the Coronary Care Unit for a non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI). He is receiving unfractionated heparin. His labs upon admission were normal. Day 5 of his admission, labs as shown (see lab results). Hb 13.1 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Platelets count 65 150-400 x 109/L WBC 10.3 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Creatinine 88 44-115 umol/L APTT 36 (30-40 sec) INR 1.1 (0.8-1.2) Prothrombin time 11 (10-13 sec) Which of the following is the most likely cause of his thrombocytopenia?

A 38-year-old woman has fever and headache for 2 days. Peripheral smear done (see image and lab results). Heart rate 110 /min Temperature 38.9 °C Hb 112 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Reticulocyte 3.2 0.2-1.2 % Platelets count 123 150-400 x 109/L Fibrinogen 1.1 2-4 g/L APTT 68 30-40 sec INR 1.8 0.8-1.2 Prothrombin time 24 10-13 sec Direct bilirubin 24.5 1.5-6.5 mol/L Total bilirubin 48.3 3.5-16.5 mol/L Lactate dehydrogenase 390 60-160 IU/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old woman has atrial fibrillation for which she has started on warfarin. Few weeks after, she fell down and developed a subdural hematoma that requires evacuation (see lab result). INR 3.9 0.8-1.2 Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Fresh frozen plasma and vitamin K

questions.stem: An 18-year-old-boy is receiving chemotherapy for acute lymphoblastic leukemia. On day 17 of chemotherapy, he has fever. He has no focus of infection (see lab results). Heart rate 110 /min, Temperature 38.9 °C, Platelets count 25 150-400 x 109/L WBC 0.6 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Neutrophils 60 40-60% Lymphocytes 20 20-40 % Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Send blood, urine, sputum cultures and start paracetamol
Send blood, urine, sputum cultures and start oral broad spectrum antibiotics
Send blood, urine, sputum cultures and start intravenous broad spectrum antibiotics

questions.stem: A 43-year-old-woman has fever, night sweats and weight loss. She has lost 12 Kg in the last 3 month (unintentional). She had no contact with a tuberculosis patient. On examination, she has bilateral cervical lymph nodes, largest 3 cm X2 cm. There is also inguinal lymphadenopathy and the spleen is palpable 3 fingers below the costal margin. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.text: Fine needle aspiration of the lymph node
Excisional biopsy of the lymph node

questions.stem: A 63-year-old man has chronic lymphocytic leukemia started on chemotherapy. His initial lymphocyte count was 73,000. 2 days after chemotherapy, he presents with fatigue and dry mouth (see lab results). WBC 5.7 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Lymphocytes 60 20-40 % Potassium 5.5 3.5-5.1 mmol/L Phosphate, inorganic 1.48 0.82-1.51 mmol/L Creatinine 139 44-115 mol/L Uric acid 620 200-410 umol/L (Male) 140-360 mol/L (Female) Which of the following electrolyte abnormality is associated with the above condition?

A 75-year-old man comes to the clinic with hypertension and gradual loss of cognitive function. He has predominant executive function impairment (see report). MRI: Reveals diffuse periventricular white-matter hyperintensities Which of the following is most likely diagnosis?

A 77-year-old man with a 7-years history of Parkinson disease reports hallucinations, confusion and worsening motor function. On physical examination, he is kinetic and rigid with no tremor. He has prominent gait disorder and postural instability. Which of the following symptoms is most strongly associated with an increased risk for dementia?

options.text: Difficulty reading an article in a single sitting

questions.stem: A son of 78-year-old patient brought a medical report of his father cognitive function status stating that he has" mild cognitive impairment'. Which of the following is indicating mild cognitive impairment?

options.text: Impairment in at least 1 activity of daily living

questions.stem: #Anki 47- A 42-year-old woman presents with tiredness and lethargy. She has tingling in her hands and feet. Investigations confirm a megaloblastic anemia. She had a total gastrectomy 3 years ago. Which of the following vitamin deficiencies is most likely to cause these symptoms?

A 25-year-old man was brought to the Emergency Department with a penetrating chest injury 45 minutes ago. He was initially fine in the ambulance but then collapsed. Emergency response personal started resuscitation. On arrival, he had a weak thread pulse, raised JVP and bilateral equal breath sounds. Blood pressure 90/60 mmHg Heart rate 140 /min Respiratory rate 30 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Oxygen saturation 85 % Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A young man was brought to the Emergency Department after he was hit in the chest while playing football. On examination, he was dyspnoeic and drowsy with GCS 11/15. Tracheal shifting to the left and raised JVP were noted. He has barely audible breath sounds on the right side. Blood pressure 80/50 mmHg Heart rate 130 /min Respiratory rate 32 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Oxygen saturation 90 % Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A young man received 4 litres of blood in the Emergency Department following a road traffic accident. Which of the following is the most likely complication?

A young man comes to the Emergency Department after being involved in a road traffic accident. A Focused assessment with sonography for trauma was ordered. Which of the following is the most likely finding?

A 5-year-old child is brought to the Emergency Department after being stabbed in the right lower chest. His abdomen is distended. A focused abdominal sonogram for trauma is suggestive of free fluid in the abdomen. Blood pressure 100/80 mmHg Heart rate 110 /min Respiratory rate 20 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Oxygen saturation 90 % Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

Which of the following is the most likely cerebral perfusion pressure in mmHg?

Which of the following is the most likely type of shock?
Which of the following has the highest diagnostic value for inhalation injuries?

options.text: AP and Lateral view cervical spine x-ray

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate strategy to avoid air bag injury in children under the age of 12 years?

An 8-year-old boy presents to the Emergency Department after a fall on his left forearm. On examination, there was swelling and a deformity with a 1 cm wound on the volar aspect of his forearm (see image). Which of the following is the first step in management?

options.text: Closed reduction and below elbow cast
Closed reduction and above elbow cast
Discharge the patient with oral antibiotic

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man was hit by a car. He was brought to the Emergency Department within 1 hour, and cleared by the trauma team. He was found to have an isolated injury to his left leg. An examination revealed tenderness over the shin and abrasions with a small oozing wound. IV antibiotics and tetanus prophylaxis were started (see images). Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Discharge from emergency department with above knee cast
Urgent surgical debridement and intramedullary nailing
Closed reduction followed by external fixation
Discharge on oral antibiotic for 3 days

options.text: Loss of abduction of the eye

Which of the following is a hard sign for vascular injury?

An 18-year-old man presented to a tertiary care hospital after he was involved in a motor vehicle accident. Primary survey was conducted and he was stabilized. While getting ready to transfer him his pressure dropped down (see report). Blood pressure 60/40 mmHg CT scan: Thoracic aortic injury and a splenic laceration with free fluid in the abdomen. Which of the following is the most appropriate transfer?

options.text: A center that has a vascular surgeon

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man presented to the Emergency Department complaining of lower abdominal pain for 3 days. He gave a history of being hit by a piece of wood in the same site of pain 4 days back. Examination revealed lethargic patient in pain, which was aggravated by moving his leg. there was grayish turbid semipurulent secretions from a small break in the skin of right lower quadrant (see lab result). WBC 33.1 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in the management?

A 37-year-old man was involved in a fight and sustained a stab wound to the neck. On presentation, patient was conscious, alert. Examination showed a 2 cm wound anterior to the left ear and close to the angle of the mandible with blood ooze. which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 19-year-old woman brought to the Emergency Department after being stabbed to the right upper quadrant. On arrival, she was conscious and oriented. Examination showed only a penetrating wound to the anterior abdominal wall at anterior axillary line just below the right costal margin. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 25-year-old man brought to the Emergency Department after he was involved in motor vehicle crash, which was driving at a speed of 130 km/hour. Patient was wearing seat belt. On arrival to the Emergency Department, he was conscious, and alert (see report). Chest X-ray: Normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step? A. US abdomen
Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 56-year-old woman was exposed to chemical burns to her trunk. On arrival to the Emergency Department, she was conscious and alert. Examination showed a 6 cm x 11 cm wound at her back with burned clothe and powder of chemicals on her clothes and skin. Which of the following is most appropriate next step after removing her clothes?

A 32-year-old man was brought to the Emergency Department after he was involved in a road traffic accident. He was diagnosed with a massive intra-abdominal bleeding due to a severe splenic injury. He underwent exploratory laparotomy and splenectomy. Which of the following is most likely to be low in the early postoperative period?

A 24-year-old man had gunshot wound in the left side of his chest; chest tube was inserted with minimal hemothorax and no air leak. The bullet entry lateral the nipple, exit point was below the left scapula. Suddenly patient becomes agitated and hypotensive. Examination revealed distended neck veins, good air entry both side of the chest with unclear heart sounds Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Needle thoracostomy in the left 2nd intercostal

A 53-year-old man presented to the hospital with fever and pain in the right knee for 2 days. On physical examination, the right knee was swollen and red with a limited range of motion. A knee joint aspiration was performed. Then, the patient started empirically on Cloxacillin. On day 3 after admission, a further report was received (see reports). Bacteriology: Gram stains showed numerous white blood cells and gram positive cocci in clusters. Bacteriology (3 days later):Staphylococcus aureus that was resistant to cefoxitin. Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

An army soldier comes to Outpatient Clinic complaining of painful flat feet after several years of service, which included thousands kilometres of marching in the desert. The pain was acute in the medial aspect of his sole. Which of the following structures is the most likely strained?
As a part of physical examination to evaluate the lower limb function of a football player, the physician asked him to stand on his tiptoes. Which of the following nerves was the physician testing?

A 20-year-old man comes to the clinic complaining of a knee pain. History reveals he received a severe blow on the inferolateral side of the left knee joint while playing football. Radiographic examination revealed a fracture of the head and neck of the fibula. Which of the following nerves is the most likely to be damaged?

A 25-year-old man is brought to the Emergency Room after a severe road traffic accident. Examination shows he has an unstable left knee joint and it was possible to pull the tibia abnormally forwards on the femur. Which of the following ligaments is most likely injured?

A 35-year-old man is brought to the Emergency Room after a road traffic accident. X-ray shows a displaced fracture of the mid shaft of the humerus. Which of the following is the most likely clinical complication?

A 24-year-old man came to the hospital with pain, swelling and difficulty in moving the arm. Examination shows he has humeral fracture (see report). X-ray: The fracture was at the level of the surgical neck. Which of the following nerves was most likely injured?
A 52-year-old woman slipped and fell, she complained of being unable to extend her leg at the knee joint. Which of the following muscles is most likely paralyzed?

A 45-year-old man was brought in the Emergency Department after a motor vehicle accident with severe pain on his left arm. X-rays confirmed left humeral and ulnar fractures. After an open reduction and internal fixation, the patient was unable to extend his forearm, wrist and fingers. Which of the following is the most likely damaged?

options.text: Median nerve at the cubital fossa
Radial nerve above the spiral grove
Median nerve at the lateral epicondyle

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man presents to the hospital with an open fracture of his right leg, after a motor bike accident on a farm. Later he develops severe pain, necrosis and blue discoloration of the skin, and apparently there is gas in the deep tissue of the leg. Which of the following is the most likely causing agent?

A 58-year-old healthy patient has a six-month history of central lower back pain. The pain is present on awakening, and without treatment, resolves after about 30 minutes. Acetaminophen seemed to help it resolve sooner. Morning examination showed mild paraspinal muscle spasm with no neurological changes (see report). MRI Lumbar: Mild lumbar spinal stenosis. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 24-year-old was running and suddenly experienced severe left leg pain. The patient was limping because of the pain, which is relieved by passive stretching. Which of the following is the most commonly involved muscle?

A 23-year-old athlete presented with foot pain while standing and walking. On physical exam, there was significant tenderness on the midline plantar surface of the foot. The patient denied any history of trauma. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old patient with history of epilepsy, is brought to the Emergency Room with complaints of left shoulder pain. The shoulder contour is flat and the arm is fixed in adduction and internal rotation. Which of the following is the most likely type of shoulder dislocation?

A 2-year-old child who refuses to walk since the day before, presents to the clinic. The parent states that the child was playing and tripped over a toy. While falling, the right leg was caught in the toy and twisted. Since then, the child has wanted to be carried. The past medical history is normal and immunizations are current. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

options.text: Spiral fracture of the right tibia
Spiral fracture of the right femur
Soft tissue swelling of the right ankle
Chip fracture of the proximal right tibia

questions.stem: A 23-year-old patient presented to the Emergency Department with pain in his finger that was caused by a hyperextension injury. An acute pain in the right second finger developed instantly. On examination, the patient cannot flex the distal phalanx of the right second finger, and has tenderness and swelling over the volar aspect of the distal phalanx of that finger. The patient also complained of pain and tenderness at the palm. Which of the following is the most likely resulting injury?

options.text: Rupture of the flexor profundus tendon
Rupture of the flexor superficialis tendon
Extra-articular fracture of the distal phalanx
Intra-articular fracture of the middle phalanx

questions.stem: A 26-year-old professional football player is brought to the Emergency Room after being hit on the lateral side of the left knee. The knee is buckled, and the patient is in severe pain. On examination, there was a swelling over the medial aspect of the left knee. There was laxity when valgus stress test was performed on the knee. Both the Lachman test and McMurray test were negative. Which of the following is the most likely type of injury?

A 12-year-old overweight boy complains of severe left hip pain after minor trauma. He cannot bear his weight on the left leg. The boy denied any history of fever. Physical examination confirmed that the left lower leg was externally rotated and the range of motion of the left hip joint is restricted and painful. Laboratory results were normal (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 80-year-old woman presents with a history of bilateral leg pain and numbness, preventing her from walking more than 50 meters for over 2 years. Her symptoms are worse when going downhill. On the other hand, she can walk further if she bent forward on a walker or if she is going uphill. When she reaches the limit, her leg pain stops her from going any further. Physical examination showed a forward stooped gait. Spine and neurological examination were normal. Both pedal pulses are present. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old boy complained of pain in his right hip and was unable to walk, associated with high fever for the last five days. physical examination confirmed that the active and passive range of motion of the hip was painful and restricted. A 71-year old man with history of osteoarthritis and previous cervical laminectomy for degenerative cervical myelopathy presents with a 2-month history of worsening gait instability and urinary urgency. Which of the following is the most likely explains his symptoms?

A 66-year-old man is referred to Neurology Outpatients with arm pain, stiffness and imbalance. Following investigations, he is diagnosed with degenerative cervical myelopathy. He misses his next Outpatient Clinic due to admission with acute coronary syndrome. He attends his appointment 2 months later and mentions his ongoing neurological symptoms. Which of the following is the most important next step in his care?

options.text: Reassure the patient of his diagnosis

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

On examination, there is paraesthesia of the skin over the le\ wrist and anatomical snuffbox , and an inability to extend her metacarpophalangeal joint. She also demonstrates wrist drop. A 3-year-old boy fell on his outstretched hand while playing in the yard. On examination, there is tenderness and swelling of the forearm, which seemed to be abnormally curved (see image). Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Perform a CT scan of forearm
Reduce the fracture and cast the forearm

questions.stem: An 18-month-old child is brought to the Emergency Department with fever, irritability and refusal to move the left lower extremity. Physical examination confirms a swollen, erythematous knee with resistance to passive mobilisation. Which of the following would be the single most important test?

A 12-year-old boy is brought to the Primary Health Care Clinic with knee pain for the past 3 weeks. The pain increases when he runs, jumps and climbs stairs. He plays basketball and football at school and has no history of injury or trauma. Physical examination is normal except for mild edema over the tibial tuberosity. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
During physical examination of a child, the physician asks the patient to face the wall, bend forward and let the arms hang down unsupported. What does this test screen for?

A 47-year-old woman presented to the Emergency Department complaining of painful cord-like swelling in the calf of left leg for 48 hours. She gave history of varicose veins for 20 years. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment?

options.text: Check the femoral deformity for bleeding

He underwent laparoscopic surgery with a plan to perform a resection with a proximal colostomy. During the operation, his vital signs changed. Blood pressure 86/45 mmHg Heart rate 124 /min Temperature 36.8 °C Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

On examination, the mass measures 15 x 15 cm, is mobile and not attached to underlying muscle. Overlying skin is thinned out due to the mass effect (see report). Physical examination confirmed a right groin reducible swelling with positive cough impulse, reaching the neck of scrotum. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step management?

A 48-year-old woman presented with a 12-hour history of a painful swelling in the right groin. Physical examination confirmed an irreducible tender swelling in the groin area that is 3 x 4cm. Surgical exploration confirmed a strangulated hernia and the neck is lateral and inferior to the pubic tubercle. Which of the following is the most likely hernia?
A 68-year-old man has been advised to undergo surgical treatment for a left reducible inguinal hernia. He is otherwise healthy. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 27-year-old man presented to the Surgical Clinic complaining of right groin pain for few weeks, which is aggravated by exercising. Examination confirmed normal external genitalia and groin region. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 5-year-old child complains of a painful left testicular swelling. On examination, there is a firm swelling in his left hemi-scrotum, it is irreducible, with negative transillumination test. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 70-year-old women p7+1 with chronic constipation presented to Emergency Room with abdominal distension and vomiting. Examination revealed abdomen is distended, tympanic, with round tender non-reducible swelling in the right groin bellow and lateral to pubic tubercle (see report). X-ray abdomen: Distended small bowel with multiple fluid levels. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-month-old baby is brought to the clinic because of umbilical bulge that appears when child is crying. Examination revealed 1 cm reducible umbilical hernia. Which of the following is most appropriate treatment?

options.text: Delayed surgical repair at age of 6 months

questions.stem: A 23-year-old military man presented to the clinic with history of bilateral groin swelling. Examination revealed there was bilateral inguinal hernia. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 55-year-old man with Liver cirrhosis is admitted to the hospital with a massive upper gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding. In addition to volume restoration, which intravenous medication is recommended before upper GI endoscopy?

A 70-year-old alcoholic complains of a 6-month history of gradual progressive dysphagia and weight loss. On examination, he is cachectic and pale. His abdomen is soft and non-tender. Digital rectal examination confirms altered coloured stool in the rectum (see lab results). Blood pressure 110/70 mmH Heart rate 110 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 36.6 °C WBC 9.5 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Hb 90 130 - 170 g/L Urea 8 2.75-7.4 mmol/L Creatinine 120 44-115 umol/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 47-year-old man reported frequent vomiting over the past 24-hours due to food poisoning. He presented to the Emergency Department complaining of a 2-hour history of vomiting fresh blood. Physical examination confirmed mild epigastric tenderness. A nasogastric tube was inserted and was draining bloody stained fluids. which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old man presented with a 3-month history of early satiety and 11 kg weight loss. Physical examination was normal (see reports). Upper GIT endoscopy: Ulcerating mass in the antrum. Multiple biopsies were taken. Histopathology: Invasive adenocarcinoma. Which of the following is the most appropriate next investigation?

options.text: CT scan chest, abdomen and pelvis

questions.stem: A 37-year-old man presented to the Emergency Department with vomiting blood after attacks of excessive vomiting (see lab results). Blood pressure 112/63 mmH Heart rate 89 /min Respiratory rate 21 /min Oxygen saturation 96 % Test Result Normal Values Hb 135 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) WBC 7.8 4.5-10.5 x 109/L. Which of the following is the most appropriate management plan?

A 63-year-old woman presented to the Surgical Clinic complaining of upper abdominal pain and shortness of breath and occasional attacks of palpitation after meals, for several years. These symptoms relieved by vomiting. Which of the following is the most appropriate method of investigations?

A 40-year-old woman presented with heartburn at the epigastric and retrosternal areas, and symptoms of regurgitation. The patient has tried conservative measures, including proton pumps inhibitors with no improvement in symptoms (see report). Endoscopy: Erythema of the esophagus consistent with reflux esophagitis. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 55-year-old man complains of dark stool and weakness. He has peptic ulcer disease and endoscopy investigations have confirmed multiple ulcers in the antrum. He has been kept on medical therapy. On examination, his abdomen is so\ and non-tender. Repeat endoscopy confirms multiple ulcers in the antrum (see lab results). Hb 58 130-170 g/L НСТ 0.18 0.42-0.52 Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 55-year-old patient is diagnosed with a gastrointestinal stromal tumour of the stomach (4 × 3 cm), confined to the body of the stomach, no surrounding infiltration, no distant metastases or lymphadenopathy. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 35-year-old man with gastroesophageal reflux disease presents to discuss his family history of esophageal and gastric carcinoma. Which of the following is the main risk factor for esophageal carcinoma?

A 52-year-old woman presented to Emergency Room with abdominal distension and vomiting, she has history of ventral hemia repair with mesh 12 years back. Examination revealed distended abdomen, no tenderness, and no signs of hernia recurrence (see reports). X-ray abdomen: Dilated bowels with air/fluid levels. CT scan: Contrast cut off at terminal ilium with soft tissue mass and target sign. Which of the following is likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is most appropriate next step?

options.text: Water ingestion to dilute the bleach
Insert NGT and drain gastric content

questions.stem: A 20-year-old primi-gravida complains of severe perianal pain post defecation along with fresh bleeding per rectum for the last 4 days. She describes the pain to be sharp and persists long after passage of stool. She denies any history of associated swelling or fever. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 36-year-old man presents with a 2-day history of constipation. On examination, he looks nervous and severe pain was experienced during parting of the perianal region. Linear cracks were noted at both at 6 and 12 O'clock positions. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

options.text: Thrombosed piles Answer: this question was not solved but I believe the answer is D

questions.stem: A 65-year-old diabetic presents with a 4-day history of severe perianal pain with high grade fever. On examination, there is no external swelling. On digital rectal examination, there is posterior bogginess and tenderness with slight purulent discharge coming from the anal canal. Temperature 38 °C Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30 year-old patient complains of a 2-year history of perianal itching and discomfort. On perianal examination, there are cauliflower-like multiple lesions clustered together. They are pink to grey in colour and tender to touch. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old complains of a 6-month change in bowel habits. On examination, he is pale, thin and emaciated. His abdomen is slightly distended. On digital rectal examination, there is a lesion 2 cm from the anal verge. On proctoscopy, the lesion appears to be cauliflower like mass, which is friable to touch. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old presents with a 2-week history of severe perianal pain and an inability to pass stool for the last 2 days. History confirmed a haemorrhoidectomy 12-months ago. On examination, he is uneasy and in distress. On rectal examination, finger could not be passed beyond the anal verge due to severe pain. Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 120 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old patient complains of perianal swelling, fresh bleeding per-rectum and we over the last 3 months. On examination, there is a mass 1 cm from the anal verge. She has obstructive symptoms (see report). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 96 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Biopsy: Adenocarcinoma. MRI abdomen: Localized lesion with cranio-caudal extension of 3 cm with associated lymphadenopathy CT scan chest: No evidence of metastasis. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 55-year-old man presents to the Emergency Department with severe abdominal pain and absolute constipation for 2 days associated with nausea and vomiting. He has a significant past history of constipation requiring use of laxatives. On examination, his abdomen is distended, tense, tender all over with a palpable mass in the left lumbar and hypochondrium (see image). Which of the following is the most likely site of volvulus?

A 25-year-old man presented to the Emergency Department with severe pain during and after defecation for 3 days associated with passage of a small amount of fresh blood after defecation. Physical examination confirmed an acute posterior anal fissure. Digital and proctoscopic examination were not performed due to the anal pain. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Botulinus toxin paralysis of anal sphincter

questions.stem: A 36-year-old woman complaining of per-rectal bleeding and prolapsed tissue masses through the anal verge. Anorectal examination confirmed grade IV haemorrhoids at 3, 7, and 11 clock positions. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 65-year-old man presented to the outpatient department complaining of alternating constipation and diarrhea for 4 months. Physical examination was normal (see reports) Rigid Sigmoidoscopy: Circumferential, ulcerating mass in the distal part of sigmoid colon. Multiple biopsies were taken. Histopathology: Adenocarcinoma. which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 73-year-old woman presents with new onset jaundice, generalized fatigability, weight loss and loss of appetite (see report). CT scan: Multiple lesions replacing approximately 70% of the liver parenchyma. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 25-year-old woman that is taking steroids for inflammatory bowel disease complains of abdominal pain and bilious vomiting. On examination, her abdomen is distended and tender in the right iliac fossa. She had a colonoscopy 2 weeks ago which was normal. Contrast barium study was ordered (see report). Blood pressure 110/70 mmH Heart rate 100 /min Barium study: Single stricture at terminal ileum, 1 cm from ileocecal valve. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 28-year-old man presented with a 4-day history of abdominal pain, associated with frequent bloody diarrhoea and vomiting . Physical examination confirmed he was dehydrated, had a distended abdomen, tenderness mainly over the lower abdomen with sluggish bowel sounds. He is known to have ulcerative colitis and is having medical treatment (see lab result and report). WBC 21.3 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Plain abdominal X-ray: Dilated transverse colon (15 cm) with loss of haustrations. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
A 66-year-old healthy man complains of rectal bleeding for 3 months. Anorectal examination confirmed 3rd degree haemorrhoids. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 68-year-old man was admitted through the Emergency Department with a 24-hour history of sudden severe lower abdominal pain, associated with progressive abdominal distension and constipation. On examination, the abdomen was hugely distended, tympanic with tenderness over the left iliac fossa. Digital rectal examination confirmed an empty rectum (see lab result and report). WBC 22 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Abdominal plain X-ray: Y-shaped shadow surrounded by a hugely distended colon arising from the pelvis. Which of the following is the most appropriate intervention?

A 28-year-old man presented with a 2-month history of frequent attacks of bloody stools. Physical examination was unremarkable. Proctoscopic examination showed multiple rectal polyps (see report). Colonoscopy: Colon and rectum were carpeted with polyps, multiple biopsies were taken. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 72-year-old diabetic presented to the Emergency Department with a 2-day history of lower abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting and bloody diarrhea. Physical examination confirmed tenderness in the left lower quadrant (see lab result and report). WBC 17.4 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Plain abdominal x-ray: Thickened descending and sigmoid colon with thumb printing appearance. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old man complains of a 2-month history of dysuria associated with the passage of cloudy urine with bubbling on micturition. He reports a 2-year history of recurrent left iliac fossa pain. Physical examination was unremarkable (see reports). Sigmoidoscopy: Narrowed sigmoid colon with intact mucosa. Cystoscopy: Erythematous area in the dome of the bladder. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

options.text: Squamous cell carcinoma of the bladder
Transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man presented to the Emergency Department with an 8-hour history of severe, sudden central abdominal pain associated with vomiting. He has a history of cardiomyopathy. He reports having passed loose stools once. On examination, the abdomen was soft with exaggerated bowel sounds (see lab results). WBC 26.7 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Amylase 155 24-151 IU/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is a recommended age in years for a low-risk adult man to start screening for colon cancer?

A 61-year-old man presented to Outpatient Clinic with general fatigue and mild on and off stool mixed with streaks of blood for 4 months. Examination revealed he was pale; abdomen is soft and lax, per rectal examination revealed 2nd degree piles (see lab result). Hb 8.3 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 q/L (Female) Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old man has chronic history of episodes of sharp anal pain with defecation, occasionally associated with small amount of fresh blood. Examination revealed posterior anal fissure with skin tag. All conservative treatments failed. Which of the following is most appropriate surgical management?

options.text: Curettage of the fissure and excision of skin tag

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man presented with history of bleeding per rectum. Anoscopy examination revealed swelling at 3,7 o'clock position. A treatment with injection of sclerosing agents is planned. Which of the following is most indicated for sclerosing therapy?

A 52-year-old man presented to the Emergency Department complaining of a 5-day history of right upper quadrant abdominal pain associated with fever, and yellowish discoloration of sclera. On examination, he was jaundiced with mild right upper quadrant abdominal tenderness (see lab results). Alkaline phosphatase: 389 (39-117 IU/L) Alanine aminotransferase: 85 (5-40 IU/L) Aspartate aminotransferase: 78 (12-40 IU/L) Direct bilirubin: 55 (1.5-6.5 mol/L) Total bilirubin: 66 (3.5-16.5 mol/L) Which of the following is the most appropriate next investigation?

A 53-year-old man with liver cirrhosis presents with several episodes of vomiting of blood and black tarry stool. Blood pressure: Supine 105/60 mmH Sitting 85/50 mmHg Heart rate: Supine 90 /min Sitting 110 /min Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.text: Intravenous infusion of H2 receptor antagonists

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man presents with low-grade fever, insomnia and progressive abdominal distention with vague abdominal pain. Physical examination reveals flapping tremor and moderate ascites. Ascitic fluid analysis showed high SAAG and neutrophil count of 350 cells/L. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 30 year-old patient presents to the Emergency Department with 8-hour history of severe upper abdominal pain that is not relieved by oral medications. History confirmed recurrent similar events over the last year that was relieved by anti-spasmodic and anti-inflammatory drugs. Examination revealed jaundiced patient, with soft abdomen and marked tenderness in the right hypochondriac region (see lab results and report). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 110 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 37.9 °C WBC 16 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Indirect bilirubin 5 3.2-12.1 mol/L Direct bilirubin 15 1.5-6.5 mol/L Total bilirubin 20 3.5-16.5 mol/L Alkaline phosphatase 400 39-117 IU/L Amylase 115 24-151 IU/L Ultrasound: Minimal CBD of 1.1 cm with dilatation of intrahepatic ducts. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old is admitted for an elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy. He is diabetic and hypertensive for 5 years. History confirms a recent admission in the Intensive Care Unit for anterior wall MI 6 weeks ago. What is the most appropriate management?

A 29-year-old woman presented to the Emergency Department with an 8-hour history of severe epigastric pain radiating to the back associated with vomiting. She underwent a sleeve gastrectomy 3 months ago for morbid obesity. Physical examination confirmed mild epigastric tenderness (see lab results and report). Test Result Normal Values: WBC 9.8 (4.5-10.5 x 109/L) Amylase 700 (24-151 IU/L) Ultrasound: Biliary sludge but no gallstone. Normal bile ducts. Which of the following is the most appropriate intervention?

A 58-year-old woman presented to the Emergency Department with a 2-day history of central abdominal pain, associated with abdominal distension, vomiting and constipation. She has no history of abdominal surgery. Physical examination confirmed a distended, tympanic abdomen, with exaggerated bowel sounds (see report). Erect abdominal X-ray: Multiple air-fluid levels with pneumobilia. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old woman presented with postprandial right upper quadrant abdominal pain, nausea, and emesis for few days that became persistent for the last 20 hours (see lab results and report). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg, Heart rate 87 /min Temperature 37.2 °C WBC 11 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Direct bilirubin 9.5 1.5-6.5 mol/L Total bilirubin 18.5 3.5-16.5 mol/L Alkaline phosphatase 463 39-117 IU/L Ultrasound: Cholelithiasis, gallbladder wall thickening, and a common bile duct of 12 mm. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 70-year-old man presents with abdominal pain. Examination revealed a pulsatile abdominal mass felt on deep palpation with mild tenderness just above the umbilicus (see lab results and report). Blood pressure 110/70 mmH Heart rate 76 /min Respiratory rate 14 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Oxygen saturation 99 % Test Result Normal Values RBC 6.0 4.7-6.1 x 1012/L (Male) 4.2-5.4 x 1012/L (Female) Hb 135 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) HCT 0.42 0.42-0.52 (Male) 0.37-0.48 (Female) Platelets count 155 150-400 x 109/L WBC 13.5 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Sodium 136 134-146 mmol/L Potassium 4 3.5-5.1 mmol/L Bicarbonate 25 21-28 mmol/L Upright chest x-ray: No air under diaphragm. Which the following is the most appropriate lab investigation to be ordered next?
Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in the management plan?

A 32-year-old diabetic woman has taken contraceptive pills for 12 years develops right upper quadrant pain (see report). CT scan: A 5-cm hypodense lesion in the right lobe of the liver. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 42-year-old woman underwent an uneventful laparoscopic cholecystectomy. 2 weeks later, she presents to the Emergency Department with vague abdominal pain (see lab results and report). Blood pressure 117/59 mmHg, Heart rate 83 /min Respiratory rate 19 /min Temperature 37.4 °C Oxygen saturation 95 % Test Result Normal Values Hb 103 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 q/L (Female) WBC 7.8 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Total bilirubin 3.7 3.5-16.5 mol/L CT scan: Large collection in the sub-hepatic area. Which of the following is most appropriate next step? A. Operative drainage

A 55-year-old woman complains of abdominal pain, distention and bilious vomiting. On examination she is pale, dehydrated, abdomen is so\, distended, with hyper dynamic gut sounds. She was diagnosed with gallstone disease 10 years ago (see report). Blood pressure 140/90 mmHg Heart rate 120 /min Temp 36.7 Hb 100 120-160 g/L Platelets count 125 150-400 × 109/L WBC 18.6 4.5-10.5 x 109/L CT scan: Air in the biliary system. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old woman complains of right upper quadrant pain and nausea. She is 20 weeks pregnant. On examination, her abdomen is soft and non-tender. Ultrasound: Cholelithiasis. Which of the following is most appropriate management?

A 28-year-old woman presented to the Emergency Department with 18-hour history of severe epigastric pain associated with vomiting. She is known to have multiple small gallstones. Physical examination confirmed upper abdominal tenderness (see lab results). WBC 13.4 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Alkaline phosphatase 289 39-117 IU/L Amylase 488 24-151 IU/L Direct bilirubin 19 1.5-6.5 mol/L Total bilirubin 34 3.5-16.5 mol/L Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?

A 33-year-old women presented with 1-day history of right upper quadrant abdominal pain associated with fever, nausea and vomiting. Physical examination confirmed marked tenderness in the right upper quadrant of the abdomen (see report). Ultrasound: Thick wall gallbladder, pericholecystic fluids and multiple gallstones. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 28-year-old woman was admitted through the Emergency Department with a 12-hour history of epigastric pain. Physical examination confirmed epigastric tenderness. Over the next 3 days during the hospitalization, the patient completely recovered clinically and biochemically (see lab results and report). Alkaline phosphatase 110 39-117 1U/L Amylase 250 24-151 IU/L Ultrasound: Multiple gallstones with mild extrahepatic biliary dilatation. Which of the following is the most appropriate intervention?

A 35-year-old woman presented to Emergency Room with vague upper abdominal pain, She underwent elective cholecystectomy for cholelithiasis 7 days ago. Examination revealed she was jaundiced with mild right upper quadrant tenderness (see lab results and report). Temperature 37.1 °C Test Result Normal Values WBC 9.3 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Alkaline phosphatase 169 39-117 IU/L Alanine aminotransferase 35 5-40 IU/L Amylase 102 24-151 IU/L Direct bilirubin 10 1.5-6.5 mol/L Total bilirubin 17 3.5-16.5 mol/L Ultrasound: Minimal fluids in gall-bladder fossa, CBD measure 9 mm Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old woman had abdominal ultrasound as part of screening for essential hypertension. She has no abdominal symptoms (see report). Ultrasound Abdomen: Gall bladder single polyp measures 0.6 cm, no stones, and normal bile ducts. Which is the following is the most appropriate management?

A 33-year-old women presents with history of right upper quadrant pain and yellow sclera. Examination reveals unwell patient with abdominal tenderness but no guarding (see lab results and report). Total bilirubin 30 3.5-16.5 mol/L WBC 15 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Alkaline phosphatase 280 39-117 IU/L Ultrasound of Abdomen: Multiple gallstone, no pericholecystic fluid, common bile duct is dilated and measures 1 cm. Which is the following is most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old man farmer presented with history of right side abdominal pain, vomiting and fever. Examination confirmed tenderness in right upper quadrant (see report). Temperature 37.6 °C CT abdomen: Calcified cyst 5X6 cm. Hydatid cvst (echinococcus) was confirmed. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 50-year-old woman presented with history of right upper guardant pain for the last 5 months associated with jaundice for 4 days. Examination revealed unwell patient, tender abdomen but no rebound. The patient started on I.V antibiotic (see report). Blood pressure 99/70 mmH, Heart rate 100 /min, Temperature 38 °C Ultrasound: Gall bladder stones, dilated common bile duct with stone. Which is the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 44-year-old woman is admitted electively for laparoscopic cholecystectomy for chronic cholelithiasis. She is obese, diabetic and sickle cell trait. Which of the following is most likely type of her gallstones?

A 38-year-old woman presented to the Emergency Department with epigastric pain for 6-days, radiating to the back, associated with frequent vomiting. She is known to have multiple small gallstones. Physical examination confirmed diffuse abdominal distention, epigastric tenderness with sluggish bowel sounds (see lab results and report). Alkaline phosphatase 115 (39-117 IU/L) Amylase 149 (24-151 IU/L) Direct bilirubin 5.6 (1.5-6.5 mol/L) Total bilirubin 15.8 (3.5-16.5 mol/L) Erect chest X-ray: Left pleural effusion. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial investigation?

A 38-year-old woman presented to Emergency Department complaining of epigastric pain and post-prandial vomiting. She was conservatively treated for acute pancreatitis 4 weeks ago. Physical examination confirmed tenderness and fullness in the epigastric region (see lab results and report). Amylase 413 (24-151 |U/L) WBC 15.9 (4.5-10.5 x 109/L) Abdominal ultrasound: Fluid collection surrounded by thick wall in the lesser sac 15 x 17 cm in size. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 42-year-old man presented to the Emergency Department complaining of a 12-hour history of severe epigastric pain. Physical examination confirmed upper abdominal tenderness (see lab results and report). WBC 14.5 (4.5-10.5 x 109/L) Amylase 254 (24-151 IU/L) Erect chest X-ray: Normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 67-year-old man presented with a 2-month history of yellowish discoloration of his sclera and skin with dark urine and pale stool. On examination, he was jaundiced with a palpable distended gallbladder (see report and lab results) Alkaline phosphatase 421 (39-117 IU/L) Direct bilirubin 122.3 (1.5-6.5 mol/L) Total bilirubin 134.5 (3.5-16.5 umol/L) Ultrasound: Dilated intra and extrahepatic bile ducts with hugely distended gallbladder. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old patient complains of recurrent episodes of upper abdominal pain for the past 2 weeks with fever. On examination, the patient is jaundiced, abdomen is soft with marked tenderness all over the abdomen (see lab results and report). Blood pressure 90/60 mmHg Heart rate 130 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 38 °C - Indirect bilirubin 5 3.2-12.1 mol/L Direct bilirubin 20 1.5-6.5 mol/L Total bilirubin 25 3.5-16.5 mol/L Alkaline phosphatase 450 39-117 1U/L Amylase 1400 24-151 IU/L Ultrasound: CBD of 1.4 cm with dilatation of intrahepatic ducts. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 44-year-old woman known to have gall bladder stones presented with biliary pain and jaundice. US abdomen confirmed CBD stones. She underwent ERCP for stone extraction. Few hours later, she developed sever epigastric pain, nausea and vomiting (see lab results). Hb 11 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) WBC 18 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Urea 11 2.75-7.4 mmol/L Creatinine 110 44-115 mol/L Total bilirubin 23 3.5-16.5 mol/L Lipase 3000 0-160 IU/L Which of the following management options has proven a survival benefit in such patient?

options.text: IV ringer lactate at rate of 250 ml/ours

questions.stem: A 67-year-old man a known case of HCV cirrhosis admitted to Emergency Room with massive hematemesis. Variceal bleeding is suspected. On examination, he is drowsy with tense ascites (see lab results). Blood pressure 110/70 mmH, Heart rate 86 /min Oxygen saturation 95 % Test Result Normal Values Hb 8 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) INR 1.3 0.8-1.2 Which of the following management options has a great benefit in reducing this patient mortality?

A 45-year-old woman presents to the Emergency Department with severe continuous mid- abdominal pain for 16 hours, associated with nausea and vomiting. She is known to have cholelithiasis. Physical examination confirmed epigastric tenderness (see lab results). WBC 13 (4.5-10.5 x 109/L) Amylase 650 (24-151 1U/L) Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old man with no significant medical history presented to Emergency Room with 1-day history of 4 episodes of hematochezia. He denies history of abdominal pain, constipation or weight loss. Blood pressure 90/50 mmH Heart rate 112 /min Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 46-year-old man presents with a 1-day history of abdominal pain, vomiting and hematemesis. History reveals he is a heavy alcohol drinker. He has previously been admitted with peptic ulceration and is receiving proton pump inhibitor therapy. On examination, he has tenderness over the epigastrium. Blood pressure 110/69 mmH Heart rate 112 /min Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 61-year-old man complains of indigestion that has been bothering him for the past 2 months. He has never had these symptoms before and he is eating and drinking well. He says he has lost weight over this period. His bowel habits are normal and he does not complain of any abdominal pains. Abdominal examination is normal. Blood tests including full blood count, renal function, and liver function as well as C-reactive protein are normal. Which of the following is the best management plan?

A 24-year-old man recovers from an attack of severe pancreatitis. He has mild epigastric discomfort, sensation of bloating, and loss of appetite. Examination reveals an epigastric fullness. The swelling increases in size over a 3-week period of observation (see report). Ultrasound: Confirmed to be a pseudocyst. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 37-year-old woman complains of abdominal fullness, epigastric discomfort and loss of appetite, She is recovering from an episode of acute pancreatitis 5 weeks ago. On examination, her abdomen is distended and there is vague fullness in epigastrium (see report). CT scan: Cyst about 24 x 18 cm in the lesser sac. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 60-year-old woman presents with a 12-hour history of severe pain in the epigastrium radiating to her back. It is associated with nausea and 2 episodes of vomiting. She has a history of cholelithiasis. Abdominal examination confirms generalised tenderness in abdomen. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old man presented to Emergency Room with history of vague upper abdominal pain and loss of appetite and weight. Examination revealed he was jaundiced; abdomen is soft and lax with palpable non-tender gallbladder. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
What is the best action to prevent this complication?

options.text: Avoid Codeine in this age group
Request frequent turning of the patient by family
Review the need for urinary catheter daily

questions.stem: A 20-year-old man presents to Emergency Department with renal colic. Which of the following is most diagnostic imaging?

A 75-year-old man in the Intensive Care Unit has developed a discharging sacral wound. Examination confirms necrotic skin and subcutaneous fat. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 45-year-old sustained a knife injury to his left wrist. Examination confirms a clean wound with division of the underlying tendons and median nerve. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
An 18-year-old man involved in burn accident, he has 2nd degree burn to his both lower limbs. Weight 70 kg Using Parkland formula, which of the following is most appropriate fluid resuscitation?

options.text: Lactate ringer's 5 L over 1st 6 hrs then 5 L over next 16 hrs
Lactate ringer's 2.5 L over 1st 6 hrs then 2.5 L over the next 16 hrs

questions.stem: A 50-year-old man post-kidney transplant, 2-year on steroid treatment underwent emergency exploratory laparotomy for intestinal obstruction. Which of the following will most likely promotes his wound healing?
Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate management in the Emergency Room?

A 28-year-old man is brought to Emergency Room with head injury after motor vehicle accident, he is making incomprehensive sounds, open his eyes to painful stimuli and flexes his limbs to painful stimuli, and his pupils react sluggishly to light. What is his Glasgow Coma Score?

A 31-year-old man was involved in road traffic accident; examination revealed he is fully oriented GCS15/15 before reaching the hospital paramedic reported interval unresponsiveness. The patient suddenly lost consciousness and dilatation of left pupil was noted (see report). X-ray of the skull: Left temporal fracture. Which is the following most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old man underwent an open appendectomy for a perforated appendix. He presented to the Emergency Department on the 6th postoperative day complaining of severe abdominal pain, distension and an inability to pass stool. On examination, there is feculent discharge from the wound site with signs of peritonitis (see lab results and report). Blood pressure 110/70 mmH Heart rate 120 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 38 °C Oxygen saturation 95 % ABG HCO3- 10 22-28 mmol/L ABG PCO2 4.8 4.7-6.0 kPa рН 7.25 7.36-7.45 ABG PO2 11 10.6-14.2 kPa Base access - 12 -2 to 2 mmol/L Ultrasound abdomen: Moderate ascites with echoes and septations. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 45-year-old diabetic man underwent a laparotomy for a diverticular perforation. On the 4th postoperative day, he developed a high-grade fever with chills and multiple spikes. On examination, his wound is healthy and his chest is clear to auscultation. On Digital rectal examination, there is bogginess anteriorly. Blood pressure 110/70 mmH Heart rate 120 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 38 °C Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A patient that underwent a cholecystectomy earlier has pyrexia with temperature spikes. On examination, the wound is healthy. His abdomen is so\ with mild tenderness in the right hypochondriac region. There is decreased air entry on the right side of the chest on auscultation. Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 120 /min Respiratory rate 20 /min Temperature 38.5 °C Ultrasound: collection of 10 x 15 cm in the gall bladder fossa. which of the following is the most appropriate management?
Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 45-year-old man presents to the Emergency Department complaining of severe abdominal pain, which was increasing in intensity with time. Patient underwent laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy 3 weeks back. Which of the following is the most appropriate diagnostic test?

A 40-old woman had laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass 5 days ago, presented with pain at the left shoulder, fever and rigors. Blood pressure 90/60 mmH Heart rate 120 /min Temperature 38.6 °C Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 26-year-old woman presented 17 days after laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy complaining of persistent vomiting and change of her mode according to the family. Examination revealed soft abdomen (see reports). Ultrasound abdomen:Normal. CT scan abdomen: Normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 65-year-old man presented to the Emergency Department with pain over the angle of his mouth for 24 hours. He underwent laparoscopic cholecystectomy 8 days prior to presentation. Blood pressure 110/72 mmHg Heart rate 104 /min Temperature 38.8 °C Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 25-year-old woman underwent appendectomy. 20 hours after the surgery, she was complaining of severe pain at the wound site with purulent discharges. Blood pressure 100/55 mmHg Heart rate 114 /min Temperature 38.8 °C Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 58-year-old man had laparotomy with sigmoidectomy and colostomy for perforated diverticulitis, presented to the clinic complaining of intermittent attacks of fever for 1 week, Examination revealed normal chest and abdominal examination with healthy looking wound. Blood pressure 116/68 mmH Heart rate 106 /min Temperature 38.2 °C Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 41-year-old man underwent laparoscopic cholecystectomy 5 days back started to experience severe abdominal pain and distension. Examination revealed a distended tender abdomen (see report). Blood pressure 100/55 mmHg Heart rate 103 /min Temperature 37.9 °C Ultrasound: Revealed the presence of ascites. Which of the following is most appropriate management?
A 40-year-old man had abdominal surgery 12 hours back; he noted drainage of 20 mL of fluid from her midline abdominal wound. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 40-year-old man who underwent a laparotomy and lysis for adhesive intestinal obstruction. On his regular follow up after discharge, there was discharges from the middle of the wound. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 55-year-old woman is admitted with obstructed ventral hernia for emergency exploration; patient is obese, diabetic and was discharged 7 days ago after surgical correction of retinal detachment. Which of following is most appropriate DVT prophylaxis?

A 72-year-old underwent a subtotal colectomy 5 days ago. His urine output over the past 8 hours has been 7 ml/hr. Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 90 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Which of the following is most appropriate to administer intravenously?

A 33-year-old man is known to have renal impairment, underwent appendectomy for acute appendicitis. On the first day after surgery, he was complaining of palpitation (see lab result and report). Potassium 6.5 3.5-5.1 mmol/L ECG: Tented T-waves. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial step in management?

options.text: Intravenous infusion of dextrose with insulin

questions.stem: A 38-year-old man has suffered from a severe hypovolemic shock due to traumatic splenic injury, and underwent splenectomy. He received 8 units of packed red blood cells during resuscitation and surgery. He was admitted to the intensive care unit. On the 3rd postoperative day, he was febrile (see report). Gram stain of blood: Positive for gram negative bacilli. Which of the following is the most likely source of the bacteraemia? A. Contaminated blood

A 41-year-old man underwent blood transfusion for postoperative bleeding. He developed pain at the site of the infusion with fever and chest tightness after a few minutes of starting the transfusion. Temperature 38 °C Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is the most common cause of fever in the first 24-hours after abdominal surgery?

A 45-year-old woman underwent open laparotomy for a ruptured appendicitis. 3 days postoperatively, she developed fever again with severe abdominal pain and vomiting. On examination, her abdomen was rigid with decreased bowel sounds. CT scan showed foreign body in right iliac fossa. Patient was taken urgently back to Operating Room and was found to have a missed infected sponge in her peritoneal cavity (see lab results). WBC 27 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Neutrophils 95 40-60% Creatinine 87 44-115 mol/L Which of the following is the most appropriate action by the surgeon?

options.text: Report the surgical assistant mistake to the administration
Do not inform the patient about the finding
Call his malpractice lawyer and report the incident
Inform the patient with apology about the mistake

questions.stem: A 68-year-old woman with history of heart failure, stroke and diabetes, admitted for hysterectomy. She was kept on normal saline due to poor oral intake. 2 days post-operation, the nurse noticed the patient pulse oxymetry was dropping with respiratory distress. On lung auscultation, there was bilateral basal crepitations Which of the following is the best action to prevent this complication?

options.text: Oxygen by nasal cannula at 2 L/min
Furosemide 40 mg iv on post-op day 1

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man had laparoscopic cholecystectomy, developed fever on 3rd postoperative day. He had no abdominal pain. Temperature 38.6 °C Which of the following is most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old woman otherwise healthy, underwent laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy. complicated by pulmonary embolism, she was started on heparin infusion, and after 5 days (see lab resuits). Platelets count 59 150-400 × 109/L APTT 53 30-40 sec INR 1.2 0.8-1.2 Prothrombin time 14 10-13 sec Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Increase IV heparin to reach PTT 60-70
Continue on same dose and repeat labs after 6 hours

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most important initial management?

options.text: Obtain detailed history from the family

questions.stem: A 40-year-old diabetic patient with good glycemic control is admitted electively for an inguinal hernia repair. What is the most accurate American society of Anaesthesiologist physical status class?

A 20-year-old woman with no past medical history, is admitted with a perforated appendix and is in septic shock. On arrival, she was intubated. She requires high inotropic support to maintain minimum recordable blood pressure. What is the most accurate American society of Anaesthesiologist physical status class?
Which of the following is most commonly cured by having a splenectomy?
Which of the following is most likely involved in neuro-hormonal stress response?
Which of the following is most important factor for small bowel adaptation?

A 30-year-old woman underwent an exploratory laparotomy for a perforated duodenal ulcer. Post-operatively she developed septic shock syndrome. Which of the following is the most common physiological response?
A 65-year-old patient is intubated in the Intensive Care Unit because of septic shock. Which of the following will best indicate adequate systemic perfusion?
A 55-year-old is scheduled to undergo laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Which of the following is the most appropriate prophylactic antibiotic regimen?

options.text: Single dose 1 hour before skin incision

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman was undergoing a laparoscopic cholecystectomy for gallstones. After creating pneumo-peritoneum and inserting the trocars, her heart rate was 40 beats/min. Which of the following is the most likely cause?

A 53-year-old man presented with sudden onset of severe right lower abdominal pain. On examination, there is a 3x3 cm right lower abdominal tender mass, which becomes more prominent with abdominal wall contraction. The patient has been on anticoagulants for atrial fibrillation for the past 4 years (see lab results and report). Blood pressure 130/80 mmH Heart rate 84 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 36.8 °C INR 1.5 0.8-1.2 Prothrombin time 11 10-13 sec CT scan: 3x3 cm enhancing mass at the right rectus muscle. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
A 23-year-old woman presented to the Surgical Clinic with a 1 X2 cm skin lesion in the left forearm since childhood. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 43-year-old man presented to the Surgical Clinic complaining of a dark colored pigmented skin lesion in the upper thigh for few months. Examination revealed a 3 X 4 cm dark colored skin lesion at the anterior aspect of right thigh with irregular borders and it was elevated above the skin. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 38-year-old woman presents with swelling of her left leg that is gradually increasing over the last 3 months, no history of travel or and surgeries over the last 6 months. Which of the following is the most important further history to obtain?

A 70-year-old woman is bed bound due to basal ganglia bleed, is having difficulty swallowing and has experienced significant weight loss. On examination, she is emaciated, and lethargic. Weak muscles of mastication and an absent gag reflex Which of the following is the most appropriate option to establish feeding?

A 24-month-old baby is brought in with a right sided red inflamed hemiscrotum. On exploration, the right testis is viable however; the cord is thick and oedematous. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-month-old baby is brought in with a red and inflamed left hemiscrotum. Examination confirms a firm, tender, irreducible lump in the scrotum extending to the groin. The left testis cannot be palpated. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 12-year-old presents with left sided lower abdominal pain. Examination confirms a slightly elevated, tender left testis with redness and edema of the scrotum. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 12-year-old presents with a 2-day history of right sided scrotal pain. Examination confirms right testis with vertical orientation. There is an area of tenderness around the superior pole and the scrotum is red and edematous. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-month-old is presented with redness of both hemi-scrotum. Examination confirms non- tender, redness and edema of the scrotum extending to both groins. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 12-year-old patient presents with a 4-hour history of right sided lower abdominal pain. Examination confirms a slightly elevated, tender right testis. The lie of the testis is horizontal with no redness or edema of the scrotum. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
A 7-day-old is presented for circumcision. Examination confirms urethral opening on the dorsal surface. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old uncircumcised boy has a history of foreskin ballooning during micturition. Examination confirms a ring of white scarred tissue and an inability to retract foreskin. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 3-day-old is presented for circumcision. Examination confirms chordee and hooded foreskin. Urethral opening is at mid-penile level. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
Which of the following is a contraindication for liver transplantation?

options.text: End stage liver disease with ascites
End stage liver disease with encephalopathy

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate management of an asymptomatic umbilical hernia in a 4-year-old?

options.text: Surgical correction D.Elastic support to the mid-abdomen

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most common intra-abdominal tumour in children?
A 3-year-old child is brought to the Emergency Room after swallowing a battery that is now lodged in the oesophagus. Which of the following is the most appropriate intervention?

A 5-year-old boy presents to Emergency Room because the parents noticed that there is only one testis in the scrotum. Examination reveals that one testis is in the scrotum while the other one is felt in the inguinal canal. Which the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 38-year-old G3 P1011 woman presents for her initial antenatal visit at 6 weeks' gestation. She is known to have type 2 diabetes mellitus for 5 years that is managed by oral hypoglycemic agents. Which of the following is the best indicator of fetal outcome in her pregnancy?

options.text: Blood glucose value in the clinic

questions.stem: A couple from Al-Ahsa Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia presents for antenatal booking. A complete blood count and blood film is ordered. Accordingly, further assessment of the risk to the fetus and to the pregnancy from the disease that is typified by the blood smear (see image). What is a diagnostic test to be performed at preconception or early in prenatal care?
A 36-year-old woman came at 10 weeks of gestation for an ultrasound. Which of the following has the highest diagnostic value?

A 37-year-old primigravida was seen in the Antenatal Clinic for a follow-up. She is a known smoker for 3 years and has a history of subfertility. A positive family history of diabetes mellitus in a second degree relative. Which of the following is a significant risk factor in her history?
A 35-year-old woman came for an ultrasound scan to confirm gestational age of her pregnancy. Which of the following is most appropriate timing?

A 33-year-old pregnant woman G4 P2012 at 38 weeks' gestation presented with a complaint of dizziness, light-headedness and fainting sensation especially in bed for 2 weeks duration (see lab results). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg, Heart rate 100 /min, Respiratory rate 24/min, Temperature 36.6° C Hb 95 120-160 g/L WBC 9 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Platelet count 200 150-400 × 109/L Which of the following is the best management?
Which of the following would be the most appropriate management?

A 28-year-old woman G5 P3013 is seen in the Antenatal Clinic. Her previous pregnancies were term normal deliveries. Currently, she is 10 weeks' gestation confirmed by a pregnancy test and ultrasound examination. Which of the following is the most important purpose of the first antenatal visit?

A 45-year-old woman who has had last normal pregnancies 15 years ago presents with amenorrhea for 7 months duration. Pregnancy test is negative. She expresses her desire to become pregnant again. Which of the following is most appropriate investigation?
A 35-year-old woman G5 P2113 presents to antenatal booking appointment and her last menstrual period of May 17, 2019. What is estimated date of confinement using the Ngele rule?
A patient is seen at 8 weeks' gestation in an Antenatal Clinic with a diagnosis of cervical incompetence. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Insertion cervical suture the same week
Confirm the diagnosis by Hegar dilator
Begin beta mimetic drugs during menstruation

questions.stem: A 28-year-old primigravida 8 weeks gestation woman attend her first antenatal appointment. During the history assessment, she reports that she never had chickenpox. A serum blood is drawn and is negative for antibodies. Which of the following is the next best step in management?
Which of the following is the primary reason for administering the intravenous medication?
Which of the following is the most appropriate therapy?
What is the most effective drug to control her seizures?

A 23-year-old primigravida presents at 38 weeks of gestation in active labor. She complains of headache. Her laboratory studies show normal complete blood count, normal liver function tests and elevated protein/creatinine ratio. blood pressure 150/100 mmHg Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old primigravida woman presented to the clinic at 37 weeks' gestation for a routine antenatal care. She reports feeling ill and has a frontal headache. A urine dipstick analysis is performed and shows proteinuria 2+. She is admitted to the hospital High Risk Unit and started on an intravenous infusion of magnesium sulfate. Blood pressure 152/102 mmHg, Heart rate 72 /min, Respiratory rate 16 /min, Temperature 37.2° C oral. Which of the following is the primary reason for administering the intravenous medication?

A 34-year-old gravida 2 para 1 woman 10 weeks gestation known to have a hypertension taking labetalol 100 milligrams twice per day. In her first pregnancy had no complications and resulted in a healthy infant. During this pregnancy which of the following risks is increased?

A 35-year-old nulliparous woman presents to the Maternal Health Clinic at 24 weeks' gestation. The significant medical history includes insulin-dependent diabetes class F with nephritis. Additionally, she has chronic hypertension which is controlled with medication. The pregnancy has been uncomplicated so far. The uterine funds measured 25 cm above the symphysis and fetal heart tones show a baseline of 160 beats per minute. Which of the following complications is most likely to occur?

A 27-year-old primigravida presented at 36-weeks of gestation with headache, blurred vision (see lab result). Blood pressure 160/110 mmHg Heart rate 76 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 36.8 °C Test Result Normal Values Protein ++ absent Which of the following is the most appropriate medication for acute treatment of hypertension? A. Clonidine
