A 39-year-old G6 P5005 Is seen in the Antenatal Clinic for routine check-up at 22 weeks of gestation. Her blood pressure found to be 140/90 mmH and no proteinuria. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 39-year-old primigravida attended her routine prenatal visit at 39 weeks' gestation. She denied any headache, visual changes, nausea, vomiting or abdominal pain. Urinalysis was negative for protein (see lab results). Vital signs at this visit: Blood pressure 160/90 mmH, Heart rate 84 /min Vitals signs at all other visits: Blood pressure 120/70 mmHg, Heart rate 68 /min Test Result Normal Values НСТ 0.34 0.37-0.48 Platelets count 165 150-400 x 109/L Alanine aminotransferase 12 5-40 IU/L Aspartate aminotransferase 22 12-40 IU/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 36-year-old woman presents with complain of headache and nausea for 3 weeks. History revealed that she is a G3 P2002 and LMP was 15 weeks back. Blood pressure 180/120 mmH Heart rate 76 /min Weight 51 kg Height 160 cm Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old woman G2 P0010 presents at 32 weeks gestation for a routine antenatal appointment. She reports mild headache, but no right upper quadrant pain or visual disturbance. Physical examination is otherwise unremarkable (see lab result). Blood pressure 150/100 mmHg Urine dipstick Test Result Normal Value Protein +3 absent Which of the following is the best next step of management?

A 39-year-old woman primigravida presents at 39 weeks gestation for a routine visit. Physical examination is unremarkable. Cervix is 2 cm dilated and 90% effaced, with the fetal vertex at 0 station. Urine dipstick is done (see image). Blood pressure 140/90 mmHg Which of the following is the most appropriate management option?

A 38-year-old woman G3 P2002 at 34 weeks gestation is admitted to labor and delivery complaining of headache, epigastric pain and blurred vision. Non-stress test is reassuring. Blood pressure 170/120 mmg Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Inform anesthesia and deliver the patient immediately.
Stabilize general condition, administer magnesium sulfate and deliver the patient.
Administer magnesium sulfate, stabilize general condition, and wait till 37 weeks' gestation.
Stabilize general condition, administer corticosteroids, and deliver the patient.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman G2 P1001 at 32 weeks' gestation is admitted to labor and delivery complaining of lower abdominal and back pain. She has a significant previous history of severe preeclampsia (see lab results). Blood pressure 140/90 mmg Platelets count 80 150-400 x 109/L Uric Acid 460 140-360 mol/L Which of the following findings would indicate severe preeclampsia?

A 24-year-old primigravida is found during antenatal care at 22 weeks gestation to have a blood pressure of 140/95 mmg in 2 different measurements documented 4 hours apart. Her urine test for protein was negative and she was asymptomatic. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
After how many weeks of gestation, it is recommended to screen for gestational diabetes mellitus in asymptomatic pregnant women?
Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?

A 25-year-old presents at 29 weeks of gestation with backache, fever and rigors (see lab results). Blood pressure 100/55 mmH Temperature 39.7 °C Protein ++ absent Leukocytes 8 0-3 per high power field Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate action?

options.text: Arrange for ultrasound of renal tract
Give dexamethasone for fetal lung maturity

questions.stem: A previously healthy 20-year-old primigravida presented at 37 weeks gestation feeling unwell and tired. Her chest X-ray showed an enlarged heart. During the process of admission, she developed shortness of breath and died despite intensive measures had been anticipated. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old Rh-negative primigravida presents at 28 weeks of gestation for a follow-up visit. She is not sensitized to D antigen. Her husband is a Rh-positive. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 24-year-old multiparous woman is in the second stage of labour. She has a history of asthma and she uses an albuterol inhaler as needed. She has a prior herpes simplex virus infection and reports outbreaks about once per year. As a child, she contracted rheumatic fever and takes prophylactic antibiotics when needed for mitral valve stenosis. Which significant medical history indicates beneficial use of forceps?

A nulliparous woman is admitted to the hospital at 42 weeks' gestation for induction of labour with cervical prostaglandin gel. On admission, a pelvic examination shows the cervix is closed, thick and posterior facing. A non-stress test shows the fetal heart rate is 130-140 beats per minute with good variability. There are 3 accelerations and 2 fetal movements during the examination. 1 hour after applying the prostaglandin gel, the fetal heart tones are 80 beats per minute and the contractions last for two minutes. Which of the following intervention is the most important?

options.text: Administer oxygen at 10 L/min by facemask
Prepare for an urgent caesarean section

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman who is 10-week pregnant and known case of gallstone presents to the Surgical Clinic complaining of recurrent attacks of biliary colic for the last 5 weeks. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 23-year-old woman involved in a motor vehicle accident, after completing her primary and secondary survey and getting ready to transfer her to definitive care. Her pregnancy test was positive. Which of the following will most indicates Rh immunoglobulin?

options.text: Rh positive, and has a wrist fracture
Rh negative, and has a wrist fracture

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman G3 P2002 at 34 weeks' gestation is admitted to labor and delivery complaining of headache, epigastric pain and blurred vision. Non-stress test is reassuring. Blood pressure 170/120 mmHg Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Inform anesthesia and deliver the patient immediately
Stabilize general condition, administer magnesium sulfate and deliver the patient
Administer magnesium sulfate, stabilize general condition and wait till 37 weeks' gestation
Stabilize general condition, administer corticosteroids and deliver the patient

questions.stem: A 29-year-old primigravida presented in labor and progressed well and had a mediolateral episiotomy. Which of the following is a theoretical benefit to performing a mediolateral episiotomy compared to a midline episiotomy?

options.text: Decreased risk of fourth degree laceration

questions.stem: A 20-year-old primigravida at 39 weeks presents in labor and she progresses well. During the delivery, it is necessary to cut an episiotomy. However, the tear extends through the rectal mucosa. What is the classification of this type of perineal tear?
which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management? A. Steroids

A 34-year-old woman presented at 33-weeks of gestation with fever, rigors and loin pain. She gave a history of urinary tract infection twice during this pregnancy. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 28-year-old woman presented to Preconception Clinic with a known diagnosis of epilepsy 6 years ago, poorly controlled and frequent epileptic attacks. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
A 29-year-old woman was seen in the clinic with a history of recurrent pregnancy loss between 9-12 weeks of gestation. Which of the following is the most likely cause of her condition?

A 37-years-old P4 with a history of 3 previous caesarean sections is undergoing an elective caesarean section at 37 weeks of gestation. The placenta was found to be attached deeply into the uterine wall. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old woman G5 P4004 presented to with amenorthes, tredness, nausea and voming during the morning hours for 3 months. Human chorionic gonadotropin test was positive. A physical examination showed no swelling in the lower extremities. The thyrold was enlarged on palpation. The tongue, conjunctiva and nail beds appeared pale. The uterine fundus was palpable 3 cm above the pubic symphysis. A peripheral blood smear showed microcytic red blood cells and hypersegmented neutrophils (see lab results). Blood pressure 100/60 mmHg Heart rate 120 /min Respiratory rate 26 /min Temperature 37.0* C oral Hb 85 120-160 g/. НСТ 0.32 0.37-0.48 МСНС 332 320-360 g/1 MCV 100 80-95 f1 Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone 0.44 0.4 - 5.0 pU/L Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment? A Intravenous rehydration

A 20-year-old pregnant woman presented with loss of fetal movements, followed by decreased urinary output and difficulty breathing (see lab results and report). Hb 100 120-160 g/L DLCO 70 75-140% Platelets count 75 150-400 x 109/L Creatinine 105 44-115 mol/L Prothrombin time 24 10-13 sec APTT 60 30-40 sec Fibrinogen 1.6 2-4 g/L Chest X-ray: Diffuse ground glass opacities. Which of the following is the most appropriate diagnosis?

A 22-year-old woman G2 P1001 at 37 weeks gestation presents after fainting and has severe abdominal pain. She is cold and diaphoretic. Fundal height is 39 cm; the cervical os is closed and there is no vaginal bleeding. Blood pressure 90/56 mmg Heart rate 130 /min Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old woman 23-week pregnant primigravida presents with a complaint of irregular brownish patches of varying sizes on face and neck (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old woman G3 P2002 presented at 38 weeks' gestation to Antenatal Clinic. She has had a history of 2 previous normal deliveries of 3 Kg babies. Current pregnancy, fetus found to be breech in presentation. The patient was counselled and consented for external cephalic version. On the scheduled day, an estimated fetal weight is 2.6 Kg by ultrasound, flexed fetal head, and uterus is bicornuate with average liquor measured. Which of the above findings is contraindicated external cephalic version?

A primigravida woman at 32 weeks' gestation brought to the Emergency Room with vaginal bleeding and abdominal pain. On examination: Fundal height equals to 30 weeks and abdomen is tense. Cardiotocography revealed fetal tachycardia, reduced variability and late decelerations. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 38-year-old woman came for routine follow up 2-months after delivery. She has no symptoms and her baby is well and lactating normally. Upon reviewing her labs, a positive urine culture: >100,000 fu/ml E.coli was noticed which was sensitive to trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole, ciprofloxacin,and nitrofurantoin. Which of the following is the best treatment option?

A 38-year-old woman, 28-weeks pregnant came for routine follow up. She has no symptoms and her pregnancy is all well. Upon reviewing her labs, a positive urine culture: > 100,000 fu/mi E.coli was found which was sensitive to ciprofloxacin, nitrofurantoin, trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole and ceftriaxone. Which of the following is the best treatment option?
A 24-year-old woman is 10-weeks pregnant. She has dysuria and is diagnosed with a urinary tract infection. Which of the following antibiotics is contraindicated?

A 28-year-old woman who is 38 weeks pregnant presents with dysuria and urinary frequency. A urine dipstick is positive for nitrites and leucocytes. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 32-year-old woman 30-week pregnant G1+0+0, presented to the clinic with pruritus and jaundice. There is no fever, abdominal pain, or vomiting. She is not on any medications and has no chronic medical illness (see lab results). Test Result / Normal Values Hb 11 / 130-170 g/L. (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Platelets count 160 / 150-400 x 109/L WBC 7 / 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Alkaline phosphatase 700 / 39-117 IU/L Alanine aminotransferase 79 / 5-40 IU/L Aspartate aminotransferase 100 / 12-40 IU/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A multiparous woman presents to the Maternal Health Clinic at 37 weeks' gestation with regular contractions occurring every 2 minutes lasting for 45-60 seconds with moderate intensity. Last pregnancy ended up with low transverse incision caesarean section. She is now pregnant with twins. Twin A is breech and twin B is cephalic. There has been small amount of clear fluid leaking from the vagina for the past hour. A nitrazine paper test turns blue-green in color. Pelvic examination shows a cervical dilation of 4 cm and 80% effacement. The obstetrician informs her that a cesarean section is necessary. Which of the following is the most likely reason for a cesarean section?

A 27-year-old primigravida had a glucose tolerance test (see lab results) During a difficult forceps delivery, an obstetrician misapplied the blade of the forceps at the child's left stylo-mastoid foramen where the forceps crushed its contents. What would be the baby's residual defect?

options.text: Inability to close the left eyelid
Reduced blood supply to the left ear
Loss of sensation from the left side of the face
Loss of taste from anterior 2/3rd of the tongue

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate therapy? ™
Which of the following is the most appropriate in management?

A 30-year-old woman G2 P2002 at 32 weeks' gestation presents to Emergency Department complaining of lower abdominal and back pain, which has increased in frequency and intensity over the last few hours. Abdominal examination shows fundal height equals to 32 cm, longitudinal lie fetus and cephalic presentation. Fetal heart was positive and cardiotocography is reactive with 2-3 uterine contractions per 10 minutes. Vaginal examination shows 1 cm dilated cervix, 70% effacement, -3 station and cephalic. Which of the following is the most appropriate step in management?

options.text: Inform neonatologist, administer corticosteroids and strict bed rest.
Inform neonatologist, administer corticosteroids and hydrate the patient.
Inform neonatologist, administer tocolylics and start intravenous antibiotics.
Inform neonatologist, administer intravenous antibiotics and strict bed rest.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman G2 P2002 at 32 weeks' gestation presents to Emergency Department complaining of lower abdominal and back pain which has increased in frequency and intensity over the last few hours. Abdominal examination shows fundal height equals to 32 cm, longitudinal lie fetus and cephalic presentation. Fetal heart was positive and cardiotocography is reactive with 2-3 uterine contractions/10 minutes. Vaginal examination shows 1 cm dilated cervix, 70% effacement, -3 station and cephalic. Which of the following is the next step to confirm the diagnosis?

options.text: Repeat vaginal assessment in two hours- (time?)
Cervical length assessment by ultrasound scanning

questions.stem: A 26-year-old multiparous woman in labor is requesting pain relief. While in the lithotomy position, the obstetrician performs a pudendal nerve block, and injects a local anesthetic into the sacrotuberous ligament close to the ischial spine. Which of the following structures will remain fully sensitive despite this pudendal nerve block?
Which of the following is the next step in management?

A 30-year-old woman presents to the Women's Health Clinic after a spontaneous rupture of membranes occurred at home 1 hour before. Patient medical records indicate a positive history of recurrent vaginal herpes simplex. Which of the following is the next best step in management?

A 30-year-old G3 P1010 woman presented at 24 weeks of gestation with preterm labor. She gave a history of preterm delivery at 34 weeks in her first pregnancy. Which of the following is the best method to evaluate her risk of preterm labor?

A 25-year-old nulliparous woman at 37 weeks' gestation presents to the hospital with regular contractions and spontaneous rupture of membranes. A pelvic examination shows cervical dilation of 6 cm and 90% effacement. Fetal heart rate 130-140 bpm with good variability. Ultrasound examination shows the fetus in a breech position and the patient is admitted for a caesarean section. When would be the optimal time to administer intravenous antibiotics?

options.text: Upon closure of the skin wound

questions.stem: A 33-year-old presented with preterm rupture of membranes at 34 weeks of gestation. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 38-year-old primigravida presents at 38-weeks of gestation with history of spontaneous rupture of membranes 24-hours ago. She has no labour pains. On abdominal examination, the uterus is soft and the fetus is in cephalic presentation. Cardiotocography shows normal fetal heart rate. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
A 29-year-old woman G7 P5015 Is admitted at 30 weeks' gestation in labor room with leaking liquor for observation. Which of the following most likely confirm the diagnosis?

A 20 year-old woman primigravida at 29 weeks' gestation presents with continuous vaginal bleeding and back pain. She denies sexual intercourse within the last 48 hours or trauma to the abdomen. Vaginal Examination reveals about 100 mL of blood in the vaginal vault and cervix is closed (see image and report). Blood pressure 110/60 mmH Heart rate 90 /min Respiratory rate 16 /min Temperature 36.0 °C Pelvic Ultrasound: Cephalic fetal presentation, amniotic fluid index of 10, and anterior-fundal placenta Which of the following is the most appropriate medication?

A 25-year-old woman primigravida at 31+5 weeks' gestation presents with abdominal cramping and lower back pain. She denies leaking of fluid from the vagina. Speculum examination shows no pooling liquor and nitrazine paper stays yellow. Cervical cultures are taken. Her cervix changes from closed and 50% effaced to 2 to 3 cm and 80% effaced. She is placed on fetal monitoring (see image). Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management? A. Terbutaline
Which of the following is the best next step in management?
Which of the following is the next best step in management?

A 22-year-old woman attends the Women's Health Clinic for a postnatal examination. She delivered a full-term baby boy 6 weeks earlier and the infant is exclusively breastfeeding and shows a good latch and weight gain. She would like to have more children, but not within the next 2 years. She does not smoke cigaretes and not at risk for heart disease. She inquired about birth control methods. Which of the following methods is most appropriate?

A 30-year-old para 1 woman presents to the Maternal Health Clinic at 20 days postpartum. She has delivered a full-term girl vaginally by forceps-assisted delivery. The weight at birth is 3.54 kg. She presents with a yellow-white colored vaginal discharge. The discharge is odorless and there is no itching or discomfort. An examination shows a pink cervix and absence of uterine tenderness. A microscopic analysis of the vaginal fluid is positive for leukocytes and epithelial cells. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 25-year-old woman complained of crampy, lower abdominal pain that occurs during the first day of her menses and usually improves by the third day. Her period is regular and all clinical assessment and pelvic ultrasound within normal. Which of the following most likely explains her clinical presentation?

A 19-year-old girl complained of recurrent painful menstruation that starts on day one of her menses and subsides between day 3 to 4. The pain is severe enough to affect her daily activities and school attendance. All investigations were negative. She was started on non-steroid anti-inflammatory drugs, her pain severity became less and she was able to resume normal function during menses. The patient is still not satisfied and insisting to receive a stronger pain killer. Which of the following is an appropriate management?

A 47-year-old woman, a poorly controlled diabetic, complains of polymenorrhagia every couple of weeks. Body mass index 37 kg/m2 Which of the following is the most appropriate investigation to establish the diagnosis?

options.text: Magnetic resonance imaging of the pelvis

questions.stem: A 59-year-old woman attends the clinic complaining of abnormal uterine bleeding for the last 2 months and concerned about her condition. She had the last menstrual cycle 12 years ago. On examination, the vagina is found to be pale with dry, smooth and shiny epithelium losing most of its rugation. Which of the following is the most probable cause of the condition?

A 59-year-old woman attends the clinic complaining of abnormal uterine bleeding for the last 2 months. She had the last menstrual cycle 12 years ago. On examination, vagina is noted to be pale, smooth and shiny dry epithelium along with loss of vaginal rugae (see report), Ultrasound Scan: The endometrial lining is 15 mm thick, the uterus is average in size with no abnormality in shape. The ovaries are normal and no adnexal masses or free fluid detected. Which of the following is the most appropriate procedure at this stage?

A 24-year-old woman presents to the clinic complaining of failure to conceive for more than 2 years of regular trials. The patient has a history of irregular periods occurring once every 6 to 7 weeks and is usually scanty (see report). Body mass index 35 kg/m2. Transvaginal ultrasound: Revealed the presence of multiple small cysts; each is 3-5mm, lining the ovarian periphery, representing pearl necklace appearance. Which of the following is the most likely factor contributing to her infertility?

A 59-year-old woman attends the clinic complaining of abnormal uterine bleeding for the last 2 months and concerned about her condition, she had the last menstrual cycle 12 years ago. An ultrasound scan was taken and endometrial polyp is suspected (see report). Ultrasound Scan: 19 mm endometrial lining. Which of the following should be offered to the patient at this stage?
A 59-year-old woman with a complaint of abnormal uterine bleeding for the last 2 months undergoes a procedure (see image). What is the name of this procedure?
A 59-year-old woman undergoes a hysteroscopy secondary to her complaint of abnormal uterine bleeding for the last couple of months (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-woman old is complaining of abnormal genital bleeding. She describes the amount of bleeding has been scanty, spotting and just staining the pad. Which of the following would be the most likely source of bleeding?

A 65-year-old post-menopausal woman complains of on and off vaginal bleeding that started 2 months ago. The amount of bleeding is mild to moderate of fresh blood. The woman is diabetic, hypertensive and obese. She has used hormone replacement therapy to control post-menopausal symptoms. Body mass index 37 kg/m2 Which of the following investigations is essential to establish the diagnosis?

A 45-year-old woman presents to the Gynecological Clinic with a history of genital warts that were treated by electrocautery 2 years back. The woman complained of recurrent occurrences of scanty fresh bleeding after intercourse. Which of the following is the likely source of her bleeding?
A 13-year-old girl presented with her mother with primary dysmenorrhea since her menarche a year ago. Which of the following is the best management?

A 15-year-old unmarried girl presents with a history of pain during menstruation. Her menarche was at age of 13 and menses are regular. Physical and pelvic examinations are normal for her age. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 19-year-old woman presented with crampy, lower abdominal pain beginning with the onset of menses every month, and lasting for 2 to 3 days. There was no pain between menses, but reported radiation of pain to the lower back and upper thighs, along with nausea, fatigue, and headache which has been present for several years and progressively getting worse. Physical examination normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 48-year-old woman patient suffers from several episodes of vaginal discharge and itching around the genital area. The discharge is white and curd-like. The patient's spouse does not have any related condition. Microscopy of the discharge revealed budding yeast and pseudohyphae. The patient's symptoms might be associated with which of the following conditions?

A 21-year-old woman patient complained of severe vulvovaginal itching and discharge. There are no urinary or other symptoms, and annual papanicolaou tests have all been normal. On inspection, Vulvar erythema with swelling. Speculum examination revealed a thick, white, curdy discharge adherent to the vaginal walls with no dour. A gross and microscopic examination of the vaginal discharge was done; the wet mount revealed no evidence of clue cells or trichomonads and the KOH prepped slide confirmed several pseudohyphae (see lab results). pH 4.0 3.8-4.5 Whiff test negative negative Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 23-year-old woman presented with a yellowish green malodorous vaginal discharge. Speculum exam showed the cervix was slightly red and inflamed. A probe for chlamydia was collected and wet prep confirmed Trichomonas vaginalis Which of the following is the first step in management?

A 28-year-old woman presented with a history of a copious white vaginal discharge associated with intense vulvar irritation and itching for four days. Microscopic examination revealed evidence of pseudohyphae. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 24-year-old woman came to the clinic complaining of yellowish offensive vaginal discharge and itching for 2 weeks. She has no other significant medical history. Vaginal swab done which showed motile flagellated organisms on wet film microscopy. Which of the following is the best treatment option?

A 24-year-old married woman came to the clinic complaining of yellowish offensive vaginal discharge and itching for 2 weeks. She has no other significant medical history. Vaginal swab done which showed motile flagellated organisms on wet film microscopy. Appropriate treatment was initiated. Which of the following is the best management option for her husband?

A 34-year-old woman presented with profuse milky vaginal discharge. Office diagnosis demonstrates fishy odor (positive Whiff test). A wet-mount preparation of the discharge (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old woman is complaining of a newly developed red and painful swelling on the vulva. On examination, the appearance of a solitary lesion is noticed, located at the 5 o'clock position on the vestibule. It is red, tender, fluid-filled and appears to be infected. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old woman comes to the clinic with anogenital lesions that appear as sharply marginalized. They are smooth, flat-topped, 1 to 2 cm in diameter, moist papules and small plaques. The patient admits of having multiple sexual partners and of use of illicit drugs (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old woman presents with a smelly vaginal discharge associated with intense itching. Her husband has a history of slight urethral discharge. A pelvic examination confirmed strawberry spots on the cervix. Which one of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 26-years-old woman presents with vaginal discharge that is characterized by a thin milky appearance with a fish-like odor. On examination, the vaginal pH of 4.5 was found. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old woman G4 P2012 at 26 weeks' gestation, presented for a 50-gram oral glucose tolerance test. 1 hour later by finger stick sample glucose was 8.1 mmol/L. Which vaginal infection is she at the highest risk of contracting?
A young adult was being treated with Ceftriaxone for acute salpingitis and pelvic inflammatory disease without benefit. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old primigravida is known to have regular menstrual cycles at 13 weeks of gestation, presents to the Emergency Room complaining of mild brownish vaginal discharge, the patient denies passing any tissue. The pelvic examination shows a closed cervical Os and the bedside ultrasound is performed (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old primigravida is known to have regular menstrual cycles at 13 weeks of gestation, presenting to the Emergency Room complaining of mild brownish vaginal discharge, the patient denies passing any tissue. The pelvic examination reveals a closed cervical os and the bedside ultrasound is performed (see image and lab result). Blood pressure 110/70 mHg Heart rate 76 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Hb 12 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Which of the following is the most appropriate advice?
Which of the following is the common cause of first trimester miscarriage?

A 23-year-old G4 P1112 with a history of abortion in her last pregnancy presents to the Emergency Room with vaginal spotting. Her LMP 7 weeks earlier. No abdominal pain or cramping reported and denies any vaginal discharge. On examination, abdominal tenderness was detected, uterus not palpable. Cervical os closed. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old woman G3 P0020 at 5 weeks' gestation presents with vaginal bleeding associated with some blood clots that started 3 hours ago. She had been diagnosed with cervical incompetence in her 2 prior second-trimester abortions. A history of dilatation and curettage in her last abortion declared. On examination; the cervical os is open and no on-going bleeding. Which of the following is the most likely cause of her current diagnosis of vaginal bleeding?

A 25-year-old woman G5 P2022 presented to the clinic at 10 weeks' gestation with painless vaginal bleeding. During her hospital admission, she developed heavy vaginal bleeding and lower abdominal pain. She has noticed passage of tissue. On examination, mild pain, vital signs are normal. Pelvic examination showed trickling blood through the cervix and os is open. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old woman P3 at 33 weeks of gestation, according to her last menstrual period, presents at the Ultrasound Unit. Ultrasound scan is done (see report). Ultrasound Scan: confirms the presence of a non-viable 30 weeks fetus. Which of the following would be best to help in breaking this news?

options.text: Right away and straight to the point
Defer any plan of follow-up till after delivery
Be as strong as you can be and hide your emotions
Address her emotions with empathetic verbal and nonverbal support

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most likely source of bleeding?

A 32-year-old married woman presents to the clinic with vague abdominal pain of 1-week duration. She claims an irregular menstrual cycle and her last menstrual cycle occurred 2 months ago. The patient is a known smoker with surgical history of open appendectomy due to ruptured appendicitis when she was 14 years of age Blood pressure 110/70 mmH Heart rate 102 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Which of the following diagnoses is to be ruled out initially?

A 32-year-old married woman presents with vague, sharp abdominal pain of 1-week duration, she claims an irregular menstrual cycle and her last menstrual cycle occurred 2 months ago. The patient is a known smoker with a history of open appendectomy due to ruptured appendicitis at the age of 14 years (see lab results). Blood pressure 90/40 mmHg Heart rate 105 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Human chorionic gonadotropin 1800 < 5 mlU/mL Hb 11 130-170 g/L. (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) HCT 0.39 0.42-0.52 (Male) 0.37-0.48 (Female) MCH 29 28-33 pg/cell MCHC 332 320-360 g/L MCV 89 80-95 fl Which of the following is the best next step in management?

options.text: Consult general surgery team to rule out acute abdomen

questions.stem: A 33-year-old woman is day 2 post laparotomy where salpingostomy was performed for right tubal pregnancy, the procedure was performed without complications and the patient is suitable to be discharged from the hospital (see lab results). Hb 12 130-170 g/L. (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) 3500 < 5 mlU/mL Which of the following is the most appropriate follow up approach?

options.text: Follow up appointment is not required
Perform a pelvic ultrasound scan 1 week post-operative
Serum hCG to be measured weekly until the level is undetectable

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman is day 2 post laparotomy where salpingectomy was performed for left tubal pregnancy, the procedure was performed without complications and the patient is suitable to be discharged from the hospital (see lab results). Blood pressure 110/70 mmH Heart rate 76 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Hb 13 130-170 g/. (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) 6488 < 5 mlU/mL Which of the following is the most appropriate follow up approach?

options.text: Single postoperative CG testing to confirm a large decline in the level
Weekly hCG level measurement until the level is undetectable
Pelvic ultrasound to be performed 6 days post-operative

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman 6 weeks post laparotomy where salpingostomy was performed for left tubal pregnancy, the procedure was performed without complications and the patient was discharged in a good stable condition. She has been followed up weekly to measure the serum human chorionic gonadotropin level, a plateau was noticed for the last 3 weeks at the following level (see lab result). Human chorionic gonadotropin 3442 < 5 mlU/mL Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.text: Reassure the patient and continue follow up

questions.stem: A hemodynamically stable woman has a tubal, ectopic pregnancy measuring 2.5 x 3 cm by ultrasound (see lab result). Test Result / Normal Value: Human chorionic gonadotropin N 5000 < 5 mlU/mL. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 28-year-old married woman presented to the Emergency Department complaining of a 6-hour history of right iliac fossa pain associated with drowsiness. Physical examination confirmed tenderness over the lower abdomen with sluggish bowel sounds. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 40-year-old woman underwent a laparoscopic tubal ligation during the postpartum period following the delivery of her 4th child 4 years ago. She presents to the Maternal Health Clinic complaining of bright red vaginal spotting. Patient last menstrual cycle was 6 weeks ago. A pelvic examination shows fullness over the right adnexa. There is no pain or tenderness. Her last pregnancy resulted in an emergency cesarean section with a midline incision. Which of the following is the best next step in management?

A 30-year-old woman with 6 weeks of amenorrhea presents with lower abdominal pain and mild vaginal bleeding. Examination reveals: she is hemodynamically stable and abdominal examination is soft and nontender. Pregnancy test is positive (see lab result and report). Human chorionic gonadotropin 4945 < 5 mlU/mL Pelvic Ultrasound: Shows a small mass <3.5 cm in right Fallopian tube, intact with no embryonic cardiac activity detected. Which of the following is the best management?

A 25-year-old woman was brought to the Emergency Department 7 weeks after her last menstruation with a positive pregnancy test. Abdominal and transvaginal ultrasound showed no intrauterine pregnancy sac. She has lower abdominal pain, mostly on the left side and mild vaginal bleeding. Which of the following is the most probable diagnosis?

A 30-year-old primigravida at 6 weeks of gestation presenting to the Emergency Room with mild abdominal pains. The trans-vaginal ultrasound reveals a normal sized uterus with no clear gestational sac and a 3 cm right adnexal mass with no fetal pole, no free fluid is noted. On examination, the abdomen is soft, non-tender. The pelvic examination reveals a normal cervix with mild cervical motion tenderness. Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg, Heart rate 76 /min, Respiratory rate 18 /min, Temperature 36.6 °C Hb 130 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Human chorionic gonadotropin 2500 < 5 mlU/mL Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old primigravida at 6 weeks of gestation presenting to the Emergency Room with mild abdominal pains. The trans-vaginal ultrasound reveals a normal sized uterus with no clear gestational sac and a 3 cm right adnexal mass with no fetal pole. On examination, the abdomen is soft, non-tender. The pelvic examination reveals a normal cervix with mild cervical motion tenderness (see lab results). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg, Heart rate 76 /min, Respiratory rate 18 /min, Temperature 36.6 °C Hb 130 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Human chorionic gonadotropin 2500 < 5 mlU/mL. Which of the following is the most appropriate management plan?

A 30-year-old primigravida at 6 weeks of gestation presenting to the Emergency Room with mild abdominal pains. On examination, the abdomen is soft, non-tender. The pelvic examination reveals a normal cervix with mild cervical motion tenderness (see lab results and report). Hb 130 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Human chorionic gonadotropin 3500 < 5 miU/mL Trans-vaginal Ultrasound: Reveals a normal sized uterus with no clear gestational sac and a 3 cm right adnexal mass with no fetal pole. What would be a prerequisite before counseling this patient for medical management?

options.text: The consent of the patient's husband
Accessibility of the patient to the hospital
The previous surgical history of the patient
They type of contraceptive previously used

questions.stem: A 30-year-old primigravida at 6 weeks of gestation is presenting to the Emergency Room with mild abdominal pains. An ultrasound reveals a 3 cm right adnexal mass with no fetal pole. On examination, the abdomen is soft, non-tender. The pelvic examination reveals a normal cervix with mild cervical motion tenderness (see lab result). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg, Heart rate 76 /min, Temperature 36.6 °C Human chorionic gonadotropin 15000 < 5 mlU/mL Which of the patient's characteristics would be causing failure of medical treatment?

A 24-year-old primigravida presents with the diagnosis of right ectopic pregnancy. The ultrasound revealed a 3 cm right tubal gestational sac with 5-week crown rump length, negative fetal heart activity and minimal amount of fluid in the pouch of Douglas. Her social history reveals that she lives in a village 80 km away from the city center (see lab result). Blood pressure 90/50 mmHg, Heart rate 110 /min, Temperature 35.6 °C, BMI 36 kg/m2 Human chorionic gonadotropin 3500 < 5 mlU/mL Which of the following would be the absolute contraindication to the use of methotrexate for this patient?

options.text: The B-hCG level and ultrasound findings
The far distance from medical services

questions.stem: A 33-year-old woman presents with amenorrhea of 8-week duration. Pregnancy test is positive (see report). Ultrasound: Shows an empty uterus and right adnexal mass noted. Which abnormality of the following processes is most likely the cause of the above case?
A 28-year-old woman is diagnosed with an ectopic pregnancy. Which of the following is the most likely predisposing factor?

options.text: Use of an intrauterine contraceptive device

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman who has 6 weeks of amenorrhea presented with vaginal bleeding, severe lower abdominal pain and shoulder pain. On examination, she had tachycardia with low blood pressure, and her abdomen was distended with guarding and rebound tenderness. Pelvic examination revealed cervical motion tenderness. Pregnancy test was positive and an ultrasound showed no intrauterine pregnancy. What is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 26-year-old patient with a 6-week history of amenorrhea presented with mild lower pelvic pain and vaginal bleeding. Pelvic examination revealed a soft uterus of normal size with mild tenderness at the right adnexa (see lab results and report). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg, Heart rate 82 /min Respiratory rate 22 /min Temperature 37.6 °C Human chorionic gonadotropin 1000 < 5 mlU/mL B-hCG 1000 1080-56500 m|U/ml Pelvic ultrasound: Shows a thickened endometrium with no intrauterine sac, minimal amount of fluid in the cul-de-sac and right adnexal mass measuring 1.2 cm. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
Which of the following would make the highest risk of endometrial cancer?

A 62-year-old patient presented with vaginal bleeding. Investigations revealed a malignant tumor of uterine fundus. Which of the following groups of lymph nodes is likely affected in this condition and to be dissected during surgery?

A 57-year-old menopausal woman, presents for evaluation of postmenopausal bleeding. She is morbidly obese, hypertensive and diabetic. Endometrial sampling showed complex endometrial hyperplasia with atypia. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 50-year-old P2+3 patient known to be diabetic and hypertensive, presented to the clinic complaining of abnormal uterine bleeding for the last 8 months, the menstrual period is regular every 30 days and lasts for 5 days, associated with blood clots and pain that is not relieved by simple analgesia. The patient had previously undergone myomectomy 12 years back and was known to have all her pregnancies induced as she had poly-cystic ovarian syndrome. On examination, the uterus was not palpable but on pelvic examination revealed a normal sized uterus and a healthy looking cervix with no adnexal mass. BMI 40 kg/m2 Which of the following is the most likely explanation for this patient's presentation?

A 60-year-old P5+3 patient is known to be diabetic and hypertensive presented to the clinic complaining of post-menopausal bleeding for the last 8 months. The patient had previously undergone myomectomy 12 years back and 3 surgical evacuation for incomplete miscarriage. On examination, the uterus was not palpable but on pelvic examination the uterus was found to be bulky and tender with no adnexal mass (see image). BMI 42 kg/m2 Which of the following is the most likely explanation for this patient's presentation?

A 60-year-old patient presents with postmenopausal bleeding for the last 8 months. The ultrasound is ordered (see image). Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in assessing this patient?

A 47-year-old woman, poorly controlled diabetic, complains of polymenorrhagia every couple of weeks. Body mass index 37 kg/m2 Which of the following is most appropriate investigation to establish the diagnosis?

options.text: Magnetic resonance imaging of the pelvis.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 40-year-old P6 patient attends to the clinic complaining of dribbling of a small amount of urine with associated dyspareunia and dysuria. She denies any history of previous surgeries or the development of fever. Which of the following is the most likely cause of the symptoms?

A 40-year-old patient who is known to have COPD comes to the clinic complaining of small amounts of urine leaking every time she coughs; the patient denies having to wake up at night to pass urine and does not have dysuria or dyspareunia. BMI 40 kg/m2 Which of the following is the most probable cause?

A 50-year-old patient presents to the clinic complaining of urinary leaking on coughing and straining. She is not known to have any medical or previous surgical history. On examination. the abdomen is soft and is non-tender. Pelvic examination reveals a normal sized anteverted, non-tender uterus. There was mild amounts of urine leakage when the patient was asked to cough. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 35-year-old woman delivered her first baby by vacuum extraction due to prolonged second stage of labor 3 months ago. The woman was complaining of leakage of urine when she coughed, sneezed or laughed. The symptoms have started since delivery and persisted since then. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old woman presented with vaginal itching and burning. Currently, she is only on calcium supplements. Physical examination revealed thinning and pallor of the vaginal mucosa and no discharge. Wet prep from the scant material present was negative for any organisms. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment?
A 50-year-old woman presented with amenorrhea for the last 6 months and has unwanted hot flushes disturbing her night sleep. Which of the following serum levels would confirm the diagnosis?

A 28-year-old healthy woman presents to her gynecologist with history of inability to conceive after 2 years of trying. Menarche at 13-year-old, regular cycles every 36-40 days and 5-day periods. Not on any medications. Semenanalysis of husband showed normospermia, Cervical component examination is required. The basal body temperature showed a monophasic pattern. Which of the following is the most probable cause of the infertility?

A 26-year-old woman presented to the clinic with secondary amenorrhea of 6 months duration. She gave history of breast tenderness. On examination; bilateral breast whitish discharge from nipples. Her urine pregnancy test was negative and elevated serum prolactin levels. Which of the following radiological assessment is most appropriate?

A 14-year-old child presented to the clinic after being sexually abused 6 hours earlier. Genital examination confirmed anogenital erythema and mild bleeding vaginally, and labia majora was swollen and bruised. Blood pressure 120/70 mmHg, Heart rate 90 /min, Respiratory rate 20 /min Temperature 36.6° C, What is the most likely site of hymeneal tear that is suggestive of penile penetration?

A 27-year-old nulliparous is concerned about not having conceived after a year of regular, unprotected intercourse. The patient denied any major medical illnesses and takes no medications. The patient's spouse is reported to be healthy but has never fathered a child. What is the most appropriate initial step in evaluation after history and examination?

A 67-year-old woman a]ended the Gynecological Clinic for the follow up of lichen sclerosus diagnosed a few years earlier. Upon examination, a small mass measuring 0.5 x 0.5 cm was identified on her right labia majora. Punch biopsy was taken from the lesion and sent for histopathology. Which of the following is the most likely histopathological finding?
A 29-year-old woman is planning to become pregnant. She has a normal menstrual period every 30 days. Which of the following is the most appropriate to prescribe?

A 24-year-old newly married woman presents to the Emergency Room complaining of sudden sharp lower abdominal pain, she does not have regular menstrual cycles and does not remember when the her last menstrual cycle began, she is not known to have any previous medical illness and had no prior surgeries (see lab result). Blood pressure 100/70 mmH, Heart rate 76 /min Hb 11 130-170 g/L. (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Which of the following is the best advice?

options.text: Further tests including BhCG and ultrasound

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman who is pregnant calls the clinic for an advice. She has just found out that her hCG level is elevated. Elevated hG level indicates which of the following?

options.text: A high level of hCG is indicative of an ectopic pregnancy
A high level of hCG in the second trimester is indicative of molar pregnancy
A high level of hCG can stimulate production of TRH, causing hyperthyroidism
A high level of hG in the second trimester is the most sensitive marker for Down syndrome

questions.stem: A 36-year-old woman Para 1 comes to the clinic for genetic counseling. Her first child was born with sickle cell disease. She has since remarried, and is requesting prenatal testing according to the premarital requirements in the country. Which of the following is appropriate to offer first?

A 30-year-old primigravida presents to the Emergency Room complaining of vaginal spotting for the last few days, her history reveals irregularity of the menstrual cycles and that she has been trying to conceive for the last 3 years. Abdominal examination reveals tenderness in the lower abdomen and the pelvic examination reveals a closed cervical Os with cervical motion tenderness (see lab results). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 105 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Weight 60 kg Height 160 cm Hb 130 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) HCT 038 0.42-0.52 (Male) 0.37-0.48 (Female) MCH 19 28-33 pg/cell MCHC 330 320-360 g/L. MCV 85 80-95 fl Platelets count 155 150-400 x 109/L WBC 4.6 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Perform an abdominal ultrasound of the pelvis
Know about the reason of infertility

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the uterus in a normal pregnancy?

options.text: Palpable midway between the symphysis pubis and the umbilicus
Palpable just over the symphysis pubis
Palpable at the level of the umbilicus

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman presents to the clinic with a 9-month history of amenorrhea concerning about her condition (see lab results).
