questions.stem: A 10-year-old boy with recurrent wheeze and cough responded partially to asthma management. He has poor weight gain and strong family history of bronchial asthma. Which of the following supports diagnosis of cystic fibrosis?

A 4-year-old child with bronchial asthma on ventolin inhaler. The mother gave history of cough attack more than twice per week and she brought her child to the Emergency Room last month twice. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.text: Admit to hospital for further workup

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most causative organism of bronchiolitis in infant?
Which of the following is the most common mode of inheritance in cystic fibrosis?
Which of the following is the expected finding in chest X-ray match child's chest finding?

A 3-month-old infant with noisy breath since birth change with positioning tends to disappears in prone position and become more obvious with supine position. Examination and growth parameter are normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-month-old infant with noisy breath since birth change with positioning tends to disappears in prone position and become more obvious with supine position. Examination and growth parameter are normal. The mother concerned about this sound. Which of the following is the most appropriate counselling should be given?

options.text: Will improve by her first birthday

questions.stem: An 8-month-old infant with recurrent wheeze and distress resistance to asthma management and required multiple hospitalizations. After detailed history and examination, his pediatrician suspects tracheomalacia. Which of the following has the highest diagnostic value?

A male newborn develops sudden respiratory distress (see report). Chest radiograph: A hyperlucent left upper lobe with adjacent lobar compression and mediastinal shift to the right. Which of the following is most appropriate treatment?

A 4-year-old child known to have bronchial asthma presents with the mother for primary clinic checkup. There is family history of asthma and father smokes at home. What is the most appropriate counselling should be given?

options.text: Refer the child for allergy test
Prescribe inhaled steroid for regular use
Counseling his parents regarding smoking cessations

questions.stem: A previously healthy 13-month-old girl has a 2-day history of fever and increasing cough. She continued to be breastfed with no vomiting. Her immunizations are up to date. She is alert and mildly ill-appearing. On examination, there is no grunting or chest retractions. There are crackles heard over the right lung base. The remainder of the examination findings are normal. She has no known allergies. ● Blood pressure: 110/70 mmHg ● Heart rate: 146 /min ● Respiratory rate: 45 /min ● Temperature: 38.6 °C ● Oxygen saturation: 95% Which of the following is the most likely pathogen?

A previously healthy 13-month-old girl comes to the clinic with a 2-day history of fever and increasing cough. She continued to be breastfed with no vomiting. Her immunizations are up to date. She is alert and mildly ill-appearing. On examination, there is no grunting or chest retraction. She has crackles heard over the right lung base. The remainder of the examination findings is normal. Bacterial community-acquired pneumonia is suspected. ● Respiratory rate: 36 /min ● Temperature: 38.6 °C ● Oxygen saturation: 96 % Which of the following would indicate a need for hospitalization?

options.text: Respiratory rate of 36 breath per min
Inability to maintain hydration or oral intake

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best management?

options.text: Admit for oxygen and hydration therapy
Send home with instruction when to come back
Admit for antibiotics and oxygen administration
Admit for bronchodilation and steroid management

questions.stem: Which of the following asthmatic patients require hospital admission?

options.text: Oxygen saturation below 92% after high dose therapy

questions.stem: A 4-year-old child presented with recurrent chest infection and poor growth. On examination, chest auscultation revealed inspiratory crepitation with expiratory wheeze and finger clubbing. Further exploration in the history revealed the presence of very offensive and greasy stools. Which of the following is expected to be further identified in the physical examination?

A 3-year-old child presented to Emergency Room with fever, headache and lethargy. On examination, clear purpuric rash, sign of shock and positive Kernig sign present. Eye exam revealed the presence of papilledema. The parents are bedside and worried about child condition and prognosis. Which of the following complication is important for the parents?

A 3-year-old child presented to Emergency Room with difficulty breathing, lip swelling and spreading skin rash. On examination, marked airway swelling was observed with rash covering all the body. The mother said he was attending a party at his friend's house and she was not with him. Which of the following will likely reveal the diagnosis?

A 3-month-old girl presented to the Emergency Room with symptoms of paroxysmal episodes of cough followed by a whooping sound at the end. It is occasionally associated with perioral cyanosis and post- tussive vomiting. These symptoms got worse when she started to have a fever of 39.5°C. History revealed she did not receive her 2-month vaccine. Which of the following is the most common expected complication?

A 3-month-old girl presented to the Emergency Room with symptoms of paroxysmal episodes of cough followed by a whooping sound at the end. It is occasionally associated with perioral cyanosis and post- tussive vomiting. These symptoms got worse when she started to have a fever of 39.5°C. History revealed she did not receive her 2-month vaccine. What is the gold standard method to diagnose this condition?

A 3-month-old boy presented to the Emergency Room with history of paroxysmal episodes of staccato cough, inspiration between each cough. It is associated with perioral cyanosis and post-tussive vomiting. There is no history of diarrhea. This illness has been preceded by conjunctivitis few days ago. On examination, the child looks unwell and tachypneic with auscultatory crackles. He has normal white blood cell count with elevated eosinophils on laboratory evaluation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-month-old boy presented to the Emergency Room with history of paroxysmal episodes of cough associated with an inspiratory whoop and possessive emesis. It is associated with fever, conjunctival redness and diarrhoea. His immunization is up to date. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-hour-old newborn delivered by cesarean section because of severe fetal deceleration and meconium stained fluid. He required intubation and ventilation with iontropic support. Few hours later, he started to have low saturation with increase oxygen requirement. The pre ducal saturation is 92 while the post ductal saturation is 81. Chest X-ray done and showed no pneumothorax. Which of the following is the next step in the management?

A term infant delivered with antenatal diagnosis of diaphragmatic hernia. She required vigorous resuscitation in the delivery room. Which of the following is the first step in managing this infant after stabilization?

A 6-month-old infant presents to the Emergency Room with sudden apnea and color change. The mother gave history of recurrent vomiting, and multiple chest infections. On examination, he looks failing to thrive with dystonic neck posturing while crying. Which of the following is considered a high-risk case for the above disease?
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis? A. Bronchitis
A 2-month-old infant presents to Emergency Room with bronchiolitis required non-invasive mechanical ventilation as a respiratory support. Which of the following is the most appropriate destination?

options.text: Admission to pediatrics critical care unit

questions.stem: An 8-month-old infant admitted to Pediatrics Critical Care for close observation. Which of the following standers continuous monitoring in pediatrics critical care measured as trans-cutaneous?
Which of the following measures would decrease the incidence of Sudden Infant Death Syndrome?

A 20-month-old child is brought to the Emergency Department due to respiratory distress with stridor and fever. Her parents mention that 2 days ago she started rhinorrhoea and mild cough with progressive worsening of the cough that is now "barky". Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 10-year-old boy is admitted to the hospital due to acute exacerbation of asthma. He is currently medicated with montelukast once daily and has last been seen by his primary care physician over 6 months ago. He reports daily episodes of dry cough and wheezing that are exacerbated by exercise. After admission, his symptoms stabilized with the administration of inhaled albuterol. Which of the following is the most appropriate long-term maintenance therapy?

options.text: Oral steroids once daily, plus a long-acting beta-2 agonist as needed
Inhaled corticosteroid twice-daily, plus a short acting beta-2 agonist as needed
Inhaled long-acting beta-2 agonist, plus a short acting beta-2 agonist as needed
Leukotriene receptor antagonist once daily plus a short acting beta-2 agonist as needed

questions.stem: A 5-week-old baby is brought to the clinic with low-grade fever and difficulty breathing. Her parents report that she had 2 episodes in which she appeared to have stopped breathing. Physical examination confirms subcostal retractions with inspiration and diffuse bilateral wheeze. Temperature 37 g °C Heart Rate 130 /min Which of the following is the most frequent agent causing acute bronchiolitis?

A 3-year-old child admitted to the hospital to initiate antibiotic treatment for pneumonia. She has long history of sinusitis and lower respiratory tract infections. During the current admission, she underwent fibre optic bronchoscopy with sputum collection and both pseudomonas aeruginosa and burkholderia cepacia are isolated. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old child is a known asthmatic who usually has 1 acute exacerbation each month. The acute symptoms are relieved by nebulizer therapy at the Emergency Department or the nearby health centre. Which of the following should be included in the daily management?

A 22-month-old boy presents to the Emergency Department with a sudden onset of respiratory distress during a family picnic. He is febrile and has otherwise been well. Physical examination demonstrates unilateral wheezing in the right hemithorax. Which of the following is the most likely to be seen in his chest X-ray?

options.text: Consolidation of the right lower lobe
Lower lobe collapse on the right side
Hyperinflation of the right lung with mediastinal shift\ to the left

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in making a definitive diagnosis?

A 1-year-old child is brought to the clinic with a high fever, cough and respiratory distress for 3 days. On auscultation of the chest, there are generalised fine crackles (see report). Chest X-ray: Showed puffy infiltrates with ill-defined margins throughout both lung fields. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old sickle cell child arrives at the Emergency Department in respiratory distress. Over the previous 3 days, the child has become progressively tired and pale (see lab result). Hb 31 112-165 g/L Which of the following is the most likely cause?

A 2-year-old is brought to the clinic with sore throat and high-grade fever for 5 days. On examination, he is febrile and mildly dehydrated. The pharynx and tonsillar area is congested along with inflammation of the mouth and lips associated with gingivitis. Lesions in the mouth and lips appear as whitish-yellow plaques with erythematous base. Which of the following is the most likely cause?

A16-year-old asymptomatic boy presents for a sports participation physical examination. He is asthmatic since the age of 4 years and uses albuterol on rare occasion, which gives rapid and complete relief. Which of the following questions is best to ask to evaluate whether the current control is satisfactory?

options.text: "Are you able to keep up with your teammates?"
"Are you using your inhaler more frequently?"

questions.stem: An 8-year-old girl with presents with a sore throat and a temperature of 38°C. History reveals, she has not received any childhood immunisation. A clinical examination confirms a severely swollen and edematous neck region with enlarged cervical lymph nodes. Her pharynx is erythematous with bleeding spots when a swab is taken for culture. An inspiratory stridor is noted upon auscultation of the lungs. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 18-month old child is brought to the clinic with mild atopic eczema. The parents report that he woke up last night with stridor and a barking cough. There are no preceding or associated upper respiratory tract infection symptoms. The symptoms resolved spontaneously a few hours later. It is the second episode of this nature over the past 6 months. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis ?
Which of the following is the most appropriate way to establish the diagnosis?

A 6-month-old boy presents to the paediatrician with a loud barking cough and a rectal temperature of 38° C. The parents report a cold for the last 3 days that worsens at night. The coughing is aggravated with crying and there is a high-pitched, rasping sound on inhalation. Physical examination confirms a reddened throat and a nasal obstruction (see report). Chest X-ray: Normal. Which of the following is the most likely cause?

A 3-year-old girl presents to the Paediatric Emergency Department at night with a barking, dry cough and laboured breathing. There is a 3-day history of nasal obstruction and cough that had worsened over the last 2 hours. The child appears anxious and cries with a hoarse voice. There is a sharp, high-pitched sound on inspiration. Physical examination confirms indrawing of the chest wail and a reddened throat. A single treatment with nebulized epinephrine results.in a quick improvement of the airway symptoms. 30 minutes after the inhalation the coughing and the breathing difficulties reappear. Which of the following is the next step in management?

A 3-year-old girl presents to the Paediatric Emergency Department in the early morning hours with a barking cough that worsens with crying. There is a history of mild cough and temperatures around 38° C (rectal) over the last 3 days. Physical examination confirms an inflamed throat and mild suprasternal retractions. Blood pressure 95/65 mmH Heart rate 90 /min Respiratory rate 34 /min Temperature 39.3° C Which of the following is the most likely at auscultatory finding?
Which of the following has the highest diagnostic value?

A 6-year-old child presents with history of increasing eye puffiness for 1 week especially in the morning. He has had flu-like illness 2 week ago. On examination, he looks well, not in distress and no lower limb edema. Eye, chest and abdomen exams are normal (see lab result). Total Cholesterol 3 <5.2 mmol/L Triglycerides 10 <1.7 mmol/L Protein +4 Absent Leukocytes 0 0-3 per high power field Erythrocytes 0 0-2 per high power field Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
Which of the following is the expected serum sodium level based on clinical finding?
Which of the following is the most appropriate next action?

options.text: 20 ml per kg normal saline bolus
Start maintenance fluid waiting for serum electrolytes

questions.stem: A 6-year-old child has asymptomatic hematuria. There is no significant past medical history and the physical examination is unremarkable (see lab result). Urinalysis Result Normal Value Erythrocytes 15 0-2 per HPF Which of the following should the initial evaluation include?

A 6-year-old boy complains of passing Coca cola-coloured urine for the last week. On examination, he had a congested throat, and anterior cervical lymphadenopathy (see lab results). Blood pressure 155/100 mmHg Heart rate 125 /min Respiratory rate 20/min Temperature 38.5° C Urinalysis Result Normal Values Colour Brown Clear or light yellow Appearance Turbid Clear Leukocytes 3-5 0-3 per high power field Erythrocytes 20-30 0-2 per high power field Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is the most appropriate investigation?

A 3-year-old girl is brought to the Emergency Department with fever and dark urine. Her parents state that she had been constipated. On examination, she looks unwell and irritable with abdominal tenderness, but no palpable liver or spleen (see lab results). Blood pressure 125/86 mmHg Heart rate 125 /min Respiratory rate 29/min Temperature 39.9° C Hb 81 112-160 g/L Platelets count 325 150-400 x 109/L Urinalysis Test Result Normal Values Leukocytes 16 0-3 per high power field I Erythrocytes 18 0-2 per high power field Protein ++ Absent Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 5-year-old child presents with features of glomerulonephritis. A week later, she developed haemoptysis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old child presents to the Medical Outpatients with a parent who reports edema over the face. Examination of urine shows selective proteinuria (3.5 g/day). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 14-year-old presents with photosensitivity, a malar rash, joint pains and purpuric rashes on both legs. Urine examination shows red cells. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 10-year-old child presents with a high-grade fever, generalized body swelling, decreased urine output, and dark-coloured urine. Which of the following is the most appropriate first investigation?

A 7-year-old child presents with a history of fever and pain in the lower abdomen for the past 3 days. The parent reports that the child's urine has been foul smelling for the past 2 days (see report). Urine culture: Gram negative bacteria, > 100,000 cells/mi. What is the most likely organism?

A 2-year-old boy is brought to the Paediatric Emergency Department. The mother reports that the boy has become increasingly irritable and feeble over the last 2 days. He has passed very li]le urine and his skin has become pale. The mother had consulted the paediatrician 2 weeks before because the baby had suffered from bloody diarrhea, vomiting and high fever. Symptomatic treatment with acetaminophen and probiotics had been started. Physical examination shows mild petechiae on the lower extremities. Urinalysis reveals microhematuria and mild proteinuria (see lab results). Hb 73 112-165 g/L INR 1.1 0.9-1.2 WBC 48.6 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Platelets count 95 150-400 x 109/L MCV 86 80-95 fl MCH 30 28-33 pg/cell RBC count 3.3 4.6-4.8 x 1012/L. Prothrombin time 12 12-14 sec APTT 34 30-40 s Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old girl was brought to the clinic because her mother had felt a mass in the abdomen last night when she was bathing her. She has been otherwise well with no weight loss, fever, or bone pain. Her blood pressure is 130/80 mmH. Physical examination shows a well-thriving kid with a palpable firm mass in the right flank (see lab results). Color Clear clear or light yellow Appearance Clear clear рн 6.5 4.3-8 Specific gravity 1020 1001-1030 Protein trace Absent Glucose absent Absent Ketones absent Absent Urobilinogen absent No more than 6 mg/day Nitrite absent Absent Erythrocytes 40 0-2 per high power field Hemoglobin +3 Absent Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old girl was brought to the clinic because her mother had felt a mass in the abdomen last night when she was bathing her. She has been otherwise well with no weight loss, fever, or bone pain. Her blood pressure is 130/80 mmH. Physical examination shows a well-thriving kid with a palpable firm mass in the right flank (see lab results). Color Clear clear or light yellow pH 7.0 4.3-8 Specific gravity 1010 1001-1030 Protein Absent Absent Glucose Absent Absent Ketones Absent Absent Nitrite Absent Absent Hemoglobin +*+ Absent Leukocytes Absent 0-3 per high power field Erythrocytes 50 0-2 per high power field Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in her diagnostic work-up?

options.text: Plain abdominal radiography and abdominal ultrasonography

questions.stem: A healthy 8-month-old circumcised boy brought to the clinic by his parents with a history of fever since morning. He has not had nasal congestion, cough, or diarrhea. He had 1 episode of emesis when he was given acetaminophen. He has continued to breastfeed and has had a normal number of wet diapers. He is mildly ill appearing. There is no clear focus of infection on examination. Temperature 39.4 °C Which of the following factors is most strongly associated with an increased probability of having a urinary tract infection?

A 3-year-old child presents to the clinic with history of passing red-brown urine. There is a positive history of flu-like prodrome 2 weeks ago. Which of the following has the highest diagnostic value?

A 4-month-old boy brought by his mother asking for circumcision. History revealed that he was diagnosed with mid-shaft hypospadias. Which of the following is the most appropriate counseling should be given?

options.text: No link between hypospadias and circumcision
It is late for circumcision as correction is often undertaken before 4 month old
Infant with hypospadias must not be circumcised as the skin will used in the surgery
Proceed with circumcision as there is no need for surgical correction for this type of hypospadias

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate next action?
Which of the following describes her shock status?
Which of the following clinical sign can be observed?

A 2-hour-old baby delivered by emergency cesarean section because of placental abruption, and required resuscitation with intubation and cardiac message (see lab results). ABG HCO3- 7 13-22 mmol/L ABG PCO2 65 27-40 mmHg pH 6.9 7.36-7.45 ABG PO2 5 8-24 mmHg (Newbor) 55-80 mmHg (Child) Base access -18 -2 to 2 mmol/L Which of the following proven to reduce death and sever disability within 6 hours?
Which of the following is the most common congenital heart lesion?

A 2-year-old child presents to the Emergency Department with high-grade fever, persistent vomiting, diarrhea and cough for 3 days. On examination, a murmur with decrease air entry over the right lung. For the last 4 visit to the pediatrician, the patient had a normal exam including cardiac (see lab results). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 125 /min Respiratory rate 22 /min Temperature 38.5 °C Oxygen saturation 97 % BC 4.5 4.8-7.1 x 1012/L (Newborn) 4.6-4.8 x 1012/L (Child) Hb 95 165-195 g/L (Newborn) 112-165 g/L (Child) MCH 20 28-33 pg/cell MCV 65 80-95 f1 Platelets count 200 150-400 × 109/L WBC 6 4.5-13.5 x 109/L (2-10 vears) 4.5-11.1 X 109/L (11 years-older adult) Which of the following is the best next step in management for the heart murmur?

options.text: Admission in cardiac ICU for monitoring and intervention
Re-examine the heart murmur after correction of the underlying illness

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis for the heart murmur?
Which of the following represent the best management approach for significant atrial septal defect (ASD)?

options.text: Treatment usually undertaken at 3-5 years of age
Treatment usually undertaken within 8 weeks form birth
No need to treat significant ASD as it will close by age of 5 years

questions.stem: An 18-month-old child diagnosed with congenital heart disease, presented to Emergency Room with severe cyanosis and hypercyantic spells. The mother mentioned that he was irritable and inconsolable crying for the last 1 hours and the cyanosis is getting worse. On examination, he looks cyanotice centrally, with loud harsh ejection systolic murmur heard at left sternal border (see report). Blood pressure 100/60 mmHg Heart rate 95 /min Respiratory rate 28 /min Temperature 37.8 °C Oxygen saturation 85 % Chest X-Ray: Showed small heart with decrease pulmonary vascular marking. Which of the following is to most appropriate management?

options.text: IV antibiotics and total parenteral nutrition

questions.stem: A 2-day-old neonate presents to the Emergency Department with sudden sever cyanosis. On examination, he looks cyanotic, lethargic; with cardiac exam reveals no murmur and normal pulses (see report). Chest X-Ray: Showed egg on side appearance of the cardiac shadow and increased pulmonary vascular marking. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 14-month-old presents to Primary Clinic with recurrent syncopal attack, associated with worsening heart failure manifestation and poor growth. On examination, he has crackles all over the chest with palpitation and abnormal cardiac rhythm (see report). ECG: Showed narrow complex tachycardia of 250-300 beats/min. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following are considered as minor manifestations of Jones criteria for diagnosis of rheumatic fever?

A 12-year-old boy comes to the clinic with symptoms of unnatural tiredness and exertional dyspnoea. He has a past history of myopia. On physical examination, he has scoliosis and a pectus excavatum (see report). Height above the 90th percentile Weight below the 25th percentile Echocardiography: Mitral valve prolapse and dilatation of the ascending aorta. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 12-day newborn girl is brought to the Emergency Department. Her mother complaining that the girl turns blue when she cries. After examination and investigation, the pediatrician explains to the mother that she had a congenital heart disease called Fallot's tetralogy. Which of the following is a part of Fallot tetralogy?

A 5-year-old overweight girl has systolic blood pressure above the 95th percentile and has a family history of hypertension. Physical examination reveals a strong radial pulses and weak femoral pulses. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 14-month-old asymptomatic boy has a grade 2 pansystolic murmur detected on a routine consultation. Echocardiography reveals a 2 mm ventricular septal defect in the muscular portion of the septum. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 4-month-old boy with down syndrome exhibits poor weight gain, tachypnea, a low-pitched grade 2 systolic murmur and a fixed splitting of S2. Chest X-ray reveals cardiomegaly and increased pulmonary vascularity. Electrocardiography documents biventricular hypertrophy and a superior frontal plane QRS axis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 4-week-old baby presents with tachypnea, tachycardia, differential cyanosis and irritability. Which of the following is the most common accompanying feature? A Cough

A 6-month-old girl presents with difficulty feeding and the parents report that her skin becomes bluish during feeding and crying. Cardiac auscultation reveals a harsh systolic ejection murmur and a loud, single S2. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A newborn child presents with cyanosis, tachypnea, irritability and difficulty feeding. Physical examination findings are a parasternal heave and a loud, single S2 on cardiac auscultation. No murmurs were heard. Which of the following is essential in the early management?
A 5-year-old girl is found to have a loud pan-systolic murmur at the lower left sternal border. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following ECG abnormalities is an expected finding in ostium secundum atrial septal defect?
Which of the following is characteristic of the cardiac auscultation of a child with an atrial septal defect?

A 3-year-old asymptomatic child is examined prior to elective oral surgery. A grade 2/6 low- pitched continuous murmur is heard at the upper right steal border when the child is sieng; the murmur disappears when the child is supine. Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Antibiotics prophylaxis prior to oral surgery
Postpone oral surgery and re-evaluate the child

questions.stem: Which of the following findings in a newborn requires immediate treatment?

A 13-year-old boy presents for a physical check-up. He has had normal growth and development and has been able to do the usual activities for his age without difficulty. His older brother had had a sudden cardiac death while walking to work. The boy's examination is normal. Which of the following must be excluded?
Which of the following patients with congenital heart disease would be expected to exhibit cyanosis?

options.text: 6-year-old girl with coarctation of the aorta

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most likely cardiac anomaly?
Which of the following congenital heart diseases is associated with the lowest risk of infective endocarditis?
Which of the following is a component of the Tetralogy of Fallot?

A 9-month-old infant has a congenital heart lesion but the parents do not know the specific diagnosis. On examination, it was found that the infant has central and peripheral cyanosis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 10-year-old boy is diagnosed with acute rheumatic fever with cardiac involvement. For how many years is rheumatic fever prophylaxis recommended for this child?
A 9-year-old presents with weakness, fatigue, and hypertension in upper limbs. Examination confirms delayed pulses in lower extremities. Which of the following is the most likely aetiology?

A 12-year-old boy comes to the clinic with multiple painful swollen joints with reduced range of motion. Examination shows multiple non-tender subcutaneous nodules. Which of the following would most probably confirm the diagnosis?
Which of the following echocardiographic findings is consistent with the diagnosis of acute rheumatic fever?
Which of the following represents the main treatment for symptomatic acute rheumatic fever?

options.text: High dose oral acetyl salicylic acid

questions.stem: Which of the following has the greatest risk of developing endocarditis in patients with congenital heart disease?
Which of the following are most consistent with the diagnosis of acute rheumatic fever?

options.text: Fever, Roth spots and ischemic stroke
Malar facial rash, joint aches and fever
Chorea and multiple painful joint swelling
Fever, cough and purulent sputum production

questions.stem: A 6-year-old boy presents for his routine preschool check-up. The cardiovascular examination reveals a systolic murmur grade Ill, with no thrill, located at the lower sternal border, it is vibratory in character and accentuated when the boy is in a supine poison. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 21-day-old newborn recently diagnosed with a patent ductus arterious undergoes surgery to ligate the duct. Which of the following nerves would be at risk?
Which of the following syndromes is associated with coarctation of the aorta?
Which of the following is most likely prognosis?
Which of the following is the diagnostic criteria for Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder in children, according to the International Classification of Diseases-10?

A 10-year-old child presents to the clinic with cutaneous manifestations. She had 7 cafe-au lait spots, 2 neurofibroma and axillary freckles. The mother mentioned a presence of nephew who had similar lesions. What is mode of inheritance of this disease?

A 10-years-old child presents to the clinic with cutaneous manifestations. She had 7 cafe-aulait spots. 2 neurofibroma and axiliary freckles. The mother mentioned a presence of nephew who had similar lesions. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is the most causative factor for retinopathy of prematurity?

A 9-year-old child has been declining in school performance for several months due to lack of attention and "daydreaming" in class. The child, of average intelligence, has brief spells of staring into space that last 10 or 15 seconds. They occur several times an hour but the child seems quite unaware of these incidences. EEG reveals frontally predominant, generalized 3-Hz spike and wave complexes. Which of the following drugs is most likely to be effective?

A 9-month-old baby is brought to the Well-Baby Clinic. He is unable to sit, and on examination his hands are fisted and his legs are crossed. His mother said that he did not cry after the birth and resuscitation. Which of the following is consistent with these findings?

A 3-year-old child falls out of a bunk bed. The child cries immediately, and there is no apparent loss of consciousness. Then he vomited twice and complains of a headache. The child has a normal mental status, normal neurological examination, and no evidence of a skull fracture. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management? A.Brain magnified resonance imaging

A 6-year-old child is brought to the clinic with sudden onset of a clumsy gait and an inability to stand or walk without support. The child is irritable and has been vomiting over the last 3 days and had chickenpox 3 weeks before. Muscle strength testing does not reveal any abnormality, but there is a resistance to neck flexion. Which of the following disorders is most likely present?

A 4-year-old child is brought to the clinic for a check-up. When performing a cover test, the child's left eye moves laterally when the right eye is covered. Which of the following is the most serious complication?

A 12-year-old boy presents with difficulty walking for the last 2 days. He states that this weakness was preceded by pain in the muscles and a tingling sensation that started down the lower limb but kept ascending upwards to the upper limbs. He gave a history of a preceding upper respiratory tract infection 2 weeks before. On examination, he had total areflexia of both upper and lower limbs, with moderate sensory involvement. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 16-year-old girl presents with throbbing headaches that last for 2 hours and occurs 3 to 4 times a week. The headaches are usually unilateral, begins with nausea, and exacerbated by noise and light. A recent brain CT scan was normal. Which of the following should be used to treat acute symptoms?

A 12-year-old girl comes to the clinic after developing progressive weakness and inability to walk. She has intermittent tingling of her fingers and toes. History reveals she had 3 days of diarrhea about 2 weeks ago. Physical examination confirms marked peripheral muscle weakness without atrophy or fasciculation. The ankle and patella reflexes are absent, and a sensory examination is normal. Motor involvement is symmetric. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

The parents reports that the child has been repeatedly choking on her saliva. The symptoms began with a prickly sensation in the fingers and toes that came along with an ascending and symmetric numbness. There is a history of viral gastroenteritis 3 weeks before. Which of the following is most likely long term prognosis?
Which of the following drugs would be most suitable for a 7-year-old child with absence seizures?

A 2-day-old baby is brought to the hospital because of reluctance to feed and seizures since last night. On examination, the baby weighed 3 kg, is inactive and has a generalized increased tone. Height 150 cm (5th percentile) Weighs 65 kg (90th percentile) Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

Intravenous infusion of glucose 2 mi/kg of 12.5% dextrose

The boy's height Is 145 cm (between 5th - 10th percentile) and his bone age is 10 years. What will be the patient's target height in cm?

options.text: A palpable liver 2 cm below costal margin
Redundant skin folds at the nape of neck

questions.stem: A 13-year-old girl presents to the clinic for an assessment of her short stature. options.text: Provide a list of low-calorie foods

questions.stem: A 2-year-old girl presents to the Emergency Room with fever, vomiting and diarrhea for the last 4 days. On examination, she looks severely dehydrated, lethargic with altered conscious stat, with mild abdominal pain. The family mentioned that they tried to use oral rehydration solution at home but she is not drinking well. A rapid correction by intravenous normal saline fluid established to manage her case. Blood pressure 75/35 mmg Heart rate 110 /min Respiratory rate 28 /min Temperature 39 °C Oxygen saturation 95 % Sodium 162 134-146 mol/L Potassium 3.8 3.5-5.1 mmol/L Chloride 115 97-108 mmol/L Bicarbonate 14 21-28 mmol/L which of the following is the most likely cause her deterioration?

options.text: Rapid correction lead to cerebral edema
Delayed in starting fluid and antibiotics
Sudden intraventricular hemorrhage because the high sodium

options.text: TSH and T4 of the newborn
TSH and T4 levels of the mother

In which of the following conditions would you expect a bone age greater than the chronologic age?

options.text: Begins with one tablespoon of food
Eliminate a refused food from the diet

options.text: Use aspirin to relive the pain
Reassure the mother and the child

options.text: Education about the risk using social media
Educating daycare providers on poisoning risks
Provide parents with education material regarding safety
Enforce legislation to require childproof caps on hazardous household cleaners and medicines

There is no history of fever, cough or diarrhea. The girl has been exclusively breastfed for good time every 3-4 hours. On physical examination, her growth parameters are at 90th percentile for age. A 2-year-old boy presents to the paediatrician with severe testicular pain and swelling that had just started 2 hours before. The child is nauseous and has vomited twice. The parents report a similar episode that had happened 3 weeks ago but was of a very short duration. The scrotum is swollen and tender and does not transilluminate. No contraction of the cremaster muscle can be provoked by stroking the inner part of the thigh. Blood pressure 110/70 mmg Heart rate 160 /min Respiratory rate 50 /min Temperature 36.6° C Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 5-year-old boy presents with fever and a rash on his lower limbs, 2 weeks after developing a sore throat. There is also a history of abdominal pain and painful knees and ankles. Physical examination confirms palpable purpuric lesions on the lower limbs that do not blanch on pressure (see lab result). ESR 92 2-10 mm/h Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is the most appropriate investigation? A.Contrast barium enema

options.text: Plain Abdomen X-ray D.Abdominal CT scan

questions.stem: A 1-month-old baby is brought to the clinic with signs of constipation, abdominal distension, and bilious vomiting. The parents explain that constipation has been a problem since the baby's birth. Which of the following tests has the highest diagnostic value?

A 7-month-old baby presents to the Emergency Department with irritability, and intermittent crying during which he pulls up his legs, followed by periods with no discomfort for the last 4 hours. He had started to vomit just before his parents brought him. On examination, the child looked ill and lethargic, with a distended abdomen, and a palpable mass in the right upper quadrant Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
A young child is brought to the Emergency Department after ingesting a large amount of baby aspirin. Which of the following is the most likely acid-base imbalance?

options.text: Respiratory acidosis followed by metabolic acidosis
Metabolic alkalosis followed by respiratory alkalosis
Metabolic acidosis followed by respiratory alkalosis
Respiratory alkalosis followed by metabolic acidosis

questions.stem: A 12-month-old girl presents to the Emergency Department with cramping, colicky abdominal pain progressively developing over the past 12 hours. She has had 2 episodes of vomiting. On physical examination, the child is irritable, and there is abdominal tenderness. Vital signs are normal. During the examination, the child passed a bloody stool with mucus. Lab testing and ultrasound shows leucocytosis and a doughnut-shaped image, respectively. Which of the following is the most appropriate step in management?

A 7-year-old boy presents with recurring upper abdominal pain and occasional vomiting The child has not gained any weight since the beginning of……. Which of the following antibiotics should be prescribed?
Which of the following is the most appropriate age to do Red reflex test?

options.text: 6 months until cooperative for vision testing

questions.stem: A 9-month-old boy presents to the clinic with skin rash noticed by his parents over the past few weeks. His parents are known to have eczema before. Which of the following is the typical site of eczematous plaques at this age?

An 8-year-old boy presents to the clinic with skin rash noticed by his parent over the past few weeks. His parents are known to have eczema before. Which of the following is the typical site of eczematous plaques at this age?

A 14-year-old boy presents to the clinic with skin rash noticed by his parents over the past few weeks. His parents are known to have eczema before. Which of the following is the typical site of eczematous plaques at this age?

A 5-year-old boy who has been treated for eczema with increasing strength of topical steroid is presenting with worsening eczematous plaques on flexural surfaces of his elbows and knees. Which of the following is the best next step in the management?

options.text: Referral to dermatologist to start narrow-band UV-B phototherapy
Inquire about parent compliance with the treatment and answer their concerns

questions.stem: A 10-year-old girl presented to the clinic with pruritic, eczematous plaques over her flexural region and xerosis. Good bathing practice and adequate hydration are recommended to the patient. Which of the following is considered a good bathing practice recommendation?

options.text: Emollients are not important after good prolonged bathing
Olive oil is superior to coconut oil in decreasing severity
Using strong soap cleansers is more effective than non-soap cleansers
Emollient choice is highly dependent on provider and patient predilection

questions.stem: A 5-year-old boy presents to the clinic with pruritic, eczematous plaques over his flexural region and xerosis. Good bathing practice and adequate hydration are recommended to the patient. Which of the following is considered a good bathing practice recommendation?

options.text: Using non-soap cleansers is preferred to avoid irritation
Emollients are not important after good prolonged bathing
Lotions have been proven to be more effective than creams
Olive oil is superior to coconut oil in decreasing severity

questions.stem: A 2-month-old girl brought to the Well Baby Clinic. On examination, she has an absent red reflex in her left eye. She is otherwise healthy and growing well with no concerns from her parents. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step evaluation?

options.text: CT of the brain and orbits
MRI of the brain and orbits
Reassurance of the parent as this is a normal variation
Dilated eye examination under sedation by an ophthalmologist

questions.stem: A 2-month-old girl brought to the Well Baby Clinic. On examination, she has an absent red reflex in her left eye. She is otherwise healthy and growing well with no concerns from her parents. Which of the following is the most likely tumour in such a patient?

A 7-year-old boy presented to the Emergency Room with acute stridor, tachypnea, pallor and hypotension. In quick history, the mother mentioned he was attending a party in the school and that he has food allergy. Which of the following is the first step in management?

A 3-year-old boy presented with his family to the Emergency Room after ingestion unknown amount of paracetamol tablets. He is quiet, with accepted vital sign and normal examination. According to his mother, the bottle was containing small amount of the syrup, and she found some of it spelled over his clothes. He is observed for 4 hours and clinically there is no change on his condition. Which of the following is the proper disposition for him?

An 8-year-old girl presents to the Emergency Room by her mother after ingestion of large amount of acetaminophen tablets. According to the mother, she ingested full 2 packs, containing 20 tablets. 1 day ago after she had fight with her. On examination, she has right upper quadrant abdominal pain, with nausea and vomiting Blood pressure 95/50 mmg, Heart rate 135 /min, Respiratory rate 25 /min, Temperature 36.6 °C, Oxygen saturation 95 % Which phase of acetaminophen toxicity she is at?

An 8-year-old girl presents to the Emergency Room by her mother after ingestion of large amount of acetaminophen tablets. According to the mother, she ingested full 2 packs, containing 20 tablets, 1 day ago after she had fight with her. On examination, she has right upper quadrant abdominal pain, with nausea and vomiting. Blood pressure 95/55 mmHg, Heart rate 130 /min, Respiratory rate 25 /min Temperature 36.6 °C, Oxygen saturation 96 % Which of the following is the most important antidote according to her stage of toxicity?

options.text: Antidote is not indicated at this stage

questions.stem: A 6-year-old girl presents to the Emergency Room with her father after ingestion of large amount of iron tablets. She ingested full bottle containing >20 tablets, 3 hours ago. On examination, she has acute abdominal pain, with nausea, vomiting and diarrhea, and she passed 2 times melaena. Blood pressure 100/60 mmHg, Heart rate 120 /min, Respiratory rate 26 /min, Temperature 36.6 °C Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment option at this stage?

options.text: No antidote required at this stage

questions.stem: Newborn delivered with ventouse due to malposition. While assessment in the nursery, a hematoma from bleeding below the periosteum confined within the margins of the skull sutures noted. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is a known side effect of beclomethasone use in children?

A 3-year-ald boy presents with painless abdominal distension, he has had occasional attacks of abdominal pain, vomiting, and bloody urine. On examination, there is a smooth firm mass in the right loin, an absent iris and undescended testes (see lab results). Urinalysis Result (Normal Values): Color: Clear (Clear or light yellow) Appearance: Turbid Clear Specific gravity: 1.025 (1.001-1.030) pH: 7.5 (4.3-8) Leukocytes: 5 (0-3 per high power field) Erythrocytes: 15 (0-2 per high power field) Color: Clear (Clear or light yellow) Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 14-month-old girl is brought to the clinic with vomiting and diarrhoea. The mother reports her child is less active. On examination, she has mild dehydration with an estimated fluid deficit of 5% (see lab results). Weight: 10 Kg Sodium: 128 (134-146 mmol/L) Potassium: 3.3 (3.5-5.1 mmol/L) Chloride: 94 (97-108 mmol/L) Bicarbonate: 12 (21-28 mmol/L) How much intravenous fluid (ml/day) should be given?

A 9-year-old boy presents with abdominal pain and swelling of his right ankle. He had had an upper respiratory tract infection 3 weeks earlier. On examination, he had multiple maculopapular lesions (see image and lab result). Test Result (Normal Value) Erythrocytes 15 (0-2 per high power field) Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A child is brought to the clinic with chronic proteinuria renal disease and hypertension. The parents are concerned about progression to end-stage renal disease. Which of the following drugs would be most useful in preventing this progression?

A 14-year-old boy presents to the clinic complaining of "brown urine" for the past 3 days. 2 weeks ago, he had 2 days of fever and a sore throat, but he improved spontaneously and has been well ever since. On physical examination, only periorbital edema is noted (see lab results). Blood pressure 136/92 mmHg Heart rate 98 /min Respiratory rate 28 /min Temperature 37 ° C Urinalysis Result Normal Values Specific gravity 1.035 1001-1030 Proteins ++ Absent Blood ++ Absent Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A newborn presents with jaundice 12 hours after birth. At 36 hours after birth, the jaundice became worse and blood smear was performed (see image and lab results). Test Results Normal Values: Hb 91 (112-165 g/L) Reticulocyte 7 (0.2-1.2 %) Total bilirubin 2800( <205 mol/L) Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in the investigation?

A 1-year-old boy is noted to have a microcytic anaemia, on routine screening. A haemoglobin electrophoresis was performed that showed an increased fraction of haemoglobin A2. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A newborn presents with jaundice 12 hours after birth. At 36 hours after birth, the jaundice became worse and blood smear was performed (see image and lab results). questions.stem: A 12-month-old boy is brought to the clinic with a complaint of decreased appetite. The child was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been fed with cow's milk formula since the age of 9 months. The body weight is 13.6 kg (> 97th percentile) and the length is 75 cm (50th percentile). Physical examination confirms pallor of the skin and buccal mucous membranes. There is also a systolic heart murmur and a palpable spleen (see image and lab results). A 12-year-old girl presents with bleeding gums while brushing her teeth. This had started 1 week ago after a viral upper respiratory tract infection. A 5-year-old boy presents with sudden and severe bone pain in his hands and feet. On examination, he appears dehydrated (see lab results). Blood pressure 110/60 mmHg Heart rate 125 min Respiratory rate 28 /min Temperature 38.8° C rectal Test Result Normal Values Hb 108 112-165 g/L HCT 0.30 0.32-0.42 MCV 76 80-95 fl Which of the following is responsible for this clinical presentation?

Which of the following signs are more likely to be associated with haemophilia?

A 15-year-old patient presents for a routine check-up (see lab results). Test Result Normal Values RBC 5.3 4.4-4.8 x 1012/L WBC 68 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Hb 98 112-165 g/L MCV 69 80-95 fl MCHC 261 260-340 g/L Reticulocyte 1.0 0.2-1.2% Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-day-old infant was delivered normally at home (? “a]ended”) by a midwife. He had never been to a hospital, but now noted to have bleeding from the umbilical cord that seems increasing in severity. He has been breastfed since delivery. The mother had a normal perinatal period, but was diagnosed with epilepsy 10 years ago, and has been taking phenobarbital (see lab results). Bleeding time 3.8 up to 4 min Prothrombin time 21 12-14 sec APTT 46 30-40 sec Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment? A.Corticosteroids

HB 40 112-165 RDW 14 11.5-14.5% MCV 70 80-95f Reticulocyte 2.4 0.2-1.2% WBC 5.5 4.5-10.5 x 109/L RBC 5.8 4.6-4.8 x 1012/L HB electrophoresis Hb A2 30 2-3% Hb F 50 1-2% Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 53-day-old boy is referred to the Paediatric Clinic for investigation of anaemia. He was born full term and he is a known case of G6PD deficiency. On examination, both height and weight are in the 10th percentile, the rest of the examination is normal (see lab results). Hb 70 112-165 g/L Platelet count 350 150-400 x 109/L Total bilirubin 25.1 <20.5 mol/L Urinalysis Result Normal Values Color Clear Clear or light yellow Leukocytes 0 0-3 per high power field Erythrocytes 0 0-2 per high power field Which of the following is the best management?

On examination, she looks pale, had a palpable liver and her spleen is 6 cm below the costal margin (see lab results). Blood pressure 93/55 mmHg Heart rate 169 /min Respiratory rate 28 /min Temperature 37.5° C Hb 52 112-165 g/L Platelet count 102 150-400 × 109/L Sickle cell screen Positive Nil Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-year-old boy presents to the Paediatric Clinic for a routine examination. He was born at full term with a birth weight of 3450 grams. The mother breastfeed him, for a year and since then he has been fed on whole formula milk with a balanced diet. His weight gain and development have always been normal for his age. At a routine check with one year, a haemoglobin level of 105 g/L was recorded and oral administration of ferrous sulphate drops was started. 6 months later the haemoglobin level was 103 g/L and lead to an increase of the daily dose of ferrous sulphate. Another 3 months later there was no significant rise in the level again. The mother reports having continued giving the ferrous sulphate drops since then. The paediatrician orders a blood cell count (see lab results). Hb 91 112-165 g/L RDW 13.1 11.5-14.5 pm WBC 10.4 4.5-10.5 x 109/L MCV 62 80-95 fl Reticulocyte 0.8 0.2-1.2 % Platelet count 280 150-400 x 109/L Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in definitive diagnosis?

A 4-year-old boy presents with a 1-day history of abdominal pain and vomiting. He was afebrile and has no diarrhea. He has bilateral knee pain, and there was some tenderness of the knee joints, but no effusions. Within 24 hours, he developed a rash on his legs and buttocks, which is petechiae and purpuric, and his platelet count was normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old girl presents with fever, many bruises over the entire body, and pain in both legs. Examination confirms pallor, ecchymoses and petechiae on the face, trunk and extremities (see lab results). Hb 63 112-165 g/L WBC 28 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Platelets count 29 150-400 x 109/L Which of the following would be the most appropriate diagnostic test?

A 5-year-old developed acute abdominal pain in the upper right quadrant, following an upper respiratory tract infection. On examination, there are normal bowel sounds and no rebound tenderness (see lab results and report). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 110 /min Respiratory rate 24 /min Temperature 38.9° C Hb 72 112-165 g/L WBC 12 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Reticulocyte 7.2 0.2-1.2 % Peripheral smear: Normochromic normocytic red blood cells with target cells and red cell inclusion bodies. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-year-old child presents with bruising and generalised petechiae, mostly on the legs. The child has always been healthy. The parents report that he had an upper respiratory infection 2 weeks before that resolved without medication (see lab results). Test Results (Normal Values) Hb 131 (112-165 g/L) НСТ 0.39 (0.32-0.42) WBC 6.8 (4.5-10.5 x 109/L) Lymphocytes 22 (20-40 %) Monocytes 2 (2-8 %) Neutrophils 58 (40-60%) Platelets count 15 (150-400 x 109/L) Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 6-year-old girl presents to the Emergency Department with a history of feeling unwell and redness over the last 10 hours. On examination, she looks pale, had a palpable liver and her spleen was 6 cm below the costal margin (see lab results). Blood pressure 93/55 mmH Heart rate 169 /min Respiratory rate 28 /min Temperature 37.5° C Hb 58 112-165 g/L Platelet count 98 150-400 x 109/L Sickle cell screen Positive Which of the following is the most useful investigation?

An infant girl, born to a 24-year-old woman, diagnosed clinically as Down's syndrome. The mother asked about the risk in any future pregnancy. Which of the following is the appropriate investigation to determine this risk?

options.text: Karyotyping for this infant and mother

questions.stem: A 7-year-old boy has had recurrent upper and lower respiratory tract bacterial infections since infancy. On examination, he has eczema and areas of ecchymosis on his skin. His brother and a paternal uncle are similarly affected (see lab results). Test Result (Normal Values) Hb 108 (112-165 g/L) WBC 7.6 (4.5-10.5 x 109/L) Platelets count 40 (150-400 × 109/L) Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 14-month-old boy is brought to the clinic with severe gram-positive bacterial pneumonia, was referred to the hospital by the family physician. This is his third infection in 4 months. He has 2 healthy sisters aged 3 and 5 years. The family lost a boy at 10 months of age to bacterial pneumonia 6 years ago. The family doctor has sent along some blood test results that shows low all classes of serum immunoglobulin levels, few B cells, but normal numbers and functioning of T cells. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 36-year-old woman with 10-year history of infertility due to male factor is brought to Emergency Room with vaginal bleeding and abdominal pain. Thereafter, she progresses to complete abortion at 8 weeks' gestation while awaiting for admission. She is crying and her husband is an overwhelmed emotionally. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Explore, identify and respond to the couple emotion
Admission to postpartum ward based on her condition
Explore, identify the cause and respond to the couple with management plan

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman G5 P0030 and her husband present to the clinic at 9 weeks' gestation with mild spotting after an intercourse, no abdominal pain reported. She has a history of 3 previous first trimester abortions. The couple are blaming themselves for the bleeding. They show a strong presentation of emotion. Which of the following is best way to deal with this situation?

options.text: Identify their emotion and calm them down
Empathic response is sufficient to calm them down
Understand their emotion without showing that to them
Explore and validate their emotion with empathic response

questions.stem: A 28-year-old G4 P0121 at 28 weeks' gestation, visitor to the country, presents with labor-like pain for 2 hours. On arrival, while trying to take history and to perform examination, the patient could not understand due to language barrier. She looks anxious and worries about her pregnancy, which is similar experience to her 4-year-old boy whom delivered prematurely. Which of the following is the most appropriate step in communication?

options.text: Showing an understanding to her emotion is inappropriate because of language barrier
Showing that her emotions cannot be validated because she had similar experience
Showing that her emotions are understood
Calling a help from other colleagues

questions.stem: A 36-year-old newly diagnosed hypertensive man presents for follow-up visit. After a thorough assessment, the physician discussed with him his diagnosis, the aetiology of his illness, the probable side effects of the prescribed medicine, and the prognosis of his illness and finally the restrictions the patient might experience due to the illness. Which of the following professional skills is the physician used?

A 45-year-old man presented to the clinic with large thyroid nodule otherwise asymptomatic, that was proven to be papillary thyroid carcinoma. The physician is planning to send him for total thyroidectomy but the patient is afraid from the surgical complication. The treating physician needs to create a lasting impression at the end of the consultation. Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Patient's agreement for referral is not required
Avoid discussing the serious surgical complications
Briefly explain the action plan with possible expected and unexpected outcome

questions.stem: A 50-year-old woman recently diagnosed with papillary thyroid carcinoma. Which of the following is an example of positive communication skill while explaining the management option of her disease?

options.text: Ask a patient to repeat your instructions
Interrupt a patient when she ask questions
Inform patients when you cannot spend any more time with them

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman recently diagnosed with Cushing's syndrome. which of the following will be considered as negative communication skill while explaining for her the course of her disease?

options.text: Looking directly at a patient when speaking
Interrupt a patient when he/she does not understand
Encouraging the patient to ask questions

questions.stem: A 22-year-old women presented to Surgery Clinic wearing revealing clothes, she come up very close to the doctor asking personal question in sedative tone with a language that is different from attending nurse language. Which is the following is the best response by the doctor?

options.text: Call for other nurse talk same language

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man presented with history of skin lesion over the right check (see report). Skin biopsy: Malignant melanoma. Which is the following is best way to make the patient comply with medical advice?

options.text: He believes you are professional and right
Taking time to provide information and gain his trust

questions.stem: A 29-year-old man presents with a 2-year history of intense fear before giving classes as a teacher in a secondary school. He claims that it is only a matter of time before a major teaching mistake is made. Which of the following phobias is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old man presents to the clinic with 2 2-month history of anxiety, irritability, impotence, difficulty in sleeping, and a weight loss of 10 kg. There is no evidence of marital disharmony or any external causes for the patient's anxiety. The physical examination was normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is the most likely characteristic of a major depressive illness?

A 52-year-old woman presents with a 5-day history of insomnia and crying because of the death of a sibling. The patient has not slept for the last 2 days. Which of the following is the most appropriate short course of therapy?
Which of the following factors indicates a poor prognosis for schizophrenia?
A 27-year-old man who lost his spouse 2 months ago after a prolonged illness presents with a sad mood, decreased appetite, and sleep disturbance. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following drug mechanisms of action is most appropriate to treat obsessional behavioural disorder?
Which of the following medications causes insomnia, anxiety and restlessness?

A 60-year-old man newly diagnosed with depression started on 30 mg amitriptyline each night. Shortly after the beginning of treatment, he complained of dizziness every morning. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.text: Change to a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor
Advise to take the medication with food
Advice to take the medication in the morning
Change amitriptyline dose to 10 mg 3 times a day

questions.stem: Which of the following is a potential side effect of amitriptyline?

A 12-year-old obese boy presents to the Primary Care Clinic with a history of being teased by children at school and, as a result, has considered "taking a lot of pills to just go to sleep and not wake up." Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

Which of the following reuptake inhibitors is the best treatment?

A 45-year-old man presents in an anxious, tearful state. He complains of chronic upper abdominal pain and is certain that he has stomach cancer, but no one believes him. He has seen 6 different physicians in the past year and has had a Gl series and barium enema performed, an ultrasound of the abdomen twice, and a CT scan. The patient was thinking of going to a herbal clinic next. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 16-year-old girl is brought by her father to the Emergency Department with complaints of tachypnoea, light-headedness, paraesthesia and palpitations. Her father gives the history of her recent failure in her math test. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
