There is symmetrical weakness of the face and all four extremities. Deep tendon reflexes are absent, and sensations are intact. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old man presents with an 8-week history of severe headache. The headaches have occurred at the same time each day, about 2 a.m. and last around 30 minutes. Headaches are accompanied by lacrimation and redness of the right eye. Which of the following is the best to prevent this type of headache?

A 55-year-old man with diabetes and hypertension complains of pain in the right eve and double vision when looking to the left. On examination, there is ptosis, limited adduction, elevation, and depression of the right eye. The pupils are equal and reactive in both sides. Fundoscopy and other cranial nerve are normal as well as the rest of neurological examination of the upper and lower limbs.Which of the following is the most likely cause of these findings?

An 18-year-old boy known to have grand mal epilepsy since childhood is brought to the Emergency Department after having repeated tonic-clonic seizures at home. He is compliant with his medication, which is sodium valproate. In the Emergency Department, he is unconscious and continuously convulsing. After oxygenation and securing the airway, which of the following intravenous drugs should be administered?
In a patient with Guillain Barre Syndrome, which of the following is the best treatment option?

A 30-year-old woman presents with pain in the right eye associated progressive visual loss over 2 days. She also reported a numbness in the left side of the face and weakness in both lower limbs. Physical examination revealed reduced visual acuity, loss of direct light reflex with preserved indirect light reflex in the right eye. Lower limbs examination showed weakness, clasp knife rigidity, hyperrefiexia in both knee and ankle jerks. There is loss of all modalities of sensation in both lower limbs. Which of the following has the highest diagnostic value?

An 80-year-old man has 2-month history of progressive gait disturbance and incontinence Lately he has been forgetful, confused, and withdrawn. His gait is slow, short-stepped and with tendency to fall backward (see report). Brain CT scan: shows dilated ventricles. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old man presents with a sudden onset of unilateral peripheral facial nerve weakness 1 hour ago. He has no medical illness and not on any medication. Which of the following is most likely to shorten his symptoms?

A 14-year-old boy with a history of epilepsy complains of progressive lower limbs weakness and tingling sensation since last two days. His face, trunk and upper limbs are not involved. He has had fever and runny nose 10 days ago. On physical examination, there is 3/5 muscle strength in both lower limbs with absent reflexes. Blood pressure 120/80 mmH Heart rate 85 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 37.4° C Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old boy is brought to the Emergency Department after an episode of convulsion that involved all limbs 1 hour ago. It continued for 3 minutes and associated with drooling and loss of consciousness. He had runny nose, mild cough and fever for last 3 days. On physical examination, he was fully active with mild congested throat. Blood pressure 120/80 mmHg Heart rate 98 /min Respiratory rate 22 /min Temperature 37.9° C Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
In which conditions circumcision should be avoided?

A 6-year-old girl presents with sudden involuntary abnormal movement in her limbs that started 10 minutes ago. It was associated with inability to speak. Few hours ago, she took metoclopramide, hyoscine butylbromide and oral rehydration solution after being diagnosed with viral gastroenteritis. The physical examination showed facial grimacing and protrusion of tongue. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 6-year-old boy presents to the Outpatient Department with frequent and brief episodes of rapid eyes blinking for 2 weeks. The episodes are not associated with pain, redness, tearing or discharge. During the episode, he communicated well with his parents. The physical examination shows normal visual acuity. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is an absolute contraindication for thrombolvtic therapy?

options.text: Blood pressure at presentation of 180/110 mmH

questions.stem: A 60-year-old patient presented with a 6-month history of a dull achy abdominal swelling associated with weight loss. Examination confirmed a 20x20 cm firm, non-tender, intra-abdominal mass (see report). Abdominal CT scan:Lobulated soft tissue mass arising from retro-peritoneum, there was multiple hypodense liver lesions. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 58-year-old woman presented with a right thigh mass that measured 5 x 6 cm (see report). Core biopsy: High grade sarcoma. Which of the following is most appropriate staging image?
Which of the following is the most appropriate biopsy for a limb sarcoma?

A 44-year-old man presented with a 6-month history of vague central abdominal pain. CT scan of abdomen: Presence of 20x10 cm retroperitoneal mass. No enlarged mesenteric or paraortic lymph nodes noted. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old woman presents with bilateral leg deep vein thrombosis. She has a history of recurrent still births (see lab result). Test Result Normal Value APTT 55 30-40 sec Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Where is the most common primary location of basal cell carcinoma?

A 75-year-old man presents to the Outpatient Department, complaining of back pain and increasing difficulty with passing urine (see lab results). Prostate-specific antigen 84 (0-4 pg/L) Alkaline phosphatase 410 (39-117 IU/L) Albumin 41 (34-56 g/L) Gamma glutamyltransferase 19 (6 to 37 IU/L) Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is the most likely source?

A 50-year-old diabetic man presented with a 5-year history of an unhealed foot ulcer. Physical examination confirmed a 2x2 cm irregular-shaped ulcer at the dorsal aspect of the first toe with pearly white discoloration. Biopsy of the ulcer reported as pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
A 58-year-old woman presented with a right thigh mass that measured 5 x6 cm (see report). Core biopsy: High grade sarcoma. Which of the following is most appropriate staging image?
A young man presented with a chronic infection of both axillae. Examination confirmed the presence of multiple discharging sinuses. Which of the following is the most likely source?

A 35-year-old man has been in the Intensive Care Unit with severe pancreatitis, ventilator dependence, and pneumonia for 2 weeks. He is receiving nutrition parenterally (see lab results). Platelets count 184 150-400 x 109/L Total bilirubin 4.6 3.5-16.5 mol/L APTT 36 30-40 sec INR 2,1 0.8-1.2 Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
A 65-year-old man who is asymptomatic and has no known allergies is seen for a general examination. What is the best approach for pneumococcus immunization?

options.text: No evidence supports vaccinating this patient

questions.stem: An 82-year-old woman at long term nursing facility who wears hearing aids and is found to have bilateral cerumen impaction, a Weber test that lateralizes to the right. and a bilaterally positive Rinne test. Which of the following is the most likely explanation?

options.text: Prebycusis that is greater on the right
Conductive hearing loss that is greater on the right
Chronic serous otitis media that is greater on the left

questions.stem: A 91-year-old man with poor performance status, dementia, and multiple medical problems who has been diagnosed with an adenocarcinoma of an unknown primary site and has upper abdominal lymphadenopathy, liver lesions, and pulmonary nodules. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Exploratory laparotomy with biliary bypass procedure
Excisional biopsy to identify the primary site

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best exercise to improve the function of a 68-year-old woman?

A 72-year-old man complains of difficulty in getting up from the chair for the last 3 months. History reveals he has controlled type 2 diabetes and long standing hypertension. Which of the following is the most leading type of injury in this patient?
A 35-year-old nulliparous on treatment for hyperprolactinemia for the past year. When would pituitary imaging be indicated?

options.text: Prolactin level is twice the normal

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman is 10 days postpartum and breastfeeding on demand. For 48 hours before presentation to the clinic, she has had episodes of chills with feeling weak and tired. Physical examination revealed redness of the left breast, and tenderness and excoriation of the areola. A left breast tender, mobile 3 cm dominant lump was found in the upper outer quadrant on palpation and left axillary lymphadenopathy was present (see lab results). Blood pressure 110/70 mmH, Heart rate 115 /min, Respiratory rate 20/min, Temperature 39.0° C Test Result Normal Values Hb 115 120-160 g/L WBC 14 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Neutrophils 80 40-60% Band cells 7 3-5% Basophils 1 0.5-1 % Eosinophils 1 1-4 % Lymphocytes 50 20-40 % Monocytes 2 2-8 % Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old woman complained of swelling on one side of the labia. The swelling was first noticed 24 hours ago and has not improved despite warm tub soaking. There was a non-tender 3 cm slightly mobile cystic mass at approximately 7 o'clock on the right side of the vaginal introitus. Blood pressure 110/70 mmH, Heart rate 76 /min, Respiratory rate 18 /min, Temperature 37° C Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 56-year-old postmenopausal woman presents with a 1-year history of recurrent irritation in the pubic area. The patient reported itchiness with blood-stained discharge at times. The patient has tried a metronidazole suppositories as well as topical cream over the labia with little relief. Recently. the patient feels a pea-sized lump on the labia. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 68-year-old woman underwent a total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo- oophorectomy. 3 days following the surgery, urinary catheter was removed and she was able to independently void 1 hour with an output of 35 ml/hr. She has been receiving fluids by continuous intravenous drip. She described the incisional pain as uncomfortable and rates it at a level 5 on the pain assessment scale. For pain relief, she was taking Ibuprofen 800 milligrams every 6 hours. The doctor considered her ready for discharge (see lab results). Blood pressure 118/68 mmHg, Heart rate 70 /min, Respiratory rate 20 /min, Temperature 37.4° C oral НСТ 0.37 0.37-0.48 Hb 122 120-160 g/L Which of the following would be a reason for this patient to remain in hospital?

A young primigravida presents with significant edema of the lower extremities and hands. The patient was admitted for evaluation and management. Blood pressure 150/95 mmHg, Heart rate 76 /min, Respiratory rate 18/min, Temperature 36.6° C Which of the following would be the most appropriate management?
What is the most common type of vulvar neoplasms?

A 45-year-old woman presented with itching of the vulva. On careful inspection in a bright light, an elevated localized watery red lesion measuring 0.5 cm was seen. She is diagnosed with vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia with carcinoma in situ. Which of the following is the best management?
Which of the following estrogen is the most abundant in human pregnancy?

An 18-year-old girl is complaining of the appearance of lesions that are firm, smooth and skin- colored. They located at the anogenital area and mons pubis. Occasionally they get inflamed and become red and are described to be of 2 to 3 mm in diameter with occasional itching (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 70-year-old comes to the clinic complaining of a slowly enlarging lesion at the labia majora, which does not heal and bleeds when traumatized (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old obese woman notices soft, skin-colored, brown papules with short, thin stalks that are 1 to 3 mm developing on the multiple areas of the inguinal folds. She states that when they are traumatized, they become blue and purpuric (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A couple suffering from infertility asked the feto-maternal consultant about surrogacy as an option to treat their infertility. The hospital does not offer the service and the consultant is not sure if surrogacy is legal in Saudi Arabia. Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Inform the couple that hospital doesn't provide the service
Warn the couple that surrogacy might be illegal in Saudi Arabia
Refer them to a colleague who has connections with surrogacy canters
Give them appointment after few weeks to have enough time to review the topic

questions.stem: A 23-year-old nulliparous woman with a history of infertility 2 years. Her menstrual cycle is regularly coming every 29 days. Which of the following is best used to confirm ovulation?

A 33-year-old woman delivered vaginally with right mediolateral episiotomy. An hour later, she was found to have an expanding 7 x 5 cm bluish, tense, and painful swelling of the perineum. Which of the following is the best management?

A 30-year-old woman gravida 4, para 3 woman presents to Antenatal Clinic at 32 weeks' gestation with headache and swelling of the feet. At the initial antenatal visit, there was +2 pitting edema of the lower extremities and the face appears swollen. Dipstick of the urine shows proteinuria. The fundal height is 28 cm and fetal heart rate was 140-150 beats per minute with good variability. She reports regular fetal movements. Blood pressure 150/100 mmg, Heart rate 90 /min, Respiratory rate 26 /min, Temperature 37.1° C Which additional clinical finding would be associated with intrauterine growth restriction?
A 34-year-old multiparous woman presents at 37 weeks' twins gestation with regular contractions. Which of the following fetal presentations is favourable for vaginal delivery?
A 2-day-old baby seen in clinic with mother for counseling about breastfeeding. Which of the following indicates adequate breastfeeding in a baby?
A 20-day-old premature baby brought to the clinic with the mother for counselling about breast feeding. Which of the following is low in mother's milk after premature delivery?
A 53-year-old woman has missed her period over the last 12 months. Which of the following hormones is likely to be altered as a result of the condition?

A 43-year-old woman G9 P5126 breastfeeding of her 5-month-old daughter comes to the clinic because of positive home pregnancy test. She does not know her last menstrual period. Which of the following would be the most useful method to determine her estimated date of delivery?

options.text: Transvaginal ultrasound as early as possible in the first trimester

questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman presents to the clinic complaining of heavy bleeding for the last 4-months. After taking a detailed history and full physical examination, the patient and her gynecologist reach a plan of management and decide to undergo a hysteroscopy. Which of the following is the most common complication of hysteroscopy?
A 22-year-old woman is seen in the Preconception Clinic. She is planning to get pregnant during winter season. Which of the following vaccine is recommended during preconception period?
A 26-year-old woman is seen in the preconception clinic for a routine visit. Which of the following is recommended during preconception period?
A 35-year-old P2002 woman presented with secondary amenorrhea for 8 months. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
A 25-year-old newly married woman presented to the Outpatient Clinic for routine gynecological examination. Which of the following has the highest diagnostic value?
A 34-year-old woman with a history of recurrent pregnancy loss was seen in the clinic. Which of the following is the best predictor for pregnancy complications?
A 40-year-old pregnant woman at 24 weeks of gestation with fever and did not seek any medical advice. What is the most likely reason for illness denial?
A 34-year-old woman came to the clinic with a history of primary infertility for 3 years. She was anxious, worried and depressed. Which of the following is a positive body language?

A 23-year-old nulligravida patient complains of inability to become pregnant after 3 months of trying. Patient periods are regular and normal. She had no prior reproductive problems. She currently is not on any contraception. Examination is normal. Her husband is 25-year-old healthy and has one autistic cousin and one with trisomy 21. Which of the following is the best action?

A 17-year-old woman comes at 39 weeks' gestation to the Emergency Department with no previous antenatal care. She delivered a healthy baby boy normally with no complications reported. Then she was given an injection of RhoGAM. What is the indication of RhoGAM?

options.text: Mother is Rh- and the baby is Rh+
Father is RH+ and the baby is Rh-
Mother is Rh+ and the baby is Rh-
Father is Rh- and the baby is Rh+

questions.stem: A 4-month-old boy presented to the clinic with a rash over the neck for 3 days. The rash is not itchy (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old child presented to Emergency Room with difficulty breathing. lip swelling and spreading skin rash. On examination, marked airway swelling observed with rash cover all the body. The mother said he was attending a party at his friend's house and she was not with him. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-month-old infant found dead at his bed. According to the mother, he was feeding normally with usual activity. No history of fever or other abnormality. On examination, no sign of trauma or bruises on the skin. Baby gram was negative for fracture. Which of the following history's part is important to make the diagnosis?

A 2-month-old infant found dead at his bed. According to the mother, he was feeding normally with usual activity. No history of fever or other abnormality. On examination, no sign of trauma or bruises on the skin. Baby gram was negative for fracture. Mother is divorced and known smoker. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is the predominant immunoglobulin secreted by breast milk?

A 32-year-old man had excision and primary closure that was 5x3 cm on the forearm, 1 year ago. He presented with an overgrowth at the scar site that extended beyond the surgical scar margins, it started few weeks after the surgery and gradually increased in size. Which of the following most accurately describes the lesion?
Which of the following is most likely to cause small bowel distension?

A patient notices one or more sharply marginated, scaling, and red plaques predominantly involving only the vulva. Psoriasis is suspected. Which of the following is required for a definitive diagnosis of psoriasis?
A 20-year-old is suffering from vitiligo, which involves the vulva. Which of the following is the cause for this condition?

options.text: Result from overuse of irritants locally

questions.stem: A 40-year-old P5005 woman presented to the Clinic. She has a strong family history of cancer where both her mother and sister died of cancer. BMI 31 kg/m2 Which of the following is the most appropriate counselling?

options.text: Meet nutritional needs through diet alone

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most objective method for identifying high-risk patients for peri- operative morbidity and mortality?

options.text: Revised cardiac risk index of lee

questions.stem: A 35-year-old man patient comes to the clinic with a painless ulcer on his penis. History reveals, he had an unprotected sexual encounter 3 weeks ago. Examination shows that the lesion has a clean base with sharp margins, and there are non-tender palpable regional lymph nodes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
which of the following is the percentage prevalence of smoking among Saudi adult men?

A 42-year-old man presented to the Primary Care Clinic for the routine checkup. He has been smoking 1- pack of cigarettes a day for 22 years. He has no intention of quitting and feels fine. Which of the following is the most appropriate cessation approach?

options.text: Set a "quit date" with the patient
Give clear, personalized advice to quit
Refer him to classes for smoking cessation

questions.stem: A 45-year-old smoker came to the clinic for his diabetes follow-up. During discussion, he acknowledged that smoking is not good for his health. He plans to quit this year. According to the Stages of Change Model, at what stage of change is this patient?
Tobacco products consists of thousands of chemical compounds including nicotine. Which of the following is the most outcome related to nicotine substance?
Which of the following is the most approved evidence-based intervention to be used in smoking cessation?
Which of the following confirms proper position of orotracheal intubation?
A trauma patient who lost 25% of his blood volume. Which of the following is most expected to be decreased?

An 18-year-old man involved in a hit and run, presented to the Emergency Room with multiple facial fractures and signs of severe brain injury. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 42-year-old woman involved in a head on collision arrived at the Emergency Room talking coherently, with the following vital signs. Her examination revealed equal air entry bilaterally with ecchymosis on her anterior chest wall, distended neck veins and her abdomen is soft and lax. Blood pressure 90/60 mmH, Heart rate 130 /min, Respiratory rate 18/min Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
An 18-year-old man presented to the Emergency Room with bleeding from a deep 10 cm anterior laceration of his right thigh. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Put direct pressure on the wound
Put pressure on the femoral artery above the wound

questions.stem: Which of the following factors is the most important in determining the success of a smoking cessation program?

A 45-year-old man newly diagnosed with type 2 diabetes presents to the clinic for futhur management. He is on time for the appointment, but because of an emergency case, the physician arrive late to the clinic. When the physician walks in, the patient appears extremely angry. Which of the following is the most appropriate response by the physician?

options.text: Explore the reasons for the anger
Help the patient understand their anger
Empathise with newly diagnosed diabetic patient

questions.stem: A 56-year-old man presents to the clinic for evaluation. The physician has difficulty in obtaining accurate information regarding reason of attendance. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in consultation?

options.text: Use medical terms that the patient understands
Control the interview with direct questions
Involve the patient in the treatment plan

questions.stem: A 76-year-old man admitted with diagnosis of pneumonia has fluctuating levels of attention, changes in awareness, and a marked disturbance of the sleep/wake cycle. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?

options.text: Isolation in a quiet, dark room
Allow a relative to stay with the patient

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman delivered a healthy baby 3 months ago. She is currently undergoing psychotherapy for postpartum depression. Which of the following is the most appropriate to be added to optimize treatment?

options.text: Prescribe very small doses of imipramine

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman presented to the police department with bruises all over her body. Which of the following is the main predictor of a domestic violence?

A 23-year-old newly married woman came to the police department after beaten up by her husband. Which of the following is the most consistent predictor of attitudes supporting the use of violence against women?
A 33-year-old woman was seen at 34 weeks of gestation with a broken arm after beaten up by her husband. When is the most common time that increases the risk of violence by an intimate partner?
A 24-year-old woman experienced sexual harassment in the workplace. Who is the most likely involves in such condition?

A 59-year-old woman attends for the first time to the clinic complaining of abnormal uterine bleeding for the last 2 months and she is extremely concerned about her condition. The last menstrual cycle was 12 years ago. The patient requests admission, preparation and booking for a hysterectomy. Which of the following is the most appropriate response?

options.text: Admit into the hospital to gain confidence
Discuss in referring to an oncologist because of age and risk of malignancy
Calm her down and conduct a detailed informative discussion about best options of her

questions.stem: A 53-year-old woman known diabetic, hypertensive and cardiac arrhythmia on amiodarone, presented to the Emergency Department with 3-days history of progressive redness and pain on her right leg. Examination showed a sharply demarcated red lesion, which was tender with no ulcer, Temperature 38.8 °C. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following sets indicates the 5 A's approach during smoking cessation counselling? A. Ask, advise, assess, assist, arrange follow-up

options.text: Ask, assist, advise, advocate, arrange follow-up
Assess, advocate, ask, advise, arrange follow-up
Advocate, ask, assess, advise, arrange follow-up

questions.stem: What is the minimum number of days per week recommended to practice muscle-strengthening physical activity?
Which of the following is the most appropriate characteristic for a new test as a confirmatory test for a disease diagnosis?

A screening test for liver cirrhosis was administered to 800 people with proven liver cirrhosis and to 800 people without liver cirrhosis. The test results were positive for 200 of the proven cases and 100 of the normal persons. What is the sensitivity of the screening test?
A new screening test for diabetes has a sensitivity of 90% and specificity of 80%. Which of the following is the best interpretation?

options.text: 80% of diabetic patients had positive result
The test was positive for 90% of diabetic patients
For each 100 positive test results, 90% were diabetics

questions.stem: A 77-year-old woman is admitted to Neurology Ward with right hemispheric intracranial bleeding. 5 days after admission the physiotherapist reported verbally to the nurse that the patient left buttock is getting red with skin loss. The nurse forgot to tell the resident and no action was taken. 2 days later, the patient spiked a fever with hypotension. On examination, the resident found purulent discharge from the pressure sore. Which of the following is the best approach to prevent this incident?

An inter was attending Operation Room for laparoscopic nephrectomy for suspicious renal mass. The urologist asked to prep for the right kidney approach. However, the intern remember from his history and exam that it was the left kidney. Which of the following is the most appropriate action by the intern?

options.text: Keep quiet since he might be wrong
Leave OR and check the electronic note
Call the chief intern to ask for guidance
Inform the surgeon about his concern

questions.stem: While doing ward round the consultant surgeon asked the resident to write Pipercillin-Tazobactam for their patient. The pharmacist reported that the patient has a questionable allergy to penicillin. The consultant insisted to write the order. Which of the following is the most appropriate action by the resident?

options.text: Write the order and let the consultant sign it
Write the order then call chief surgeon to complain
Gently refuse to write the order
Write the order and keep quiet fearing retaliation

questions.stem: Which of the following best explains the increase of diseases prevalence when incidence is constant?
which of the following provides the highest level of evidence for establishing effect of exercise on the quality of life?
Which of the following is the most appropriate measurement to estimate the impact of obesity prevention on the prevalence of type 2 diabetes?
Which of the following is recommended to improve the general health of a person?

options.text: Performing regular physical activity C.Switching from cigarette use to waterpipe
Consuming at least 2 servings of fruits and vegetables per day

questions.stem: Which of the following fulfils the minimum recommended time of moderate physical activity for healthy adults?
On average, how many years of life the average smokers are expected to lose?
in a screening program in a population with a low prevalence of a particular disease, what most of the positive results would likely to be?
Natural history of the disease has various stages. In which of the following stages a screening program would be most useful?
Which of the following criteria is supporting the use of a screening test for community screening program?

options.text: The test is quick and easy
Natural history of the disease is not yet clear

questions.stem: Which of the following screening test parameter is most likely to be affected by the disease prevalence?

A 30-year-old man presented to the Surgical Clinic while taking medical history he want his perceptions of why he felt ill and the doctor wants more detail about his symptoms and medical problems. Which is the following the most appropriate response?

options.text: Allow him to complete his thought
Inform him to change his appointment with other doctor
Till him other patient are waiting outside and clinic is busy now
Politely interrupt him and continue with close-ended question

questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman presented with progressive redness over the dorsum of the left hand associated with pain and fever. She gave a history of a knife prick at the affected area 3 days ago. Temperature 37.9 °C Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 50-year-old man who is known to have non-insulin dependent diabetes, presented with a progressive painful swelling on the back of the neck for 5 days. On physical examination, there is a 5x6 cm swelling and redness with multiple discharging openings. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old man was brought to the Emergency Department after being involved in a motor vehicle accident. He opened his eyes spontaneously and responded appropriately to verbal commands. His respiration was shallow and he had left chest wall contusion. He was able to shrug his shoulders but unable to move his elbows or lower limbs. Blood pressure 80/40 mmHg Heart rate 70 /min Respiratory rate 30 /min Which of the following is the most likely cause of the hypotension?

A 45-year old man is just admitted to the Critical Care Unit with polytrauma following road traffic accident because of hypotension. He is sedated and mechanically ventilated. His heart sounds are distant with no added sounds. Lung auscultation showed equal air entry to both sides with no added sounds (see report). Blood pressure 85/55 mmHg Heart rate 110 /min Temperature 36.0 °C Oxygen saturation 100 % Central venous pressure: Right atrial pressure 15 mmHg Chest radiograph: Cardiomegaly and fractured sternum. Both lungs are normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
An unstable trauma patient has confirmed multiple liver lacerations. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 35-year-old man is evaluated in the Orthopedic Ward because of dyspnea, tachycardia and confusion. The patient had fractured left femur for which he undergone internal fixation 2-days ago. He is on enoxaparin as prophylaxis and pain-killer as needed. On examination, the heart sounds are normal and there are scattered crepitations in both lung fields. Petechial rash around the neck and axillae are noticed (see lab result and reports). Blood pressure 120/70 mmH Heart rate 110 /min Respiratory rate 26 /min Temperature 37.8 °C Oxygen saturation 85 % ABG HCO3- 22 22-28 mmol/L ABG PCO2 4.7 4.7-6.0 kPa pH 7.26 7.36-7.45 ABG P02 9.5 10.6-14.2 kPa Chest radiograph:Bilateral diffuse alveolar infiltrate. Electrocardiogram: Sinus tachycardia. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 12-year-old boy presents to the Emergency Department after a fall that led to a supra- condylar fracture. Presently his distal pulses are not palpable. Blood pressure 110/70 mmH Heart rate 120 /min Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 60-year-old man presents to the Emergency Department with epigastric pain radiating to the back. He is a smoker and has long-standing diabetes and hypertension. Abdominal examination reveals a pulsatile supra-umbilical mass. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old patient presents to the clinic with leg pain brought on by walking and relieved by rest. The patient reports a history of many years of smoking. Physical examination confirms loss of hair over the lower shins as well as dystrophic nails. An ankle-brachial index 0.80 Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old diabetic and hypertensive patient presents with a history of bilateral intermittent leg pain brought on by walking for 300 metres and relieved by rest. What is the most likely diagnosis?

An 81-year-old diabetic presents to the clinic with a recent onset of redness of the skin on the left lower extremity. The redness worsens when the leg is in a dependent position. On examination, pedal pulses in the left leg are diminished. The leg is cold and there is no tenderness on palpation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is the most likely pathogen to infect a polytetrafluoroethylene vascular graft?

A 50 year-old man becomes disoriented on the 4th post-operative day of abdominal aortic aneurysm repair. Vital signs remain outside of normal limits despite attempts at fluid resuscitation. He has passed a negligible volume of urine since he was catheterized one hour ago. His peripheries are warm to the touch. Blood pressure 90/40 mmHg Heart rate 140 /min Respiratory rate 36 /min Temperature 36.6 °C What type of shock is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67-year-old man with ischemic heart disease presented with a 24-hour history of severe central abdominal pain. Physical examination was unremarkable (see lab results and report). Test Result Normal Values WBC 28 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Amylase 600 24-151 IU/L ABG HCO3- 17 22-28 mmol/L ABG PCO2 4.2 4.7-6.0 kPa рН 7.2 7.36-7.45 ABG PO2 14 10.6-14.2 ka Plain X-ray abdomen: Dilated small bowel with a thickened wall. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old woman comes to Outpatient Clinic complaining of pain in her left hand and fingers from typing on the keyboard for a while. Investigations reveals insufficient blood flow into the superficial palmar arch. Occlusion of which of the following arteries is the most likely cause?

Blood pressure 60/40 mmH. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Remove the packs and repair the injury

questions.stem: A 56-year-old woman presents to the clinic with a non-healing ulcer over her right lateral Malleolus, she is hypertensive but not diabetic. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 56-year-old woman presents to the clinic with a non-healing ulcer over her right lateral Malleolus, she is hypertensive but not diabetic. Her pulse examination is normal and her local examination shows dark discoloration of the skin around the ulcer and a viable ulcer bed. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 38-year-old woman presents with swelling of her left leg that is gradually increasing over the last 3 months, no history of travel or surgeries or trauma over the last 6 months. Her distal pulses are palpable and her leg shows non-pitting edema with thickened skin and a dark discoloration. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 38-year-old woman presents with swelling of her left leg that is gradually increasing over the last 3 months, no history of travel or surgeries or trauma over the last 6 months, no family history of similar problems. Her distal pulses are palpable and her leg shows non-pitting edema with thickened skin and a dark discoloration. Which of the following is the most appropriate diagnostic test?

Her distal pulses are palpable and her leg shows non-pitting edema with thickened skin and a dark discoloration. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 52-year-old man develops sudden severe retrosternal chest pain that radiates to his back. Within minutes, he became unconscious. He is a heavy smoker and has history of hypertension. Blood pressure 85/56 mmHg, Heart rate 92 /min. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 63-year-old smoker man presents with pain in his left leg, which is exacerbated by exercise and relieved by rest. Examination revealed weak pulses in the left leg compared to the right. The ankle brachial pressure index is 0.84. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

options.text: Peripheral arterial disease with critical ischaemia

questions.stem: A 55-year-old hypertensive diabetic with ischemic heart disease woman presented with sudden onset of left sided lower abdominal pain associated with vomiting for 6 hours. On examination, she is pale, dehydrated and flushed. Peripheral pulses are regularly irregular. Her abdomen is distended, tender all over (see lab results). Blood pressure 170/100 mmHg Heart rate 121 /min Respiratory rate 20 /min ABG HCO3- 13 22-28 mmol/L ABG PCO2 5.2 4.7-6.0 kPa pH 7.23 7.36-7.45 ABG PO2 10.8 10.6-14.2 ka Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old man diabetic complains of intermittent claudication of his right leg, the foot and sole are cold and numb. He underwent right lower limb angiography showing diffuse disease. 2 days later he developed a painful swelling in his right groin, On examination, there is a firm swelling below the inguinal crease, partially mobile, irreducible, nonexpansile, and tender with transmissible pulse. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old woman underwent surgery for her right leg varicose veins. On the 2nd postoperative day, she complained of pain and paraesthesia on the medial aspect of her leg and foot. On examination, there is sensory loss of fine touch and pain in her right leg and foot, but no motor loss. Wounds are healthy. Which of the following nerves is most likely injured?

A 65-year-old smoker with diabetes mellitus presents with a long history of intermittent buttock pain and claudication that has worsened over the past few weeks. On examination, there is atrophy of buttock muscles with decreased power and painful movements. The femoral pulses are weak (see report). Angiogram: Aortoiliac insufficiency. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 42-year-old man complains of chest pain after being involved in a motor vehicle accident. Examination confirmed a patent airway, equal air entry on both sides of the chest, and distended neck veins. Blood pressure 88/45 mmHg Heart rate 110 /min Respiratory rate 30 /min which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old was involved in a head-on motor vehicle accident. On examination, he was unresponsive, had distended neck veins, absent breath sounds, and hyper-resonant percussion on the right side. His GCS score was 8. Which of the following is the most urgent initial management?

A 33-year-old presented with a lump in her neck. Physical examination confirmed enlarged right cervical lymph nodes with normal thyroid gland. She underwent percutaneous biopsy of the lymph nodes (see report). Histopathology:Normal follicular thyroid cells. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 42-year-old woman presented with a right breast mass that has been present for 3 months and is not associated with other symptoms. Physical examination confirmed a 2 x 2 cm firm partially movable mass with associated skin tethering and an enlarged axillary lymph node (see report). Bilateral breast mammogram and ultrasound: Ill-defined lobulated dense mass that is hypochoic on ultrasound, measuring 2 x 2 cm, not associated with speculation or suspicious microcalcifications. Coded as BI-RADS IV. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 54-year-old woman complains of a left breast mass that has been present for 9 months. Physical examination confirmed a 3 x 3 cm firm fixed mass at the left retro-areolar area with associated nipple retraction (see report). Bilateral breast mammogram: Speculated mass at left retro-areolar region associated with suspicious clustered microcalcifications. There are multiple pathological left axillary lymph nodes. Findings coded as BI-RADS V (Probably Malignant). Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 14-year-old patient presented with a painless neck swelling. Examination confirmed a midline neck swelling below the hyoid bone that moves up and down with swallowing. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
mass, the patient was referred to the endocrine surgical team for an elective adrenalectomy. Which of the following investigations should be done prior to an elective adrenalectomy?

options.text: Aldosterone to plasma renin activity ratio

questions.stem: A 42-year-old woman presented with a 4-month history of an anterior neck swelling. Physical examination confirmed a solitary nodule in the right lobe of thyroid (see lab results and report) Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone 0.05 (0.4 - 5.0 U/mL) Thyroxine (T4 free serum) 37 (8.5 - 15.2 pmol/L) Ultrasound: Right thyroid lobe solitary solid nodule 2 x 3 cm. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 33-year-old woman presented with a lump in her neck. Physical examination confirmed enlarged right cervical lymph nodes with normal thyroid gland. She underwent percutaneous biopsy of the lymph nodes (see report). Histopathology: Normal follicular thyroid cells. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 52-year-old woman presented with a 3-month history of a progressive anterior neck swelling with stridor. She has a 12-year history of Hashimoto's thyroiditis. Physical examination confirmed a diffuse, large, non-tender thyroid swelling with retrosternal extension. A core needle biopsy was ordered (see reports). Ultrasound: Diffuse thyroid enlargement, encasing bilateral carotid sheaths. Histopathology: Malignant thyroid tumour. Which of the following is the most likely tumour?

A 35-year-old man post total thyroidectomy for multinodular goitre presented with persistent hypocalcaemia despite adequate replacement with oral and intravenous calcium. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
A hypothyroid patient is scheduled to undergo an elective surgery. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Start thyroxin and proceed with surgery
Delay surgery until the patient is euthyroid

questions.stem: Which of the following is the strongest indicator for surgery in Graves' disease?

A 20-year-old woman presents with a lump in the right lower quadrant of her breast that has been present for the last 2 years. The lump was initially small but over the past 6 months has constantly been growing in size. On examination, the mass measures 8 x 10 cm, is mobile and not attached to underlying muscles. Overlying skin is thinned out due to pressure effect of the mass. There are no signs of surrounding inflammation or infection. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 25-year-old man underwent a thyroidectomy due to multinodular goiter. Post-operatively, he was unable to maintain high pitch sound. Which of the following nerves is most likely injured?

A 32-year-old woman presented to the Emergency Department with severe pain in the right upper quadrant of the abdomen following a fatty meal 6-hours ago. This pain has decreased in severity over the last 2 hours. The pain was radiating to the right subscapular area associated with vomiting. Physical examination was normal (see lab results and report). Test Result Normal Values WBC 8.2 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Amylase 134 24-151 IU/L Ultrasound: Multiple gallstones with normal gallbladder walls. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 46-year-old man underwent an ERCP for biliary obstruction; the procedure was prolonged and difficult. 4 hours later, he developed extensive surgical emphysema of the abdomen, chest, and neck. Where is the most likely injury?

A 22-year-old man underwent an open left inguinal hernia mesh repair 2 weeks ago, presented with continuous discharge from the surgical wound. Examination confirmed a 2 x 3 cm pus-discharging wound with part of the mesh exposed. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Open entire wound for daily di

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most preferred mesh placement for a ventral hernia repair?

A 22-year-old woman presented 1-week after a laparoscopic appendectomy with mild abdominal pain not associated with nausea or vomiting, she reports passing infrequent loose stool. Physical examination confirmed a soft abdomen with mild tenderness at the wound site (see report). CT scan of abdomen: 2 x 2 cm retrocaecal collection. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 30-year-old underwent a laparoscopic appendectomy 2 weeks ago (see report). Histology: Carcinoid tumor at the tip of the appendix measuring 0.5 cm. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

options.text: CT scan of chest abdomen and pelvis

questions.stem: A 38-year-old patient developed a painful swelling in the right lower quadrant of his abdomen after moving a heavy object. Examination confirmed a localized tender swelling in the right lower abdominal quadrant with negative cough impulse; it persisted even with contraction of abdominal muscles. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old presented with intermittent perianal pain associated with purulent discharge. Examination confirmed a low-lying perianal fistula with an external opening posteriorly close to the anal verge. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

Heart rate 84 /min Temperature 37.2 °C Test Result Normal Value WBC 8 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old is 4-days post-exploratory laparotomy for a perforated acute appendicitis and is complaining of generalized abdominal discomfort and vomiting. A 38-year-old multiparous woman presented with a 3-year history of abdominal bulging. options.text: Slow loss of lean body mass

A 25-year-old presented to the Emergency Department with a 2-day history of diffuse colicky abdominal pain, associated with abdominal distension, vomiting and constipation . Ultrasound: Distended gallbladder with thick wall and pericholecystic fluid but no gallstone. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

Alkaline phosphatase 320 (39-117 IU/L) Direct bilirubin 77 (1.5-6.5 mol/L) Total bilirubin 88 (3.5-16.5 mol/L) Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 58-year-old man presented to the Emergency Department complaining of right iliac fossa pain for 5 days. Physical examination confirmed a tender mass in the right iliac fossa. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

On examination, he was jaundiced (see lab result and report). Alkaline phosphatase 312 (39-117 |U/L) Direct bilirubin 87 (1.5-6.5 mol/L) Total bilirubin 97 (3.5-16.5 mol/L) Ultrasound: Dilated intrahepatic biliary tree with collapsed gallbladder. A 41-year-old woman presented to the Emergency Department complaining of a 2-week history of upper abdominal pain associated with vomiting and fever. Physical examination confirmed tenderness in the epigastric region (see lab result and report). Blood pressure 110/70 mmH Heart rate 100 /min Temperature 38.1 °C WBC 20.2 (4.5-10.5 x 109/L) Amylase 245 (24-151 IU/L) Ultrasound: Well circumscribed collection (15 x 17 cm) in the lesser sac. A 45-year-old presented to the Emergency Department with a 12-hour history of vomiting fresh blood. He has a 10-year history of recurrent peptic ulcers. Physical examination was normal (see report). A 48-year-old man complains of right upper quadrant abdominal pain for 4 months. Physical examination was normal (see reports). Serology: Echinococcus granulosus was positive. Ultrasound: Large cystic lesion (10x15 cm) in the right lobe of the liver with multiple intra-cystic daughter cysts, but no calcifications. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 29-year-old woman presented to the Emergency Department with diffuse abdominal pain for 1 day associated with progressive abdominal distension, vomiting and constipation. Physical examination confirmed abdominal distension, diffuse mild tenderness and exaggerated bowel sounds (see report). A 63-year-old woman comes to the clinic for an annual check-up. On examination, she has a small and asymptomatic right femoral hernia. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A middle-aged woman with hepatomegaly underwent upper abdomen MRI and found to have a 3cm lesion in the liver that shows peripheral beaded enhancement in the early phase with progressive central filling in the delayed phase. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 31-year-old woman presented to the Emergency Room with mild acute cholecystitis. She was started on intravenous fluids and empiric antibiotics. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 34-year woman presented with recurrent biliary colic for 5 months. Liver function test is within normal limits. Liver ultrasound shows cholelithiasis. Which of the following procedures is the most appropriate?

A 57-year-old man presents with 2 days of abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. Examination revealed a distended, tympanic and mildly tender abdomen without rebound or guarding (see lab results and reports). Hb 153 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) WBC 12.6 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Plain Abdominal X-ray: Multiple air-fluid levels. CT scan: Multiple dilated loops of small bowel with a transition point in the distal small bowel, with some adjacent mesenteric fat stranding. A 60-year-old woman complains of a large amount of fresh bleeding per rectum and weakn She had similar episodes 2 weeks ago. On examination, she looks pale and dehydrated. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 43-year-old woman is evaluated during a follow-up visit. She is overweight and has hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, both of which are well controlled. For several years, she has attempted to lose weight through various commercial diets; dietician-monitored, calorie-restricted diets; and physical activity but her weight has remained stable. Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 76 /min Respiratory rate 13 /min Temperature 36.6 °C BMI 28,5 kg/m2 In addition to continuing calorie restriction and exercise, which of the following is the most appropriate management to help this patient achieve weight loss with tolerable side effect?

A 50-year-old man underwent an open mesh repair of a left inguinal hernia. He presented 2 months later because he noticed that the left testes had become smaller in size. Which of the following is the most likely cause?

A 47-year-old man presented with a 6-month history of right groin swelling. The swelling recently increased in size. Examination confirmed an inguino-scrotal swelling with positive cough impulse and separable from testis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 38-year-old man sustained a pelvic fracture in a motor vehicle accident. There was blood per urethra (see report). Retrograde urethrogram: Retroperitoneal urethral injury. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 21-year-old patient presents with an abnormal left testicle. On examination, the area adjacent to the left testicle feels like a bag of worms, which gets larger with a valsalva maneuver. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 80-year-old man presents with dull aching pain in the loins (see lab results and report). Test Result Creatinine 280 (Normal Value: 44-115 mol/L) Urea 12.5 (Normal Value: 2.75-7.4 mol/L) Ultrasound abdomen: Bilateral hydronephrosis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old male comes to the clinic with a mild intermittent urinary flow reduction. Rectal examination, urinalysis and prostate specific antigen studies are normal (see report). Ultrasound prostate: Enlarged median lobe. Which of the following is the best way to investigate?

A 45-year-old diabetic man presents with a non-healing wound, which he developed after incision and drainage for diabetic foot 2 months ago (see lab result). bA1c 6 5.8 - 6.2 % Which of the following is the most likely etiology?
A 30-year-old woman sustained a burn from an oven grill. 8 days later, she noticed greenish discharge in the wound. Which of the following is the most likely cause?

A young man presents with a lump on the right mid-thigh. On examination, the overlying skin is normal, the mass is soft movable with positive fluctuation test. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is the most effective way to minimize excessive scar formation?

A 35-year-old woman presented with partial thickness burns on her arms and leg due to hot water spillage 1 day ago, with wound edema and congestion. Which of the following is the most likely responsible mediator?

A 35-year-old man sustained a right tibia fracture in a road traffic accident. He is being managed by closed reduction with cast but he develops swelling in his toes and pain. Which of the following is the earliest alarming sign?

A 32-year-old man had excision and primary closure of a skin contracture that was 5×3 cm on the forearm, 1 year ago. He presented with an overgrowth at the scar site that extend beyond the surgical scar margins, it started few weeks after the surgery and gradually increased in size. Which of the following most accurately describes the lesion?
A 17-year-old girl was admitted with a 20% burn transferred to the burn unit for proper resuscitation. Which of the following goals will most indicates that adequate resuscitation is achieved?

An elderly man is brought to the Emergency Department with an altered level of consciousness after he fell down the stairs (see report). CT scan: Suggestive extradural hematoma. Which of the following arteries is most likely involved?
An elderly man presents for follow-up after he sustained road traffic accident 3 days back. On examination, "Battle Sign" is noted. Which of the following is the most likely cause?
A patient presented with an infected wound at the forehead. Which of the following lymph nodes will most likely enlarged?

A 30-year-old woman complains of recurrent attacks of sudden onset dyspnea, chest and throat tightness. Inhaled salbutamol is of little help; however, her symptoms improves suddenly. On examination, she is found to have inspiratory wheeze during dyspnea spells. which of the following is the likely cause of symptoms?

A 30-year-old woman underwent endoscopic sinus biopsy of soft tissue mass at the roof of left maxillary sinus. After recovery, the patient experienced numbness and paraesthesia in her left lower eyelid and upper lip. Which of the following is the most likely affected nerve?

A 70-year-old man is admitted for stomach resection for gastric cancer. On the 4TH postoperative day. the patient developed retrosternal chest pain accompanied with dyspnea and perfuse sweating. Physical examination is remarkable only for S4. Aspirin, clopidogrel and nitrate were administered (see report) Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg, Heart rate 76 /min, Respiratory rate 18 /min, Temperature 36.6 °C Oxygen saturation 95 % Electrocardiogram: Shows ST elevation in leads V2-V5. Which of the following is the most appropriate step in management?

A 29-year-old man underwent left open inguinal hernia mesh repair 3 weeks ago. He presented today with continuous intractable groin pain radiating to the left upper thigh and associated with persistent hyperesthesia. Physical examination excluded any recurrence or surgical site infection. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A patient in Intensive Care Unit who is post-major surgery received 15 units of blood. The patient developed bleeding from the incision; nasogastric tube and vein puncture sites. Which of the following is the most likely cause?
A heavy smoker man is going for major surgical procedure. Which of the following is the most sensitive predictor of postoperative respiratory complications?
Post laparoscopic cholecystectomy, transection of the common bile duct above the cystic duct is confirmed. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 36-year-old was undergoing a caesarean section, just before closure the surgeon noticed profound bleeding coming from the upper abdomen. Which of the following is the most likely source of bleeding?

A 42-year-old woman complains of left sided chest and abdominal pain that is worse on inspiration. She underwent a splenectomy a few days ago. Examination confirms a decreased air entry at the left lung base, dullness to percussion and left upper quadrant tenderness. Temperature 38.6 °C Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A young man is hypoxic 24 hours after major upper abdominal surgery. Which of the following is the most likely cause?
An elderly woman developed hypoxia 24 hours after major pelvic surgery for ovarian cancer. which of the following is the most likely cause?

A 22-year-old married woman has had severe, recurrent depression associated with multiple suicide attempts. She has been stabilized for the past 3 months on paroxetine and is now pregnant. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Discontinue paroxetine due to avoid prematurity
Continue paroxetine and monitor for depression
Discontinue paroxetine to avoid fetal damage

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman in her first trimester of pregnancy has come for a routine prenatal visit. She used to smoke one pack of cigarettes per day, and is now being advised to quit smoking. Which of the following is the greatest risk to her unborn child?

A 28-year-old primigravida 8 weeks gestation woman attended her first antenatal appointment. During the history assessment, she reports that she never had chickenpox. A serum blood titer is drawn and is negative for antibodies. Which of the following is the next best step in management?

A gravida 2 para 0 woman presents to the Maternal Health Clinic reporting that she has not menstruated for the past 2 months. The previous pregnancy had resulted in a stillbirth at 34 weeks' gestation. A human chorionic gonadotropin test is now positive. She has been trying to conceive for the past 6 months. She is afraid of having another stillbirth and asks to be vaccinated against everything. Which of the following vaccines is most appropriate to administer?

A gravida 3, para 2 is 16 weeks' pregnant presents to the obstetrics Clinic concerned about an outbreak of illness in her child's school and the potential effects on the fetus. Which of the following vaccines is recommended at this time?
Which of the following vaccine is contraindicated during pregnancy?
Which of the following interventions is the best to use with pregnant women who smoke?

A 32-year-old multiparous woman is admitted for induction of labour at 41 weeks and 2 days gestation. She had prior 2 uneventful vaginal deliveries. A pelvic examination shows the cervix is dilated at 2 cm and is 50% effaced with a medium consistency and mid-anterior position. The presenting part is at -2 station. Which of the following methods would be most appropriate for labour induction?

A 29-year-old primigravida presented at 22 weeks of gestation with mild lower abdominal pain. Abdominal examination reveals that the uterus is corresponding to the gestational age with positive fetal heart. Vaginal examination reveals a short soft cervix, which is 1.5 cm dilated with herniation of fetal membranes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A patient is seen at 8 weeks' gestation in an Antenatal Clinic with a diagnosis of cervical incompetence. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Insertion cervical suture the same week
Confirm the diagnosis by Hegar dilator

questions.stem: A woman presents at her 9th week of pregnancy with severe vaginal bleeding, lower abdominal pain and passage of the fetus through the vagina. On vaginal examination, cervix is open and tissue seen in the cervix. Which of the following the most appropriate management?

options.text: Fluid replacement and evacuation and curettage.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old woman G3 P02002 at 20 weeks' gestation with history of previous 2 preterm deliveries attend Antenatal Clinic. Current pregnancy is uneventful. An ultrasound shows size corresponds to date, anterior placenta and cervical length is 30 mm. Which of the following is the most appropriate intervention?

A 21-year-old primigravida is being monitored in the Labor and Delivery Unit. She is currently at 37 weeks of gestation and the cardiotocogram is done. It is persistently showing the pattern for the last 90 minutes. Therefore, she is concerned about the reason of this pattern in the fetal monitoring (see image). Which of the following would best describe the cause of this pattern in response to the patients concern?

A 37-year-old woman G2 P1001 at 20 weeks' gestation presents for a routine prenatal visit. She has no complaints. Her previous pregnancy has been unremarkable. She has chronic hypertension and history of cholecystectomy. She admits to smoking cigarettes several packs a day for relaxation and says she has read several papers that show no increased risk of congenital anomalies. Doppler shows fetal heart rate at 156 beat per minute. Blood pressure 108/68 mmHg Heart rate 100 /min Respiratory rate 16 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Oxygen saturation 95 % Which of the following is the best course of action?

options.text: Schedule her in 4-week time in antenatal clinic
Refer her to a social worker for possible substance abuse
Educate her about the possibility of delivering a small infant
Acknowledge that she is correct about no increased risk of congenital anomalies

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most common cause of morbidity in multiple gestation?

A 30-year-old woman G4 P3003 at 37 weeks pregnant with breech presentation presents to the clinic inquiring about external cephalic version. which of the following is a contraindication of external cephalic version would be conveyed to the patient?

options.text: The presence of a low lying placenta
History of smoking 10 cigarettes per day
An umbilical cord length of 35 to 38 cm

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman G4 P3003 is pregnant at 37 weeks with a history of cesarean section due to non- reassuring fetal heart trace. Currently, she is in labor with breech presentation. Her inquiry is the possibility of an external cephalic version. Which of the following would be an absolute contraindication of the external cephalic version?

A 40-vear-old woman has achieved a pregnancy via in-vitro fertilization presents with her spouse at 11 weeks' gestation to the clinic (see report). Ultrasound: Shows a twin pregnancy. A 5-mm nuchal translucency (NT) is discovered in one of the fetus. Which of the following is an implication of NT finding?

options.text: The fetus has a high risk of NT enlargement by 18 weeks' gestation
The fetus has a high risk of cardiac malformation
The fetus has a high risk of neural tube defect
The fetus has a high risk of Turner syndrome

questions.stem: A 23-year-old G2 P1001 at 22 weeks' gestation presented with a complaint of her abdomen is larger than her previous pregnancy (see report). Ultrasound: Showed dizygotic twin pregnancy. Which of the following best described membranes and placenta of dizygotic twins?

options.text: Monochorionic and monoamniotic for conjoined twins
Monochorionic and diamniotic for the foetuses of same sex
Dichorionic and monoamniotic for the foetuses of same sex
Dichorionic and diamniotic regardless of the sex of the foetuses

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman G2 P0010 at 29 weeks has not felt fetal movement for 1 day. Fetal heart tones are heard by Doppler. Non-stress test is reactive. Biophysical profile demonstrates a score of 8. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Give steroid and repeat biophysical profile within 24 hours

questions.stem: A 24-year-old nulliparous woman presents to the Maternal Health Clinic in the evening at 34 weeks' gestation and complaining of decreased fetal movement. She says she had been at work all day and then came directly to the hospital when she noticed that the baby has not been moving as much as usual. There has been no leaking of amniotic fluid. There are no uterine contractions and also no vaginal bleeding. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

topics.title: Diabetes Mellitus and Gestational Diabetes Mellitus

questions.stem: A 27-year-old primigravida had a glucose tolerance test (see lab results). Patient's results Normal Values Fasting 5.7 3.3 to 5.5 Mmol/ 1 hour 9.4 Less than 11.1 Mmol/ 2 hour 9.8 Less than 8.6 Mmol/I 3 hour 7.2 Less than 7.8 Mmol/ Which of the following is the next best step in management?
A 35-year-old G2 P1001 at 30 weeks' gestation with poorly controlled gestational diabetes on diet.Which of the following medications is the most appropriate treatment?

A 39-year-old G5 P2114 at 23 weeks gestation presents to her routine antenatal visit. Ultrasound shows a large fetus for date and she is scheduled for an oral glucose tolerance test (GTT). She had previous pregnancy ended up with preterm labor due to polyhydramnios. Result of GTT shows abnormal of fasting and 2- hour plasma glucose. What is the following pathophysiology statement explains the above condition?

options.text: Normal pregnancy is a diabetogenic state mediated by placental inhibin hormone
Normal pregnancy is a diabetogenic state mediated by placental progesterone hormone
Normal pregnancy is a diabetogenic state mediated by placental estradiol hormone
Normal pregnancy is a diabetogenic state mediated by placental lactogen hormone

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman has delivered a boy. On inspection of the umbilical cord, a single artery was noticed. Which of the following is associated with the above finding?

topics.title: Pregnancy Related Medical and Surgical Conditions

questions.stem: gram oral glucose tolerance test. 1 hour later by finger stick sample glucose was 8.1 mmol/L. Which vaginal infection is she at the highest risk of contracting? A Candidiasis

A 34-year-old primigravida presented to the obstetrician for an initial prenatal visit after self- confirming pregnancy with a home pregnancy test. She complained of breast tenderness and occasional nausea. There were no complaints of urinary frequency or urgency. Urine dipstick analysis was performed and a mid-stream urine sample was obtained (see lab results and report). Nitrites +* Negative Leukocyte esterase Positive Negative Culture Report: Escherichia coli count is 50,000 CFU/ml. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A woman in her last month of pregnancy is diagnosed with right lower lobe pneumonia. Immune response to this infection leads to the formation of specific IgG antibodies. The fetus would be immunologically protected when born owing to which of the following mechanisms?

A 20-year-old nulliparous woman at 20 weeks' gestation has been on iron supplement therapy throughout her pregnancy to treat anemia. She complained of weakness and becoming easily tired (see lab results). Hb 78 120-160 g/L MCV 60 80-95 fl RBC 5.4 4.2-5.4 x 1012/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old woman G5 P4004 presented to with amenorrhea, tiredness, nausea and vomiting during the morning hours for 3 months. Human chorionic gonadotropin test was positive. A physical examination showed no swelling in the lower extremities. The thyroid was enlarged on palpation. The tongue, conjunctiva and nail beds appeared pale. The uterine fundus was palpable 3 cm above the pubic symphysis. A peripheral blood smear showed macrocytic red blood cells and hypersegmented neutrophils (see lab results). Blood pressure 100/60 mmH, Heart rate 120 /min, Respiratory rate 26 /min, Temperature 37.0° Coral Hb 85 120-160 g/L НСТ 0.32 0.37-0.48 MCHC 332 320-360 g/L MCV 100 80-95 fl Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone 0.44 0.4 - 5.0 jU/L Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
A 40-year-old Healthy Primigravida with a history of previous deep venous thrombosis. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

During a difficult forceps delivery, an obstetrician misapplied the blade of the forceps at the child's left stylo-mastoid foramen where the forceps crushed its contents. What would be the baby's residual defect?

options.text: Inability to close the left eyelid
Reduced blood supply to the left ear
Loss of sensation from the left side of the face
Loss of taste from anterior 2/3rd of the tongue

questions.stem: A 32-year-old primigravida at 34 weeks' gestation presents for urgent care after falling down a flight of stairs. The patient complains of uterine tenderness and reduced fetal movement in the 45 minutes since the fall. There has been a small amount of dark red vaginal bleeding. The fetal heart monitoring revealed a heart rate of 150 bpm with irregular uterine contractions every 3 to 4 minutes. Her pregnancy has been uncomplicated. She has a positive history of cigarette smoking. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
What is the most common risk factor for abruptio placenta?
What is the most common cause of disseminated intravascular coagulopathy in pregnancy?

A 24-year-old primigravida who is a heavy smoker presented at 34 weeks of gestation to the Emergency Department with sudden heavy painful vaginal bleeding associated with uterine tenderness. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 21-year-old G2 P1001 at 15 weeks of gestation according to her last menstrual period, she presents with mild vaginal bleeding and is planned to undergo suction evacuation (see image). Which of the following is the most expected complication of the procedure?

A 40-year-old pregnant woman at 32 weeks gestation with a history of 2 previous cesarean sections presents with mild painless vaginal bleeding few hours ago. Ultrasound shows partial placenta previa. Cardiotocogram is reactive. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A pricharavida woman at 32 weeks' gestation brought to the Emergency Room with vaginal bleeding and abdominal pain. On examination: Fundal height equals to 30 weeks and abdomen is tense. Cardiotocography revealed fetal tachycardia, reduced variability and late decelerations. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old pregnant woman with polyhydramnios presented at 37-weeks of gestation with painful vaginal bleeding and uterine tenderness following spontaneous rupture of membranes. Cardiotocography, shows persistent bradycardia. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old woman 16 weeks pregnant presents to the clinic with vaginal bleeding, abdominal enlargement and vomiting for the past 4 days. On examination , the uterine size is larger than expected for the gestational age (see lab result and report). Test Result Normal Value Human chorionic gonadotropin 80,000 < 5 mlU/mL Ultrasound: "Snowstorm-like" appearance. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old pregnant un-booked patient is presenting to the Emergency Room with vaginal bleeding. the patient denies any abdominal pain and did not feel the fetal movements for the last few hours, and she was finally able to attend to the Emergency Room, as she had no form of transport to the hospital. Abdominal examination reveals a 34 cm fundal height. Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 101 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.text: Admit the patient to the ward

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman G2 P1001 at 36+4 weeks gestation with a history of prior cesarean section presents with abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding. Fetal heart baseline 160 bpm with minimal variability and repetitive late deceleration (see lab results). Blood pressure 170/100 mmHg Heart rate 120 /min Temperature 37.7 °C Hb 75 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Platelets count 110 150-400 x 109/L Fibrinogen 2.5 2-4 g/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-week pregnant woman presents in labor with contractions occurring every 4 minutes, she also has vaginal bleeding which is heavier than normal menstrual flow. The fetus is in a back- down position, transverse lie, and the cervix is dilated 3 cm with bulging membranes. The fetal heart rate is 170 bpm. The sonography showed a posterior fundal placenta with a retroplacental sonolucent area. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?

A 25-year-old primigravida at 38 weeks of gestation is being monitored in the Labor and Delivery Ward. Abdominal examination reveals an average size fetus of 3 kg in cephalic presentation and well engaged head. Cervical examination shows 5 cm dilated, 70% effaced and -3 station for the last 4 hours. She is not distressed and not on epidural analgesia. Fetal monitoring is done (see image). Which of the following is the best next step of management?

A 35-year-old woman G5 P4004 in labor and has been fully dilated for the last 2 hours. Maternal exhaustion is noted after pushing efforts for the last hour. She is not on epidural analgesia and the cardiotocogram shows category 1. Abdominal examination shows an average size fetus of 2.7 kg, cephalic presentation with 4/5 palpable head. On pelvic examination, the cervix is fully dilated and 100% effaced with -3 station. Which of the following is the best next step?

A 38-year-old woman G5 P4004 at 39 weeks of gestation is in labor room and on epidural analgesia. She has been fully dilated for the last 30 minutes and all of sudden, the uterine contractions cease despite of oxytocin infusion along with fetal deceleration and mild vaginal bleeding. Which of the following is the best next step?

options.text: Stop oxytocin infusion and perform an immediate cesarean section
Left lateral position and review in 20 minutes
Stop the epidural analgesia infusion pump

questions.stem: A 39-year-old woman G2 P1001 at 37 weeks of gestation presented in labor. She has history of cesarean section due to breech presentation 2 years ago. It has been 2 hours since she was declared fully dilated and current pelvic examination reveals 10-cm dilatation, fully effacement and +3 to +4 station. She is contracting 4 strong contractions in 10 minutes. The cardiotocogram is showing occasional early deceleration. Which of the following in the best next step?

A 40-year-old woman at 37 weeks of gestation with polyhydramnios presented in active labor following spontaneous rupture of membranes. Cardiotocogram shows persistent fetal bradycardia. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old woman G2 P1001 admitted to the hospital in active labor and ruptured membranes at 38 weeks of gestation. Upon vaginal examination, the cervix was 6 cm dilated and 1 cm long. The orbital ridge and orbits, saddle of the nose, mouth, and chin were palpable. What is the scientific term for this fetal presentation?

A primigravida at 37 weeks gestation known to have bicornuate uterus complains of subcostal discomfort and fetal kicking is appreciated in the lower abdomen mainly. Leopold maneuver; shows global soft presenting part with sluggish ballottement by first and second pelvic grips. Fetal heart detected at the level of maternal umbilicus. Which of the following is the most likely fetal presentation?

A primigravida at 37 weeks gestation known to have bicornuate uterus complains of subcostal discomfort and fetal kicking is appreciated in the lower abdomen mainly. Leopold maneuver; shows global soft presenting part with sluggish ballottement by first and second pelvic grips. Fetal heart detected at the level of maternal umbilicus. What is the recommended method of delivery if this fetal presentation persisted?

A 21-year-old woman primigravida at 38 weeks' gestation is in active labor. Her cervix is 5 cm dilated and fetal vertex is at +1 station. The tocodynamometer is done (see image). What is the best description of the initial acid-base status of the fetus?

A 27-year-old primigravida at 39 weeks' gestation presents to the hospital complaining of spontaneous watery gush. A speculum examination is performed and small amount of fluid is seen in the vault. Nitazine paper test indicates a pH of 7. Which of the following is another reliable test to confirm amniotic fluid leaks?

options.text: Indigo carmine injection into the amniotic sac
Methylene blue injection into the amniotic sac
Ultrasonography to assess amniotic fluid volume
Microscopy to detect arborization or ferning of fluid

questions.stem: A 31-year-old diabetic woman in active labor. Cardiotocography shows abnormal fetal heart tracing. What is the most appropriate next step in management?
A 35-year-old woman in active labour. Cardiotocography for fetal monitoring done (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 23-year-old primigravida presented in labour. The mid wife advised mediolateral episiotomy during the 2nd stage of labour.What is the advantage of a mediolateral episiotomy?

A 22-year-old primigravida presented at 38 weeks' gestation in labor. Vaginal examination showed ticm dilated cervix, full effacement and vertex. An hour later the obstetrician noticed a loop of the umbilical cord below the fetal head. Foetal Heart Rate 120 beat/min. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate management?

A 30-year-old woman G2 P1002 admitted at 40 weeks' gestation with onset of labor and ruptured membranes. Her cervix was 5 cm dilated and 100% effaced with 0 station vertex for 3 hours. A fetal monitoring strip showed 2 contractions in 10 minutes with a reassured non-stress test. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
