A 25-year-old woman G2 P1001 was admitted at 39 weeks' gestation in Labor Suite with labour pains. On Abdominal examination, 3 moderate contractions every 10 minutes. The cervix was 6 cm dilated, 80% effaced. Mouth, lips, nose and orbital hollows were palpable. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 30-year-old woman is in the second stage of labour for 3 hours by now. She is not on epidural analgesia. Abdominal examination shows an average size fetus of about 3 kg, in cephalic presentation with only 1/5 palpable head abdominally. Pelvic examination confirms that her cervix is fully dilated, fully effaced at +2 station. Which of the following is the most appropriate action at this point?

A 32-year-old pregnant patient at 36 weeks is in active labor and complaining of abdominal pain that has been increasing in intensity and continuous. She denies any bleeding. Abdominal examination reveals a 38 cm fundal height, and the uterus is found to be tender and tense. Pelvic examination reveals a 6 cm dilated cervix. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 30-year-old G3 P2002 patient at 38 weeks of gestation in the Labor Room is in active labor, the patient is free of pain after initiation of epidural analgesia. She was diagnosed with pre- eclampsia with severe features and was started on MgSO4. On examination, the abdomen is showing a cephalic term pregnancy with 2/5 palpable head. On pelvic examination, the cervix is 6 cm dilated and fully effaced at - 1 station. The patient is on oxytocin infusion and is contracting regularly. The cardiotocogram is done (see image). Which of the following is most possible cause of cardiotogram findings?

A 30-year-old G3 P2002 patient at 38 weeks of gestation is in active labor, she is free of pain after initiation of epidural analgesia. She was diagnosed with severe features of pre-eclampsia and was started on MgSO4. On examination, the abdomen is showing a cephalic term pregnancy with 2/5 palpable head. On pelvic examination, the cervix is 6 cm dilated and fully effaced. The patient is on oxytocin infusion and is contracting regularly. The cardiotocogram is done (see image). Blood pressure 90/50 mmHg Heart rate 76 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Which of the following is most possible cause of cardiotogram findings?

A 30-year-old woman G3 P2002 at 38 weeks of gestation is in the Labor Room. Changes on the cardiotocogram is noted while she is on oxytocin infusion with regular contractions. The diagnosis of pre- eclampsia with severe features was entertained earlier on and started her on MgSO4 accordingly. The labor pain is well-controlled after initiation of epidural analgesia. On examination, the abdomen is showing a cephalic term pregnancy with 0/5 palpable head. Pelvic examination shows cervix is 6 cm dilated and fully effaced and presenting part is at +1 station (see image). Which of the following would explain the cause of the cardiotocogram findings?

A 22-year-old primigravida woman at 38 weeks gestation is in active labor for 4 hours. Cervical dilatation is 5 cm, +1 station. Examination 5 hours later demonstrates no change compared to the previous findings. Contractions occur every 3 minutes and lasts 60 seconds. Fetal hear rate is of category 1 cardiotocograph. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
Which of the following positions of a patient in labour would most likely result in the development of a third or fourth-degree laceration?

A 30-year-old woman G4 P3003 at 34 weeks of pregnancy with breech presentation is asking about the possibility of external cephalic version, after reviewing the patient's information. Her first delivery was a caesarean section and was followed by a spontaneous vaginal delivery 4 years ago; she has no other significant medical or surgical history. The ultrasound is showing a single viable fetus of 3.2 kg with an anterior low-lying placenta and an amniotic fluid index of 4 cm. On examination, the patient is found to be in early labor and the pelvic assessment reveals a 3 cm dilated cervix with an intact membrane. Cardiotocography is done (see image). Which of the following indicates the absolute contraindication for external cephalic version?

A 30-year-old postpartum woman is admitted to the General Ward with diagnosis of right leg DVT. She was started on enoxaparin 80 mg bid, but in the same day of admission, she developed sudden onset dyspnea and right pleuritic chest pain. On examination, she was dyspneic and apprehensive. Heart sounds showed loud P2 and lungs were clear to auscultation (see lab results and report). Blood pressure 125/70 mmHg Heart rate 100 /min Respiratory rate 22 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Oxygen saturation 95 % ABG HCO3- 22 22-28 mmol/L ABG PCO2 4.2 4.7-6.0 kPa pH 7.48 7.36-7.45 ABG PO2 12 10.6-14.2 kPa Spiral CT chest: Thrombus in the right lower pulmonary artery. Which of the following is the most appropriate step in management?
What is the most common cause of postpartum hemorrhage?
After spontaneous vaginal delivery of P2 woman, she had primary postpartum hemorrhage due to uterine atony. Which of the following is considered the standard of care?

A mother brings her 2-week-old infant to the Well-Baby Clinic for a check-up. During the visit, the physician found the child to be normal, but the mother gave inappropriate answers to the questions. She appeared disoriented in time and date. She states that the child is deformed and unlikely to live long. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old woman presents to the clinic for postpartum care. She has experienced tearfulness and irritability during the 1 week following the delivery of her child. This episode resolved spontaneously, and her mood has been normal since then. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 38-year-old multipara had a postpartum hemorrhage after a normal vaginal delivery of a macrosomic baby. Which of the following is the best management of this condition?

A 38-year-old woman had postpartum hemorrhage after a normal vaginal delivery. She was started on oxytocin and bimanual massage of the uterus, but failed to control the bleeding. What is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 40-year-old woman has just delivered her 7th child at 38 weeks with 4 kg baby boy vaginally 10 minutes ago. The placenta is still in place and she starts to bleed profusely. The estimated amount of blood loss visually is around 800 ml. Which of the following best describes this case?

A 38-year-old G9 P8008 woman presented at 38 weeks gestation in labor and diagnosis of prolonged 2nd stage of labor was entertained and finally delivered 4.3 Kg baby by vacuum extraction. Anticipated management was taken because of risk of postpartum hemorrhage and hypovolemic shock. Which of the following is considered a best reliable indicator of above complications?

A 37-year-old woman G8 P7017 at 36 weeks' gestation has history of recurrent postpartum that required blood transfusion. She has no significant medical problem. Which of the following is the most appropriate preventive measure at delivery?

options.text: Deliver the patient in the operating room
Perform an elective cesarean section at 38 weeks gestation
Perform active management of 3rd stage of labor
Give the patient preload of crystalloid fluids while in labor to overcome the possible post- delivery hypovolemia

questions.stem: A patient who had a vaginal delivery 3 months ago is complaining of fecal incontinence and passage of vaginal flatus. These symptoms have started 1 week postpartum. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old woman presents to the Maternal Health Clinic and reports that she has not had a menstrual period for the past 2 months. Human chorionic gonadotropin tested positive. Her significant health history included a needle-stick injury 1 year ago from a patient with hepatitis C. She was treated with interferon and has received monthly screening examinations. She asked if she would be able to breastfeed her newborn. Which of the following complications would most likely prevent breastfeeding?

A 25-year-old breastfeeding mother, who delivered a month ago, presents with fever and pain in the right breast for the past 2 days. The fever comes with chills and malaise. On examination, the right breast shows a skin wound on the areolar with a reddened and indurated surrounding area. Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 86 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 39.0° C Which of the following is the most likely causing pathogen?

A woman presents to the Emergency Department 15 days after giving birth by cesarean section She complains of persistent vaginal bleeding. Blood pressure 110/70 mmH Heart rate 85 /min Temperature 38.1 °C Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 34-year-old delivered 5 months ago presents with failure to breastfeed her baby, dizziness and fatigue. Her obstetrics history revealed that she had a vaginal delivery complicated with retained placenta and severe postpartum hemorrhage. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 24-year-old woman P2 at 38 weeks' gestation developed atonic post-partum hemorrhage after delivering a healthy baby girl, APGAR 9 and 9, weighing 3.8 Kg. She is known to have bronchial asthma and it is controlled on regular medications. The obstetrician has started the uterine massage, infused adequate amounts of fluids and is going to initiate uterotonic medications. Which of the following is contraindicated to use to manage the case?

A 20-year-old G3 P2002 is in Labor and Delivery Ward in active labor at 6 cm dilatation. The patient is pregnant at 34 weeks and is known to have twin pregnancy. What would be the characteristic that puts this patient at risk of postpartum hemorrhage?
In regards to the placental delivery during a cesarean section. Which is the most accurate recommendation to reduce the incidence of postpartum hemorrhage?

options.text: Fundal pressure and massage is advised to help separate the placenta
Check for complete placental delivery by using a sponge inside the endometrial cavity

questions.stem: A 30-years-old hospitalized woman post cesarean section was treated for 6 days with clindamycin and cefuroxime for post-partum endometritis when she developed profuse, watery diarrhea, cramping abdominal pain and fever. An enzyme immunoassay of the stool revealed the presence of a bacterial enterotoxin. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

topics.title: Puberty Disorders, Pediatrics, Adolescent and Young Gynecology

questions.stem: Which of the following is the first female physical sign of puberty?

A 20-year-old is complaining of asymptomatic solitary, benign, soft, smooth-surfaced cyst appearing on the vulvar vestibule. On examination, it is found to be domed, translucent and filled with clear, viscous mucin. Incision of the lesion allows jelly-like mucinous material to be extruded. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old girl presents to the Emergency Department with vaginal bleeding and pain. Her mother reports that has been passing stool in her pants for 2 weeks despite being toilet trained. On examination, there are bruises on with blood staining labia majora (see lab results). Test Result Normal Values Hb 120 (112-165 g/L) WBC 9.4 (4-10.5 x 109/L) Platelet count 344 (150-400 × 109/L) Prothrombin time 13 (12-14 sec) APTT 36 (30-40 sec) Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old woman complained of recurrent behavioral symptoms that started a few days before her menstrual cycles and usually disappeared around the second day of the cycle. These symptoms have led to reduced work productivity, increased work absenteeism, and increased visits to ambulatory healthcare. What is the most common affective or behavioral symptom for her diagnosis?

A 25-year-old woman complained of recurrent behavioral symptoms that started a few days before her menstrual cycles and usually disappear around the second day of the cycle. These symptoms have led to reduced work productivity, absenteeism from work, and increased visits to ambulatory healthcare. Which of the following is the most reliable method to establish the diagnosis?
A 16-year-old girl is complaining of infrequent cycle occurring once every 6 to 8 weeks. Which of the following is most likely the cause?

options.text: Physiological variation in menstrual period timing
Uterine benign masses in particular uterine fibroids

questions.stem: A 14-year-old healthy giri has painless vaginal bleeding occurring at interval of 3 weeks to 2 months. The bleeding usually lasts 2 to 4 days, not preceded by premenstrual symptoms and not associated with clots. Review of systems is not significant. Physical examination shows a normal appearing pubertal girl along with normal development of secondary sex characteristics (see lab results). Hemoglobin 120 112-165 g/L RBC 6 4.6.4.8 x 1012/L WBC 4.8 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Platelets count 220 150-400 x 109/L Pregnancy test Negative Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 16-year-old presented to the clinic for evaluation of primary amenorrhea. Examination showed normal adult-size breasts. But coarse pubic and axillary hair (see lab result). Testosterone 13.86 0.7-2.8 mol/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A young couple has been trying to conceive a baby for 6 months with no success. The wife has regular cycles every 23 days and 4-day periods. Which of the following is most appropriate investigation?

A 27-year-old nulliparous presents for a routine examination. Her gynecological history indicates a 5-year history of oligomenorrhea with only about 2-3 menses a year. She denies inter-cycle spotting or premenstrual symptoms. The last menses was 3 months ago. The physical examination confirmed a moderate amount of facial hair and inflammatory acne while the pelvic examination is normal. Weight 60 kg, Blood pressure 120/75 mmHg, Heart rate 72 /min, Respiratory rate 17 /min. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 17-year-old healthy girl and gymnast in her school team presents with a history of absence of menstruation. She reports that she develops breasts later than her friends and never began menses. On examination, her Tanner stage V development of breasts and pubic hair. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this girl's primary amenorrhea?
A 13-year-old girl presents 8 months after menarche with irregular menstrual bleeding and intermenstrual bleeding. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

topics.title: Menstrual Cycle Abnormalities and Abnormal Uterine Bleeding (AUB)

questions.stem: A 56-year-old nulliparous and menopaused for 4 years, presented to the clinic with intermittent vaginal bleeding for the last 4 weeks. The bleeding was scanty and bright in color. Pelvic examination shows a healthy vagina and cervix with a small amount of blood in the cervical os. Which of the following is the next step in management?

A 24-year-old obese woman, no previous pregnancy, complains of irregular menstrual periods Menarche was at age of 14 and her periods were irregular in timing, duration and flow. The last menstrual flow was scanty 3 months ago. History of weight gain since menarche along with facial acne and mild facial hirsutism (see lab results). Testosterone 3.4 0.7-2.8 mol/L Sex hormone-binding globulins 9 13-17 mol/L Luteinizing hormone 31 5-22 U/L Follicle-stimulating hormone 2.1 5-20 IU/L Random Glucose 6.1 3.9-5.5 mmol/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 48-year-old woman nulliparous presented to the Emergency Department with heavy vaginal bleeding associated with slight dizziness. No other significant past medical history except heavy menstruation in the past few months. The examination was normal apart from the presence of a large amount of blood in the vaginal vault (see lab results). Supine: Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg, Heart rate 90 /min Standing: Blood pressure 104/66 mmHg, Heart rate 100 /min Temperature 36.6° C Hb 10 120-160 g/L Pregnancy test -ve Which of the following is the first step in management?

A 41-year-old patient presents to the Gynecological Clinic with heavy bleeding. After a complete evaluation, the gynecologist determines the patient has dysfunctional uterine bleeding. Which of the following is the first step in management?

A 14-year-old girl has a 6-month history of lower mid-abdominal pain, colicky in nature, radiates to the back and upper thighs. It often begins with onset of menses which lasts for 2-4 days. She has missed several days of school during the last 2 months because of the severity of pain. Physical examination is normal for the abdomen and pelvis. Normal secondary sexual development is also noted, Which of the following is the first step in management?

A 23-year-old woman presented with breast tenderness, abdominal bloating, and food cravings. She has a 6-month history of tiredness, anxiety, emotional lability, difficulty concentrating and insomnia. There are no menstrual irregularities or prodromal life stressors. The symptoms recurred on a regular basis during the week leading up to the menstrual period but completely resolved within the first 3 days of menses. The patient felt totally incapacitated when symptomatic, and the symptoms adversely affected personal and professional life. Which of the following is the best-evidenced treatment?

A 42-year-old obese woman presented with a 5-year history of irregular vaginal bleeding. Thyroid studies are normal. She noticed that her irregular menstruation has started to put on weight (see report). Body mass index 35 kg/m2. Endometrial Biopsy: Adenomatous hyperplasia. Which of the following is the most likely cause?

options.text: Local genetic mutation of the endometrium
Peripheral conversion of precursors to estrogen

questions.stem: A 42-year-old obese nulligravida patient with polycystic ovary syndrome has had irregular vaginal bleeding since menarche. She has used no medication to control her periods (see lab results and report). Test Result Normal Values Cortisol 8 a.m. 335 138-635 mol/L Estrogen 630 90-550 pmol/L Follicle-stimulating hormone 38 5-20 IU/L Testosterone 3.1 0.7-2.8 mol/L Prolactin 590 < 870 pmol/L T3 (Total serum) 1.2 0.9-2.8 mol/L Thyroxine (T4 Total serum) 82 64. 155 mol/L Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone 4.5 0.4 - 5.0 NU/L Endometrial Biopsy: Adenomatous hyperplasia. Which of the following is the most likely cause of the adenomatous hyperplasia?

A 30-year-old woman P1+0 presented to Obstetrics and Gynecology Clinic complains of inability to conceive for the last 3 years. During that time. She was not on contraceptives and her menstrual periods every 45 days but no period for the last 6 months (see lab results). Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone 9.2 NU/L 0.4 - 5.0 wU/L Follicular phase 5-20 IU/L Mid cycle peak 15-35 IU/L Follicle-stimulating hormone 5.3 yU/L. Luteal phase 5-15 IU/L Postmenopausal women 50-100 |U/L Men 5-20 IU/L Men 3-15 U/L Luteinizing hormone 7.2 U/L Follicular phase 5-22 U/L Luteal phase 5-22 U/L Ovulatory phase 30-250 U/L Postmenopausal Women > 30 U/L Prolactin 140 ng/ml < 25 ng/ml Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 12-year-old girl presented to the Emergency Department complaining of cramping over the lower abdomen and radiating to the back and inner thighs. She declared that the pain was recurrent, associated with nausea and often after menstruation since her menarche. Which of the following is the best treatment?
A 45-year-old woman is complaining of abnormal genital bleeding. Which of the following would highly suggest a uterine source of bleeding?
A 35-year-old woman is complaining of abnormal genital bleeding. Which of the following would suggest a cervical source of bleeding?

A 35-year-old woman is complaining of abnormal genital bleeding, she states that the amount is scanty and not associated with blood clots, but noticeable for post-coital bleeding. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 47-year-old woman presents with abnormal uterine bleeding, she describes the interval between the onset of bleeding episodes to be less than 21 days, heavy and prolonged. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 27-year-old woman presents with abnormal uterine bleeding, she describes the interval between the onset of bleeding episodes to be less than 21 days, heavy and prolonged. BMI 21 kg/m2 Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 36-year-old woman presents with abnormal uterine bleeding. The bleeding has been persistent for the last 8 months. She denies any significant family history of endometrial cancer, BMI 41 kg/m2 Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in assessment?

A 28-year-old woman at 24 weeks' gestation presented to the clinic for a routine examination. A pelvic examination showed a watery grey-colored discharge, fish-like smell. There were no signs of inflammation of the vagina or cervix. She reported some itching and moderate discomfort. The vaginal pH 5.1. A sample of the vaginal discharge was collected for analysis. Which of the following is the most likely finding?

A 25-year-old woman presented to the clinic with an unpleasant-smelling discharge. A speculum examination showed vaginal discharge, grey-green in color. The cervix was covered with papillae with light-red color. A specimen of vaginal secretions was obtained for a wet-prep microscopy which showed unicellular organisms with flagella. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 26-year-old nulliparous patient presented to the clinic with vaginal itching and increased vaginal discharge. She had been diagnosed with a positive pregnancy test 3 months ago. A pelvic examination showed a yellow-white discharge at the vaginal introitus. The labia were inflamed and covered with scratch marks. The vaginal discharge was fishy smell pH 4.8. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 23-year-old woman presented with vaginal discharge with an unpleasant smell. Examination confirmed a homogenous greyish-white vaginal discharge that has a high PH. A saline wet- preparation examination of the discharge showed "clue cells* and with application of potassium hydroxide a fishy smell was generated. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 21-year-old woman presented with an abnormal vaginal discharge, burning on micturition, and blood spotting for the past 2 months. On genital examination, there was an eroded and friable (strawberry appearance) cervix, with a yellow-green mucopurulent discharge (see report). Lab Testing: >10 PMNs per oil immersion field. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old diabetic woman presented with vaginal discharge and pruritus. The discharge is thick, grey and odorless. On physical examination, her vulva was erythematous and swollen. The vagina has a white-grey discharge that is adherent to the mucosa. Microscopic examination of the discharge confirmed the presence of spores. Which of the following is the most likely pathogen?

A 27-year-old woman presented with vaginal itching and an unpleasant smelling discharge. Itching gets worse at night and after intercourse. Physical examination confirmed a frothy and yellow-green vaginal discharge. Her vulva is erythematous and edematous and the cervix is inflamed and friable (see report). Wet Preparation: Flagellated protozoa. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old woman attended the Gynecological Clinic complaining of greenish-yellow purulent vaginal discharge that has started after her period. Upon vaginal examination, there was multifocal rounded macular erythematous lesions (like a spotted rash or bruise), and there was pelvic tenderness. Which of the following conditions is the most likely diagnosis?

A 29-year-old woman complaining of a heavy vaginal discharge for the past 2 weeks. The discharge was thin and a greyish white color with a slight fishy vaginal odor. On examination, a copious, thin, whitish discharge is seen adherent to the vaginal wall. Vaginal pH 5.5 Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 25-year-old woman had a severe pelvic inflammatory disease 2 years ago that was treated by intravenous antibiotics. The isolated organism was chlamydia trachomatis. Since then the woman was trying for pregnancy and failed to conceive. She had a normal regular period and her husband had a normal seminal analysis. Hysterosalpingogram revealed normal uterine cavity and no free spillage of the injected dye bilaterally (see lab results). Body mass index 35 kg/m2 Follicle-stimulating hormone 4.5 5-20 IU/L Luteinizing hormone 3.9 5-22 U/L Which of the following is the most appropriate method of management?

options.text: Induction of ovulation followed by normal intercourse
Induction of ovulation followed by intrauterine insemination
Weight reduction to reach body mass index of 23 kg/m2

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman had a severe pelvic inflammatory disease 2 years ago that was treated by intravenous antibiotics. The isolated organism was chlamydia trachomatis. Since then the patient was trying for pregnancy but failed to do so. She had a normal regular period and a normal seminal analysis of her husband. Which of the following investigations is recommended?

options.text: Magnetic resonance image of the pelvis

questions.stem: A 21-year-old patient presented to the clinic complaining of diffuse abdominal pain for the past 3 days. Her history included dyspareunia, nausea, and several episodes of vomiting. On examination, external genitalia and cervix appeared normal. However, the patient reported cervical motion, adnexal, and lower abdominal tenderness. Blood pressure 120/60 mmHg Heart rate 72 /min Respiratory rate 16 /min Temperature 38.4° C Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 23-year-old woman who just recently had an intrauterine device fitted, complaining of watery brown vaginal discharge and abdominal pain. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old woman presents with a longstanding history of lower abdominal and right hypochondrial pain. Diagnostic laparoscopy confirms pelvic and perihepatic adhesions. Which of the following is most likely responsible?

A 25-year-old woman presents with a 6-hour history of lower abdominal pain associated with nausea and 1 episode of vomiting. Examination confirms minimal tenderness in the suprapubic and left iliac fossa region. Urine dipstick and pregnancy tests are normal (see lab results). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 76 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Hb 110 130-170 g/L (Male) | 120-160 g/L (Female) WBC 9 (4.5-10.5 x 109/L) Neutrophils 50 (40-60%) Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 40-year-old woman is on Tamoxifen 20 mg daily as a hormonal treatment of breast cancer. She complains of heavy and prolonged menstrual period. Her transvaginal ultrasound revealed the presence of 28 mm endometrial thickness with cystic changes. Which of the following is the next step in the patient's evaluation?

A 48-year-old obese woman complains of nausea. Patient LMP was 2 months ago. She is using a barrier method (condoms) as a birth control method. Examination is normal except for a slight dusky discoloration of her cervix. Which of the following is the next step in management?
A 58-year-old menopausal woman presents with sexual dysfunction, dyspareunia. On examination, vaginal atrophy is noticed. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 22-year-old woman attends the Women's Health Clinic for a postnatal examination. She delivered a full-term baby boy 6 weeks earlier and the infant is exclusively breastfeeding and shows a good latch and weight gain. She would like to have more children, but not within the next 2 years. She does not smoke cigarettes and not at risk for heart disease. She inquired about birth control methods. Which of the following methods is most appropriate?

A 45-year-old woman has undergone a total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo- oophorectomy for a benign reason. Immediately post operation, she started to have acute vasomotor symptoms. Accordingly, she was counseled for hormone replacement therapy and agreed. Which of the following is the most appropriate hormone replacement therapy regimen?

A 42-year-old P3 is seeking advice for the possibility of inserting an intrauterine contraceptive device for family planning. The patient's history reveals that she became pregnant while using an intrauterine contraceptive device 4 years ago and in her second pregnancy; she underwent a cesarean section, which was complicated by postpartum endometritis. Her menstrual cycles have been irregular for the last 4 months with heavier flow than usual. Which of the following is an absolute contraindication to the insertion of an intrauterine contraceptive device?

A 30-year-old woman is undergoing a laparotomy for ovarian cystectomy. She is a known smoker and she is on oral combined contraceptive pills for the last 6 years. During surgery, she developed tachycardia, hypoxemia and hypotension. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

Postmenopausal women asked her gynecologist for hormone replacement therapy. The gynecologist explained to the women that no evidence supports the use of hormone replacement therapy in her case. The women insisted. Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Refer the women to another gynecologist
Consult the hospitals clinical ethics committee
Refuse to prescribe the hormone replacement therapy

topics.title: Abortion, Pregnancy Loss, and Intrauterine Fetal Demise (IUFD)

questions.stem: A 20-year-old woman has a history of 3 first trimester abortions. She was diagnosed last year with pulmonary embolism (see lab results). Prothrombin time 11 10-13 sec APTT 69 30-40 sec Platelets count 320 150-400 x 109/L Lupus anticoagulant positive Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old primigravida at 37 weeks of gestation was just informed about the finding of a confirmed non-viable fetus with no obvious identified reason. She is now questioning the urgency of deciding the timing of delivery (see lab results). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg, Heart rate 76 /min, Respiratory rate 18 /min, Temperature 36.6 °C, Oxygen saturation 95 %, BMI 22 kg/m2 Hb 12 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) Platelets count 200 150-400 x 109/L INR 1 0.8-1.2 Which of the following would be the best advice to be given to the patient?

options.text: It is necessary that the patient is urgently admitted for induction
She has time to go home and take time in deciding the next step
Timing of induction should solely depend on the Bishop score
Waiting for spontaneous labor is not an option

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman G2 P1001 at 38 weeks of gestation with a history of cesarean section in her first delivery 4 years ago due to breech presentation. Current pregnancy. a diagnosis of intrauterine fetal demise is confirmed and mode of delivery to be discussed accordingly. Which of the following would best be performed at this stage?

options.text: Direct to a trial of vaginal delivery to avoid CS
Direct to have a CS to avoid pain and emotional distress
Thorough counseling about the benefits and risks of vaginal delivery versus CS

questions.stem: A 20-year-old primigravida at 37 weeks of gestation has just been informed that the fetus is non-viable. She starts to feel guilty and blames her habit of smoking up to 5 cigarettes per day which causes her fetal demise. Which of the following to be considered in counseling this patient?

options.text: Smoking has no definite relationship with fetal demise
She should stop smoking for the sake of future pregnancies
The cause is yet undetermined and investigations will be performed
Smoking 5 cigarette per day will increase the likelihood of fetal demise by 10 folds

questions.stem: A 39-year-old primigravida presents at 30 weeks of gestation with sudden loss of fetal movements. An immediate ultrasound is performed and confirms the diagnosis of intrauterine fetal death. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate action?

A 26-year-old presents with mild vaginal bleeding after a 7 weeks history of amenorrhea. Pelvic examination reveals a closed cervix and the uterus size is compatible with the duration of amenorrhea. Which of the following is the most likely type abortion?

A 30-year-old primigravida with 10 weeks of amenorrhea presents with abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding. Pelvic examination reveals a partially dilated cervix, and the product of conception felt at the cervix. Which of the following is the most likely type of abortion?

A 24-year-old woman presents at 7 weeks' gestation complaining of mild vaginal bleeding and lower abdominal pain, colicky in nature. Upon examination; normal vital signs and speculum examination shows the cervix is closed and fresh blood coming through the cervix. Which of the following is the most likely cause of the bleeding?

A 22-year-old primigravida at 7 weeks' gestation is brought to the Emergency Department complaining of moderate vaginal bleeding with passage of tissue like material and lower abdominal colicky pain. Speculum examination; tissue is in the vagina, uterine cervix is opened and admitting one finger. Product of conception is protruding through the cervical canal. Bimanual examination reveals bulky uterus corresponding to seven-eight weeks gestation. Adnexa were free and there was no cervical excitation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old G3 P0020 admitted to the hospital with an incomplete abortion. She underwent dilatation and curettage during which excessive bleeding developed that required vigorous curettage. She returned to the clinic 6 months later complaining of no menstruation since her curettage despite positive premenstrual symptoms. Which layer of her endometrium is damaged based on history?

A 22-year-old patient presented at 10-weeks of gestation with mild vaginal bleeding and suprapubic pain. Vaginal examination reveals a bulky uterus corresponding to the gestational age and a closed cervix. Which of the following is the most likely type of abortion?

A 38-year-old presented to Labor Ward with severe abruptio placenta. She was diagnosed with intrauterine fetal death and disseminated intravascular coagulopathy (DIC). Vaginal examination revealed 6 cm dilated cervix. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 22-year-old patient presented to the Emergency Department with a history of expulsion of products of conception at home. On examination, the cervix was closed with minimal vaginal bleeding. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old G3 P2002 at 8 weeks of gestation presents to the Emergency Room complaining of mild per vaginal bleeding, she denies history of passage of tissue and on examination the abdomen is soft and nontender. Pelvic examination reveals a healthy normally looking, closed cervical os with evidence of brownish discharge and no active bleeding seen (see report). Bedside Ultrasound: Reveals an intrauterine pregnancy with a crown-rump length of 7 weeks. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

topics.title: Gestational Trophoblastic Disease (Molar pregnancy and Choriocarcinoma)

questions.stem: A 26-year-old at her 8 weeks gestation presented with excessive nausea and vaginal bleeding. Abdominal examination revealed an enlarged uterus with absence of fetal heart sound. An ultrasonographic examination showed as in the image along with high B-hCG (see image), Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 37-year-old primigravida presented to the clinic with amenorrhea for 12 weeks, hyperemesis gravidarum, and raised human chorionic gonadotropin levels. Uterus size is equivalent to 16 weeks' gestation (see report). Ultrasound: Fetus is small for dates. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old G3 P0020 with a history of 2 miscarriages presents to the Emergency Room with mild vaginal bleeding, she denies history of passage of tissue. The last menstruation started 6 weeks ago, she complains of a cough associated with hemoptysis for the last few days. On examination, the uterus is 12 weeks in size and is slightly tender. Pelvic examination reveals aggressive looking, irregular mass that bleeds on touch arising from the cervix (see lab results). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg, Heart rate 100 /min, Temperature 36.6 °C Human chorionic gonadotropin 1005023 < 5 mlU/mL Hb 7 130-170 g/L (Male) 120-160 g/L (Female) HCT 0.21 0.42-0.52 (Male) 0.37-0.48 (Female) MCH 25 28-33 pg/cell MCV 70 80-95 f1 Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 19-year-old married woman complains of a 6-hour history of right lower abdominal pain and nausea. On Examination, she is tender in her right lower abdomen with rebound tenderness. Her LMP was 2 weeks back (see lab results). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg, Heart rate 100 /min, Temperature 36.4 °C Hb 105 120-160 g/L CT 0.31 0.37-0.48 WBC 9.8 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 65-year-old postmenopausal woman presented with vague abdominal pain and bloating for the last 6 months. Pelvic ultrasound showed a complex ovarian mass 7 cm in diameter. Which of the following tumor markers is essential during the work up?

A 62-year-old woman presented with abdominal pain, constipation and anorexia for 8 months. On examination, a solid irregular fixed pelvic mass was appreciated. Pelvic transvaginal ultrasonography showed a multilocular ovarian mass. Based on staging and histological classification, she was diagnosed with an advanced epithelial ovarian cancer. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 30-year-old woman presented to the Emergency Department at 03:00 o'clock with right-sided abdominal pain in the lower quadrant. She rates the pain at a level 9 on the 1-10 pain scale. The pain was sudden, associated with nausea and vomiting. A human chorionic gonadotropin urine test was negative. On palpation, there is tenderness and a mass is noted. An ultrasound confirms a mass of 6 cm diameter. Blood pressure 120/70 mmHg, Heart rate 110 /min, Respiratory rate 20 /min Temperature 37.0° C oral Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old woman comes to the clinic complaining of loss of appetite, bloating and abdominal pain. Clinical assessment and investigations confirmed the presence of moderate ascites, pleural effusion and bilateral ovarian masses. Cancer antigen 125 (CA-125) was 95 unit/ml. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old woman comes to the clinic complaining of loss of appetite, bloating and abdominal pain. Clinical assessment and investigations confirmed the presence of moderate ascites, pleural effusion and bilateral ovarian masses. Cancer antigen 125 (CA 125) was 100 unit/mL. Which investigation is the most helpful in making a diagnosis?

options.text: Magnetic resonance imaging of the pelvic soft tissue

questions.stem: A 25-year-old married woman is found to have a 5-cm left adnexal mass during a routine pelvic examination, which is confirmed by ultrasound. She denies symptoms or using any contraceptives. Her last menstrual period was 2 weeks earlier. A urine pregnancy test is negative. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 33-year-old woman presented to the Emergency Department with severe lower abdominal pain. On examination, abdomen was diffuse tenderness, more in the lower quadrants, Bimanual pelvic exam showed bilateral adnexal masses and palpable. A diagnosis of bilateral tubo- ovarian abscesses was entertained. Blood pressure 130/70 mmH, Heart rate 100 /min, Respiratory rate 22 /min, Temperature 39.9° C Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

There are many characteristics that may differentiate a malignant from benign adnexal masses by ultrasound images. Which of the following ultrasound characteristics of a mass is suggestive of a benign ovarian cyst?

A 60-year-old woman presented to the Emergency Room with 1-week history of abdominal pain, the ultrasound finding showed a multiloculated, solid, right adnexal mass (see image and lab result). Test Result Normal Values CA-125 900 < 35 U/mi What would be the recommended most suitable option?

options.text: Work up and consultation of a gynecologic oncologist

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman presents to the Gynecology Clinic with diffuse lower right-sided abdominal pain and low back pain that has been progressively worsening for the past month. The pain intensity worsens after sexual intercourse. Patient menstrual periods occur irregularly and with heavy bleeding. Palpation reveals a tender mass in the lower right quadrant. Ultrasound pelvis scan shows a 9X9 centimeter heterogeneous mass filled with calcifications. Which of the following is the most appropriate method of treatment?

A 21-year-old woman G2 P1001 presents to the Emergency Room with a severe lower abdominal pain for 1 day. Pain is dull and intermittent that lasts for 10-15 minutes and is associated with nausea and vomiting. Examination confirms tenderness and guarding in the lower abdomen, it is more on right side and slight fullness in the right iliac fossa (see report). Blood pressure 90/60 mmHg, Heart rate 110 /min, Respiratory rate 13 /min, Temperature 37.6° C, Pregnancy Test: Negative. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 36-year-old asymptomatic woman diagnosed with a 5 cm subserosal uterine fibroid. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
Which of the following is the most common degenerative change of leiomyoma during pregnancy?

A postmenopausal woman undergoing tamoxifen treatment for breast cancer, she had her last gynecological assessment by ultrasonography during her pre-menopausal period 5 years ago. At that time, she had an intramural uterine fibroid measuring 2 x 3 cm. The patient complained of on and off moderate amount of vaginal bleeding and her ultrasound confirmed intramural uterine fibroid measuring 5 x 8 cm and homogenous endometrium 5 mm in thickness. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 48-year-old asymptomatic woman attended the Gynecology Clinic for her Pap smear screening. During pelvic examination, pelvic mass was felt, further assessment by transvaginal ultrasonography indicated the presence of solitary uterine fibroid on the uterine fundus measuring 5 x 6 cm. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Regular follow up with yearly pelvic ultrasound
Regular follow up with pelvic ultrasound and complete blood count every two months

questions.stem: A 39-year-old woman presented with menorrhagia. Pelvic ultrasound confirms the presence of uterine fibroid. What is the most likely location of this fibroid?

A 32-year-old known case of secondary infertility found to have a submucosal uterine fibroid measuring 6 cm on pelvic ultrasound. She desires to preserve her fertility. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 50-year-old woman with menorrhagia due to a large uterine fibroid was seen in the clinic to complete the consent form of an elective hysterectomy. What is the most appropriate step in this condition?

A woman comes to the clinic for having a history of increasing pelvic pain, which is cyclic in nature and increasing in intensity just before menses. Which of the following is an acceptable method for diagnosing endometriosis?
A 30-year-old woman with a history of infertility for 6 years complains of severe dysmenorrhea unrelieved by naproxen. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 20-year-old woman was recently diagnosed with endometriosis. She is concerned with the progression of endometriosis to malignancy. What would be the best provided information to the patient about endometriosis regarding her concern?

options.text: Has no relationship with cancer in general
Has clear relationship with thyroid cancer
Appears to be associated with epithelial ovarian cancer

questions.stem: A 33-year-old woman was referred to the Gynecology Clinic because of secondary infertility. Detailed clinical history revealed that she has a history of severe dysmenorrhea. Which of the following will typically be the cause of her dysmenorrhea?

A 24-year-old married nulliparous has an 18-month history of cyclic, debilitating pelvic pain related to menses which are regular and heavy requiring 10-15 thick pads on the days of heaviest flow. For the past year, the patient has been engaging in regular intercourse without contraception in an attempt to conceive. Pelvic examination showed normal-size, immobile, retroverted uterus with nodularity and tenderness on palpation of the uterosacral ligaments. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old nulliparous presented with an 18-month history of cyclic and debilitating pelvic pain related to menses. Menses are regular and heavy, requiring 10-15 thick pads on the days of heaviest flow. The patient has been engaging in regular intercourse without contraception for 1 year in an attempt to conceive. Pelvic examination revealed a normal-sized, immobile, retroverted uterus with nodularity and tenderness on palpation of the uterosacral ligaments. Which of the following would most likely help in the diagnosis?

A 39-year-old woman, who is a mother of 3 children and has completed her family, she is a known case of endometrioma in the right ovary that has been removed 2 years ago. She came to the clinic complaining of mild to moderate dysmenorrhea and deep pain during intercourse along with her chronic lower abdomen pain. Pelvic ultrasonography revealed the presence of a left ovarian cyst measuring 6X7 cm that appeared to be an endometriotic cyst. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Removing the cyst when the size becomes more than 10 cm
Aspiration of the content of cyst under ultrasound guidance
Total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy
Removing the cyst laparoscopically with ablation of any endometriotic spot

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman presents to the clinic complaining of pelvic pain, dysmenorrhea, and dyspareunia. She denies any history of fever or vaginal discharge. Ultrasound was performed (see image and report). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg, Heart rate 76 /min, Respiratory rate 18 /min , Temperature 36.6 °C Ultrasound: Describes the appearance as containing "ground glass* internal echoes Which of the following would be best described to the patient regarding her condition?

options.text: Antibiotics are required to be initiated
Association with infertility to be considered

questions.stem: A 45-year-old P5005 woman is complaining of severe secondary dysmenorrhea and menorrhagia. Pelvic examination reveals the uterus is symmetrically enlarged and tender. Endometrial biopsy is normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old P5+3 presented to the clinic complaining of abnormal uterine bleeding for the last 3 months, the menstrual period is regular every 30 days and lasts for 5 days, associated with blood clots and pain that is not relieved by simple analgesia. The patient had previously undergone myomectomy 12 years back and 3 surgical evacuation for incomplete miscarriage. On examination, the uterus was not palpable but on pelvic examination, the uterus was found to be bulky and tender with no adnexal mass. BMI 40 kg/m2 Which of the following is the most likely explanation for this patient's presentation?

A 33-year-old woman presents with a history of amenorrhea for a year following dilatation and curettage because of abnormal uterine bleeding. She underwent both progesterone and combined estrogen and progesterone withdrawal tests with no response. Her serum FSH level was normal, Which of the following syndromes is the most likely diagnosis?

A 48-year-old woman has had 2 inflammatory pap smears 3 months apart and a normal pelvic examination. A colposcopically directed biopsy of a normal appearing cervix revealed invasive carcinoma. Which of the following is the best next step in management?

A 22-year-old woman presents to the Women's Health Clinic for a routine examination. Her menstrual cycle occurs every 28 days and lasts for 5 days with moderate bleeding. Clinical breast examination showed bilateral symmetry with no abnormal findings on palpation. However, she reported regular breast tenderness that began 3 days prior to menses. There was no known maternal or paternal history of cancer. She wishes to become pregnant within the next 2 years. Which of the following screening tests should be done?

A 60-year-old woman's recent pap smear yielded a result of Atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance (ASC-US). She was given topical vaginal estrogen for one month and was scheduled for another pap smear a week after the treatment cycle has completed. The second pap smear showed ASC-US as well. Which of the following is the most appropriate next investigation?

A 34-year-old woman non-smoker with 2 previous normal deliveries presented for a routine pap smear and her last pap was normal 7 years ago. The patient has had 1 episode of venereal warts at 18 year-old with no recurrence. The rest of her history is not significant (see report). Pap smear: A typical squamous cells of undetermined significance. What will be the first step in management?

A 30-year-old married woman has had an abnormal Papanicolaou test result. Repeated smears were suggestive of high-grade intrepithelial lesions. Pelvic and rectal examinations were normal. Which of the following is the next step in management?

A 30-year-old para 3 woman presented with a significant history of smoking 2 packs of per week for the past 7 years. She was using a progestin-only pills. She has had annual Papanicolaou examinations for the past 9 years and all results have been normal. Bimanual pelvic examination showed normal findings. Papinicolaou smear repeated with results of low-grade epithelial lesions. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

A 40-year-old sexually active patient presents for cervical cancer screening. Physical examination is unremarkable, menstruation is regular with a 28-day cycle and last menstrual period was 5 days ago. Which of the following is the best advice about Pap smear?

options.text: Three negative results and no further screening

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman presented with postmenopausal bleeding. Pelvic examination revealed a fungating irregular mass from the cervix. Which of the following has the highest diagnostic value?

A 33-year-old woman presents to the clinic after an incidental finding of a mass in the cervix. She denies any complaints of pelvic pressure, pain or menorrhagia but admits to have occasional post coital bleeding (see image). Which of the following is the most appropriate in counselling the patient?

options.text: Excision to be performed in the clinic
Admission and further workup is required
Reassurance and follow-up in a few months
Broad spectrum antibiotics need to be started

questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman complains of Post-coital bleeding. Speculum examination reveals cervical mass. Which of the following is the most appropriate next investigation?

A 35-year-old healthy woman attended the Gynecological Clinic for her regular Pap smear screening. Upon speculum pelvic examination, the uterine cervix appeared raised irregular mass measuring 10 X 12 mm localized on the cervix left lateral aspect.Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Reassurance until the pap smear result

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman attended Outpatient Clinic complaining of fresh vaginal bleeding occurring after each intercourse. This problem has been disturbing her over the last 3 months. Upon examination, her speculum examination revealed normal cervix. The report of Pap smear is showing squamous cell carcinoma. Which of the following is the most appropriate next immediate action?

A 31-year-old woman P2 presented to the Women's Health Clinic for a routine physical examination. She has presented to routine health examinations annually for the last 5 years. Records indicate that in the previous year, she has negative tests for both the human papilloma virus and the papanicolaou cervical smear. This year both tests are with no abnormal findings. When should the tests be repeated?

A 35-year-old pregnant woman at 13-weeks of pregnancy presented with painless vaginal bleeding. Vaginal examination shows a suspicious lesion of the cervix (see report). Fetal ultrasound: Shows normal viable fetus and size corresponds to her gestational age. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
A 27-year-old sexually active woman came for annual examination. 3 years ago, she had a pap smear which was reported to be normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
A 24-year-old woman comes to the clinic. She is married for 3 years and has no previous pap smears. She asks for a pap smear during the visit. Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Should get pap smear during this visit
Do not screen now, wait until she is 30 years of age
Next screening after 5 years with a combination of cytology and HPV testing
Cervical cancer screening in women younger than 30 years is likely to lead to more harms than benefits

questions.stem: What is the recommended age to start Pap smear screening for cervical cancer in married women? A. 20-24
Which of the following is the recommended frequency of Pap smear screening for cervical cancer? A. Every year

A 55-year-old woman comes to the Gynecology Clinic complaining of a mass protruding through her vagina when standing for quite sometimes especially during cough and straining She has 7 children that were delivered vaginally. The last delivery was complicated by prolonged second stage and ended up with vacuum extraction delivery of a 4.2 Kg baby. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

A 67-year-old woman attended the Gynecological Clinic for the follow up of lichen sclerosus diagnosed a few years earlier. Upon examination, a small mass measuring 0.5 x 0.5 cm was identified on her right labia majora. Punch biopsy was taken from the lesion and sent for histopathology. Which of the following is the most likely histopathological finding?

A 57-year-old menopausal woman, presents for evaluation of post-menopausal bleeding. She is morbidly obese, hypertensive and diabetic. Endometrial sampling showed complex endometrial hyperplasia with atypia. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A 43-year-old woman gravida 2 para 2 has had oligoovulation due to polycystic ovary syndrome and used cyclic progesterone for withdrawal bleeding. Approximately 5 years ago, she discontinued taking progesterone. Which of the following risks is increased?

A 32-year-old obese woman with history of irregular menstruation and chronic anovulation, found to have atypical complex hyperplasia on endometrial biopsy. Which of the following is the most definitive treatment?

A 40-year-old woman is complaining of abnormal uterine bleeding. She is known diabetic on oral hypoglycemic agent for 5 years and her menarche at the age of 13. The last 3 cycles were heavy, however, denies any weight loss or palpitation. Which of the following would make the highest risk of endometrial cancer?

A 38-year-old woman presented with dysuria and increased frequency of urination. History reveals, she is allergic to sulfa, penicillin, and shellfish (see report). Blood Pressure 120/80 mmHg, Heart Rate 80 /min, Respiratory Rate 16 /min, Temperature 38.0° C Urine Dipstick: Positive for leukocyte esterase. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A patient comes for a follow-up 2 weeks after a vaginal hysterectomy with anterior and posterior repair; the patient had leakage of urine from the vagina during micturition. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old woman presented to the clinic with urinary leakage for the last 6 weeks. She cannot hold her urine and urine leaks even before she reaches the bathroom. History revealed she has been menopause for the last 6 years. Which of the following is the first step in the evaluation?

A 58-year-old multiparous woman is complaining of urine leakage at laugh or cough. She is not able to hold her urine along with feeling of "dragging" or "balloon-like" sensation in the genital area for the past 4 months. Physical examination is normal except for bulging of the lower anterior vaginal wall. Which of the following is the most likely cause of those symptoms?

A 23-year-old pregnant woman presented with frequency and dysuria for 5 days (see lab result), Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg, Heart rate 76 /min, Temperature 37.6 °C Leukocytes 30 (0-3 per high power field) Which of the following is the best treatment option?

A 42-year-old P6036 complaining of vaginal fullness, heaviness and discomfort that progress over the day and becomes noticeable after prolonged standing. She used to apply manual pressure to empty her urinary bladder completely. She also had stress urinary incontinence. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 66-years-old woman presents with a single and asymptomatic bright-red papule at the urethral meatus. The surface bleeds easily on touch (see image). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 56-year-old multiparous patient on oral estrogen, complains of painless urine incontinence when coughing, sneezing, or laughing for 1 year. On examination, there was mild vaginal atrophy and constrictor muscle laxity. Urinary incontinence is demonstrated in the lithotomy position with Valsalva maneuver (see report). Urinalysis: Normal. Which of the following would be the recommended management?

A 70-year-old man presents with urinary incontinence. The patient's bladder is palpably distended after voiding. The patient stated that he voids frequently, although he has difficulty initiating the urine stream.Which of the following is the most likely type of incontinence?

A 35-year-old woman delivered her fifth baby by vacuum extraction due to prolonged second stage of labor 3 months ago. The woman was complaining of leakage of urine when she coughed, sneezed or laughed. The symptoms have started after delivery and persisted since then Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 6-year-old girl brought by her mother with vulvar itching and bloody vaginal discharge for few days. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old menopausal woman presented with vulvar irritation associated with urgency and frequency. Examination of the external genitalia revealed odorless watery discharge and generalized vulvar erythema with excoriation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 22-year-old woman presented with headache, malaise and fever. Examination revealed multiple, bilateral painful anogenital vesicles. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 32-year-old pregnant woman at 26-weeks of gestation diagnosed with large genital warts in the vulva. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
A 34-year-old patient at 38-weeks of pregnancy with genital chlamydia trachomatis. Which of the following is most commonly acquired infection by the newborn in such a condition?
A 27-year-old woman presented at 24-weeks of gestation with dysuria and lower abdominal pain. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
An infant presents to Well Baby Clinic. She can keep her head up unsupported and need back support to set. She can smile and can reach mouth. What is the developmental age in months?

A 2-week-old infant seen in the clinic. Rubbing side of his mouth with tip of the little finger is one of the primitive reflexes (see image). What is expected age (in months) for this reflex to disappear? A.
A 2-week-old infant seen in screening clinic (see image). What is expected age (in months) for this reflex to disappear?

A 5-year-old boy is brought to the clinic by his mother. She is concerned of bed-wetting overnight despite toilet training, compared to his sister when she was in his age she controls herself. Until what age this is considered as a normal behaviour?
When assessing development in a 9-month-old infant, which of the following is expected to observe at this age?

options.text: Beginning to use a spoon rather sloppily

questions.stem: A 7-month-old infant visits Well Baby Clinic. Which of the following this infant should be able to do?

options.text: Hold crayon and draw a circle
Transfer objects from one hand to the other
Use thumb and index finger in crude pincer grasp

questions.stem: A 15-month-old child brought to the clinic by his parents. He was born at 36 weeks by normal vaginal delivery. At 8 months' test for hearing was done, which was normal. The parents say that he babbles, but does not speak 2-3 word phrases yet. On physical examination, the child appears normal. Which of the following is the appropriate action?

options.text: Reassure the parents that this is a normal variant

questions.stem: A child who can jump on 2 feet, build a tower of 6 blocks, use 2 word phrases and compares 2 items. What is the developmental age?

A 4-year-old boy present to the clinic with a worried mother, for general assessment and evaluation of his development. He can hop on 1 foot but not able to balance for 10 seconds, draw square, tells a story but not able to use the future tens and has a preferred friend. Which of the following is the most appropriate response to his mother?

options.text: He is growing normally according to his age
He has delayed development in gross and fine motor aspect
He is growing normally but delayed in the speech and language
He is delayed in all aspect and required further investigation

questions.stem: A 4-year-old child presented to the clinic with delayed language and speech, and learning difficulties. Which of the following is the most appropriate test?
The illnesses and problems children encounter are highly age dependent. Which of the following represent an infant age group?
Which of the following phases contribute the most for the final height of the child?
Which of the following statements is normal weight gain in infants?

options.text: Double their birth weight at 10 months
Mean weight gain by 10 g/day in the first 3 months
Mean weight gain by 15 g/day in the first 3 months
Mean weight gain by 30 g/day in the first 3 months

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate advice to a mother about the breastfeeding schedule for her full-term newborn in the first year?

options.text: On demand every 2-4 hr for first 2 months
On demand 6 times per day for first 2 months
On demand 6-8 times per day at age 8-12 months

questions.stem: Which of the following is a common reaction to a parent's illness in 12-year old girl considering her developmental stage?

options.text: Difficulty speaking directly about strong or difficult feelings
Unable to understand or appreciate details of diagnosis, prognosis and treatment
Incorporate themes of illness in their play, such as pretending to have their parent's symptoms
Likely to shift to earlier, less mature behaviors (e.g., fussiness, difficulty with separations or bedtime

questions.stem: An 8-week-old infant presents by his mother to Well-Baby Clinic worried about her baby crying with diagnosis of infantile colic. Which of the following is the most appropriate counseling should be given?

options.text: Infants cry an average of 5 hours per day, peaking at 6 weeks of age and gradually decreasing
Infants cry an average of 6 hours per day, peaking at 6 weeks of age and gradually increasing
Infants cry an average of 2 hours per day, peaking at 6 month of age and gradually decreasing
Infants cry an average of 2.2 hours per day, peaking at 6 weeks of age and gradually decreasing

questions.stem: An infant sits in the tripod position, can roll from prone to supine and vice versa and attempts to reach a toy beyond reach but cannot pick up cereals between 2 fingers. What developmental age in months is this most consistent with?

A mother of a 3-year-old child asks about his language development. He easily communicates with other children and 75% of his speech is understood by strangers. He asks questions frequently and follows 2-part commands. What is the best description of this language development?

In a prone position, an infant can lift his head 45 off the examination table and moves his head from side to side while following an object. He smiles and coos when the doctor plays with him, but cannot maintain a seated poison. What is the age in months this child most likely at
Which of the following language milestones is appropriate for a 4-year-old child?

options.text: Can count to 4 and tell a story

questions.stem: By what age in months should a child smile?

A child is brought for a well-child visit. He is healthy and developing normally. The child can name 4 colours, define 5 words, understand prepositions, hops on 1 foot, and gets dressed with little assistance. What developmental age in months is this most consistent with?

A 6-month-old child is brought to the paediatrician for a well-child visit. The infant was born at full term after a normal pregnancy and spontaneous vaginal delivery. The linear growth and the amount of weight gained over the past 6 months are both appropriate. The mother began feeding the infant pureed baby foods approximately 1 month before while also continuing breastfeeding. The infant has been well since birth. The physical examination is normal for age. developmental screening exam is performed. Which of the following gross motor skills is most appropriate at his age?

options.text: Rolls from prone to supine position
Rolls from supine to prone position

questions.stem: By what age in months should a child learn to speak a few words?

A child is brought for a health maintenance check. The parent states that the child sits up alone without support, pulls himself into a standing position, explores around furniture, crawls without difficulty. grasps objects with a thumb and forefinger, uses repetitive consonants such as "dada", and responds to the sound of his own name. What age in months is the child most probably at?

A 4-month-old girl is brought to the Paediatric Clinic for a routine monthly exam. The baby smiles back at people and imitates facial expressions. She uses eyes and hands together and reaches out with one hand for a toy. There is babbling along with a facial expression. The girl pushes up to her elbows when lying on the tummy. Weight 7300 grams (=50th percentile) Length 67 cm (=75th percentile) Which additional developmental milestone is most likely to have?
Which of the following is usually the first sign of puberty in boys?

An apparently normal child is being evaluated. He runs around, tells short stories and plays a "father role". He draws his brother with a head, hands and feet. He undresses himself for the examination. What is the most likely age of this child?
Which of the following is the most typical milestone for a 4-year-old child?

A 5-month-old baby referred to the doctor from the Well-Baby Clinic. His mother is concerned, because he could not pass the developmental screening tests done by the nurse. What is the best developmental test would help the doctor to reassure the mother?
Which of the following can the average 3-year-old child perform?

options.text: With alternating feet catch a ball

questions.stem: While in the clinic, a child runs towards the doctor, walks upstairs with one hand held and pours out pellets from a bo]le. The child does not handle a spoon well and cannot put 3 words together. What is the approximate age in months?
During a health supervision examination, a mother reports that her son can say his name, feeds himself, separates easily from parents and rides a tricycle. What is the developmental age in years?

While at the clinic, an infant crawl toward the doctor, rolls over, sits briefly, transfers objects from hand to hand and grasps objects using his radial palm. The infant is unable to use a pincer grasp. What is the approximate age in months?

A child walks with one hand held, says a few words besides "mama" and "dada", and picks up pellets with an unassisted pincer grasp, but does not insert them into a bo]le. What is the approximate age in months?

While in the dinic, a child demonstrates an ability to run, is able to open a door and climb onto furniture. The child uses 3-word sentences, but does not know his full name and does not climb up stairs using alternate feet. Which of the following is the approximate age in years?

An infant lies with his head to one side and raises his head slightly, but the head lags when pulling up to a sieng position. The infant smiles when involved in social interactions and follows moving objects 180 degrees, but does not a]empi to reach for them. What is the approximate developmental age in weeks?

A child's developmental assessment conforms the following (see table). Motor Walks alone, crawls up stairs Adaptive Makes a tower of three cubes, makes a line with crayons Language Jargon, follows simple commands Social Indicates desire by pointing Which of the following is the most likely age in months?
Which of the following is a developmental screening tool that relies only on information from the parents?

options.text: Bayley scales of infant development D.Safety word inventory and literacy screener

questions.stem: When a mother placed her infant on the examining table, the infant laughs out loudly. As the doctor approaches him, he squeals and reaches for his mother. What is the most likely developmental month for this child?

A child accompanied by his parents walked into the examination room. He is holding a ball. The doctor asks to let him see the ball; he threw the ball towards the doctor. Then he reaches out to catch it when the doctor throws the ball back to him. He draws a straight line on the paper and then picks up a few blocks from the floor and stacks one on the top of the other. What is the most likely developmental month for this child?

A child enters the clinic and says "hi" to the doctor then turns to the mother and says "milk". The mother gives her a bottle of milk, and the child tries to give her doll a drink. The mother shakes her head, and the child says "no". After which the child smiles and points to her own mouth and says "mouth". When her mother wipes the doll's face, the child says "me" and begins to imitate the mother's action and gives the doll a hug. What developmental age in months is this most consistent with?

A 9-year-old boy is brought for a check-up. Parents are worried because he is short. On examination, his height is below the 5th percentile for his age but increasing steadily. The parents ask if he will always be short in the future. What is the most important factor to answer the question?

options.text: Weight for height and age DUpper to lower segment Ratio

questions.stem: During a routine check-up, a child shakes hands, knows his name, gender and age. He can dress with help and ride a tricycle. He points to red colours when asked to do so but had difficulty copying a square. What is the age in years this child is most likely at?
A full-term baby delivered normal vaginal delivery, received initial care and ready to be discharged home. Which of the following vaccines should be given before discharge?

A 3-hour-old newborn seen in the Nursery for assessment. The mother gave a family history of early infancy death secondary to primary immunodeficiency. Which of the following is the recommended first vaccination (Saudi program)?

options.text: Give BCG and follow up in clinic
Give vaccines as per national program

questions.stem: A 1-year-old boy has come for vaccination. The mother explains that his 6-year-old sister has received a renal transplant 2 months ago and is currently on immunosuppressive medications. Which of the following vaccines should be avoided?

A 2-year-old boy is brought to the clinic with a large left-sided abdominal mass. IV pyelogram shows, the mass appears to arise from the left kidney and distort and displace the collecting system (see report). Chest X-ray: Multiple pulmonary nodules. which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 13-year-old boy with sickle cell disease, presents with severe unilateral hip pain, which has developed over the past few weeks. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
What is the recommended age (in months) to screen for haemoglobin level in infant with no risk factors?

A 2-year-old girl is seen in the clinic for pallor and tiredness. On examination, she looks healthy with normal vital signs; growth parameter and physical exam apart from conjunctival pallor (see lab results). Blood pressure 90/70 mmHg Heart rate 97 /min Respiratory rate 18 /min Temperature 36.6 °C Oxygen saturation 95 % RBC 4.5 4.8-7.1 x 1012/L (Newborn) 4.6-4.8 x 1012/L (Child) Hb 87 165-195 g/L (Newborn) 112-165 g/L (Child) HCT 0.32 0.44-0.64 (Newborn) 0.32-0.42 (Child) MCH 25 28-33 pg/cell MCV 74 80-95 fl Reticulocyte 1.1 0.2-1.2 % Platelets count 350 150-400 x 109/L Iron 7 7.2-17.9 mol/L (Infant) 9-21.5 umol/L (Child) Total iron binding capacity 94 17.9-71.6 mol/L Ferritin 12 20-200 pg/L Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 9-month-old infant is suspected to have iron deficiency anemia. CBC and iron profile ordered pending the results. which of the following indexes is expected to be high?

A 4-month-old infant seen in the clinic with CBC result. The mother concern about the findings (see lab results). Hb 9 165-195 g/L (Newborn) 112-165 g/L (Child) MCH 25 28-33 pg/cell MCV 77 80-95 fl Reticulocyte 1.1 0.2-1.2 % Platelets count 330 150-400 x 109/L WBC 10 9.1-30.1 × 109/L (Birth) 6.1-17.5 x 109/L (1-23 months) Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is the most suggestive of hemolysis as a cause for neonatal hyperbilirubinemia?

A 13-year-old boy who has a palpable lymph node in his neck. One of his close relatives has been diagnosed recently with lymphoma and his family are very worried about it. Which of the following is most suggestive of a malignant rather than an infectious cause of lymphadenopathy?

An 11-year-old girl is brought to the clinic for a physical exam because one of her cousins has been diagnosed with lymphoma recently. She is worried about a palpable lymph node in her neck. Which of the following lymph node locations would be most concerning for malignancy?

A 2-year-old child presents with painful swelling on the dorsal surfaces of the hands, feet, fingers, and toes (see lab results and report). Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 100 /min Respiratory rate 22 /min Temperature 38.9° C Test Result Normal Values Hb 77 112-165 g/L Reticulocyte 3.9 0.2-1.2 % Blood smear: Several elongated and crescent shaped red blood cells. Which of the following is the most appropriate on-going care?

A 5-year-old child presents with bleeding from the nose and gums and easy bruising of the extremities for 3 days. Prior to this presentation, the child had a viral upper respiratory tract infection. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

options.text: Idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura B. Henoch-schönlein purpura

questions.stem: A 3-year-old child presents for a routine physical examination. The parent is concerned that the child appears pale. The child's diet includes a lot of milk but very little red meat. Haemoglobin is 80 g/L with hypochromic and microcytic indices. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

A 13-year-old boy who has a palpable lymph node in his neck. One of his close relatives has been diagnosed recently with lymphoma and his family is very worried about it. Which of the following may influence the physician to consider lymph node biopsy?
Which of the following vitamins is administered to newborns to prevent haemorrhagic disease?

A 6-year-old child is brought to the Emergency Department with chest pain and signs of respiratory distress. The child has a minor upper respiratory tract infection, which suddenly worsened with temperature elevation. The physical examination found an increased pulmonic and systolic ejection murmurs (see lab results and report). Нь 65 112-165 g/L WBC 18 4.5-10.5 x 109/L. Reticulocyte 12 0.2-1.2 % Chest X-ray: Shows lobar infiltrates. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-year-old boy presents with imitability, lack of atention, and an abnormal craving for chalk to eat. He was born full term by vaginal delivery and has had appropriate developmental milestones. He was breached and weaning started at the age of 9-months. The examination is normal except for pale conjunctiva (see lab results). Hb 76 112-165 g/L НСТ 0.22 0.32-0.42 WBC 5 4.5-10.5 x 109/L Platelets count 250 150-400 x 109/L MCV 65 80-95 f1 MCH 22 28-33 pg/cell MCHC 248 260-340 g/L Reticulocyte 0.9 0.2-1.2 % Total iron binding capacity 701 17.9-71.6 mol. Which of the following is the most suitable treatment?

A 7-year-old boy is brought to the clinic with the complaints of mild abdominal pain, constipation and aggression. The mother told the physician that he is used to eating tissue paper and chipped off wall paint (see lab results and report). RBC 3 9 4 6-4.8 x 1012/L Hb 74 112-165 g/L MCH 23 28-33 pg/cell MCV 70 80-95 fl Peripheral blood smear: Microcytic hypochromic. Which of the following is the most likely type of anaemia?

A13-year-old boy presents for elective surgery. He has a significant past history of bleeding tendency and has contracture of right knee and hemarthrosis. Which of the following is the most likely underlying clinical disorder?

A 4-year-old boy presented to the clinic with a history of decreased appetite and activity over the past month. He lost significant weight since his last outpatient visit. Which of the following is the most common cause of cancer in such patients?

A 2-year-old girl brought to Primary Clinic because the mother noticed she is pale. She had history of drinking 3 glasses of cow's milk daily, very picky eater and refusing to eat meat.
